WoW Forever Bots 0.1.28 (client builds 70707 and 70685)

A big update with a new look for the launcher, many quest fixes, and smarter bots in dungeons and raids.

Launcher
• The launcher window is larger, sharp on 4K screens, uses Segoe UI lettering and is blue by default.
• New Realm type window: Normal, PvP, RP, RP-PvP or FFA PvP.
• The Bots window now has the plain Bots lines (Reserve, ActiveCap, PerZone, InCity). One choice controls the settings file the server really uses, and old bot numbers become the plain Bots size at the first start.
• Fixed a mistake in the launcher's manifest that could stop Windows from starting the launcher.

Bots
• Dungeons and raids: the tank pulls with line of sight in mind, the group waits at the return point while the tank pulls back, and a boss the bot cannot attack is no longer treated as the next pull. Dire Maul bots take the wing the group stands in.
• Bots that fall more than 15 seconds out of range are brought to their player.
• Shaman bots put down their air and fire totems, not only Healing Stream.
• Bot hunters read the Tranquilizing Shot book at 60.
• The auction house buyer buys player stacks and buys out instead of bidding.
• Hired bots: settings for gear, health and what each broker sells. Hire brokers now show their talk option in the client.
• World bots no longer invite players who walk past to a group.

Quests and world
• Zephras Isle: the Al'Aketh Skypriests and Honor Guards at the Shrine of Akir move and fight; carry Fillion Flamebreeze to safety; get the Mark of Akir back; Resaan's Heirloom can be retrieved for The Fate of a Loved One; Vayn Moongaze sells his reputation items.
• Among the Faithful, The Affray, The Defias Brotherhood, Shiny Junk, Lost in Battle, Finding Warmth (the Fallen Logs are back) and the note you found (79007/79008) work again.
• Nine quest-starting items that could never drop now drop normally.
• Warrior trainers Seena Skybreaker, Corsan Earthrazer and Blademaster Ren offer training.
• Creature and object spawns that our world data lacked are back.

Game rules
• Mage: pressing Comprehend Scroll deciphers the first untranslated scroll in the bags.
• Honor is credited as the Honor currency, so the PvP quartermasters can be used.
• Victory Rush is usable after a kill on the Classic 1.60 client; periodic damage and healing can crit; joining an arena reads the Classic 1.60 packet.
• Talents are not reset when a level below 10 is gained with no point spent.
• Camp buffs no longer stack with their class buff.
• Fixes for crashes: quest lookups with no player in the world, a taxi node outside the taxi mask, an emptied vein used again, a battleground template with no map.

Good to know
• Game builds 70707, 70685 and older (the list in client-builds.txt) keep working.
• Log in with your account name written as name@local (with the @local part) and the password from the secrets folder, or with the account made by Create account.

• To update from an earlier release, use the Update button in the launcher (close and reopen the launcher after it says the launcher was updated).

WoW Forever Bots 0.1.27.2 (client builds 70707 and 70685)

This is a fix for 0.1.27.1. A server whose game is still on build 70685 (or older) could not start after 0.1.27.1: it stopped while loading the game tables ("Incorrect layout hash in SpellDuration.db2"). 0.1.27.2 starts with the game tables of both builds, so the server runs from a game on 70707 and also from a game on 70685 or older.

What changed
• The server converts the spell duration table of an older game (70685 and before) into the layout of build 70707 when it starts. The old file is kept next to it as SpellDuration.db2.legacy-layout. Nothing for you to do.
• Nothing else is different from 0.1.27.1.

Good to know
• If your server did not start after 0.1.27.1, press Update in the launcher (or use the update zip below) and start the server again.
• Game builds 70707, 70685 and older (the list in client-builds.txt) keep working.
• Log in with your account name written as name@local (with the @local part) and the password from the secrets folder, or with the account made by Create account.

WoW Forever Bots 0.1.27.1 (client build 70707)

This is a fix for 0.1.27. After the game updated itself to build 70707, a server set up from that game could not start: it stopped while loading the game tables ("Incorrect layout hash in SpellDuration.db2"). 0.1.27.1 reads the 70707 tables, so the server starts again.

What changed
• The server reads the build 70707 layout of the spell duration table (the game added a column). Updating a server whose game is on 70707 now finishes "Updating the server's game tables" and starts normally.
• Nothing else is different from 0.1.27.

Good to know
• Run the server from a game on build 70707. A server whose game is still on 70685 or older cannot read the tables of that build any more; update the game through Battle.net first. Friends on an older build can still join a server that runs on 70707.
• If your server did not start after updating to 0.1.27, use the Update button again (or the update zip below) and start the server; no other step is needed.

Install and update
• To update from an earlier release, use the Update button in the launcher (close and reopen the launcher after it says the launcher was updated).
• For a new install, download WoW-Forever-Bots-0.1.27.1.zip, unzip it into a folder whose path has no spaces (for example, C:\WoWForever), and run WoWForeverLauncher.exe or double-click Install.cmd.

WoW Forever Bots 0.1.27 (client build 70707)

This release supports the new game build 1.60.1.70707 (clients on 70685 and older still connect), brings back hosting for friends, keeps the login fix of 0.1.26.3, and fixes how bots tank, how dungeons are walked, and several quests.

Launcher
• Host for friends through a Cloudflare tunnel is back. Press Turn on and the launcher asks how friends should reach you: the Cloudflare tunnel (nothing to set up in your router, a new join code each time) or port forwarding. If your network cannot reach Cloudflare, the launcher says so before it tries.
• The login key is written into the real key table only, as in 0.1.25 and 0.1.26.3, so the crash after login stays fixed. The launcher keeps waiting until the table appears (it only exists once you press Login), and writes keyscan.txt next to itself if it never finds one.
• Still in: playing a newer game build at your own risk, and finding a game that was moved to a new folder.

Bots
• Hunter pets gain loyalty again.
• On the owner's Attack order in the open world, the tank now walks to the mob and starts the fight first, and the damage dealers wait for its lead, the same as on Pull. A Protection warrior or paladin no longer stands still while the others run in.
• Dungeons: boss routes match their waypoints in Razorfen Downs, Gnomeregan, AQ40 and seven more vanilla dungeons; a damage bot that reaches a mob running for help switches to it; healers dispel a member taken out of the fight before healing; the group keeps its kill focus while anyone still sees it; a failed path blocks only its own floor; walking into the frostwyrm lair raises Sapphiron.

Quests and world
• The Taming Rod now works on the Windsong Crawler (the client refused the cast with "Invalid target"). The quest "Taming the Beast" can be finished.
• Spawns for nine quest NPCs and twenty Forever quests, built from our own sources.
• Chol'aruk the Ravener and his quest (Bainham in the Barrens) are rebuilt from our own sources and he stands on the floor of his cave under Thorn Hill. His model is a stand-in for now, and how players get into the cave is not solved yet.
• The quest, NPC, vendor and loot data that was copied from another server's database is no longer shipped. An update keeps what your server already has. A new install has fewer Forever-only quests and NPCs than 0.1.26 until we have rebuilt them from our own sources. Quests that depended on removed NPCs are taken out so none can be accepted and not handed in.

Server
• The start script refuses to start the server when a setting appears twice in one file of server\worldserver.conf.d and names the file and the two lines (before, the server window just closed).

Not in this release
• Hired bots: the code and the Playerbot.Hire.* settings are in but off by default, and no hire NPCs are placed.

Install and update

addons.description:
PawnFind upgrades, do more damage, win.
Pawn helps you find upgrades for your gear.

You can use it if you're just starting out. Pawn comes with advice from the experts (Ask Mr. Robot and others) who know that some stats are far more useful than others. Fire mages want a lot of crit, and shamans don't want strength at all, so just because that new ring has a higher item level, it might not actually be that good for your spec. Pawn will show you green arrows to help you spot the upgrades.

You can also use it if you run your character through simulations and build your own Excel spreadsheets: all of Pawn's stat weights are customizable so you can tailor it for your exact character and preferences. It's useful for all roles, not just DPS.

addons.changelog:
GatherMate21.52.4 (2026-10-22)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Update TOC
• Add separate minimap icon alpha setting
This adds independent alpha controls for world-map and minimap node icons.
Previously, the existing world-map alpha setting was also applied to minimap pins. This made it difficult to reduce the opacity of GatherMate2’s minimap tracking circles without also fading icons on the world map.
Changes:
• Add a separately saved minimapAlpha preference.
• Add distinct “World Map Icon Alpha” and “Minimap Icon Alpha” controls.
• Apply minimapAlpha only to minimap pins.
• Preserve the existing alpha preference for world-map icons, maintaining backward compatibility.
This makes active gathering-node blips easier to distinguish from GatherMate2’s nearby spawn indicators.
• Updates for Coiled Isle
Co-authored-by: Leon
Co-authored-by: Hendrik Leppkes
• Check for secret target in Collector:SpellStarted
Opening a Mislaid Curiosity treasure in a delve throws this on every cast. Even the check for spellcast secret wasn't enough - the target also needed checked. This adds issecretvalue(target) to the same early return.
• Add separate locale for the vanilla names of nodes
Blizzard renamed these in some locale (deDE, maybe more) during late
vanilla, but classic and forever use the old names, so add an override
here to allow both names to be used.
Fixes #62
• More secrets protection
• Hide options for other gather types on Forever
• Only load locale files on their matching client
Always load english as fallback.
• Update TOC for future 12.1.5 support, and only loading on mainline clients
• Only load retail storage mods on Standard client
• Add WoW Forever support and skip spells missing on the client
Add interface 16001 for the WoW Forever client, which shares the Mainline API.
Not every client knows every spell, eg. spell 195122 does not exist on Forever,
so C\_Spell.GetSpellName returned nil and the spells table was built with a nil
key, which raised "table index is nil" at load time. Build the table from a list
and skip entries whose spell name failed to resolve.
addons.name: GatherMate2

addons.description:
A fan-made project that upscales every icon in WoW Forever from 64×64 to 256×256.

Download the icon pack · How to install it

Originals are shown stretched, the way the game draws a 64 px icon at a larger size.
Black-frame version
A second pack swaps the game's grey bevel for a thin black frame. The bevel is cropped off, not framed over, and
round or shaped icons are left as they are. Download forever-icons-black-frame from the same release.

If you use a UI addon that skins action buttons (ElvUI, for example), it already trims the icon edges and adds its own
border, so the main pack is the better fit.

addons.description:
SilverDragon tracks rares in World of Warcraft. It will try everything possible to notice them and tell you about them.
How does it search?Vignettes
Those little skull icons you see on the minimap. If one of them is a rare SilverDragon knows about, it'll yell at you.
Targets
If you mouse over or target a rare mob, SilverDragon will notice it.
Nameplates
If you have enemy nameplates turned on, SilverDragon will keep an eye on them to look for the names of known rares.
Macro
SilverDragon can also create a macro to target any rares that are known in the current zone. You can stick this on your actionbars as a button to spam while chasing after a rare, or bind it to a key. This is sort of a last resort.
Chat
Some rares yell in zone chat. If SilverDragon notices those yells, it'll alert you.
Dark Magic
This abuses detection of when Blizzard blocks attempts to call a protected function (TargetUnit) to work out when you're in targetting range of a unit with a given name

This inherently causes in-game errors, so it is disabled by default. Enable in the addon config under Scanning > Dark Magic.

By default it's less-aggressive, scanning through rares in the zone without known vignettes at a rate of 1/second. However, you can turn that rate way up if you'd like. You can also turn on an option to automatically hide the error messages it causes, but beware that this will potentially cause taint issues that'll leave you needing to /reload eventually.
How will I know when a rare is seen?Frame
When a rare appears, SilverDragon will pop up a frame that you can click on to target it.

Warning: If you're in combat, secure action restrictions mean that it won't show up until combat finishes.
Sounds
You can choose from assorted sounds to play when a rare is seen. The sound can loop for a while, to make sure you don't miss it.

There's special settings for rares that drop mounts and world boss rares which you might want to call up a group for. If you're sitting mostly-AFK on a Time-Lost Proto Drake spawn, you probably want the sound that plays to be utterly ridiculous and go on for a good long while, to make sure you don't miss that sucker.
Messages
A notice can be sent to a number of places:
• your scrolling combat text
• your chat frame
• a channel in your chat frame (announcing it to your party, for instance)
• a popup window
• etc

addons.description:
Can I Mog It? adds a line to item tooltips to tell you if you have learned a transmog appearance in World of Warcraft.
• Curse
• WoWInterface
• GitLab Project
• Issues
• Wiki/FAQ
Features
• Informative tooltips about the learned status of an item's appearance.
• Bag icon overlays for telling at a glance what to mail or sell.
Why do I need it?
The default UI tooltip only tells about items the character you are on can wear. Can I Mog It works across your account for all of your characters and tells you:
• If you have learned it.
• If you have learned it, but from a different item.
• If you have learned it, but can't transmog it (wrong armor type, faction).
• If you can learn it.
• If you can't learn it on this character.
• If it can't be learned (necks, trinkets, rings, etc.).

addons.description:
Premium ElvUI Plugin & Complete Interface Suite for World of Warcraft
About •
Features •
Screenshots •
Addon Profiles •
Installation •
Chat Commands •
Changelog •
Credits

About
Eltruism is a feature-rich ElvUI plugin that extends ElvUI with extensive customizations, signature gradients, combat voice alerts, and tailored interface profiles for World of Warcraft.

Both the DPS/Tank profile and the Healer profile are handcrafted for 16:9 displays and thoroughly tested across 1080p, 1440p, 4K, and Ultrawide resolutions.

Every single feature in Eltruism is 100% modular and can be toggled on or off to match your personal preference.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Eltruism is an ElvUI plugin and requires ElvUI to function.

Features
• Dual Tailored Profiles: Dedicated DPS/Tank and Healer layouts with pixel-perfect unitframes, actionbars, and raid anchors.
• Signature Gradients: Silky smooth color gradients across Unitframes, Blizzard Raid Frames, Nameplates, and Aurabars with Lua-cached performance.
• Audio & TTS Voice Alerts: Text-To-Speech announcements for offensive/defensive cooldowns, interrupts, and low health/mana warnings.
• Dynamic Nameplates: Dynamic height scaling, threat-colored borders, integrated power bars, and debuff highlighting.
• Cursor HUD: Rotating HUD rings anchored to your cursor indicating cast time progress, GCD, and cooldown timers.
• Actionbars & Glows: Customizable spell activation and proc glow animations with bespoke speeds, plus Shaman totem tracker glows in Classic.
• Sleek Themes & Skins: Soft shadows, dark & light themes, custom class textures, role icons, and reskinned Character Panel, Quests, and companion AddOns.
• Transparent Unitframe Health: Quickly toggle sleek transparent unitframe health backgrounds via /eltruism transparent.
• Navigation & Waypoints: Enhanced /way command with real-time distance calculations, ETA arrival estimation, and navigation arrow tracking.
• Instant Fast Loot & Wishlist: True instant auto-looting with zero window lag, movable LootText alerts, junk vendor automation, and personal loot wishlist tracking.
• Chat Enhancements: Inline item icons in chat links, smooth chat fade, and the !keys shortcut to share your Mythic+ dungeon keystone.
• Combat & AFK Immersion: Contextual combat music playlists, relaxing AFK screen with 3D character models and music, and bespoke mail arrival sounds.
• Unified Castbars: Unified player, target, and focus castbars with dedicated interrupt protection shields and timer tags.
• Multi-Expansion & Modular: Actively maintained for Retail, MoP, Wrath, Classic Era, and WoW Forever.

Screenshots
Click any preview image to open the full-resolution 4K screenshot.

DPS & Tank Profile

Streamlined combat layout with centered actionbars, dynamic resource trackers, Details! skinning, and non-intrusive raid anchors.

Healer Profile

Optimized central raid frames with gradient health bars, debuff prioritization, out-of-range fading, and dedicated mana monitors.

Themes & Skins

Modern soft shadows, character panel enhancements, quest dialogue restyling, transparent unitframe health, and bespoke borders.

Dynamic Nameplates & Castbars

Gradient nameplates with dynamic height, threat-colored borders, integrated power bars, aura glows, and unified interrupt castbars.

Addon Profiles
The Eltruism installer includes tailored profiles for the following companion addons:
• Details! Damage Meter
• BigWigs
• Capping
• Deadly Boss Mods (DBM)
• DynamicCam
• Immersion
• Questie
• Gladdy
• Nameplate Scrolling Combat Text
• WarpDeplete
• ElvUI Floating Combat Text

addons.description:
AHDB scans the whole auction house, keeps a price history per item that you can see as a graph (Alt-click any item),
shows vendor and AH prices in item tooltips and warns you before you list something for less than a vendor would pay.
Your characters on other accounts can share their prices, and one parked at the AH can look up current prices for you.
Anyone in your guild or group can ask for a price with !ahdb in chat.

The Classic / Mists / retail versions (and their MoLib based code) are on the
legacy branch.
Price history graph
Alt-click any item (bags, bank, chat links, AH lists, merchant...) or use /ahdb price (or
/ahdb graph for just the window; a link, itemID, name or part of a name like wool cloth) to see its price
history, even away from the AH:
• Each bar goes from the lowest to the median unit price: per scan for the recent scans (side by side, a line marks the
hours without scans), per day for the last 30 or 180 days. Hover for the values.
• The quantity listed is under the graph, the vendor price is the green line.
• 7 and 30 day median prices and the lowest price seen, for each auction house (Alliance, Horde, Neutral).
• Drag the bottom right corner to make the window bigger, it keeps its size and place.
• Each auction house's last 30 scans are kept (whole days, up to 7 days), then one summary per day for 180 days, so the
saved data stays small even when scanning every 15 minutes.
Sharing prices between your accounts
Saved data is per WoW account. To use the prices one account scanned on another one's characters (e.g. one
character parked at the AH, another one out in the world):
• /ahdb trust (or target the character and /ahdb trust) on both sides, then:
• Item tooltips tell when an online trusted character has newer prices ("AH price 3h old, Alt: ask Wa"): hold Alt
to get them. The price window gets them by itself. They're added to your price history.
• Live button of the price window (or /ahdb live ): a trusted character at an open AH searches the item
right now (fresher than its last scan) and sends its current min / median price and quantity listed; both
characters show it in chat and add it to their price history.
• Only between characters of the same faction (whispers don't cross factions): each faction has its own trusted
characters. /ahdb trust lists who's trusted and online.
• Out of the game, ahdbmerge
merges the price history of all the accounts of a WoW install, and keeps it in sync between your computers.
What does it do?
• Opening the auction house starts a full scan (Blizzard allows one every 15 minutes per game session; hold Shift to
skip it). The "AHDB Scan" button above the AH shows when the next scan is possible. Away from the AH, a chat
message tells when it's possible again, and the minimap button's tooltip (or /ahdb next) shows the time left
(right-click the button for the options, drag it to move it).
• Prices are kept separately for the Alliance, Horde and neutral (goblin) auction houses.
• Item tooltips show the vendor price per unit (the game's own line is for the whole stack) and the last scan's
AH min and median price, how many are listed, and the 30 day min - median. Also install
BVP
(BetterVendorPrice) for full stack and stack size vendor prices: BVP then shows the vendor lines and AHDB the AH
ones, no duplicates.
• On the AH sell page, the price turns red with a warning when, after the AH cut, you'd get less than a vendor pays.
• Items vendors refuse even though they have a sell price are learned and get no vendor price (/ahdb unsellable).
• Price history graph of any item: Alt-click it or /ahdb price (see above).
• Prices shared with your characters on other accounts, and live AH prices from one parked at the AH (see above).

addons.description:
Your game. Front and center.

Umbra preserves the idea, not every old design decision.

A project for modern, readable unit frames in World of Warcraft Retail, WoW: Forever and the Classic clients — Mists of Pandaria, the Anniversary realms and Classic Era. Inspired by ShadowedUnitFrames, with a visual identity of its own: class-colored edges, rectangular character portraits beside the bars, and information right where you need it.

The idea · Design principles · The frames · Using it · Installing · Supported clients · Contributing

> Where it stands. All six design principles are implemented, and every frame in the table below that is not marked otherwise. Everything is set in a small options window or through /uuf, which do the same, and Clique is not supported. Which version is current, the release badge above says; the changelog says what each one settled.

The idea
Your character, your target, and your group should be the focus. The interface should help you understand their status — not compete for your attention.

Umbra brings together compact unit frames, a clear information hierarchy, and restrained styling. Rather than replacing the entire user interface, it stays with the unit frames: player, target, pet, target of target, the boss column and the party column.

> Familiar to use. Distinct by design.
Why “Umbra”?
Umbra refers to the dark inner region of a shadow. The name acknowledges the project's visual inspiration without simply repeating “Shadowed.”

It also captures the thinking behind the project: The interface steps back. Your game stays in focus.
Design principles
Color, shape, and placement should make different kinds of information easy to distinguish. These six principles define Umbra's visual direction, and all six are implemented.

| Principle | Approach and purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| Class color at the edge | A 3-pixel edge and the character's name carry the class color. The health bar stays neutral green by default, and /uuf health class gives it the unit's color as well for anyone who would rather have it there. Class identity and health each have a distinct visual role. |
| A dedicated portrait column | A narrow, rectangular character portrait sits to the left of the name and bars—including on the target frame. Subtle class tinting replaces circular medallions, glowing portrait rings, and images behind the numbers. |
| Resources as a hairline | Mana, energy, and rage use a thin line rather than a second dominant bar. Health remains the primary information. |
| Auras with an underline | A slim colored line beneath each icon replaces a prominent full border. Personal and important effects stay easy to identify without cluttering the grid. |
| Distinct shields and healing | Hatching indicates absorbs; a light, translucent segment represents incoming healing. Both stay clearly distinguishable from current health. |
| Range through fading | Out-of-range units fade together with their portraits. Class color and character identity remain intact rather than being replaced by a grayscale filter. |

Accent color belongs to the interface. Class color belongs to the unit. The health bar belongs to health.
The frames
Every frame shares the same anatomy — the portrait column, class color at the edge, the name, a health bar and the power hairline — and is then cut down to what it is for. Names are set in a font family the way Blizzard's own labels are, one file per alphabet, so Cyrillic, Korean and Chinese names draw as well as Latin ones.

> The sheets on this page are drawings, not screenshots. tools/mockups.py redraws the frames from the same metrics Core/Defaults.lua lays them out with, deriving the heights and offsets rather than copying them, so what they can show is geometry and color. The fonts, the spell art in an icon and the portrait models belong to the client and stand in here.

| Frame | What it carries |
| :--- | :--- |…

addons.description:
BVP shows what your items are really worth to a vendor (per item and per full stack, not just the stack you happen
to hold) and, when your bags are full, restacks them and tells you which item is the cheapest to throw away.

Made for WoW Forever, and the same version also works on retail. The Classic / Mists versions (and their MoLib
based code) are on the
legacy branch.
Bags full? BVP knows what to throw away
BVP highlights in your bags the item that's the cheapest to get rid of. When your bags get full, it first restacks
your partial stacks (also into the reagent and profession bags) to free slots without losing anything, then tells
you in chat which item it is.

It's smarter than "lowest vendor price": a stack that's still filling up with what you're looting counts for what it
will be worth. Say you have 4 of something that sells for 3s each and 2 of something else for 4s each, and both keep
dropping: if both stack to 5, throw away the 4, that slot is worth 15s full, the other one 20s. If they stack to 20
and 5, it's the other way around. BVP does that math for you.

It only looks at your main bags (where loot goes), not the reagent or profession bags, skips items that can't be
sold (Hearthstone, quest items...), and never destroys anything itself. Cheap but needed, like your fishing pole?
/bvp keep and it moves on to the next one.
Tooltip info
The game's own "Sell Price" line is for the stack under the mouse. BVP adds only what that line doesn't tell you:
• the price per item and how many stack together,
• what a full stack sells for.

Works anywhere item tooltips show, including bags, vendors, item links in chat and the auction house.

For auction house prices and history in the same tooltips, also install
AHDB (Auction House DataBase): BVP shows the vendor
lines and AHDB the AH ones, no duplicates.
Commands and options
• /bvp cheapest: restack and show the cheapest slot, anytime.
• /bvp restack: merge partial stacks to free bag slots.
• /bvp keep: never suggest the current cheapest item again; /bvp keep for any item (again to undo),
/bvp keep list to see them.
• /bvp config: options (Options > AddOns > Better Vendor Price): single line tooltip or only with Shift held,
highlight, chat message when the bags are full, auto restacking.
• /bvp lists all commands.
More information
Get the binary release using curseforge client or other
addon manager or on wowinterface.

The source of the addon resides on https://github.com/mooreatv/BetterVendorPrice

Releases detail/changes are on https://github.com/mooreatv/BetterVendorPrice/releases

addons.description:
This is a library addon for the popular MMORPG "World of Warcraft.
Description
LibEditMode is a library that allows a developer to integrate their frames into the Edit Mode introduced in Dragonflight.

It has feature parity with the systems Blizzard added to the Edit Mode, but limits its re-use of methods to limit taint issues.

For details on how to implement this in your own addon, please see the wiki:
Feedback
If you have a question, please use the discussions section on GitHub.
If you would like to report a bug or contribute to the project, please follow this link to get started.
Legal
Please see the LICENSE file.

ClassicUI Forever
Version 0.41.1 (2026-11-03)
Links:
• Full Changelog
• v0.41.1 on GitHub

Changed
• The interface size questions and check boxes name the game's UI Scale and the percent they set, in fewer words. The classic layout's size question also says what your UI Scale is now.
addons.description:
Puts the original Classic look back on top of the modern interface in World of Warcraft: Forever. Every piece has its own toggle, so you can keep any of the new stuff you like.
What it restoresBars and buttons
• The main bar with its gryphons and stone band, the micro menu and bags in their old sockets, and the old square buttons.
• Shaded XP and reputation bars, the key ring, and Classic-sized bag slots if you want them.
Unit frames and combat
• Player, target, focus, target of target, pet and party frames with the old art, elite dragons and class colors.
• Classic cast bars, combo points, swing timers, the breath and fatigue bars, and classic damage numbers over the mob you hit.
• The 1.x nameplates, with the elite dragon and class colors if you like.
• The game's damage meter in the old look.
Windows
• The 1.x spellbook, quest log and character sheet, with the old reputation, skills, PvP, currency and stats tabs.
• The classic talent window, with an option to show all three trees side by side.
• A classic Legacy window for Forever's Legacy trees, challenges and reward track, also with its three trees side by side if you like.
• The classic professions book, the 1.x trade skill window (or a wider double pane) and the classic trainer.
• The social window with the old friends list, Who list, guild roster and raid tabs, and the group finder dressed to match.
• Classic bags, or one bag for everything, with the reagent bag inside it if you like.
• The classic world map with its quest list, and Era's quest watch.
• The merchant, mail, quest, gossip, trade, bank and loot windows in the old metal border and stone, and the old loot roll frames.
• The game menu and settings as the old dialogs, with the old check boxes, sliders and drop downs.
Minimap and chat
• The round minimap with the old tracking, mail, zoom, calendar and clock spots.
• Micro menu buttons as icons on the minimap ring, and a bag that collects other addons' minimap buttons.
• The old chat look.
Themes
• Dark and Bronze themes for the classic art, and a flat color look.
Move and size your windows
Unlock any window with the lock in its title bar, drag it anywhere, size it from its corner grip, and click reset to put it back. Reset windows in the options puts every window back at once. Windows open side by side as they did in Era.

An optional classic edit mode layout, offered on first login, puts the bars where 1.x kept them. Your current layout and keybinds are left alone.
How it works
Every piece is a checkbox in the options window (/fcui) or in the game's Settings. Turn one off and the modern look comes back in place. The art is read from the game client, with bundled copies of the original Classic files as a fallback for the pieces the client no longer ships.

The addon also loads on retail, for the pieces retail has.
Commands
• /fcui opens the options window; /fcui settings opens the same toggles in the game's Settings.
• /fcui help lists every toggle and command; /fcui on|off sets one, for example /fcui classicBar off.
• /fcui status opens the status report: addon version, game build, the settings you changed and your other addons, to copy into a bug report.
• /fcui layout creates and selects the classic edit mode layout; /fcui prompt shows the first-login question again.
• /fcui welcome shows the welcome note again; /fcui whatsnew shows what changed in recent versions.
• /fcui legacy opens the classic Legacy window.
• /fcui textures builtin|bundled reads the art from the game client or from the copies in media/.
• /fcui reset puts every setting back to its default.
Feedback
Bug reports and ideas are always welcome.
• Issues: https://github.com/fallenguards/classicuiforever/issues/new/choose
• CurseForge: https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/classicui-forever
• Changelog: CHANGELOG.md

addons.description:
About M.A.M.A. Multiboxing
MAMA is now Mama-forever: Multiboxing helper for WoW Forever (the new beta client, interface 16xxx). One standalone addon, no libraries and
no other addon needed. It is the successor of MAMA + DynamicBoxer + MoLib, rewritten for Forever only.

It lets all your windows of the same team:
• find each other and form a group automatically (one-time setup: on one PC, just type a slot number per window),
• follow and assist whoever is the lead, with one key or one macro,
• follow in a train ordered by team slot, with one key,
• share, accept and abandon quests together,
• sell the same junk at every vendor (a team wide sell list, greys optional),
• with master loot, give each item to the team member who uses it (quest items to whoever still needs them),
• be managed from a small team status window (invite, disband, party/raid, target, ...),
• mark a member away for a while (Alt+Left click its status window row, or /mama away): no invites, follow
alerts or quest/dialog sync, still trades and forwards whispers.

Names in Forever are First Last (with a space) and there is no realm part: Mama-forever treats them as opaque names.

releases.changelog:
Simple Item Levelv74.1 (2026-10-16)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• TOC for 12.1.5

Simple Item Levelv74 (2026-10-16)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Tweak a few other display settings for Forever
• Fix position of character item level in Forever

Simple Item Levelv73 (2026-10-05)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Inspecting a player could error when an item level was unknown
The average item level added up the slot levels without checking them.
Inspect data can be incomplete, and the sum could fail with a nil error.
If any level is nil, skip the averaging until the data arrives. The core
inspect-refresh should be called again when that happens.

Simple Item Levelv72 (2026-09-27)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Profession equipment had no item levels unless misc items were shown
Profession tools and accessories are not weapons or armor, so they only
showed under "Show on anything else". The profession frame's gear slots
were also skipped. Treat them as equipment, and handle those slots like
the character frame.
• Remove a dropdown init guard that never took effect
Nothing set frame.initialize, so the dropdowns initialized on every show.
That is the behaviour we want, because it keeps the selection in sync
after slash command changes.
• Guild bank and Inventorian ignored the bags option
The guild bank and Inventorian's cached (offline) items still showed
item levels when bags were turned off.
• Classic: ranged items were compared against the main hand
Before Pandaria, ranged weapons, thrown weapons and relics go in the
ranged slot, but the upgrade check used the main hand slot for them.
Thrown weapons and relics were never checked.
• Shared ContinuableContainer could drop callbacks
A container keeps only the latest ContinueOnLoad callback. The character
and inspect average levels shared one, so the average could stay hidden
when both loaded at once. ItemIsUpgradeAsync also shared one, so callers
that checked several uncached items got only the last callback.
• Slash command could toggle non-boolean settings
"/simpleilvl position" set the position to false, which made every item
button error until the saved variable was fixed. The same applied to the
other position settings and to quality. Only toggle boolean settings.
• Forever: inspecting players caused an error
InspectPaperDollFrame\_UpdateButtons => InspectPaperDollFrame.UpdateButtons
...but only for Forever, so far.
Fixes #64

addons.description:
tullaCTC is a World of Warcraft addon that provides additional options for
theming cooldowns. It is built to work with the new secrets APIs that were
introduced in of World of Warcraft v12.0.0 (Midnight). With it, you can do
things like:
• Show cooldown counts on everything
• Change the font and color of cooldown text
• Show text in red when under 5s
• Show tenths of seconds
• Hide cooldown spirals

The configuration UI can be brought up via /tullaCTC
Themes & Rules
You can customize cooldown appearances for different parts of the UI via creating themes and then asigning them to different parts of the UI via the rules panel. tullaCTC comes with a bunch of builtin rules for
different parts of the UI, as well as an API to add in additional ones:

OmniCC Feature Comparison
With World of Warcraft v12.0.5, tullaCTC can do just about everything that
OmniCC could do, except:
• Min Size
• Max Duration (though you can replicate this via setting a transparent text color above a duration)
• Conditional Scaling
• Finish Effects

addons.description:
Dejunk is an addon for World of Warcraft that helps determine which items are considered junk based on options and lists, then allows selling them in bulk or destroying them one at a time.
Features
• Sell junk automatically or on demand
• Destroy junk one at a time, with optional confirmation
• Separate settings and lists per profile, shareable across characters
• Tooltips explain why an item is considered junk
• Auto-repair equipment at merchants
• Overlay icons on junk in your bags
• Open lootable items one at a time from a dedicated frame
• Use keybindings or chat commands for most actions
Options
Profile Options has three groups. General holds Auto Repair and Auto Sell. Include and Exclude determine what's considered junk, and several of their options support per-quality checkboxes, letting them apply only to specific quality tiers.
Include
• Include Artifact Relics — Include artifact relic gems (Retail only)
• Include By Quality — Include items by quality tier (poor quality included by default)
• Include Below Item Level — Include equipment below a set item level
• Include Below Price — Include items with a stack price below a set value
• Include By Equipment Type — Include equipment of the selected armor and weapon types (cloaks never match)
Exclude
• Exclude Above Item Level — Exclude equipment above a set item level, even if it's on an Inclusions list
• Exclude Above Price — Exclude items with a stack price above a set value, even if it's on an Inclusions list
• Exclude By Equipment Type — Exclude equipment of the selected armor and weapon types (cloaks never match)
• Exclude Equipment Sets — Exclude equipment saved to an equipment set (Not available on Classic Era or TBC Classic)
• Exclude Unbound Equipment — Exclude equipment that is not yet bound
• Exclude Warband Equipment — Exclude equipment eligible for the warband bank (Retail only)

Each Include and Exclude option applies to selling, destroying, or both. They start on both, except Include Below Price on selling and Exclude Above Price on destroying.

The price options compare the price of the whole stack and never affect items with no vendor price.
Lists
Inclusions and Exclusions lists are available at both the global and per-profile level. Per-profile lists take priority over global ones.
• Inclusions (Global) — Always considered junk across all characters, unless overridden by a per-profile exclusion, Exclude Above Item Level, or Exclude Above Price
• Exclusions (Global) — Never considered junk across all characters, unless overridden by a per-profile inclusion
• Inclusions (Profile) — Always considered junk for the active profile only, regardless of any other setting except Exclude Above Item Level and Exclude Above Price
• Exclusions (Profile) — Never considered junk for the active profile only, regardless of any other setting

Items can be added to lists by dropping them directly into the list frame or the Junk Items frame.
Import/Export
Each list has its own Import/Export frame, opened from a button on the list frame itself. It shows the list's item IDs as plain text, ready to copy out. Paste in a new set of IDs and click Import to add them to the list, or click Export to refill the box with the list's current IDs.
Junk Items
The Junk Items frame, opened via /dejunk junk, its keybind, or a right-click on the merchant button or the minimap icon, lists items currently considered junk along with their total sell value.
• Left-click an item to sell it
• Right-click an item to add it to an Exclusions list
• Drop an item into the frame to add it to an Inclusions list
• Start Selling and Destroy Next Item act on the listed items that are junk for selling and destroying, respectively

The Auto Junk Frame option shows the frame automatically at a merchant when you have junk items, and closes it once you don't.
Profiles…

releases.changelog:
Changelog[3.4.1] - 2026-10-13Changed
• Updated the Retail interface version for patch 12.1.5.

Changelog[3.4.0] - 2026-10-11Added
• Added a Keybindings page to the main window. Click a button, then press a key, a mouse button, or the mouse wheel to bind it, or right-click a button to unbind it. A key set here takes priority over the game's own binding for it, and a note names the game binding it covers. Keybindings cannot be changed in combat.
Changed
• DejunkApi:IsJunk() now reuses its results until the bags, the options, or the equipment sets change, and refreshes the equipment sets at most once per frame. This is an attempt to reduce the CPU spike when opening the bank or Warband bank with Baganator enabled (#280).
Fixed
• Fixed the game freezing on WoW Forever with gamepad support enabled after opening and closing the game's Keybindings page with Dejunk enabled.
Removed
• Removed Dejunk's section from the game's Keybindings page. Keys bound there are lost, so set them again on the new Keybindings page.
• Removed the keyboard button from the main window's title bar, which opened the game's Keybindings page.

Changelog[3.3.1] - 2026-10-09Changed
• New profiles start Include Below Price, Include Below Item Level, and Include By Equipment Type with only Poor quality checked, instead of every quality. Existing profiles are not changed.

Changelog[3.3.0] - 2026-10-08Added
• Added Exclude Above Price and Include Below Price, which compare the price of an item's whole stack with a set value. Each applies to selling, destroying, or both: Include Below Price starts on selling and Exclude Above Price on destroying. Items with no vendor price are never affected. Like Exclude Above Item Level, Exclude Above Price takes priority over Inclusions lists.
• Added Include By Equipment Type and Exclude By Equipment Type, which apply to equipment of the selected armor and weapon types and qualities, with the types shown as columns of checkboxes. Cloaks never match.
• Added an Applies To setting to all other Include and Exclude options, so each can apply to selling, destroying, or both. They start on both, which is how they worked before, and your saved settings are kept.
• Added a Size setting to Bag Item Icons: Small (the default) or Large, which covers the whole slot as it did before 3.2.0.
Changed
• The main window now has a sidebar for switching between your lists, Global Options, and Profile Options. Each options page gets the whole window instead of sharing it with your lists.
• The options pages are split into groups: General, Include, and Exclude on Profile Options, and Safety, Interface, and Bags on Global Options.
• The lists search box now sits at the top of the lists, always visible, instead of opening in the title bar.
• Each option shows a short description under its name, and clicking anywhere on an option turns it on or off.
• Options with extra settings, such as an item level or item qualities, show them right under the option, faded while the option is off.
• Item quality checkboxes are labeled with each quality's name.
• Item tooltips show separate Selling or Not Selling and Destroying or Not Destroying verdicts, each with its reason, instead of one verdict. An item that cannot be sold or destroyed says so.
• Item levels are typed straight into the option and saved as you type, instead of right-clicking the option to open a popup.
• Options that don't apply to generic, cosmetic, or fishing pole items are marked with an asterisk, explained by a note at the bottom of the page.
• Toggle Options Frame is now Toggle Main Window in the key bindings, the minimap icon tooltip, the AddOns settings page, and /dejunk help. Existing key bindings are kept.
• Item quality names and the Alt, Ctrl, and Shift key names now come from the game, so they match its language.
Fixed
• Bag Item Icons did not appear in the default bags on WoW Forever.
• Items in the reagent bag were not scanned on WoW Forever, so junk in a bag in the reagent slot was never found.
• On WoW Forever, characters with the same first name and different last names shared a profile assignment, because only the first name was used. Affected characters may need their profile selected again.
• Left-clicking an item in the junk frame tried to sell it even when it cannot be sold.
• Opening Dejunk from the addon compartment menu caused a forbidden action error and could freeze the game on WoW Forever with gamepad support enabled.
Known Issues
• On WoW Forever with gamepad support enabled, Dejunk's key bindings taint the game's Key Bindings screen, which can crash the game.
Removed
• Removed Include Unsuitable Equipment in favor of Include By Equipment Type.

Changelog[3.2.0] - 2026-09-27Added
• Added Auto Lootables Frame, a global option that shows the Lootable Items frame automatically when you have items to loot, and closes it once you don't.
• Manually opening the Lootable Items frame with nothing to loot now prints a message instead of showing an empty frame.
Changed
• Bag Item Icons now overlays a small icon in the item's top-left corner instead of covering the whole slot, with a lighter background behind it.
• Auto Junk Frame now reacts to whether you actually have junk while at a merchant, instead of just opening when the merchant window opens and closing when it closes. It opens as soon as you have junk, even if that's not until partway through the visit (a list or setting change can turn bag items into junk, buying an item back can too), and closes itself once you no longer have any. Closing it yourself keeps it closed for the rest of that visit; leaving the merchant always closes it.

addons.changelog:
1.1.0
Full Changelog
• Modern Aura Groups now behave like Dynamic Groups. The row starts where you place the group, and each display’s X/Y Offset moves only that display. Groups you made before 1.1.0 keep their old layout automatically (a single “Use old row layout” checkbox in the group settings), so nothing you have changes.
• Bars, progress textures and textures can now sit anywhere in a Modern Aura Group row, after a Modern list, and move with it, including in combat. Bars keep their overlays, ticks and texts; progress textures work in both their straight and circular forms.
• The options preview now lays rows out the same way the live row does, including the display limit’s cut-off.
• Fixed member offsets in Modern Aura Groups being measured from the wrong display, which pushed rows and neighboring icons sideways.
• Fixed Centered growth rows not centering correctly, and ordinary displays landing in the wrong place in mixed rows.
• Fixed the Grid preview showing members that the live grid leaves out, and the Lua error when switching a row group to Grid with the editor open.
• Fixed an error after reloading during combat (“Auras cannot be accessed when secret”).
• Cooldown Manager: entries are found more reliably, including on login and when Blizzard’s viewers load late, and no longer loop on failed lookups.
• Spell Known triggers wait for spell data when it isn’t loaded yet instead of reporting the spell as unknown.
• Many option tooltips and warnings rewritten to say exactly what the addon does; confusing or outdated ones removed.
• Known limit: after a reload during combat, Modern displays appear when the fight ends.

ForeverAuras is a powerful and flexible framework that allows the display of highly customizable graphics on World of Warcraft's user interface to indicate buffs, debuffs, and other relevant information. This addon was created to be a replacement for WeakAuras2 in WoW Forever.
Quick Start
To open the options window, type /fa or /foreverauras into your chat and hit enter or use the minimap icon.

• A non-exact 'Spell Known' load condition naming a rank you don't have no longer fails at login while the client is still loading that spell's data; the aura loads as soon as it arrives.

1.0.0
Full Changelog
• Two gaps in the loading-screen settle closed: a reminder unloaded by the editor during the second after a loading screen stays unloaded, and one reloading during that second no longer sees the empty aura list as settled.
• Dynamic groups can no longer be left stuck by an error in another aura, the editor, or a groups own layout: every group is resumed, and errors keep their traceback.
• A failed display update is reported with its traceback and retried on the next update, rather than treated as done.
• The editor's mass delete and button layout jobs release the groups they paused if they fail midway.
• Aura (Modern) Aura(s) Missingdisplays no longer flash for a moment after a loading screen while the client's aura data settles.
• Aura (Legacy) Aura(s) Missing triggers no longer flash after a loading screen: the players momentarily empty aura list is ignored and the player is rescanned a second after entering the world, including for reminders that load during that second.
• Note: during that second the players last known auras are kept for every trigger type, so a buff that genuinely vanished in the zone can read as present for up to a second.
• The Cast triggers note now says that another unit's spell is secret on this server in and out of combat.
• A capture for Aura(s) Missing icons that show after a zone: /run ForeverAuras.debugMissing = true.
• Spell Known load conditions go back to the plain check from .121; the rank-family handling added in .123 is removed as a precaution.
• Unloading or hiding a Modern display now switches off everything it owns, including the group shadow and a unit frame glow that combat had locked; those are retried after the fight.
• Stand-in copies in Modern Aura Groups stop their positioning and glow work while hidden, and pick it up again when shown.
• Pulsing Border and Pulsing Glow highlights only run while an aura is shown.
• Closing the editor during a fight no longer re-runs the preview teardown every frame.
• A Modern aura whose load conditions first become true in combat is built and shown right away instead of after the fight.
• Fixed an error when a Modern display had 'Icons per row' set and Max Icons was 1.
• Went back to the nameplate handling from .126, at 40 plates, which keeps the anchor fix and drops the pool.
• Removed the region warm-up. It built every unloaded aura after login, and the Modern ones stayed live in the client; that was the heavy feel after logging in.
• Editing, importing or updating a pack no longer leaves live displays behind for auras that aren't loaded.
• Unloading or hiding a Modern display now switches off everything it owns, including the group shadow and a unit frame glow locked by combat, which is retried after the fight.
• Stand-in copies in Modern Aura Groups stop their positioning and glow work while hidden, and resume when shown.
• Pulsing Border and Pulsing Glow highlights only run while an aura is shown.
• Closing the editor during a fight no longer re-runs the preview teardown every frame.
• A Modern aura whose load conditions first become true in combat is now built and shown right away, instead of waiting for the fight to end.
• Fixed an error when a Modern display had 'Icons per row' set and Max Icons was 1.
• Performance optimizations
• Fix LUA error for Max Icons under Aura Display
• Displays prepared in the background while you're idle no longer keep watching unit and nameplate events until they first load. They're put to rest once their preparation finishes, so a combat-only aura doesn't end up with missing icons when it loads in combat.
• Renaming an aura right after logging in no longer risks it being switched off by the background preparation.
• Performance optimizations on PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED
• Aura (Modern) displays on nameplates now line up with the plate's health bar on the game's own nameplates. They used to sit off to the side because the plate frame is wider than the bar you see.…

0.92.125
Full Changelog
• Aura (Modern) displays on nameplates now sit against the visible health bar the same way Dynamic Groups do. They were anchored to the wider nameplate frame behind it, so they could float some way off to the side.

0.92.123
Full Changelog
• 'Spell Known' load conditions now work for classes that forget old ranks, like Warriors and Rogues. Entering any rank of a spell counts as known if you know that rank or a higher one. 'Exact Spell ID' still means that one rank only.

• Conditions on an Aura (Modern) display that come from other triggers now show a note explaining they can't change the live icon during combat. This is a game restriction, not a bug.

addons.description:
========
For the first time in World of Warcraft, your character can literally become a bard!

Play music for you and the other players, from MIDI files or live, using 22 instruments and 2 percussion sets from various styles: medieval, celtic, folk, tribal and heavy metal. 🤘

Quick links

• 💬 Discord server (EN/FR) for help, good music and more!
• 🔌 Additional modules:
• 🎷 Musician: Extended — Add even more instruments to Musician.
• 📜 Musician List — Save and load your songs in-game.
• 🎹 Musician MIDI — Play live music using your MIDI keyboard.
• 📖 Wiki — Tips and tricks, FAQ and detailed documentation for gamers, developers and music producers.
• 🐞 Bug tracker — Report issues
• 👨‍💻 GitHub repo — Contribute to the project

Un Guide en français est également disponible. 🇫🇷🥖🍷

tl;dr

Left-click on the minimap button to open the main menu.

Type /mus help in the chat window to get the command list.

How to listen to music

All you need is to have the add-on installed. Nothing more is required.
• Enable nameplates with SHIFT+V (or from the add-on options) to see cool animations on characters playing music and show a 🎵 next to the name of your fellow music addicts.
• To mute a player, right-click on their name or portrait to open the menu then select Mute. Do the same to unmute.
• You can also just stop the song being played by clicking the [Stop] hyperlink in the player's emote.
• Right click on the minimap button to enable or disable all the music from the add-on.
• The characters currently playing music can be shown on the world map and the minimap.

How to play music

Musician plays music files in MIDI format. MIDI files have a .mid, .midi or .kar extension and do not contain any sound like MP3s, but a sequence of notes. This is why a MIDI file sounds differently according to the software or musical instrument it's played on.

💡 You can find millions of MIDI files very easily by searching for MIDI + music genre/title/etc. on Google. I also made a selection of cool music files you can try with the add-on.

⚠️ Don't try to convert audio files such as MP3s or YouTube videos into MIDI, the result will be disappointing. This is a tedious work that can only be done manually by experienced musicians.
How to play a song
1. Open the MIDI import tool located at musician.lenwe.io/import in your web browser. (You can also find the import tool in the Interface/AddOns/Musician/MidiConvert folder.)
2. Drag and drop a MIDI file.
3. Copy the generated music code by clicking the Copy button.
4. Back in WoW, left-click on the minimap button to open the main menu then choose Import and play a song to open the main window (or type /music).
5. Click the Select all button then paste the music code in the edit window (Ctrl+V or CMD+V on Mac).
6. Click Play.
Save and load songs in game
Songs can be saved and loaded back in game using the optional add-on MusicianList.
Play as a band
Songs can be played in sync as a band, in which each member is playing a different part.

To allow synchronized play, all band members should be grouped in the same party or raid and have the same song loaded into Musician.

Use the Link/Export button to share songs with your band members.

1. Load the same song as the other members of the band from MIDI, from the list or from a song chat link.
2. Open the Song Editor then check Solo for the tracks you want to play with your character. Adjust other track settings as you like.
3. Click the Play as a band button when you're done (the green LED starts blinking).
4. When every member is ready, the band leader clicks the Play button for synchronized start (the green LED turns on).
5. Song stops playing if the band leader clicks the Stop button.

Remarks:
• Mouse over the Play as a band button to check which members of the band are ready.
• Each band member can do all the changes they want in the Song Editor, except changing the start and end points that would result in being out of sync.…

KeyUIv4.3.1 (2026-10-21)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• feat: support WoW Forever
Forever (1.60.1, interface 16001) plays in classic Azeroth but runs the
Mainline client: the 12.1.5 API with secret values, the Mainline templates
and atlases, and none of the legacy spell globals. Its build number fell in
the isVanilla range, so KeyUI would have taken the Classic Era paths there:
bundled BLPs instead of atlases, no ActionButtonSpellFXTemplate, no combat
lock on action changes and no BINDINGS\_LOADED.
VersionCompat gains isForever and isModern (Retail or Forever). Everything
that follows the client rather than the game now checks isModern, and
USE\_ATLAS follows it. Retail and the Classic clients keep their flags. The
combat-lock message no longer says "on Retail".
Checked against the 1.60.1.70450 dump; no Forever client was available to
test in-game. COMPATIBILITY.md documents the new snapshot layout and re-runs
the API audit against all five clients.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• chore: pull API snapshots from wow-ui-source and watch for new builds
API/ held hand-made client exports named after their build, so every bump
meant re-exporting four clients and rewriting the paths in COMPATIBILITY.md.
tools/update-api.sh now fetches the Interface/AddOns tree of the matching
Gethe/wow-ui-source branch into API//, plus the atlas, global API
and template lists from Ketho/BlizzardInterfaceResources, which stand in for
the Helix folder wow-ui-source does not carry. Before it replaces a snapshot
it lists which API documentation files changed.
check compares each branch's version.txt with the Interface line of
KeyUI.toc. The API Watch workflow runs it every Monday and opens one issue
per interface version the TOC does not list yet.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

releases.changelog:
KeyUIv4.4.0-beta1 (2026-11-03)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• fix: take key input only in edit mode; withdraw ESC at combat start
Key input:
• Mouse and controller keys switched keyboard and wheel input on for every
hover. In combat that is a blocked call: EnableKeyboard, EnableMouseWheel
and EnableGamePadButton are protected functions on secure buttons.
• After an edit session their OnKeyDown handler stayed installed, so a
keypress over a locked key renamed it and was swallowed.
• Keyboard keys never switched input on when hovered, only once at creation.
Renaming a key by keypress in edit mode therefore failed on any key that
had been hovered before.
All three devices now take keyboard, wheel and gamepad input only while
hovered in edit mode, never during combat. The handlers are installed once
per key instead of on every hover.
ESC in combat: lockdown begins only after PLAYER\_REGEN\_DISABLED has been
handled (Clique and Bartender4 still write secure attributes there), so
ApplyEscClose asked InCombatLockdown() too early and left KeyUI's frames in
UISpecialFrames. With "Stay open in combat", ESC then hit a blocked Hide().
It now goes by KeyUI's own combat flag. Combat start also switches off
input on a key hovered in edit mode while that is still allowed.
Also:
• remove the per-device "layout dirty" OnShow/OnHide handlers; Core
replaced them with SetScript, so all but one were dead, and the survivor
generated the mouse keys a second time after a profile import. Core now
hooks instead of replacing, which also brings back SetupButtonFade's
fade-out whenever a device frame appears
• the tutorial probed for its arrow template by creating a frame on
UIParent each time and left it behind; it now asks GetTemplateInfo
• the Controls window's close button discarded keyboard edits only and left
a mouse or controller layout stuck in edit mode
• hide\_all\_frames no longer builds device frames just to hide them
Not yet tested in-game.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• perf: redraw keys only when a binding or slot changes
State events that fire several times a second in combat
(ACTIONBAR\_UPDATE\_STATE, UPDATE\_SHAPESHIFT\_COOLDOWN/\_USABLE,
PET\_BAR\_UPDATE\_COOLDOWN/\_USABLE) rebuilt every key with set\_key. Blizzard's own
buttons only update state or cooldowns on them. KeyUI now does the same and
rebuilds keys only for structural changes (page, bonus bar, slot contents,
bindings, macros). A light icon pass re-reads textures for spell overrides
(SPELL\_UPDATE\_ICON, newly registered), macro conditions and form icons. It
also notices addon bars that page through their own state drivers
(Bartender, Dominos, ElvUI) and rebuilds only the key whose slot moved.
UPDATE\_BINDINGS went through refresh\_layouts, which rebuilds all key
geometry and is deferred during combat, so bindings changed in a fight
(Clique hover-cast, vehicles, other addons) only showed after it. It now
redraws just the keys whose binding differs, which also works in combat.
While closed (by default that includes every fight) KeyUI unregisters all
high-frequency events and pauses its flash OnUpdate. Page, held modifiers
and overlays are read again on opening.
Bindings and what KeyUI makes of each binding string (matched pattern,
label) are cached and dropped on UPDATE\_BINDINGS. Reading bindings was never
restricted in combat; the cache saves work, it does not get around lockdown.
Clicks in combat: the secure "action" attribute could only be written out
of combat, so a Shift+click during a fight used the slot from before it.
With "Detect Modifier" on, all eight modifier layers are now written ahead
as prefixed attributes (shift-action, alt-ctrl-action, ...), which the
secure template picks by itself. Paging during combat still clicks the slot
from the last sync; see COMPATIBILITY.md.
Also:
• every open created a new controller image frame and leaked the old one,
for all users, including those without a controller layout…

Description
This addon is a collection of modules to display various informations ingame about the game, your character, friends, guild and many many more. :-)

Recommentation
It is recommended to use this addon with a data broker display addon... A little list of possible addons:
• panel-addons:\
Bazooka, ChocolateBar, DockingStation, NinjaPanel, TitanPanel\
~~FuBar~~ (was a good old partner in classic times, R.i.P.)
• single-button-addons:\
Candy, StatBlockCore\
~~Fortress~~ (outdated/abandoned/owner is missing)
Broker (Modules)
See List of Modules
Important
• CPU / Memory Usage
Any enabled module need cpu time and memory and this addon is a summary of modules. It is normal heavier than single broker addons but i try to
• For Iconsets and Localization
I have add some php scripts. the script generates the 3 example files for iconset and localization.
I will try to use the php script in this folder to keep all examples up to date... :)
• ElvUI / TukUI skin support missing?
Please install/enable the addon AddOnSkins or AddOnSkins Classic.
It is not a plugin from ElvUI/TukUI, but it is required to help other addons support ElvUI/TukUI skins.
Known bugs
• GPS/Location/ZoneText: Currently the transport menu has a problem with items that must be equipped before use.
Icon sets support
A few years ago i added support for icon sets. My coal was support third party addons to change the icons used by modules from broker_everything. An outdated demo can be found here.
Bug reports, feature requests and Support
Please use the Issues page for bug reports and feature requests.
Localization
Do you want to help translate this addon?\
See Curseforge localization tool

addons.description:
Naowh's companion addon for World of Warcraft Forever

Your BiS list, a dungeon journal, professions, a training planner, gear swaps
and a lot of quality of life, all in one window.

Install | What's inside | Commands | Changelog | Contributing

What's inside
| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| BiS List | Your best-in-slot list in its own window: your gear on a paperdoll, every pick per slot ranked with stars, where each drops and where to run next. Marked on tooltips and called out when it drops. Open it with its own key too. |
| Stat Weights | What each stat is worth to your spec, with your own changes: a line on gear tooltips ("Fire: +9% upgrade" and what it is weighed against), and the BiS List's upgrades and enchants. On BiS List's Stat Weights tab. |
| Dungeon Journal | Every dungeon on Forever, the new ones included, and the raids: its bosses in order and what they drop, your BiS marked, your quests there with what to do first, a tip from Naowh for each boss and how many times you have killed it. A map of each classic dungeon with every boss on it, and in a dungeon the world map (M) shows it, with the Journal beside it. Open it with its own key too. |
| Discovery | Library books to find around Azeroth and who to hand them to, and the Cozy Sleeping Bag's chain step by step. Its Quest List tab has every quest of every zone for your character, your progress per zone, and every quest chain with the step you are on; its Rares tab every rare of every zone on the map, with an alert when you see one. Open the Quest List with /nfquests. |
| Training Planner | What you can train now, what each level brings and what it costs, with the way to your nearest trainer. |
| Professions | Recipes, reagents and crafting in one window, including the recipes you have not learned yet. |
| Gear & Trinkets | Swap equipment sets from a bar, or automatically while you ride or rest. |
| Blessings | Paladin blessings by class and player, shared with your group's paladins. |
| Macros | Class, consumable and focus macros, written and kept up to date for you. |
| Action Bars | Your action bars saved by name and put back whenever you want them. |
| Buffs & Reminders | Buff, consumable and campfire reminders, and a low health warning. |
| Threat Meter | Threat on your target for the whole group, and a warning before you pull. |
| Group Inspect | Everyone in your party or raid in one window: their Naowh Score, item level, gear, talents and stats, and who runs Naowh Forever. Also on a party or raid member's right-click menu. |
| PvP | What your target is doing in a fight: their short buffs and the crowd control on them, and battleground displays. |
| Swing Timer | Your swings from the game's own timer, with marks for timing around them. |
| Druid Mana | A druid's mana while shapeshifted, with the five second rule, the cost of shifting back and how many shifts you have left. |
| Raid Debuffs | The raid debuffs you pick on your target, Sunder Armor to the warlock curses, with the missing ones easy to spot, in combat too. |
| Quality of Life | Questing, loot and bag space, alerts, casting, tooltips, trainer ranks, flight and camp, mail and more, and the Top Bar: friends, guild, the clock and your addon buttons across the top of the screen. |

addons.description:
Voiced quests and NPC dialogue for World of Warcraft: Forever, with audio you
generate yourself from a local text-to-speech model.

The quest text for Forever additions is crowd sourced, please help out by downloading the addon and occasionally running /fvo export.

Four addons on CurseForge: the player, and three voice packs that stack.
• Forever Voiceover
(ForeverVO) — the player, and the only one you need to start. Reads quest
offers, turn-ins, greetings and gossip from installed voice packs and plays
them through a talking-head frame styled after the client's own, with a queue
you can pause, skip and reorder, and a replay button on each quest you open in
the quest log. It also records every line it sees so new audio can be
generated for what is still missing.
Voice packs, each its own CurseForge project, no line in two of them:
• Forever Voiceover: Classic Quests
(ForeverVO_Data_Classic_Quests) — Classic's quests up to level 40.
• Forever Voiceover: Classic Endgame
(ForeverVO_Data_Classic_Endgame) — Classic's quests from level 41 up.
• Forever Voiceover: Classic Gossip
(ForeverVO_Data_Classic_Gossip) — what Classic's NPCs say when you talk to
them.
• Forever Voiceover: Forever Quests
(ForeverVO_Data_Forever_Quests) — the quests Forever adds. These are the
lines being crowd sourced, so it grows as players run /fvo export.
• Forever Voiceover: Forever Gossip
(ForeverVO_Data_Forever_Gossip) — what Forever's NPCs say, crowd sourced
the same way.
• Forever Voiceover: Books
(ForeverVO_Data_Books) — books, letters and plaques, Classic's and
Forever's, read by the narrator when you press Play under the book.

The Classic packs change only when a voice is redone; a reworded Classic quest
stays in its Classic pack and is updated there. Every pack carries the
alternate narrator voices for its own lines. Until 2026-10-06 the packs were
Base, Base Endgame and Data: Forever (ForeverVO_Data_Base,
ForeverVO_Data_Base_Endgame, ForeverVO_Data_Forever); a copy of one still in
AddOns is only consulted for what the new packs lack, and can be deleted.

Install any of the packs, all of them, or none — the player works on its own, it just has
nothing to say until a pack is there.

Built for the Forever client only (Camelot, interface 16001). It uses the
Retail engine APIs: the Settings panel, the addon compartment, mixins, frame
pools. No embedded libraries.
How it works
Quest and gossip text is not in the client files; the server sends it. So the
addon captures text as you play, and the tools turn the captured lines into
audio:

1. Play. Every quest you accept or hand in and every NPC you talk to is
recorded in ForeverVOCaptureDB, with the speaker's creature ID and model.
2. Log out, then ./tools/run.sh tools/ingest.py merges the saved
variables into tools/data/capture.json.
3. ./tools/run.sh tools/generate.py picks a voice per speaker (race and
gender from the client's display tables), synthesises the missing lines with
Chatterbox on your GPU, and rebuilds the pack tables.
4. Restart the client (new sound files are only seen at launch) and play on.

The capture persists between sessions (the beta reads saved variables back
since late September 2026; before that each login started empty), so ingest.py
can run whenever you like. It merges, so running it after every session costs
nothing.
Voice pack format
A pack is an addon that depends on ForeverVO and calls
ForeverVO.RegisterPack(pack); see ForeverVO_Data/Data/Pack.lua and the
comment at the top of ForeverVO/Core/Packs.lua. Quest audio is keyed by quest
ID and event; gossip by speaker ID plus a hash of the normalised text
(tools/textkey.py mirrors Util.HashText), with a fuzzy fallback. Packs have
priorities, so a pack of new or revised lines can sit on top of a base pack.

packs pick a Forever NPC's voice from it: Fizzlefuse, a goblin, was voiced

from, /fvo export sends that NPC along, so the pack can fix the voice.

Peacekeepers on Zephras Isle or city guards, speak in the voice of the one
in front of you. The voice packs carry both once someone has met both
(starting with the next voice pack), and the addon remembers every sex it
has seen an NPC as, so /fvo export fills in the rest.

so the pack can tell where a quest says your class ("Greetings, mage")
from where it means the word. Your character name is still removed.

plays, and a reload at that moment left it off for good, since the client

addons.description:
MoveAny is a World of Warcraft add-on for moving, scaling, hiding, and fine-tuning Blizzard UI elements. It complements Blizzard's Edit Mode with access to many frames and options that are otherwise unavailable.
Features
• Move and scale a large selection of Blizzard UI elements and windows.
• Hide elements, make them click-through, or keep them attached to MoveAny's UI parent.
• Adjust frame strata, frame level, and context-dependent opacity.
• Snap movers to a configurable grid or to the edges and centers of other elements.
• Find frames directly with the built-in picker or search the categorized element list.
• Configure action bars, aura layouts, duration text, stack text, status bars, and other supported elements.
• Create multiple account-wide profiles and select a profile per character.
• Export and import profiles or share them through clickable in-game chat links.
• Use a localized interface in all supported game languages.

The exact list of available elements and options depends on the World of Warcraft client and the frames currently provided by Blizzard.

addons.description:
Never lose a whisper again.

Every conversation lands in one messenger window with history, online status and unread badges, like the messenger you already use, inside World of Warcraft.

🏆 5th place in The Addon Trials, CurseForge's 2026 WoW addon contest.

Why players install it
• Whispers stop drowning in raid, trade and guild spam. Each person gets their own conversation with an unread badge, so you always know who is waiting on you.
• Say it in one message. Whispers can run to about 800 characters instead of the game's 255.
• Trade and General without the spam. Follow world channels in their own tab, with ready-made filters for gold sellers, boosting ads and link spam.
• Looks like it shipped with the game. The Native WoW HUD style uses Blizzard's own window frame and tabs.
• Yesterday's conversation is still there. History survives logout and is shared across your characters.
• See who is online and where before you whisper. Class, faction, zone and Battle.net status sit right in the contact list.
• Battle.net and character whispers, side by side. No more guessing which tab a friend wrote in.
"Can't I just make a Whispers chat tab?"
You can, and it helps. A tab still mixes everyone into one scrolling stream, forgets everything on logout, has no unread count per person and no online status. Whisper Messenger gives every person their own thread with all of that.
FeaturesMessenger-Style Conversations
Chat bubbles with timestamps, date separators and sender labels. Right-click any message to reply, copy it or add a reaction. An emoji picker sits next to the message box.
• Long whispers run to about 800 characters. They go out in up to four parts and show as one message when your friend also uses Whisper Messenger. Group chats keep the game's normal length.
• Reply quotes the original line above your message.
• Quick replies drop in a saved line like "On my way" (up to 10, edit them under Options > Behavior).
• Drafts stay with each chat, even after a reload.
• Queued messages wait safely when whispers are paused, and nothing is sent until you click.
• Filtered messages that the game flags as inappropriate stay hidden until you click to reveal them.

Contact List
Online status dots, unread badges, last-message previews, and the zone or dungeon a friend is in. Pin and drag contacts to reorder them. Search across names, nicknames, notes and message history.

Right-click a contact to mute them, set a nickname, add a private note, or get told when they come online.

Whispers, Groups, Channels and Requests
• Whispers holds your private conversations.
• Groups collects party, raid, instance and guild chat, with reactions and @mention highlights.
• Channels (optional) turns Trade, General, Local Defense, LFG and your custom channels into chats of their own. Pick them under Options > Chats.
• Requests (optional) holds whispers from strangers until you accept or delete them. Turn it on under Options > Behavior.

Global Channels
Trade, General, Local Defense, World Defense, LFG and Trade (Services) each get their own chat and icon in the Channels tab. A busy channel only counts as unread when someone says your name, so Trade never buries a friend's whisper.

Spam Protection
• Block players for a day, a week or forever, with an optional note. Their whispers, group and channel messages disappear, in the messenger and in the game's chat.
• Keyword rules hide matching lines. Ready-made rules cover "Anal" link spam, Thunderfury links, Mythic+ and raid sellers, profession sellers, power-leveling sellers, guild and community recruitment, and WTS / WTB / LFW.
• Ready-made rules only touch channels such as Trade, never your guild, party or raid, and never whispers.
• Nothing is hidden from the game's chat in Mythic+, boss fights or PvP.

Battle.net Integration
Character whispers and Battle.net friend whispers live in one list. Contact details stay in sync with your friends list in real time.
Friends Who Also Use It…
