addons.changelog:
• The destination pin says what the step is, not only how far. The in-world pin now carries one short line of the current step's wording under the distance, taken from the journey's current row and falling back to the journey title when no row is current, cut at a word so it fits the pin. It is reread only when the goal or the stop index changes, so the per-poll cost is unchanged, and the map pin's tooltip still carries the full text of every step. Asked for on the pin that shipped in 1.22.18.
• Alt-clicking the world map no longer plans a journey and drops a TomTom waypoint at once. TomTom's click-to-
waypoint is on by default and reads the same press. While that option is on the click is left to TomTom, and a
journey is planned from the quest menu, a pin or Shift-click as before.
addons.description:
Plan journeys in WoW: Forever, on foot, by air, by sea and through portals.

Shift-click the world map or minimap, or choose a quest, to plan a journey. Shortest Path Forever gives directions in the objective tracker and on both maps.

Planning a journey from the map: the route settles, the next boat counts down in the tracker and the compass turns
with you.
Features
• Plan a journey. Shift-click the world map or minimap, or choose Plan journey on a quest. Routes combine walking, flights, boats, zeppelins, lifts, the tram, portals and teleports, and replan as you move. A spot inside a dungeon or raid leads to its entrance. Walks go round zones whose lowest level is 4 or more above yours and round the other faction's towns, and say so in the tracker when they can't. Keep journeys after a reload in Guidance restarts your own journey after a /reload.

The tracker shows each step, with time and distance remaining. Hover the destination's pin on the world map for the same steps, and, with the other faction's routes hidden, whether their boats would be at least two minutes faster.
• Follow your guide. Journeys follow RestedXP's current target by default, without TomTom or a bridge addon; Resume guide returns to it after another journey, unless Adventure Guide's RestedXP display leads instead. With TomTom absent, other guides' TomTom waypoints start journeys here.
• Type a waypoint. /way [zone] x y [title] plans a journey there, written as for TomTom, while TomTom and other addons leave /way free; /path way always works. With TomTom installed, Follow TomTom's arrow in Guidance follows its arrow.

The current stop lights up like a tracked quest.
• Choose your guidance. Keep the route on both maps while hiding the Journey tracker or direction arrow. The arrow eases round to each new bearing; move and scale it in Interface. Click the current step to complete it manually; skipping a Hearthstone leaves it out for that journey.

Breadcrumbs show the walking route; the waypoint leads to the next step. A goal off the minimap waits on its rim.
• See flights and departures. Flight maps highlight your next flight, and a flight master's world map tooltip lists its flights and their times. Dock tooltips show destinations and departure times; nearby services count down in the tracker. Ride times improve estimates and are shared with other players.

Flight lines follow the route between flight points.
• Find nearby services. The map and minimap tracking menus offer trainers, repairs, reagents, vendors, inns, banks, auction houses, flight masters and stables. Requires installed QuestieDB; class trainers also use Tweaks Forever.

Choose a service to plan the trip there.
• Travel prompts and alerts. Hearthstone and teleport steps show the item or spell to use. A banner, transport sound and taskbar flash warn before your boat arrives. Play a sound when you reach the goal in Alerts plays the map's ping on arrival.

The prompt clears as the journey continues.
• Compass and corpse routes. The compass marks turns, stops and your destination, and can show the time left under it. As a ghost, a red route leads to your body; your journey resumes when you are alive.

The strip can be moved and resized separately from the tracker. While moving it or the arrow, Shift-drag, or rest the pointer on it and use the arrow keys, to place it to the pixel.
• Quest areas. Inside a quest's area, the client draws it in gold instead of a stop pin and line.

The highlighted area is the game's own quest boundary.

More detail: features and API.
addons.name: Shortest Path Forever

The client only reports another player's position as a fraction of a zone map, so a refresh is due once a second and only after a visible move; the replan is handed to the next frame no walking search is using, which a bench over real Ashenvale and Darkshore data shows keeps it out of the frame the search was already spending. It ends when you are within 40 yards of them or they leave the group. Asked for by a player whose wife could use the direction, in the CurseForge comments.
• A pin on screen over the journey's destination. Settings > Guidance gains Show a pin over the destination: the game's own waypoint pin, held over where the journey ends, turning with you as you face it and fading when it is behind you, with the distance under it. It is off until you ask for it, only draws in the zone you are in, and stands down while Waypoint UI is navigating so the two never draw a pin over each other. That was the other half of the CurseForge request that shipped its Waypoint UI half in 1.22.5.

• The first journey after a login or /reload no longer stalls. The planner threw away its transport topology on every reset, so each journey's first plan rebuilt it inside the click: 476 ms on the first journey after a reload against 5 ms on the second. The topology now survives a reset and is rebuilt only when one of its inputs changes, so the cold build is paid once a session rather than once a journey. Reported by JohnChrin, who measured it around API.NavigateRoute on v1.22.16.

• Every line now reads in all nine shipped languages. The locale check found lines still shown in English: the flight-master and transport strings, and the phrases the report and shopping-list work added. All nine locale files cover Locales/phrases.txt, so no window falls back to English. tools/typecheck.sh runs the locale check with --release from now on, so an English line added without its translations fails the change that adds it.
• Riding the Great Lift names it once. The chat line after a ride read "synced the The Great Lift schedule from your ride."; the lift is now called the Great Lift everywhere the addon names it, its map labels included.

• THIRD_PARTY.md credits more of the players behind the addon. Its Ideas and contributors table gains rows for players whose reports, ideas or fixes shipped but were not yet credited there. Thanks to Mouchoir and z1ck for what they reported, asked for and fixed.

addons.description:
https://www.patreon.com/deadlybossmods
History:
Initially, the Heroes of the Storm countdown sounds were added to DBM-Core directly. These expanded the countdown sound options with several Characters that launched with base game. Since then, several more character countdowns have been added to game such as Illiden, Li'Li, etc. I weighed for a while on whether I should keep adding new files to DBM core and continuing to inflate the media foot print, or split the package into a stand alone before adding additional media options.

I have finally decided now is best time to split the media out of core and into stand alone. Then I can more easily update the Heroes of the Storm counts without worrying about how big it gets in media size since it's not something you have to redownload often (versus dbm which can be downloaded daily, or more if using alpha versions).

You might wonder, why concern self with how big the DBM download is. Believe it or not, MANY players still play on rural internet connections or on connections that have limited bandwidth monthly caps. A few megabytes per download can make a big difference for a very active user who updates DBM daily. Not to mention the many thousands of users who download the file directly from deadlybossmods.com as well. Not that the bandwidth is killing us by any means but it's still inefficient. I want the core package to be more minimalistic so when core is updated it's a small download and all the media to be stand alone from now on.

addons.description:
The WeakAuras you know, running on WoW Forever (client 1.60.1).
Open the options with /wa or /weakauras, or with the minimap icon.
⚠ Before you import auras
WoW Forever looks like Classic, but it runs on the modern game engine (12.1).
That engine changed what addons are allowed to see, so many auras made for
Classic Era, SoD or Retail will not work as they are:
• Auras that read the combat log (CLEU triggers, "Combat Log" events) never
fire. The combat log is closed to addons on this engine.
• Most combat data is hidden from addons during combat. Musca Auras
lets the game draw it (timers, bars, texts set to only %p or %s), but conditions
and thresholds on that data wait until combat ends.
• Some old game functions no longer exist. Custom code calling them errors
and must be updated to the modern C_ API (C_Spell, C_UnitAuras, C_Item...).
• Talent load options list the talents of your own specialization: select it alone in Class and Specialization. Aura (Modern)
spell lists take a spell ID or a spell name; a name is replaced by the IDs of all its ranks.

In short: expect to adapt most of the auras you import, especially the ones
with custom code. Damage taken, for example, works through UNIT_COMBAT:player
instead of the combat log.

Read the tutorial: how WeakAuras works on Forever, and
step-by-step recipes for auras that keep working in combat.

Coming from ForeverAuras? Paste your exported strings in the import window:
they are converted (tutorial, section 10).
Utility packs
/wa, then Packs: 24 packs for every class, each installed in one click.
• Combat: Ready Flash, Combat Text, Combat Items, Engineering Items, Shield Meter, Center Mark.
• Group and Buffs: Buff Check, Raid Coverage, Pre-Pull Check, Conjured Supplies, Announcements.
• Target and Enemies: Target Debuffs, Nameplate Aggro, Crowd Control, Armor Shred, Enemy Targets.
• Character: Level Progress, Character Stats, Group Experience, Equipment Sets.
• World: World Reminders, Campfire, Guild Campfires, Object Highlight.

Group Experience and Guild Campfires only show the players who also run the pack.

Ultimate Bank Changelog (formerly TOG Bank / TOGBankClassic)[v1.11.1] (2026-10-31) - Tidy-UpBug Fixes
• WIPE-001: any guild member could wipe every guildmate's data. Guild:Wipe's guard read
if not guild and not CanViewOfficerNote(), so it stopped only a guildless non-officer: any member
could send /togbank dev wipeall, and a guildless officer reached a nil concatenation. The receive
branch (Modules/Chat.lua, wipe-command) never asked who sent it. Sending is now officer-only
(with a chat line saying so), and a heard wipe is obeyed only from the home guild's GM or an
officer (Guild:WipeSenderAuthorized, Modules/Guild.lua) -- never a bank character on its note,
never a sister guild's officer. Found by the 2026-10-31 docs audit, which also found README.txt
calling it officer-only. Tests/settings_spec.lua pins both sides.
• DEBUGLOG-FILTER-001: /togbank debuglog [N] [filter] ignored the filter. Since CMD-001 the
dispatcher hands the first word and the remainder separately; the handler read the first word
only. It joins both again, and a non-numeric first word is the filter (/togbank debuglog MAIL).
Tests/chatcommand_spec.lua drives the typed command.
• ARCHIVE-TOOLTIP-001: the Requests window's Archive tab tooltip said "Completed and cancelled
requests", but the tab splits by age alone, so an old open request is there too. Both tab tooltips
now say what the split is (Modules/UI/Requests.lua).

(Modules/Constants.lua), DeltaComms:ShouldUseDelta and its Guild:ShouldUseDelta wrapper, and

protocol no longer claims delta sync is "enabled/disabled" against the dead threshold; it prints
the protocol v2 share.

TOGBankClassic Changelog[v1.10.1] (2026-10-31) - One Stack Per OrderBug Fixes
• MAIL-ONE-STACK-001: an order that fits in one stack went out as several attachments. The
operator, 2026-10-31, with a mail to January-Atiesh carrying 7 Mountain Silversage as a stack of 5
and a stack of 2: *"why does it send a stack of 5 and a stack of 2 instead of making it one stack
of 7?"*. CalculateFulfillmentPlan's first phase takes any bag stacks that add up exactly, so 5 + 2
won over splitting, and MAIL-SPLIT-MERGE-001 only merged when a split was needed anyway; each
extra attachment costs 30c postage. CalculateFulfillmentPlan (Modules/Mail.lua) now replaces
any plan that takes more than one attachment with a one-attachment plan when the order fits under
the item's max stack: the largest stack smaller than the order is attached, and the rest is moved
onto it from the smallest other stack that covers it. Moving all of a stack is a pickup rather
than a split (tog_liftOntoCursor), because the client cannot split a whole stack; that also
frees a bag slot. Applies to Fulfill Oldest, the row's Fulfill icon and the hand-off split. When
no single stack covers the rest (7 from 3 + 2 + 2 with nothing bigger), the stacks still go as
they are. Tests/multifill_spec.lua gains three examples; three Tests/mailcoverage_spec.lua
examples about slot handling now use items whose max stack rules out a merge, and the planner
example now expects the merge. Confirmed in game by the operator the same day: *"tested the fix in
game, it works now"*. The cost: a 5 + 2 fill that went straight to ATTACH now takes a SPLIT click
first, trading one click for 30c postage.
• Peer Review 349c7141 on MAIL-ONE-STACK-001. B1: the whole-stack move was decided from the
plan's stack count, so a source stack that grew between picking the order and the SPLIT click would
be moved whole, and ATTACH would then wait forever for a merged count it could never read.
tog_liftOntoCursor now decides from the live stack, and both the SPLIT phase and the Split popup
refuse (the batch restarts) when the source no longer holds what was planned. B2: the popup no
longer moves a whole stack into an empty slot when its target changed -- that changed nothing --
and says the stacks changed instead. F4: tog_oneAttachmentPlan builds its target through
tog_mergeTarget, so the same-item and max-stack rule lives in one function. N1: its comment now
says the list must already be sorted. Tests/multifill_spec.lua gains four examples (source grew
before SPLIT, popup source changed, popup target changed, unknown max stack).
Improvements
• The CurseForge page names the sister addons by their current titles, Ultimate Profession Master
and Ultimate Tools (Peer Review inbox thread f2dc805e, routing TOGWiki's report). Older patch notes
keep the names they shipped with.

order's partial stack). The status bar then says to trade it and record the trade with Mark

Modules/UI/Requests.lua. Tests/mailcoverage_spec.lua, Tests/requestsactions_spec.lua.
The Requests '?' help (HELP-CURRENT-001) said the split icon meant "quantity must be split
manually"; it now says a click splits, and how the in-person hand-off goes. README.txt's…

Bug Fixes
• SPLIT-ROOM-001: too few free bag slots for a mail's splits split nothing, with no word in chat.
Discord, #tog-bank, 2026-10-24: *"someone requested three items, which all exist in stacks of 20.
Two bag spaces available, none of the stacks will attempt to split, there is not a notification

refused the whole mail when the bags had fewer free slots than the mail had splits, saying so only
in the Requests status bar -- Tests/multifill_spec.lua pinned exactly that refusal for exactly

order with no slot for its own split stops the click. Either way a warning is printed to chat as

popup's accept (Modules/Mail.lua) set the Requests status line ("Split 5 Linen Cloth complete.
Click Fulfill again..." or, for HANDOFF-SPLIT-001, "...Trade the order to X, then use Mark
hand-off.") and THEN redrew the list, and the redraw writes its own "Showing N requests" line, so
the banker never saw what to do next. It now redraws first, the order Cancel Stale already uses.

and Record modules and the harness's bags -- live Fulfill icon away from a mailbox, the Split

chat warning, not only the status line. What only a client can still show: the server's timing of
the split, and how the popup draws.
• STATS-P2P-001: the delta statistics no longer print a P2P section that could never fill.
Self-audit 8680287b F7 led here. The "P2P Requests (what I asked peers for)" section and the
"P2P offered/sent" line read p2pRequestsBroadcast, p2pBankerFallback and p2pOffered, whose
writers (BroadcastP2PRequest, the old offer path) moved into DeltaSync with LIBREQ-DS-008.
DeltaSync reports neither an ask nor a fallback, so since then the section always read "No P2P…

TOGBankClassic Changelog[v1.9.1] (2026-10-17) - Safer Order SyncBug Fixes
• MUT-ID-001: a received order change could overwrite a different order. Peer Review eee82c0f,
Q1. Guild:ApplyRequestMutation (Modules/RequestLog.lua) keys the merge by entry.requestId
and looks up requests[requestId] for its permission checks, but mergeRequest stores the
snapshot as it arrived, so a mutation whose request.id differed from its requestId put one
order's record under another's key. An "add" passes when the snapshot's requester is the sender,
so a peer could replace any order with a newer snapshot of its own. Every sender in this addon
sets both ids from one value, so only a mismatched or hostile peer reaches it. A mutation whose
two ids differ is now refused. Tests/requestlogcoverage_spec.lua, confirmed red with the check
switched off. Not wire-visible: nothing this addon sends changes.
• ADD-OWNER-001: an "add" could take over or close someone else's existing order. Peer Review
e5b7e0c8, R1, the other half of MUT-ID-001. The add check only compared the snapshot's requester
with the sender, never the order already held under that id, so a peer naming itself requester
could send a newer snapshot of another player's order and mergeRequest replaced it: the order
changed hands, or arrived cancelled or complete without the cancel and complete permission
checks, which run only for those mutation types. An add for an order already held is now refused
unless the sender is that order's requester; the requester's own add arriving twice still merges.
The only sender of an add, Guild:AddRequest, mints a fresh id, so a modified client is needed to
reach it. Tests/requestlogcoverage_spec.lua: a takeover and a cancelling add are refused (red
with the check switched off), and the requester's repeated add still merges.
• ADD-OPEN-001: a requester could close or fill their own order by re-sending it as an "add".

addons.description:
WoW quests are full of the language you actually want to learn — but they fly by. You accept, scan for the objective, and the words are gone.

QuestWordHunter keeps the quest on screen as clickable text. See a word you don't know? Click it, add a meaning, mark it Learning. Next time it turns up in another quest it is already coloured. After a while you have a real vocabulary list built from the game, not from a textbook.

What you get
Controller support includes the map and quest-log side tabs: X / Square opens the selected quest's reader and Y / Triangle opens the library. In the library, LB/RB changes tabs and LT/RT changes pages; the D-pad selects controls, A / Cross activates them and B / Circle returns. Lists and settings use the same selection outline, and left/right adjusts a selected slider. The English panel scrolls with up/down or LB/RB. With the voice engine loaded, the reader's triggers replay and pause/resume speech. Explicit WordHunter bindings take priority. ConsolePort uses its own interface cursor and configured button hints; addon windows and side tabs are registered through its public API.
• Quest text you can click instead of retyping into a notes app
• Colours and underlines for New, Learning, Known and Ignored, so you see progress in the paragraph itself — keep both or pick one
• A meaning, a personal note, and the sentence the word came from
• Previous / Next in the word editor, on the row with Cancel and Save (also the arrow keys when no box has focus, and LB/RB on a controller), so a quest can be read word by word without the mouse
• An optional recall check: a word you have been learning for a day asks how well you knew it, 1 to 5, before it shows its meaning. Words that keep scoring low are difficult, and you can export them for a flashcard app
• A word list and simple stats — /whw words, /whw stats
• A quiet Ready for Known hint after five different quests and two weeks. It never promotes anything by itself
• Separate lists per language, so German and French don't mix
• Windows you can move, resize and theme — /whw settings
• A controller works too: the D-pad moves between words; the reader and editor show which buttons open, save, close or switch reading mode. Needs the game's own controller support; the full map is under Settings

Buttons stay in English. Quest text stays in the language you set in WoW.

Assign shortcuts under Options → Key Bindings → AddOns → WordHunterWoW. The reader's footer and the word editor show the current bindings and update when you change them. With controller support enabled in both WoW and the addon, hints use the client's controller button labels, including its selected Xbox/PlayStation glyphs. Explicit WordHunterWoW controller bindings override the panel's default controls. Unassigned keyboard actions have no invented default. The editor's arrow keys and recall ratings 1–5 work locally outside combat; arrows move the text caret while typing. Enter saves from the translation field, and Escape closes the windows.
Quest library
Open /whw quests, or click the WordHunterWoW book side tab beside the Quest Log.
The library follows your learning language from Settings. The reader displays
English alongside that language when both texts are available. Words and recall
ratings are saved separately for each language.
The German Dictionary includes German and English Classic quest texts,
plus native Forever cache records; no separate quest-data addon is needed.
Text actually seen in your client takes
precedence, and offers are archived immediately so you can study them after a
fast party has completed the quest.
No quest needs to be selected. The library opens on My quests, containing
this character's current and completed quests. **Show only current quests in
quest log hides the completed-only entries. The All in game quests** tab
contains all quest records stored for this game client. Both tabs display English…

addons.description:
This addon collects ingame text from book items and objects, and allows them to be read anywhere. To open the frame, a button on the Minimap and AddOn Compartment Frame are both provided, as well, as the slash command /lorekeeper or /lorek.

Items are collected upon closing a text item or text object. Items can't be retroactively collected from past books (otherwise it would be very easy to make this addon and data contributions wouldn't be necessary). Usually a copy of an item is stored in the collected data if the text content has changed due to a quest progression (ie artifact books). If the player-saved data is different from locally stored data, it will instead usually display the player-saved data. Some game objects are not real text items but in fact are NPCs in disguise using gossip text (which this addon does not collect). Mail items (when available) are collected and stored in the mail module upon closing the "Plain Letter" item itself, rather than necessarily scanning the mail. Plain Letters with no sender name (ie letters transferred cross-server or from NPCs) can't be stored as the GUID data is unavailable for some reason.

Eventually the plan is to implement a collection-based system and track progress on various achievements, not too unlike mount, pet, or transmog collection, but with a focus on ingame lore items. It will be a continuous work-in-progress, as collecting a baseline of known texts will take some time.
Lorekeeper now also supports Text to Speech
For additional voice chat options you can visit the Blizzard Support Page. More "Natural Voice" options can additionally be found and set up with NaturalVoiceSAPIAdapter.

To help contribute your own data, you can submit your data on the github issue template or place it in the #addon-dev channel in my discord. You'll need to find a file located here: retail\WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\Lorekeeper.lua If you would like to be credited for your submission, please provide a username or some sort of online handle by which you want to be addressed as (this is public info in an addon). Do not include Lorekeeper_Mail.lua as it is not a necessary upload and contains your personal mail items and custom items. It will not be contributed to the addon.

Happy hunting!

addons.description:
This addon enables Masque (CurseForge, Wago, WoWInterface) to skin built-in WoW inventory elements. An up-to-date version of Masque is required for it to work.

If you like the base WoW interface and don't want to use a separate bag or inventory mod, you're in the right place.

You can install this addon from CurseForge, Wago, or WoWInterface.
Features
Masque Blizzard Inventory can currently skin the following elements, according to your game version:
• Backpack
• Main Bags
• Combined Backpack
• Reagent Bag
• Bank (including Warband Bank)
• Guild Bank
• Mail
• Merchants
• Loot
• Character
• Inspect Character
• Equipment Flyouts
• Keyring (Classic before Cataclysm and Forever)
• Bag Bar (Classic and Forever)

Each element type is its own group so you can configure them independently from Masque's Skin Settings.

The Warband Bank and Bank use the same inventory elements in Retail, so they share skin options as well.

An additional options panel is provided to hide background and slot artwork that might clash with certain Masque skins.
Forever Support
World of Warcraft: Forever has a unique mixture of Classic and Retail inventory features, and should be fully supported.

In Forever, bags are grouped as follows:
• Main Bags includes all common bags including the Keyring
• The Reagent Bag is always skinned independently
• The Backpack is skinned independently unless you have enabled the Combined Backpack
• The Combined Backpack takes over the Backpack and Main Bags, except the Keyring, which is still skinned from the Main Bags group
• Bank Bags are now part of a combined Bank that works like the Combined Backpack and cannot be skinned independently
Classic Support
Classic versions available in the US are fully supported. Elements not available in Classic will not appear in Masque's Skin Settings.

In Classic, all bags are consolidated to a single Bags group, including the Keyring. This is due to the way the game reuses Bag windows.

Most interface frames in Classic are built using a single background image, rather than multiple layers, so the options to hide background and slot artwork are not feasible. Adding this feature would require drawing replacement artwork and including it with the addon, so it is not planned.

I don't play Classic so testing is somewhat limited, but I'll do my best to address bug reports promptly.
Compatibility
This addon is intended to skin the base WoW interface. Addons that heavily modify parts of the base interface may conflict. If you experience a conflict, use Masque's Skin Settings to disable the affected group and reload your UI. This should allow the other addon to control the interface without interference.

If you'd like to see Masque support in a conflicting addon, try sending a feature request to that addon's author directly.
Localization
If you'd like to help localize this addon, please submit translations here.
LLM Policy
LLM ("Generative AI") agents are not used for development of this project and such contributions will not be accepted.
Other Mods
If you want to skin the built-in action bars as well, check out Masque Blizzard Bars (CurseForge, Wago, WoWInterface)!
Special Thanks
Thanks to StormFX, the author of Masque, for a ton of feedback and development tips and for creating a logo for the addon.

addons.description:
This addon provides a modern update to merchant (vendor) interfaces in WoW.

You can install this addon from CurseForge, Wago, or WoWInterface.
Features
Merchant Plus adds an additional tab to all WoW merchants, which provides the following enhancements:
• Wider vertical scrolling list to allow more information to be viewed at once
• Sortable columns of item data
• Optional columns containing additional item data

An options panel is included to configure basic settings.
Planned Features
In future updates, the following major improvements are planned:
• Additional data columns and options to choose the visibility and order of them
• Filtering based upon data in one or more columns
• Searching based upon data in one or more columns

There is no specific timeline for these features to be completed.
Forever Support
World of Warcraft: Forever has the same interface features as Retail, so it is fully supported.
Classic Support
Merchant Plus requires interface features only available in Retail. Blizzard periodically backports features to Classic versions, so the required functions may be available eventually. Until that time, Classic support is not planned.
Compatibility
This addon does not replace the existing UI, but it makes many changes to the merchant window, so it may conflict with other addons that modify the contents or layout. Addons that replace the window will prevent Merchant Plus from appearing entirely. ElvUI is supported when the Blizzard Merchant Frame skin is enabled. Other addons that re-skin the merchant window may cause layout problems.

Ideally, Merchant Plus will not be the cause of any conflicts. If you discover any, please report them, and I'll fix what I can from the Merchant Plus side.
Localization
If you'd like to help localize this addon, please submit translations here.
LLM Policy
LLM ("Generative AI") agents are not used for development of this project and such contributions will not be accepted.

addons.changelog:
Fixed

for a moment each time the map opened.

addons.description:
OpenMap is an open-source, seamless world map addon for WoW Forever that keeps the original Vanilla art style. Zoom and pan across the whole world map with a truly open-source, community-built map addon.

Help us build it as a community into the best world map, while staying true to the classic spirit.

There are already a bunch of map addons for Forever, and some of them are great. What I couldn't find was one that's seamless (lets you zoom and pan through the entire world), open source, and keeps the map looking like Blizzard's original map.

OpenMap stitches every zone map into one continuous map. Scroll out of Elwynn and you're looking at Westfall, Duskwood and Redridge, then the whole continent, then the world. No more clicking in and right-clicking out between zones. It lives inside the normal world map, so your quest log, the map's buttons, Questie and the rest of the standard map work as intended.
What it does
• One seamless map. Zoom from the whole world down to street level, toward your cursor. It uses the map art from the game files, with the game's minimap blended in for extra detail at the closest zoom, without breaking the map's look.
• Zone borders that blend. Neighbouring zones fade into each other, and the border mountains are colour-matched.
• The whole map made visible. Land Forever has no zone map for (Gilneas, the ridges round Orgrimmar, the mountains west of Searing Gorge, the edges of Stonetalon, Feralas, Silithus and more) is drawn from Blizzard's own classic and pre-Cataclysm maps of it, which ship with the game but the game doesn't show. Land no map ever drew is left as clean parchment, like an unfinished map.
• Ocean and continent names rebuilt so they zoom properly, lettered in the game's own map font.
• Dungeon and raid entrances with level ranges, coloured for your level. Click one and Blizzard's own map of that dungeon opens right in the map, every floor of it, with its bosses and its quests beside it (with Questie, Dungeon Journal or NeedRoll). With Dungeon Journal, an entrance can open its page there instead. For loot, OpenMap recommends NeedRoll: every boss's drops, what you've collected and a wishlist.
• Boats, zeppelins and airships, WoW Forever's own too: click one to jump to the other end (the airships to Zephras Isle open its map), and see their routes. Dungeons, boats and zeppelins each have their own switch.
• Underground. Zoom into a cave, mine, crypt or a dungeon's entrance area and its map appears:
Blizzard's where it drew one, else the game's own minimap of it.
• Flight paths. Learned ones in colour, the rest greyed out. Click two flight masters to see the route you'd fly and roughly how long it takes.
• Getting around. Search for a zone, city, dungeon or flight master; a "Find me" button (or middle-click the map); choose how the map reopens; party and raid members are shown across the whole map. Or take your own arrow off the map and find your way old-school.
• Map pins and drawing. Ctrl-click for as many pins as you like, each with a note and a colour, followed with Blizzard's waypoint (and TomTom's); share them with your group, guild or a friend. Draw on the map with a pen, lines, arrows, circles and raid marks, on its own or on a pin.
• Vendors, spirit healers and rares (needs Questie): repair, innkeepers, trainers, bankers, auctioneers, stable masters, spirit healers and rare mobs. Questie's quest icons can be switched on or off from OpenMap's menu too. (Still working on performance here.)
• A map that fits your screen. No more black bars at the sides: resize the window to any shape, or go full screen and the map fills it.…

releases.changelog:
Fixed
• The map's art is there at once when you open it: since 0.7.4 the zones showed blank parchment
for a moment each time the map opened.
• Clicking a quest on the map keeps the map as it is: the quest is tracked and the map zooms in on
it, full screen or windowed. It opened the quest's details, which Blizzard shows in the windowed
map, so a full-screen map left full screen. With the quest log open beside the map, its details
show there too.
• Hiding your pins hides their drawings too (the menu's Pins, right-clicked): what you drew on a
pin stayed on the map without it.

New
• Chat over the full-screen map (the menu's Look tab, and Options): the chat windows stay on show
over the map while it's full screen, to keep talking while you look. Off unless you turn it on (a
player's request).
• Faster to load: only your language's translations are read (the other nine were a quarter of
OpenMap's code), and its look through every addon's map icons for combat waits till you're in the
world, not the loading screen (a player's report: half a second more load time).
• The zones' detail comes in sooner when the map first opens up close: it took a couple of
seconds after a login or reload.
• /openmap status says what loading costs: OpenMap's files, the login, the map's setup and
building the map (a player found it added load time: this shows where).

New
• Key bindings (the game's Keybindings > OpenMap): Find me, Drop a pin, Pins, Quill,
Quest log and the map's menu, each opening the map first if it's closed (players' requests).
• The quill draws on dungeons' maps: with a dungeon's map up, what you draw goes on its picture
and is kept with that dungeon, not on the world map behind it (a player's request).
• Only places you've found (the menu's On the map tab, under Places): dungeon entrances, docks
and zeppelin towers once you've explored where they are, flight masters once you've learned them.
Off unless you turn it on (a player's request).
• Townsfolk from another addon's NPC database: an addon with a database in Questie's shape can
give it to OpenMap (OpenMapAPI.RegisterTownsfolkProvider, docs/api.md), so townsfolk and rare
mobs show without Questie (a player's request).
Fixed
• Smooth zooming at any Take colour out: the zones' fast pre-drawn art was only used at the
setting's default (10%); at any other, every zone was drawn from its hundreds of pieces and the
frame rate dropped as their detail came in. It's now used at every setting.
• Full screen stays full screen, and the quest log you closed stays closed, the next time the
map opens: it went back to the window and the quest log each time (a player's report).
• Improves performance under Fade icons while zooming no longer stays on show over the menu's
other tabs (a player's report).
• Riverglades and Zephras Isle show their levels on the zone hover (35-45 and 1-12, from the
Warcraft Wiki; a player's report).

Improved
• Zooming is smoother with unexplored areas darkened: greying the land you haven't found cost
a lot of frame rate while zooming; it now costs far less.
• Unexplored areas for one character only: the menu's Only for this character, under
Unexplored areas, gives this character its own choice (darkened, hidden or shown); every other
character keeps the shared one (a player's request).
• Fade icons while zooming says Improves performance under it in the map's menu, so it
isn't turned off unawares.
Fixed
• The map loads the zone you pan or zoom to again: with an addon adding map icons (Questie,
GatherLite ...), it could stay on the zone you started on, so the zone or continent you'd panned to
showed none of their icons until you clicked it (a player's report from 0.6, and ours). Its setting,
once Follow the view, is now Load the zone in view (the menu's More tab), saying what it does.
• The map window drags and resizes with Move Any installed but turned off: OpenMap asked whether
Move Any was on for a character named by your first name alone (WoW Forever gives a first and last
name), which the game took as on, and left the window to it (a player's report, with the fix).

addons.description:
Displays a bar on screen that allows quick access to enchanting, jewelcrafting, and inscription professions by presenting a Disenchant/Prospect/Mill button and all of the breakable items you have for that profession next to it. Also displays a bar for any locked junkboxes in your inventory if you're a Rogue. This allows one-click access for breaking down items instead of finding the item in your bag, clicking the appropriate profession/skill button, and clicking the item for each and every item you want to break. For prospecting and milling, you will see the number of items you have alongside the number of times you can break it. In the prospecting screenshot on the right, the player has 169 total Saronite Ore in his bags which will allow for 33 total prospects.
Usage
By default, if you have the appropriate profession and items in your inventory, a bar will appear with the profession ability followed by any items that are eligible for breaking. You can hold shift to drag the bar around if you want to move it. Clicking the profession button will activate that ability (disenchant/prospect/mill) and clicking an item will break it. You don't have to click the profession button first as simply clicking the item will automatically break it down. Right-clicking an item will place that item on the ignore list so it won't show up in the list again. The ignore list can be managed in the addon's configuration panel.
Configuration
Typing /brk will open the configuration settings (or you can get to it from Blizzard's Interface options) which consist of:
• Hide if no breakables: this will control whether you see the profession button or not when nothing breakable is detected
• Max number to display: this controls the highest number of items that you will see next to your profession button. If this is 5 but you have 10 breakable items in your bags, you will only see 5 at a time.
• Show soulbound items: aimed at enchanters, this controls whether or not you will see items that are soulbound as breakable items or not.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon. Download locations: CurseForge | Wago

Transmog Loot Helper (TLH) shows icons for unlearned transmog, mounts, pets, toys, recipes, decor, and more. These show on:
• Bags and bank
• (Black Market) Auction House
• Mailbox
• Loot window and loot rolls
• Vendors
• Profession window
• World quests and quest rewards
• Encounter Journal
• Great Vault

There are several styles of icons to choose from!

It also features a loot tracker, showing you transmog looted by your fellow party/raid members that you still need, and features icons to show items' collection status. Alt+clicking lets you whisper them to ask for the item!

Currently supported addons:
• ArkInventory
• Baganator
• Bagforge
• BetterBags
• ElvUI
• Krowi's Extended Vendor UI
• World Quest Tab
• World Quests List
• WoWNotes Bags
If you are experiencing issues
• Check if the issue occurs with only this addon enabled, or if the issue is a feature you can disable from the addon's settings menu.
• If you run into any issues or if you have other feedback, feel free to join the Discord and ask in the #transmog-loot-helper channel, or create a ticket on GitHub. :)

DoesItDiev0.9.0
Restart the game fully after updating (not just /reload): this version adds a new file.
• For addon authors: a public API, so unit frame, nameplate and UI addons can show DoesItDie's estimate on their own frames. See API.md on GitHub. Thanks to curse-wa for the idea.
v0.8.4
• Threat Plates: the nameplate marker now really shows on its health bar (v0.8.2's fix looked in the wrong place). No setting needed: you can clear anything typed under Advanced > Nameplate health bar. Thanks to adamkm123 and WEEDWIZARD420__.
• German: the addon's chat messages and its description in the AddOns list are in German too. Thanks to Cortexyn.
v0.8.3
Restart the game fully after updating (not just /reload): this version adds new files.
• Portuguese (Brazil) and Chinese (Traditional and Simplified) clients: your DoTs are read there too. If one isn't picked up, a /did debug log helps (issues #19 and #20 on GitHub).
v0.8.2
Restart the game fully after updating (not just /reload): this version adds a new file.
• Plater: the nameplate kill icon is back (it went missing in v0.7.0 with some nameplate addons), and Plater's health bar is found more reliably. Thanks to tuwzz for the report.
• Threat Plates: the nameplate marker finds its health bar too.
• Korean client: your DoTs are read on Korean (koKR) clients. If one isn't picked up, a /did debug log helps (issue #18 on GitHub).
• German options window: set Advanced > Window language to Deutsch (or Auto on a German client), then /reload. Thanks to thecodingcortex.
• French client fixes: Immolation and Plaie d'agonie are read again. Thanks to gou-gouze.
• Tracking fixes (thanks to Ironship):
• Two DoTs of the same school ticking at the same moment are both counted (one was dropped before).
• A DoT whose ticks a shield absorbs is no longer dropped.
• A melee hit landing just before a bleed's tick is no longer learned as the bleed's size.
• Combo points built on one mob are no longer used for a finisher on the next.
• DoTs cast on your soft or mouseover target go on that mob, and never on a friendly target.
v0.8.1
• Plater and other nameplate addons: the nameplate marker finds their health bars automatically. If yours still doesn't show it, Advanced > Nameplate health bar takes the path to its bar.
v0.8.0
Restart the game fully after updating (not just /reload): this version adds new files.
• Focus frame: the marker and kill icon also show on your focus's health bar (Blizzard's, EllesmereUI's, or a custom one under Advanced), with its own tab (Focus) for its look and a focus frame in the options preview. /cast [@focus] macros put the DoT on your focus. Thanks to toughnuts99 for the patch.
• Dungeons: where mobs can't be told apart by ID, DoTs are tracked per mob through its nameplate, so tab-dotting a pack works (needs enemy nameplates on). Thanks to Staypuft.
• Window language setting (Advanced): the options window can now be translated. No translations yet; see issue #10 on GitHub if you'd like to help.
• The options window is a little wider, so all tabs fit.
v0.7.1
• Immolation Trap is tracked. The DoT starts on whichever mob springs the trap.
v0.7.0
Other UIs
• EllesmereUI: the marker sits on EllesmereUI's nameplates and target frame health bars, and the kill icon on
its portrait.
• Platynator: the nameplate marker and kill icon anchor to Platynator's plates.
• Nameplate addons that hide Blizzard's bar no longer get a stray box above the plate.

Languages: German, Spanish and French clients read your DoTs. If something isn't picked up on your client, a
/did debug log helps a lot.

New
• Estimate while casting: DoTs with a cast time (Immolate) show as soon as you start casting, and disappear if
the cast is interrupted. Can be turned off under Advanced.
• Learned tick sizes viewer (Advanced > View, or /did ticks): what each of your DoTs really ticks for next to
its tooltip, with spell icons and tooltips. Shift-click a spell to link it.…

addons.description:
Beta for World of Warcraft Forever (Interface 16001).

Yellow ! start markers for normal quests, blue ! for repeatable, red-orange ! for dungeon and raid, class-colored ! for class quests, and copper ! for profession quests on Blizzard’s native world map.

Forever already has a modern quest tracker and objective pins for quests in your log. This addon does not replace that. It adds start locations for unaccepted quests.
Requirements
• World of Warcraft Forever only (not Retail, Classic Era, or Cataclysm Classic)
• Folder name must be exactly ForeverQuestPins
• No other addons required (not TomTom or HereBeDragons)

TomTom is an optional waypoint provider. The default is Blizzard Map Pins.
Features
• Yellow ! pins for normal quest starts, blue ! for repeatable, red-orange ! for dungeon and raid, class-colored ! for class quests, and copper ! for profession quests
• Map pin tooltips with [level] quest name (Forever tracker level when available; Questie inline name when the client has not loaded a title) and NPC names (IDs only if debug is on)
• NPC mouseover tooltips listing quests you can accept and quests ready to turn in (on by default)
• Pins stay on the map art in windowed and fullscreen layouts
• Nearby spawn points for one quest group share one pin (up to six per quest). Hover to see the spawn count in the tooltip and every spawn location on the map. Turn off Show spawn clusters to show one pin per quest instead
• Overlapping starts on the same spot stack into one pin
• Shift-click a pin to hide it (every quest on a stacked pin) for the current character; restore with Reset hidden quest pins in settings or /fqp unhide
• Adjustable low-level range: choose how many levels below you a quest must be before its pin is hidden (default 9)
• Optional auto-accept and auto-turn-in when talking to NPCs (off by default; hold Shift to skip once)
• Seasonal / holiday starts (Lunar Festival elders, Darkmoon Faire, …) off by default
• AQ opening war effort commodity pins in Orgrimmar / Ironforge on by default (turn off in settings if the stack is too noisy)

Quest coordinates, quest-giver IDs, turn-in targets, and restrictions come from QuestieDB Forever data, with holiday and instance-tag policy from Questie. The Go tool go run ./cmd/fqp build-db generates the addon database. Quests without a usable spawn stay in the database for tooltips and prerequisites but may not get a map pin.

addons.description:
One library for every addon.

Arcane Wizard: Library is a World of Warcraft addon that provides the shared foundation for all Arcane Wizard addons. It brings common functionality together in one place, making it easier to develop and maintain the addons that use it.
For Players
Install Arcane Wizard: Library alongside your Arcane Wizard addons and keep it enabled. It provides the shared functionality they need, runs in the background, and has no interface of its own.
For Developers
Arcane Wizard: Library provides reusable components that simplify addon development and maintenance. Shared functionality can be maintained centrally and used across multiple addons. Other addon developers are welcome to use the library in their own projects.
FeaturesAddon Context
The library provides shared addon registration, access to settings, minimap and Addon Compartment integration, and debug output.
Frames, Tables & Controls
Reusable windows, scrollable tables, tabs, and input controls match Blizzard's native appearance for each supported game version.
Prebuilt Windows & Dialogs
The library provides ready-to-use changelog windows, link popups, and confirmation dialogs.
Utilities
Shared helpers handle character identifiers and copy nested tables.
Settings
The library integrates addon options into Blizzard's settings menu with reusable layouts, profile support, and native key binding controls.
How to Integrate
1. Add the following to your .toc file:

> ## Dependencies: ArcaneWizardLibrary

2. Set the dependency on the CurseForge project page to ensure users download it automatically.
Library Revision
X-Revision in ArcaneWizardLibrary.toc is an integer maintained separately from the release version and exposed as ArcaneWizardLibrary.ADDON_REVISION. Increase it when addons need to distinguish changes to the library's public functions or behavior. Builds preserve the revision.

Each Arcane Wizard addon declares its minimum revision as X-Library-Revision in its TOC and checks it before using the library. Equal or higher revisions are accepted. A missing, invalid, or older revision stops addon startup and reports the required and installed revisions in chat and through the Lua error handler. SavedVariables are left intact.

When an addon starts using newer library functionality, raise only that addon's minimum revision to the first revision providing it. Higher library revisions must continue to support addons that require earlier revisions.

addons.description:
Your unfinished WoW: Forever Legacy challenges, on the world map, for the zone you're looking at.

Legacy Forever shows unfinished challenges on the world map and tracks the ones you choose.

Discover an area and its shading lifts as the corner's percentage goes up. Click the corner to fold it away.

Half of Ashenvale explored: the shield's number is what's left on this map, and its menu lists it by challenge.

Zoom out and each zone with dungeon objectives left gets a badge.

Challenges you track sit in the objective tracker under the game's own header, with live progress.

Tick a challenge in the menu to track it.
Features
• Map button in the world map's top-right button column: a Legacy shield with a number inside, the unfinished objectives on the map you're viewing. Its menu lists them by challenge, with a tick box to track each one. Challenges with no fixed place are grouped the way the Legacy panel groups them.
• Tracker: a Legacy section in the objective tracker, under the game's own All Objectives header, lists what you track, with live progress. A zone ticked in the map menu tracks just that zone, such as "0/12 Explore Felwood". Click a challenge to open it in the Legacy panel, or right-click to stop tracking it. How it lists steps.
• Map pins on dungeon and raid entrances, with the challenge each counts toward and its Legacy points. With AtlasLoot installed, tooltips also show its recommended level range. Left-click a pin to travel there: with Shortest Path Forever it plans the whole journey, otherwise it sets the game's own waypoint. If another addon already marks entrances, the map menu turns these pins off.
• Undiscovered areas are shaded darker in their real shape on the zone map, so you can see where to go at a glance. Hovering one names it and, when a Legacy challenge counts it, shows the challenge, its points and how many of the zone's areas are left. The map menu turns the shading off.
• Zone completion, Guild Wars 2 style: how much of a zone's areas, dungeons, raids and Legacy objectives you've done, as a percentage in the map's corner, a badge on each zone of a continent map and, if you tick it, the tracker. Flight paths, local reputations and, with Questie, quests can be added under "What counts". A finished zone gets a toast and a sound. What it counts.
• No fixed location lists challenges whose remaining work isn't tied to a place, such as levels, skills and ranks.

Progress comes from the game each time, so it matches the Legacy panel and follows whichever challenge set your character sees.
addons.name: legacy-forever

addons.changelog:
GuildCrafters 0.15.0
A stability release. There is nothing to set up, and it works together with guild members who are still on 0.14.
New
• Works on every game language. Professions now show correctly, with icon and rank, between players on different client languages, for example German and English.
• No sync during combat. GuildCrafters stays quiet while you fight and catches up a few seconds after. The open window is not refreshed in the middle of a fight either.
• Old data cleans itself up. Members who left the guild disappear from Crafting, Mats and the tooltips right away, and are removed from your saved data after 7 days. A profession you dropped is hidden from the guild right away and removed after 7 days. If the member or the profession comes back within that week, nothing is lost.
• /gc sync asks the guild for fresh data now, instead of waiting for the next automatic update.
• Status line at the bottom right of the window: when you last received data, and how many guild members with the addon are online. Hover it for details.
• /gc tooltip on|off turns the "Crafted by" and "Guild has" lines on item tooltips off or on. Inside the GuildCrafters window they are always shown.
Improved
• Lighter in large guilds: the Crafting tab opens and searches with far less work when many members use the addon, and guild roster updates no longer cause extra work.
• After a reinstall or a move to a new PC, your next change always reaches the guild. Before, others could keep showing your old data.
Fixed
• /gc help showed "tankealer|dps|uto" instead of "tank|healer|dps|auto".
• Craft List: the crafter on an item row is shown by short name, and one of your own characters is preferred.
Good to know
• The footer texts in Craft List and Mats are shorter, to make room for the status line.
• Cleanup only happens on your own computer. Guild members on 0.14 keep seeing departed members until they update.

addons.description:
Your Hunter has an XP bar. Why shouldn't your pet?

A World of Warcraft Forever and Classic (Anniversary, Seasons, Hardcore, Era) addon that adds a compact XP bar and level display to your Hunter's pet frame, so you can track your pet's progress without constantly opening the Pet window.

Designed to feel like a natural extension of Blizzard's UI, it's lightweight, unobtrusive, and stays out of the way when the information is no longer useful.
Features
• Pet XP bar and current level at a glance
• Automatically hides the XP bar when your pet can't gain XP
• Automatically hides pet level at max level
• Options to show, hide, or always display either element
• Forever and Classic XP bar color presets plus a custom color picker
• Moveable and lockable with persistent positioning
• Native Blizzard-style appearance
• Supports WoW Forever, Classic Anniversary (TBC), and Classic Era (Hardcore, SoD). Not tested with Classic (MoP).
Commands
/pxp options — Open settings
/pxp lock — Lock the display
/pxp unlock — Unlock for repositioning
/pxp reset — Reset its position
Acknowledgements
Inspired by PetXPBar by weryis and PetXP by waggz81

PetXPBarPlus is maintained by StormtrooperTK421 on GitHub. Please submit issues and I'll do my best to troubleshoot, replicate, and resolve any issues as well as add recommended features.

addons.changelog:
Language-aware catalogs
• Respect the selected addon language for catalog labels, item-name search, set previews, classes, inventory slots and permission roles.
• Recognize locale aliases such as enUs/enGB and esMX. Auto follows the game-client text locale, not Windows.
• Bundle 24,312 English item names and all 154 skill labels in English, French and Spanish. Import available localized quests, NPCs, objects and achievements.
• Support modern item APIs, request uncached English names once, and refresh loaded names without resetting the entered quantity.
• Do not silently fall back to French when another language is selected. Missing translations are explicitly labeled with the record ID; mismatched-language native tooltips use a localized summary instead.
• Translate the remaining compatibility warning and Auto setting label.
Collections and bulk tools
• 24,335 items, 141 client-referenced mount spells and 277 client-defined equipment sets.
• Selectable, confirmed all-mount and verified GM-spell learning, with captured-target protection. Existing all-compatible-skills previews remain available.
• Direct T1, T2, T3 and BiS filters, plus responsive four-button toolbars.
• Nine sourced Classic Era PvE Phase-6 candidate collections, with availability-checked item IDs and source links.
Important limits
• This is not a claim of 100% translation of every custom record. English offline item coverage is 24,312 / 24,335; French and especially Spanish exports still have gaps. Matching-language client APIs can resolve additional item/spell names. Full coverage reports are included in docs/LOCALIZATION.md and docs/LOCALE_COVERAGE.json.
• Five newly exposed mount references await matching-language names; server learnability and faction/race restrictions are not bypassed.
• All 27 original tier sets are visible. The 18 original T1/T2 sets with missing member metadata remain inspectable but cannot be granted. T3 uses verified member IDs.
• Phase-6 collections are verified subsets of sourced recommendations, not complete optimized loadouts or guarantees for custom realm balance.
• Chat transport is unchanged from 0.11.1. The reported "Interface action failed" error has not been reproduced or confirmed resolved in the live client by this release.
Installation
Download ForeverGM-0.12.0.zip, extract its ForeverGM folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the previous addon files, then run /reload. Select English (enUS), or Auto on an English game client. Existing SavedVariables are kept. The SHA-256 file is supplied alongside the ZIP.
Validation
58 TOC modules parse in Lua 5.1 mode; static dataset/locale checks and 6,313 mocked runtime assertions pass. All 93 packaged files were checked against the source and locally installed copy. Mocked tests do not claim successful live-client rendering or server command acceptance.
addons.description:
An icon-driven Game Master toolkit for WoWForever.

ForeverGM brings searchable game data, illustrated collections, skill management and server commands into one resizable in-game panel. Browse immediately, inspect an entry, then choose the action you need. No external application or database connection is required while playing.

Download the latest release · Changelog · Command reference · Report an issue
Compatibility
Targets WoWForever Classic beta 1.60.1, with Interface 16001, and its ForeverCore / TrinityCore-derived server using Vanilla world data converted from VMaNGOS. The local executable observed on 2026-10-16 is build 70374 (previously 70338); automated mock tests are not a live-client execution guarantee.

This is not a generic addon for every VMaNGOS server, the original 1.12 client, or official retail WoW. Command syntax, permissions and available IDs may differ on another server. See compatibility notes.

An authorized GM account is required for privileged actions. ForeverGM does not grant permissions or bypass server-side RBAC.

addons.description:
Parchment Reader is an in-game library for World of Warcraft. Save stories,
notes, roleplay material, and other long-form text, then read it in a focused,
resizable window.
Features
• Create, edit, and organize saved books and notes.
• Rename books while keeping their bookmarks and reading positions.
• Recover deleted saved books and notes for 30 days through a quiet Trash window
in Settings > General > Maintenance.
• Switch between Library, Favorites, and the 20 most recently opened books.
• Search titles and collections by default, or enable the compact Aa scope
to find a complete phrase in book content within the active collection.
• Open a content result with Enter or a click, highlight the matching phrase,
move between occurrences, and return without replacing saved reading progress.
• Read continuously with automatic position saving.
• Group books into collections.
• Add, rename, navigate, delete, and restore bookmarks, ordered by reading position.
• Reopen the bookmark list at the selected bookmark. Repeated + Here clicks
at the same exact point select the existing bookmark and keep its name.
• Keep older duplicate bookmarks independently usable, including rename and Undo.
• Read clearer bookmark titles and excerpts with separate progress percentages,
wrapped hover excerpts with continuation ellipses, and a theme-colored rename pencil.
• Capture text quickly without leaving the game through Quick Note.
• Resume the last saved Quick Note in its current collection, or start a new
note without losing an unsaved draft.
• Use Compact Mode or minimize the reader to a movable floating icon.
• Assign a shortcut that switches a visible Reader into or out of Compact Mode.
• Keep the Reader or minimized launcher in its saved screen position between
sessions, and pin the Reader to prevent accidental movement or resizing.
• Enable keyboard navigation only when the book page has focus, leaving
gameplay keys available to WoW at other times.
• Configure reader size, font, transparency, shortcuts, and minimap access, with
an optional transparent background override while in combat.
• Choose Off, Always, Smart, or Custom reader transparency. Custom reveals a
live 0–100% slider and a Transparent until hovered checkbox. Text keeps its
opacity; at high transparency in a light theme, use Azeroth Glass or enable
Transparent until hovered to keep reading comfortable.
• Choose Azeroth Glass, Light Parchment, or Warm Parchment, and assign the
sun/moon theme switch independently. Themes update open windows immediately.
• Choose Hallow's End appearance across the reader, editor, Quick
Note, and settings. A pumpkin control returns to the previous ordinary theme;
Holiday appearance in Settings controls availability.
• Discover seasonal appearance through a localized invitation, with improved
collection scrollbar dragging and clearer list-row separators.
• Find settings in Reading, Appearance, Controls, and General, with a live font
sample and theme previews.
• Choose the interface language independently of the WoW client: English,
German, French, Russian, Spanish, or Brazilian Portuguese.

addons.description:
MyAccountant is a World of Warcraft Addon that helps track where your money is going with powerful customization options.

Heavily inspired by AccountantClassic, see a detailed breakdown by source or zone across any timeframe you choose. Whether you're farming gold, managing your auction house empire, or simply curious about your spending habits, see exactly where your money is moving!

MyAccountant currently supports all versions of WoW.
FeaturesSee your gold per hour
Track your gold per hour on the configurable minimap icon.

The minimap tooltip can show summary data from as many of your views as you like and allow you to pick exactly what appears on hover in the minimap tooltip settings.
See your income
The configurable income panel allows you to see where your money is coming and going from, showing you a session or historic breakdown.

See it by source

Or by zone

Mouse over an income or outcome to see a breakdown. Configurable in options.
Calendar integration
For days with data, MyAccountant will add icons to the Calendar (if your WoW version has one). See at a glance if you've made or lost money. Highlight over it for more info.

Visualize your data easily. Left click on a day to see it in the income panel or right click to add multiple days and shift + right click to see a report.

Also available through the /mya report commands.
Configure your views
MyAccountant is built around views - data sets like your current session, realm balance, or any date range you define. Each view can be surfaced in several places independently: as a tab on the income panel, an entry in the minimap tooltip, an entry on the information frame, or as LibDataBroker data. Manage all of this from the Views options page.

After enabling views as tabs you can configure their order and where they linebreak in the Tabs subsection in Income panel options.

Advanced mode allows you to create your own views and configure them with lua snippets, specifying the exact date range you want to see.

See the Custom Tab API Documentation for more information.
See all your characters
Track your income as a whole or by each of your characters.

Configure which characters to track in the Characters options tab. Choose from presets like all characters, current realm, current faction, or build a custom selection. You can also delete characters you no longer need from the database.
See what you want on the information frame
MyAccountant can display a small information frame containing income data. Configure it in Addon options to show what you want to see.

See your balance
MyAccountant tracks your gold balance across your Warband and all your characters on your realm and offers several ways to show that information. You can turn off unwanted display methods in Addon options.

By default the balance covers your current realm. To see every character on your account instead (across all realms and both factions) set Which characters to show for realm balance to All characters on account (all realms) in the Characters options tab. Characters from other realms are shown with their realm name.
Faction icon
Hover over the faction icon to see your total balance.
Balance tab
Use the balance tab on the income panel. You can disable this in tab configuration.
Information panel
You can also configure the information panel to show your balance.
LibDataBroker support
MyAccountant registers data from your views with LDB (Lib Data Broker). For each view you can pick exactly which values are exposed, using individual checkboxes in the Views options page.

This lets you see MyAccountant information in any addon that supports showing LDB data like Titan Panel or Bazooka.

Sort by what you want
Configure the income panel to either sort when opening, or click on a table header to sort either by descending or ascending.
Configure your week
Set which day of the week your weekly data starts from in the General settings tab.

addons.description:
PlateColor is a lightweight World of Warcraft nameplate addon built for players who want clean visuals and fast combat awareness without complex configuration. Its design focuses on simplicity, low overhead, and practical improvements that make nameplates easier to read in real combat.

It provides targeted customization for the most important nameplate elements, including name text, health bars, cast bars, auras, threat indicators, execute lines, target and focus markers, and personal resource display. Rather than trying to cover everything, PlateColor keeps its scope narrow and useful.

The addon is designed for players who prefer a minimal setup that works well out of the box. It avoids unnecessary menus and complicated layers of options, while still delivering the information that matters most in combat.
🌟 Features
• Minimalist, lightweight design – Optimized for performance.
• Clean and readable – Nameplate enhancements designed for clarity.
• Core Support – Health bars, cast bars, auras, threat, and markers.
• Personal Resource Display – Better visibility for your own resource bar.
• Simple Setup – No complex configuration or menu bloat.
🛠️ About the Author
Built by a long-time Mythic+ player. Features are added based on practical need and real gameplay requirements.

PlateColor 是一款面向魔兽世界姓名板的轻量级插件，适合希望获得更清晰战斗信息、但不想面对复杂设置的玩家。它的设计重点是 极简、低负担和实用增强，让姓名板在战斗中更易读、更直观。

插件提供了对姓名板核心元素的针对性调整，包括姓名、血条、施法条、光环、仇恨提示、斩杀线、目标与焦点标记，以及个人资源条。PlateColor 不追求大而全，而是专注于战斗中真正需要的信息展示。

这是一款面向喜欢干净界面、开箱即用体验的插件。它刻意避免冗余菜单和复杂配置层级，同时保留对战斗识别最有价值的内容。
💎 特性
• 极简轻量化设计 – 极致的代码优化，确保战斗流畅。
• 清晰直观增强 – 强化姓名板视觉层级，信息获取更迅速。
• 核心功能支持 – 完善支持血条、施法条、光环、仇恨和标记调整。
• 个人资源条显示 – 针对性优化个人资源条展示。
• 配置简单 – 没有复杂的设置负担，上手即用。
👤 关于作者
由一位 资深大秘境玩家 制作。功能会根据实际需求和玩法需要，持续添加对应功能。

命令
| 命令 | 功能 |
|------|------|
| /pc 或 /platecolor | 打开设置界面 |

快速安装
1. 下载最新版本 Releases
2. 解压到 World of Warcraft\retail\Interface\AddOns\
3. 确保文件夹名为 PlateColor
4. 启动游戏，在角色选择界面确认插件已加载

依赖
• 本插件不依赖其他插件，独立运行
• 如安装了 LibSharedMedia-3.0，可自动使用其注册的状态栏材质

addons.changelog:
ChangelogA note on WoW 12.1 addon development
Retail 12.1 protects more combat, aura, cooldown, and unit data as secret values. Addons can often display those values only by handing them directly to Blizzard-owned widgets instead of reading or formatting them, which is why one visual layer may keep working while related text or logic disappears; safe fixes increasingly require narrow ownership boundaries between Blizzard and other addons.

Release note rule: each version entry must include only what changed since the previous release (delta-only).
Do not repeat older items from prior versions in newer entries.
Writing workflow: Tools/CHANGELOG_GUIDE.md. Lead with player benefits, then explain substantial development work and remaining limits.
5.35.1-JuNNeZ (2026-10-31) - Blizzard Raid Bar Stays HiddenHighlights
• Blizzard's raid bar stays hidden when you turn it off. With Show Blizzard Raid Bar off at /az -> Group Frames, the bar could come back on every map change while your group was listed in the Premade Group Finder, until you switched the option on and off again. It now stays hidden, and the option is the only thing that decides. Thanks to Luciful for the report.
Access and known limits
• If the game shows the bar during combat, it stays visible until combat ends, because it cannot be hidden safely before then.
• Checked offline only so far, not yet confirmed in game.
5.35.0-JuNNeZ (2026-10-31) - Raid Panel, Rogue and ShamanHighlights
• A raid and party panel of AzeriteUI's own. It shows member and role counts, raid group filters for AzeriteUI's large raid frames, target and ground markers, ready check, role check, a 10-second countdown, all assist, party/raid conversion, difficulty and ping permission menus, and leave buttons. It is on by default for grouped players, sits folded out at the left edge and moves with /lock. Settings are at /az -> Group Frames -> Raid / Party panel; /azraidtools previews it. Actions you have no rights for are disabled. Thanks to Luciful for the request.
• Target markers lite: a small separate marker bar. Off by default, and it works with the full panel switched off. Choose which markers it shows and in what order, as a row, a column or two rows. Left-click sets a marker, Shift-click sets a ground marker and the clear button removes all target markers, or all ground markers with Shift. Settings are at /az -> Group Frames -> Target markers lite; /azmarkerlite previews it once enabled.
• Rogue theme (WIP): Venom & Steel. Choose it at /az -> Themes or with /azrogue on. Health endcaps are Twin Guard, Serrated, Venom Vial or None, with a separate Venom Vial or None choice for the cast bar.
• Shaman theme (WIP). Choose it at /az -> Themes or with /azshaman on. Health endcaps are Maelstrom, Tides, Lava Totem or None, with a separate Ancestral Totem or None choice for the cast bar.
• Something extra.
Development
• The raid panel keeps Blizzard's panel out of it. Markers use the game's own secure button actions, with no custom secure code and no changes to Blizzard's raid panel. Changes made in combat wait until it ends, and group administration is never replayed automatically. New steel and gold panel artwork was painted to match the toolbar, and all ten languages are translated.
• Theme work focused on fit. Both themes went through repeated in-game review and repainting of their casings, buttons and crystal holders, and the shared art checks now also verify source images and how crystal casings seat. Both also work with Lite+ crystal and orb mixes.
• Crystal and orb casings stay in front. Live testing showed the game lowering these casings during resource updates, so they now return to the correct layer afterwards, waiting for combat to end if needed.
Access and known limits…
addons.description:
This is an unofficial fan-edited version of AzeriteUI 5 by GoldpawsStuff.

AzeriteUI is a complete custom World of Warcraft user interface replacement for Retail (WoW 12.1 — Midnight) and WoW Forever beta (1.60.1). This JuNNeZ Edition includes additional bug fixes, compatibility patches, and quality-of-life improvements not found in the original release.

> Note: This is a personal project maintained independently. For official support, use the original AzeriteUI or visit the Discord where JuNNeZ has a channel for this addon.

Table of Contents
• Installation
• Getting Started
• Slash Commands
• Features Overview
• Unit Frames
• Action Bars
• Nameplates
• Explorer Mode
• Aura Header
• Minimap
• Chat
• Tooltips
• Objectives Tracker
• World Map
• Bags
• Info / Clock
• Top Center Widgets
• Detailed Options Reference
• JuNNeZ Edition Changes
• FAQ
• Compatibility
• Credits & Original Author

addons.description:
A small addon that copies the Gossip / Quest / Book Item text into the chat frame and displays it as though an NPC were speaking in /say.

Much of the time, players skip over quest text, dialog, or book items and not even read them. Gossip Text altogether is disabled by default. Rather than forcing it to be enabled for everyone, this addon will grab the text while still printing the text into chat. Other addons for enabling gossip text frame like NPC RP Gossip Text Re-enabler are there for you - and GossipChatter is fully compatible with NPCRPGossip.

There aren't really any options that come with this yet as it's a fairly simple function. So far this covers: Gossip dialogs, Quests / Quest Turnins / Quest Progress, and Book items found across the world.

Gossip Chatter now also supports Text to Speech

For additional voice chat options you can visit the Blizzard Support Page

New options have been added for text to speech, including choosing voice options per target gender, adjusting the rate and volume for each voice, and an auto-play speech feature complete with a toggleable button and option to interrupt queued messages.

A link to my discord for addon projects and other things can be found here.

The "?" icon stays automatic when you save.
• Saving no longer freezes the icon of a #showtooltip macro on the
spell it showed at that moment. WoW never tells an addon which icon a
macro stores, only the one it shows, and the guess MacroForge made from
the spell being cast moved with the game state (a castsequence step, a
clause not active right now): the editor then wrote the shown icon back
and the macro kept it. The editor now hands WoW no icon at all unless you
picked one, the guess also recognises every spell and item the body
names, and a set, a duplicate or a restored revision that carries a
shown icon writes "?" instead.
• Revisions: a #showtooltip macro no longer gets a new revision each

addons.description:
Your macro is broken. You will find out mid-pull.
No syntax check. No spell verification. No history. Blizzard's macro frame is a text box, and it has been for twenty years.

MacroForge is the editor that should have shipped with the game. It checks every line as you type, tells you what your macro would do right now, keeps every version you ever saved, and swaps whole macro sets when you change spec — without emptying your action bars.

It catches the mistake before the boss does
• Live analysis — every command, condition and spell checked against your own spellbook
• "Did you mean…?" — /csatsequence becomes /castsequence, a misspelt spell gets the closest match
• Plain-language explanation of every line, right next to the code
• One-click fixes — click an issue to jump to its line, click Fix to correct a mistyped command
• Live test — one click and the panel shows which clause fires right now, on which target, and follows as you change target, hover a unit or hold Shift
• Live 255-character counter, with the shortener one click away
One window, built for speed
Everything opens inside it: templates, history, sharing and duplicates are pages of the window (Esc goes back), and the spell list, commands, condition builder and icon picker slide in next to the code. Search by name or content. Filter to what is broken, what sits on a bar, what nobody uses. Drag a macro straight onto your action bars. Right-click for duplicate, share, move between Character and Account, or its full history.

Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+Z undo · Ctrl+F search · ↑ ↓ walk the list · Del delete

Your macros follow your spec
Save your character macros as a set — Raid, M+, PvP, whatever you run. Bind it to a spec. Change spec, and the right set is in place before the pull. Macros that exist in both sets keep their action bar slots, and anything you changed is saved into the set before it swaps.
Nothing is ever lost
• Every version of every macro is kept — including the edits you make in Blizzard's own frame
• Deleted a macro? It is in the Trash, body intact, one click from coming back
• Automatic backup before every set swap or restore
• Unsaved changes are marked, and MacroForge asks before dropping them
Also in the box
190 templates — stances, traps, totems, seals, curses, druid forms, focus interrupts, mouseover heals: 11 for every class and 16 to 21 per class on WoW Forever, every spell checked in the client. Browse any class, not only yours. Spell names are resolved from spell IDs, so they are always in the client's language.

Audit — one panel listing every macro that needs attention, worst first.

Share — export a macro as a short code, send it to another MacroForge user in game, or paste any macro copied from a guide: it is named for you.

Condition builder — build [@mouseover,harm,nodead] from menus instead of memorising it.

Your language — the whole addon, analysis and explanations included, follows your client's language:
