releases.changelog:
The "?" icon stays automatic when you save.
• Saving no longer freezes the icon of a #showtooltip macro on the
spell it showed at that moment. WoW never tells an addon which icon a
macro stores, only the one it shows, and the guess MacroForge made from
the spell being cast moved with the game state (a castsequence step, a
clause not active right now): the editor then wrote the shown icon back
and the macro kept it. The editor now hands WoW no icon at all unless you
picked one, the guess also recognises every spell and item the body
names, and a set, a duplicate or a restored revision that carries a
shown icon writes "?" instead.
• Revisions: a #showtooltip macro no longer gets a new revision each
time the icon it shows changes.
• Dev bridge (tools/bridge.sh): finds the account that is logged in
and the addon folder the client loads; the addon reloads by itself once
the query ran.

Spell ranks on WoW Forever: the picker offers every rank you know.
• Spell picker and autocomplete know ranks: "Earth Shock" (the highest
rank you know, with its rank under the name) and "Earth Shock(Rank 1)",
"Earth Shock(Rank 2)" for the lower ones, each with its own tooltip. The
list used to show the spell once per rank, all inserting the plain name
and all showing the top rank. Searching "rank 1" finds them.
• /use Earth Shock(Rank 1) is verified against your spellbook (it was
"Unverified"), and the detected-spells icons and the icon picker show
that rank.
• Flyouts, spells not learned yet and passives are no longer offered
by the picker; a spell listed in two spellbook tabs shows once.
• Learning a spell (a new rank, a trainer visit) refreshes the picker
and the analysis without a reload.
• Code colouring: castsequence steps are checked one by one (the whole
line used to turn orange), reset= has its own colour, and a space
before a ; no longer shifts the coloured overlay.
• A pasted macro is named after its spell without the "(Rank 1)".

Broken macros turn red, and one click fixes them.
• Syntax checker: a line whose [ ] or ; are broken turns the code box's
frame and line number red, and a strip at the bottom of the box says what
is wrong, with a Fix button when the intent is clear: conditions typed
after the spell (/target Boss[@mouseover]), a missing ; between two
clauses, spaces instead of commas ([combat mod:shift]), a [ never
closed, a stray ], [[. One click fixes every mistake of the line
that has a clear fix; ambiguous ones ([known:Fire Blast Fire Blast)
are reported without a guess. Works for every command that takes
conditions, not only /cast.
• Unknown conditions ([noddead]) are errors now, on every command that
takes conditions (they were warnings, and only checked on /cast): Fix
renames the typo to the closest condition ([nodead]) when it is clear.
• Condition Builder inserts at the start of the clause the cursor is
in, never in the middle of a spell name.
• Condition Builder reads as three steps: who the spell goes on, the
conditions that must all be true, and the result. Conditions are added one
at a time (+ Add, X to remove) instead of five empty slots; hovering one,
in the list or in its row, says what it checks. Insert stays greyed out
while there is nothing to insert. Fixed: empty argument buttons showed
next to unused slots.

MacroForgev7.5.0 (2026-09-24)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• release: 7.5.0

the CurseForge page.

the Release workflow now uploads to CurseForge by itself.
• feat: Italian, Korean and Traditional Chinese locales
• feat: German, Spanish (esES/esMX), Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Simplified Chinese locales
CI now checks every locale file against enUS.
• feat: clickable problems on Home, Ctrl+N remembers the scope, Duplicate opens the copy
• Home: the macros that need attention open on click, like the recent ones.
• Ctrl+N and Home's New button reuse the scope (character or account)
picked last time; the button's label says which.

opens it in the editor.

v7.4.0 packaged fine but the packager got 403 'Resource not accessible by
integration': the default GITHUB\_TOKEN is read-only.

releases.changelog:
2.0.8

Overlord Forever 2.0.8

Ready for launch: 2.0.8 is the minimum version from launch. Older versions no longer exchange maps or captures with it: update required.

Fronts: a capture made with another version of a front (other points) is no longer shown or applied: no more impossible siege timers coming from another version.

Network: relayed messages travel in larger pieces, so the relay sends fewer messages.

Chat channels: the Overlord channel waits for your own channels at login and normally takes the number right after them. It no longer takes General's or Trade's number, so your channel numbers and colours stay as you set them.

Overlord panel: once you close it, it stays closed at your next login, even on a new day.

2.0.7

Overlord Forever 2.0.7

Smoother play: a full pass over the addon to reduce stutters and CPU spikes, mostly in the interface. Overlord also creates far less throwaway data, so it causes far fewer short pauses.

World map: closing and reopening the map on the same front no longer rebuilds every circle and path; zooming and maximising do much less work.

Ranking and PvP Groups: both windows are prepared quietly about half a minute after a loading screen, so the first click opens them faster. Scrolling the ranking only redraws the rows that change.

Overlord panel: the nearby-enemies counter and contested outposts no longer trigger heavy work every few seconds.

Floating next objective (option): the small window now also shows the capture timer and its bar while a point is being captured.

Instances: the action bar shortcut is no longer touched inside dungeons and battlegrounds, like the rest of Overlord.

Plays alongside 2.0.6: nothing changes in what players exchange.

2.0.6

Overlord Forever 2.0.6

Lighter on your computer: the minimap circles now follow the pace you move at instead of being recalculated at every frame. They glide just as before, with far less work while walking or riding. With a rotating minimap they still follow every frame.

Rank badges on nameplates: when news about a player's rank arrives, only that player's badge is redrawn, instead of every nameplate in sight once a second.

Overlord panel: the list of the front's points is prepared once, instead of several times a second.

/ov perf: the measure also shows its three heaviest moments and what ran in them.

Plays alongside 2.0.5: nothing changes in what players exchange.

2.0.5

Overlord Forever 2.0.5

Top ranks seen by everyone: from rank 11 (Dragon Lord, Warmaster, Crown Prince, Sovereign, Overlord), other players now see your rank badge next to your name, in the ranking and on nameplates, in your faction and in the other one. Each client checks a rank for itself before showing it, so a badge can take a few weeks of play to appear, and a rank once shown is kept.

Update required: older versions neither announce nor show these badges.

Captures on the world map: a point being taken keeps its defender's colour (grey for a neutral point) under stripes in the attacker's colour, with its orange edge.

New outpost in Feralas: Anad'Ora Moonwell, near the entrance of Dire Maul, a guild outpost open all the time, like Lesi's Bear Cave in Darkshore. Players on 2.0.4 or older do not see it.

Mines on the compact map: a bigger mine icon, sized like the capture points' icons, with the reserve written larger in an arc just above it.

Smoother maps: map icons and faction emblems keep their place and size while the world map is zoomed or scrolled, also with world map addons that scroll freely, and the minimap circles follow the minimap's zoom right away.

Minimap button tooltip: the front you are on, its points held by the Alliance, the Horde or nobody, and your rank with your Glory.

PvP Groups: the faction emblem breathes while the search connects and listens for groups.

2.0.4

Overlord Forever 2.0.4

Coins become Platinum: same uses (mines, the featured front, Attack and Reinforce), a new name and the game's platinum bar icon, in every language.

Most Wanted becomes Nemesis: the week's five best enemy killers keep their skull under a new name, in every language. Their alerts are switched on or off in the options only (the /ov wanted command is gone).

Platinum for a Nemesis: your killing blow on one of the five Nemesis now earns +10 platinum, shown like a mine's gain (once per player per half hour, never in instances, up to the usual 100 cap).

Very large fights told apart: recent fighting now shows 750+, 1000+, 1500+ and 2000+ HK above 500+. Players still on 2.0.3 or older do not know these brackets: for such fights they show 500+ or nothing at all, so update.

A quieter addon:

keep and outpost captures no longer play the raid warning sound, whoever takes them;

when your guild's keep or outpost is attacked, a red line now shows in the middle of the screen, without sound, next to the chat line;

a total victory no longer plays music or a sound; its red line stays;

the General's duel music is off for now.

Sound settings respected: with sound effects muted in the game's options, Overlord no longer plays its sounds through the master channel. The Overlord option that mutes its sounds now also mutes the click of the PvP Groups window and of the world map button.

Overlord Rank: an "i" at the top right of the tab reminds you that your rank is saved on this computer only.

Colours: a few stray colours brought back to the addon's palette; tutorial commands are now in gold.

addons.description:
============

Load and save songs in game for the Musician add-on.

The song list is accessible from Musician main menu on the minimap or by clicking the list button in the main import window.

To save the current song to the list, press the Save button in the main import window or in the song editor.

Highlight a song to show the action buttons (play, rename, share, delete).

Type /mus help to get the command list.

Special thanks to Mystic Zaru, Eldorias and Oliira-Moonguard for the demo songs!

Command list

Open song list
/mus list

/mus songs
Save the current song
/mus save []

If omitted, the song name shown in the import field will be used.
Load a song
/mus load (|)
Load and play a song
/mus play (|)
Load and preview a song
/mus preview (|)
Filter song name
/mus find

/mus search

/mus filter
Delete song
/mus delete [(|)]

/mus del [(|)]

/mus remove [(|)]

If no song name or number is specified, the currently loaded song will be deleted.
Rename song
/mus rename [ []]

/mus ren [ []]

/mus mv [ []]

If no parameter is specified, the currently loaded song will be renamed.
Restore demo songs
/mus demosongs

addons.description:
The controller / gamepad addon for WoW Forever: quality-of-life tweaks that make playing
with a controller even better. Works with Xbox, PlayStation (DualSense) and Switch Pro controllers.
Everything is set up and used from the controller, no keyboard step needed. Every module but
Controller and Wheel works with the mouse and keyboard too: the windows follow what you used last
(the pad's legend and cursor with the pad; buttons to click, the wheel to scroll, tooltips on hover
and Esc with the mouse).

Free on CurseForge.

Each feature is its own addon (enable only the ones you want in the AddOns list); all of them need
the core, Improved Forever:

| Addon | What it does |
|---|---|
| ImprovedForever | The core: button glyphs, the configuration panel, the Bindings tab (every press on one drawing of the controller, and its keyboard / mouse press), bag clean-up, touchpad corners, the game data (QuestieDB's, recipes) and the item verdict every module shares. Required. Holds the former Controller module. |
| ImprovedForever_Wheel | Wheels on R3 combos, the recent action slot. |
| ImprovedForever_Vibration | Vibration on game events and spell casts. |
| ImprovedForever_Minimap | Names beside the minimap's dots (herbs, ore, quests, NPCs, party members: you choose), gathering alerts. Formerly Gather. |
| ImprovedForever_Map | The peek map. |
| ImprovedForever_Chat | The chat with the controller: pick a line, then an item or other link in it. |
| ImprovedForever_Auction | The controller auction window, prices over time, tasks. |
| ImprovedForever_Junk | Finds and marks junk, sells it with the vendor's Sell All Junk, destroys it from the bags or the loot window. Formerly Destroy. |
| ImprovedForever_Wiki | Everything about an item. |
| ImprovedForever_Journal | A diary of your days, read as a book. |
| ImprovedForever_Fishing | Fishing from the controller: fishing mode, a cast bar of its own, the session's stringer, the Fish Collection. |
| ImprovedForever_Camp | Sitting by a campfire as a cutscene: the HUD gone, black bars, the camera cutting between shots round you, your day told back from the Journal, the camp's benefits when they come, what's said near you as subtitles. |
| ImprovedForever_Immersion | The game's HUD made immersive: the target's health across the top, yours bottom left in the same look in a ring of your experience, your health and power as lines along the bottom edge, your pet and party as cards, the gamepad bar as Hogwarts Legacy's spell diamonds bottom right, the chat as just its lines until used. Needs Journal and Spoken. |
| ImprovedForever_QuestTracker | The objective tracker, rebuilt as the game's own: sorted quests (zone, level, title, distance, completed), an objective complete sound, full controller support. Formerly Improved Quest Tracker. |
Features
• Wheels on R3 combos, laid out like the game's radial menu. Built in: Quest Items and
Consumables (each fills itself from your bags) and Emotes. Make wheels of your own, mixing
spells, items, macros, emotes and chat phrases you add (D-pad up / down picks a phrase's channel on
the wheel), or a shaman's totems, or a trinket swap. Aim with the right stick.
• Recent action slot on R3, placed in Edit Mode.
• Touchpad corner actions.
• Chat lines: with the chat open on the controller, D-pad Up picks its lines, left / right the links in a line
(their tooltips); Cross opens an item in the Wiki, Square puts the link in your message.
• Button overrides for L3 click and double-click.
• Vibration on game events and spell casts, with per-action patterns.
• Junk: what the bags no longer need is marked junk (the game's coin on its slot), from quests (QuestieDB's
data), your professions' recipes, auction prices, your class and whether it's soulbound. L2 + L3 on a bag item
marks it junk or not junk, remembered per character. A vendor's Sell All Junk sells it all. Its Destroy…

addons.description:
Download: latest release · on CurseForge · MelloUI Oldschool (the painted skin) · voice pack, optional: part 1 + part 2 · changelog

Discord: discord.gg/gdpQ6ep7bW · help, bug reports and every new release

Support: patreon.com/Mello_UI · MelloUI stays free; supporters get a thank-you role on the Discord

Everything is a switch. On your first login the installer sets MelloUI up with you, fitted to your screen. Type /mello for the settings any time.
The look
• Three skins: Default (the game's own look), Modern (MelloUI's own) and Oldschool (painted RPG art, a separate download).
• Fonts, bar textures, colours and icons in one place, and Dark Mode for the whole UI.
• The game's windows dressed to match, and a Fader that hides parts of the UI until you need them.
Frames and bars
• Unit frames for you, your target, focus and pet, with a designer: click a part, drag it.
• Party and raid frames with indicators for heals, shields and debuffs.
• Frame effects: heals, shields, cooldowns and buffs land on the frames, and a halo shows who has aggro.
• Personal Display: your health, power and big cooldowns under your character, and a swing timer.
• Nameplates with threat, combo points, crowd control, quest marks and your debuffs; class medallions over your party; glints on herbs, veins and quest items.
• Action bars, cast bar, XP and reputation bars, and a Level Up Card with your gains and new spells at every level.
• Minimap with a Services row (the nearest repair, inn, flight master and more) and one tidy group for other addons' buttons.
• Damage meter: a race bar in fights, numbers on your frames and a fight history.
Chat
• A cleaner chat with channel tabs, chat buttons and a whisper window.
Quests and travel
• A world map of its own: one seamless map with your quests, party, route, dungeons and other addons' pins.
• Route finds the quickest way over roads and flights; an arrow and a marker in the world lead you.
• Quest Tracker and a Quest List of every quest near you.
• Dungeon Info: every dungeon's bosses, loot and drop rates.
• Guide addons: RestedXP, Follow The Arrow, APR and TomTom steps show on the map, the marker and the tracker, with one arrow at a time.
Quality of life
• Auto repair and junk selling, Restock for your supplies, quests accepted and handed in for you.
• Reminders for low supplies, mail, repairs, training and missing buffs.
• Bags sorted by kind, item quality gems, a junk Discard button and cooldown numbers.
• Combat text, gains beside your character, on-screen notices, quieter error messages, FPS and latency, and dark tooltips.
Sound
• Voice Over: quest givers read their text aloud, with subtitles.
• Custom Sounds for clicks, windows and alerts, in each skin's style.
And
• Edit Layout: move and size anything, the game's Edit Mode parts too. Your layout follows your screen's shape.
• Profiles to save, share and import your setup.
• The settings in English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese and Korean.

• A heal bursts with a shockwave and stars flung off the frame, a heal over time seals onto the portrait, a shield's barrier closes round the frame in its own shape, Blessing of Protection stamps its crest onto the portrait, Lay on Hands drops a column of light, a resurrection unfolds wings behind the frame, a group heal runs through the group as a wave, Chain Heal bursts along the bars of every frame it reaches.
• Cooldowns: a roar sends square shockwaves out of the frame, a taunt springs a red !, Shield Wall, Barkskin and Dispersion clamp steel guards onto it, Last Stand and Vengeance beat a heart, Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Ice Block grow a golden barrier, Evasion and Deterrence leave afterimages.
• In a raid they stay inside each frame. The Quiet look keeps its own.
• Buff Landings: a buff landing on your group plays on its frame: motes spiral round the portrait into the buff's star while a light runs along the frame, in its school's colour (Fortitude gold, Mark of the Wild green, Arcane Intellect blue, Shadow Protection violet, Battle Shout amber), whoever cast it. A group buff runs out from the caster's frame, a buff on your target lands on the target frame too, and in a raid each frame only glints. Buffs you can only cast on yourself play nothing. Its switch is in Heal Effects.
• Party frames: Flip Horizontally (Party > Layout) mirrors the party portraits for a party on the right side of the screen: the portrait on the right, the name, level, bars, icons and buffs to its left. The effects play mirrored too.
• The frame previews in the configurator: a part you drag stays inside the preview, and the preview fits the frame with every part shown on it. The party portraits' preview shows the members' aura row as the game does.
• Indicators: right-click one on the preview to remove it, and size its time and stacks right under the preview (Party or Raid > Indicators).
• Indicators: spell groups (Party or Raid > Indicators). Drag a whole group onto your frame: your heals over time, your shields, your other buffs, defensives from others, their own defensives, haste and power, speed and freedom, group buffs, lockouts (Forbearance, Weakened Soul), and debuffs by their kind. Each group holds every class's spells, read from the game's own spell data, each with its switch; move a spell to another group, add one by name, or show them in your own order with a colour each. Every class starts with a set of its own; lists you made yourself stay as they are.
• Party and raid frames: one look. A party in raid frames now wears the look you set on Raid; the Party page is for the party frames with portraits.
• Hide Combat Flash, unticked, now shows a soft halo round each unit frame's own shape while it has threat: amber when close to pulling, red while holding the enemy. It fits the player, target, focus, pet and party portraits in every skin, and the game's own flash, which never fitted the frames, stays hidden.
• Hide Heal Numbers (Unit & Group Frames > Player, its portrait): your portrait no longer shows the green numbers of the heals you take; damage, misses and mana gains still show.
• Your party stays in one place when you switch between raid frames and portraits, and your raid frames keep their top-left corner when you change how many stand in a column (the top-right for a party flipped to the right).
• Damage Meter: your numbers and your party's now sit in a small tab on the end of the name plate, on your player frame and on each party frame, in the frame's own look; yours move, scale and fade with your frame (Your Values no longer has its own box in Edit Layout). The party's no longer turn on the game's Show Party Pets, which is back to your own setting.…

• Route: Repair, Innkeeper, Flight Master and the other service buttons route to the nearest one at once again. Since 1.1.0 a click could take several seconds while far ones were measured that could never be the nearest.
• Route: routes to the other continent are found faster, and while one is found "Loading navigation..." shows with its bar, as on the first route of a session.
• Route: a route to a place the roads don't reach (inside a building, on a ledge, behind a fence) starts at once instead of after several seconds.
• Fixed: after one route from a spot the roads don't reach, routes to the other continent could keep failing until you learned a new flight point.
• Route uses less memory: the roads go in with about half the memory thrown away, and finding a route leaves far less behind, so MelloUI's memory reading swings much less.
• Swing Badge: the strike shows when your blow lands, not when the swing starts, and a critical hit or a parry shows on the blow it belongs to.
• Fixed: an error in fights from the Personal Display's Big Cooldowns when the game keeps aura updates secret.

• Dungeon Info: each dungeon and raid has a Trash section: the rare and epic drops of its other creatures, with who drops each and the chance.
• Dungeon Info: a new look. Every dungeon and raid shows its picture, cut to fit and never stretched (Forever's own dungeons, such as the Hall of Thanes, the Excavation Site and Dalaran, their loading screen): on its row in the list, behind its name at the top of its page, and on its bosses' pages.
• Dungeon Info counts what falls in front of you: a boss's kills and drops, and the corpses you loot with their rare drops, so drops the data does not know get a chance too. /dungeoninfo export puts what you have seen in a text to post in MelloUI's Discord; it goes into the next update for everyone.
• Dungeon Info: with DungeonJournal installed, its loot lists for the bosses and the trash show in Dungeon Info too.
• Dungeon Info: the bosses of Forever's own dungeons (the Hall of Thanes, the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site) list their loot, and the classic dungeons Forever changed (the Deadmines, Wailing Caverns, Shadowfang Keep ...) show Forever's drops: from DungeonMaster's lists, by MalkDev. A drop's chance shows once it has been seen falling.
• Dungeon Info shows the drop rates players collect for Everloot (everloot.app, CC BY-SA 4.0) for the bosses of Forever's own dungeons, whose loot is not in the game's files, as they come in.

• Fixed: after learning a new stance or form, the game could block MelloUI's actions in a fight and drop to a few frames a second until a restart. A blocked action now costs MelloUI next to nothing, so the game recovers by itself, and /mellobug counts repeats instead of listing each one.
• Fixed: the installer said your screen was too small for Mello's layout, at any UI scale, whenever some of your own settings did not fit it. It now says it is your settings.
• Combat Text: an aura that comes and goes again within a few seconds (a warlock's Demonic Knowledge as the pet moves in and out of range) is shown once, not every time.
• Fixed (MelloUI Oldschool): popups that ask you to type something, such as renaming a hunter pet, show their text box again.
• The Dungeon Info button on the map is drawn from a copy made for its size, sharp like the other icons.

addons.changelog:
Changelogv1.8.1
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Faster again: since v1.7.1, checking whether a quest objective is done rebuilt the list of
every place its monsters stand each time (on level steps, for each quest of your log). Ding
reads the objective's text first and keeps that list once built.
v1.8.0
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Problem with this step? An orange flag in the guide window's title bar, right beside the
NPC directory's pin (with a gamepad: up from the first line in focus mode), its own key binding
(Settings > Keybinds, a button or two like the others) and /ding bug. A window shows in plain
words what the report will contain: the guide, the step and its place in the guide's file,
where you stand, your character's level, race, class and side, the step's quests and the ones
of your log the next steps need, with their counters, what the arrow points at, the settings
that change your route, Ding's and the game's versions. Never your character's name, your
realm or your account.
• Pick what went wrong among four ready answers (handy with a gamepad) and add your own words if
you can type, then Create the text: 1. the address of the GitHub page to open, 2. the text
to paste into it, each selected by its button for Ctrl+C (an addon cannot copy for you). Ding
keeps your last 20 reports in its saved variables (WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\Ding.lua),
so a player without a keyboard can send that file instead; "Restore all defaults" keeps them.
v1.7.1
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• The arrow no longer leads to monsters you have already killed enough of, when the game names
them in your language and Ding only knows their English name (Forever's own monsters, the
Skyborne start among them): it matches the quest's objectives by their order too. Their
marks and counters above the nameplates come back the same way.
• "Choose quest rewards" never takes a piece your class cannot wear (a druid's reward was taken
in mail): only what you can wear counts as an upgrade, and when none is, the reward that
sells for the most among what you can use. The chat says which reward Ding took and why.
v1.7.0
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Dungeon quests: a new pack, Ding! - Dungeon quests (Settings > Guide, under
"Dungeons"), with one guide per dungeon for your side, listed by level (the ones above your
level are greyed, you can still pick them). Each guide takes you to every quest giver of that
dungeon and through the chains that lead to them, in an order that keeps the trips short, then
to the dungeon's entrance, then through the dungeon with a note for each quest (which boss or
monster drops what, where it waits), and back to the turn-ins and the quests they open. Every
dungeon from Ragefire Chasm, the Deadmines and Wailing Caverns to Blackrock Depths, Lower
Blackrock Spire, Dire Maul, Scholomance and Stratholme, and Forever's own: the Hall of Thanes,
the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site of the Wetlands and the City of Dalaran.
• The first step of each chain says what it brings (a weapon of your choice, armor of your
kind, a ring, a big amount of XP) and when it is long or far away; very long or far chains are
optional and say why. A quest that starts from a drop shows only once the drop is in your bags.
Raids, the Upper Spire and the level 60 armor-set chains are not in the pack.
• A step that takes you to a dungeon's entrance now passes once you are inside: the game gives
no position in a dungeon, and the step stayed on screen for the whole run.
• "Take this guide up where I am" keeps your place: it stops only on a quest of your log still
to finish or a quest of the route you never took. With "Elite quests" turned on, it used to
send you back to the first elite quest of the section.…
addons.description:
A free, open-source leveling guide for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60). Ding
shows what to do next, points the way with its own arrow and moves forward on its own as you
accept, complete and turn in quests. It is built from the ground up to be played **with a
gamepad**.

Download on CurseForge

> Version 1.8, released during the Forever beta.
> Alliance 1–60: Human, Dwarf/Gnome and Night Elf starting zones up to level 20, then a
> common route to 60. Horde 1–60: Orc/Troll, Tauren and Undead starting zones up to
> level 20, then a common route to 60.
> Levels 30 to 60 have not been played in game yet (the beta stops at 30): they are checked
> by the offline tools only. Please report what you find in the
> issues.
addons.name: Ding!

Changelogv1.4.0
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Setup assistant at the first launch: four short screens to choose how you play, what
Ding! does for you, your route and the guide to start with, the recommended choices already
selected. "Keep the recommended settings" ends it at once; run
it again from the Guide tab or with /ding intro.
• NPC directory: open it from the new button of the guide window, a key binding or
/ding find .
• Nearby, anywhere in the world: the nearest vendor, repairer, innkeeper, bank, auction
house, flight master, class trainer, stable master, ammunition, food and drink, reagents,
poisons, trade supplies and profession trainers.
• Cities: the six capitals and Booty Bay, Gadgetzan, Ratchet and Everlook, service by
service, named in your game's language.
• Weapon masters, by weapon: only the weapons your class can learn and does not know yet.
• The arrow takes you there the fastest way, flights, boats and zeppelins included, and the
guide window shows the whole way.
• Cancel the trip from the "Cancel the trip" line of the guide window, its right-click menu,
the directory or /ding cancel; moving the guide yourself (next, skip, mark as done) ends
it too.
• Weapon to learn: when you carry (or a quest offers) a weapon your class can use but you
have not learned, the guide window says so, why, and which weapon master teaches it; a right
click (Left in focus mode) and it is never suggested again.
• Quest monsters: a mark above the nameplate of the monsters your quests need, with the
count; a line in their tooltip; an option to see enemy nameplates from farther.
• Beside an NPC's window: what the guide does with each quest the NPC offers: now, later in
the guide, in another section, or not in the guide and why.
• Plain words: what a color, an icon or a number means is now said in words too.
• Hover a line of the guide window (X in focus mode with a gamepad): done, still to do, not
possible yet and why, marked by hand or skipped; the quest's level, and why it is orange
when it is above yours.
• Quest lines done say so ("Turned in …"); the next steps sit under a "Next steps" header;
"and 2 more" instead of "+2".
• With a gamepad, focus mode shows what A, X and B do.
• The minimized window, the minimap pins, the item button, the quest monsters' tooltip line,
the NPC directory ("8 min away", "by flight"), the panel beside an NPC ("level 24") and the
arrow ("distance unknown", "farming loop: 2 of 10") say what they show.
• Why the guide does this: when the guide sends you out of your way (a trip to another zone
and back, a quest taken now for much later), one line under the step says why, with the XP
and the time ("Why this detour (about 5 min): turning in “The Legend of Stalvan” opens a chain
of quests worth a lot of XP (about 13,000)."). The whole reason shows in the tooltip of the
step's rows (mouse over a row, or X in focus mode). Option "Guide explanations" (Guide tab).
• Guide window
• Each quest's level and name above its objectives; the next steps show the quest's level too.
• Texts are never cut: rows grow to show them whole.
• Messages about the whole window (quest log or bags almost full, the way there) get a box of
their own; the quest log one opens the cleanup page.
• A step you marked as done or skipped by mistake: go back to it and undo it, from the line
under it or the right-click menu.
• What the step asks comes first; everything else (the way there, other quests on your way,
the weapon to learn, new spells at the trainer, a gear upgrade, bags or quest log almost
full) comes below a line, under "Good to know", never as a red line to do.
• Another quest's objectives shown on the way sit under a line that names that quest and
says why it is there, in grey: they no longer look like the step's own work.
• A gear upgrade says how much better it is in words ("Clearly better than … for your class")…

addons.changelog:
v2.1.10 - 2026-10-14
Requires RGX-Framework 2.7.18 or later for the database hotfix.
• Framework database adoption no longer recurses when an old consumer writes its
live settings view into the SavedVariables global.
• Framework profile-store recovery accepts subsequent settings writes again.
• SQP keeps its module-local settings view and raw SavedVariables owner separate;
regression coverage verifies recovered settings remain serializable.
• Retail 12.1.5 / Interface 120105 and Forever 16001 unchanged.
• Operator reports no issues after testing and explicitly approves stable
publication. Update both addons and fully restart WoW; preserve SavedVariables.
v2.1.8 - 2026-10-06Changes
• One Background style dropdown with Blizzard and RGX groups; choices include Classic (default), coin/medal/badge Blizzard artwork, and bundled RGX addon logos (LevelUp set, SQP, BLU, RND, ETL, CCU, BPU).
• Quest-count background chip is available on every supported client with shared artwork (no Forever-only atlas requirement).
• Logo picks show a texture preview in the menu; the selected label centers on the dropdown button.
• Selecting Classic no longer forces Text Mode on; background and text-mode choices stay independent after Reset All.
v2.1.7-beta.3 - 2026-09-29Changes
• Added the AGENTS.md framework-build and interface-versioning directives.
v2.1.7-beta.2 - 2026-09-29Changes
• Match quest progress to the correct unfinished objective rather than an unrelated unit with shared name words.
• Disable the percent icon and its background by default; keep the preview and options toggle synchronized.
• Use the configured addon icon consistently in the options panel and update the Retail interface target.
v2.1.7-beta.1 - 2026-09-25Changes
• New Unified nameplates option: quest overlays attach into Blizzard's own nameplate UnitFrame with a native level-style count chip. Off by default.
• Fixed default alignment in non-unified mode (health-bar anchoring, Offset Y 0); icons re-anchor after Blizzard recycles plates (death/rez).
• Fonts default to the Blizzard UI font (Friz Quadrata) and inherit globally; legacy defaults migrate automatically.
• New options: Quest Marker toggle + size (Icon tab), target glow toggle (General), percent sign side (Percent), kill/loot icon side (Kill/Loot).
• Options pages use the framework's centered two-column layout.
• Addon list Category and Group are now RealmGX instead of RGX.
v2.1.6-beta.1 - 2026-09-25Changes
• Fixed options tab buttons not using the SQP brand green via the framework (requires RGX-Framework 2.7.8).
v2.1.5 - 2026-09-17Changes
• Added WoW Forever Beta 1.60.1.69893 compatibility at Interface 120007.
• Added the C_TaskQuest.GetQuestsOnMap fallback used by Forever's Retail-style task API.
• Synced the runtime version with the TOC metadata.
v2.1.4 - 2026-08-08Changes
• RGX-Framework DB migration: SQPSettings ? RGX:NewDatabase("SQPSettings", ...) with profileIsGlobal = true
• Timer migration: Replaced manual C_Timer throttling with RGX:After / RGX:Every
• Backward-compat: SQPSettings global remains as proxy to SQP.db.global
• Removed manual C_Timer fallback in nameplates (RGX-Framework is RequiredDeps)
v2.1.3 - 2026-08-07Changes
• Add Category/Group RGX for addon menu section.
v2.1.2 - 2026-08-07Changes
• TOC bump: Now retail-only (Interface 120007). Removed Classic/Cata/MoP interface entries.
v2.1.1 - 2026-06-30Changes
• Updated for WoW Retail 12.0.7 (Interface 120007).
v2.1.0 - 2026-05-02Changes
• Migrated all sliders to the RGX Framework UI:CreateSlider with custom track-style design using RGX brand colors.
• Removed per-slider manual label, reset button, and OnValueChanged boilerplate � the framework now handles all of this internally.
• SQP:CreateStyledSlider now delegates to UI:CreateSlider when RGXUI is available, with fallback to the old Blizzard slider.
• Sliders support click, drag, scroll wheel, and show value label on hover.…

addons.summary: Simple Quest Plates - Displays quest progress icons on enemy nameplates in World of Warcraft

addons.author: ruscuu
addons.changelog:
Changelogv0.9.0
New
• Effects: new options page to control the buff and debuff icons the game draws. On enemy nameplates (mostly what you cast on them): show or hide, size and position. On the target frame: buffs and debuffs separately, their size, and the same on the focus frame. On you (next to the minimap): your buffs and your debuffs (curses, poisons...) separately. Buttons to Blizzard's panel that chooses which buffs and debuffs the Cooldown Manager tracks, and to Edit Mode.
• Hide any frame by its name: put the mouse over it, type /fstack, and write its name on the Effects page or with /rcm hide . Write it again to show it back.
• The addon never reads the effects: it only hides, resizes or moves Blizzard's icons, so it also works in combat, and everything goes back to Blizzard's look when you set the defaults again.
v0.8.0
New
• Save your interface: new Interface options page (also /rcm ui). A snapshot keeps your frame positions (the active Edit Mode layout), all your keybindings (with Shift, Ctrl and Alt combinations), all your account and character macros (also the ones that are not on a bar) and what is on action bars 1 to 8: spells, items, macros, mounts, toys, pets and equipment sets. Snapshots belong to your account, so you can restore them on any character.
• Restore chooses which parts to put back. Positions are saved as an account Edit Mode layout named "Ruscuu" plus the snapshot name and the interface reloads to apply them; missing macros are created again and changed ones get their saved text back, and anything the character doesn't know is listed in the chat. Only out of combat.
• Export a snapshot as text to keep it or share it, and import it on another account.
• Export everything / Import everything: all your snapshots and style profiles in a single text, to move them to another game version (for example, from the beta to the release) or another computer. Importing replaces snapshots and profiles with the same name, so a fresh install gets your style back.
v0.7.2
Fixed
• Threat meter: the bar could still stay purple in combat when an enemy was attacking you. The color is now painted on the bar's texture (which accepts the values the game hides), and if the threat level can't be used it falls back to whether the enemy is attacking you (red) or not.
• /rcm debug shows whether the game hides the threat level and where the bar's color came from.
v0.7.1
Fixed
• Threat meter: in combat the bar stayed purple ("hidden by the game") even when the enemy was attacking you. The game hides the threat level in combat, but the addon now passes it to a color curve, so the bar shows the right color (green, yellow, orange or red) without reading the value.
• Threat meter: changing the width (and the other size, position and color options) now updates the meters already on screen right away.
v0.7.0
New
• Threat meter on enemy nameplates: above each enemy you are fighting, your threat as a bar, a percentage or both (100% means you would pull it), colored by the danger: low, about to pull it, pulled but barely, and attacking you. New Threat options page: what to show, width, height, position, every color, the number's size, color and place, and a 10-second test to adjust it out of combat. Needs enemy nameplates turned on (V key).

Fixed
• Shooting with a wand no longer makes every cooldown light up: the golden border on the Cooldown Manager and action buttons, and the active cooldowns bar, now ignore the short lock each wand shot puts on all spells (the game doesn't report it as the global cooldown). Real cooldowns keep showing while you shoot.
• /rcm debug shows which spell is used to recognize that lock.
v0.6.2
Fixed
• Characters of different classes no longer mix their spells and icons. Each class now gets its own profile the first time you log in with it (a copy of Default's look, without spells from other classes), used by every specialization until you pick another one.…
addons.description:
Español abajo

Ruscuu visual style for Blizzard's Cooldown Manager in World of Warcraft: Forever: square icons with neon purple borders, purple bars, styled cooldown numbers, a pulsing golden border when a cooldown is about to end, and one-click themes.

It only changes how things look — it never reads combat data, so it follows Forever's addon restrictions. Everything it changes can be customized and goes back to Blizzard's look instantly when you turn it off.
Features
• Ruscuu style for the four Cooldown Manager viewers (essential, utility, buff icons, buff bars): square icons, icon crop, borders (custom or class color), swipe color, swipe edge, finish flash, bar texture and colors (custom or class color).
• Active cooldowns bar: only the cooldowns that are running, in one centered line together with the active buffs (icons and bars), with a flash and an optional sound when each one ends. Choose any spell (spellbook, pet, by ID or name), your trinkets and any item, their order, the icon size and spacing, and where the bar goes (drag it or set its position). Test it for 10 seconds from the options.
• Keybinds on Cooldown Manager icons: the key that casts each spell, taken from your action bars.
• Golden border during the last seconds of a cooldown, on action buttons and Cooldown Manager icons: seconds, color, thickness, glow and blink style/speed — and you choose which spells get it.
• Border when a buff is about to end, on the Cooldown Manager's buff icons and bars.
• Threat meter on enemy nameplates: a thin bar above each enemy you fight that fills with your threat and turns yellow, orange and red as you get close to pulling it.
• Effects: control the buff and debuff icons the game draws: on enemy nameplates (show, size, position), on the target and focus frames (buffs and debuffs separately, size) and on you (your buffs and your debuffs, like curses). Hide any other frame by the name /fstack shows.
• Choose which cooldowns are shown through Blizzard's own Advanced Cooldown Settings, one click away.
• Cooldown numbers on the Cooldown Manager and action bars: font, size, outline and color for every text.
• Works with Bartender4, Dominos and ElvUI action bars.
• Themes: Ruscuu Neon, Minimal, Dark, Class color and Blizzard style.
• Profiles per specialization that switch automatically, plus rename, duplicate and reset. Each class starts with its own profile, so spells never mix between characters.
• Import / Export your style as a text string to share it.
• Save your interface: snapshots of your frame positions (Edit Mode layout), all your keybindings, all your macros and your action bars (spells, items, macros, mounts, toys, equipment sets). Restore them on any character, choose which parts to restore, and export them as text. Export everything puts all your snapshots and style profiles in one text to move them to another game version (for example, from the beta to the release). Only out of combat.
• Options with live preview, help on every control, values you can type and a Defaults button on each page.
• Minimap button with the Ruscuu bear (round or square minimaps).
• English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese and Russian.
Commands
| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| /rcm or /rcmf | Open options |
| /rcm cooldowns | Choose which cooldowns are shown (Blizzard's panel) |
| /rcm test | Preview the golden border for 5 seconds |
| /rcm skin | Reapply the style |
| /rcm minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |
| /rcm ui | Save or restore your interface (positions, keybindings, action bars) |
| /rcm hide | Hide or show again any frame by its name (see /fstack) |
| /rcm debug | Diagnostic information |
| /rcm reset | Reset all settings (asks first) |

addons.description:
DOINK is an addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that tells your guild
about your adventures. It watches for nine kinds of in-game event
(level-ups, loot, deaths, quest turn-ins, boss kills, profession skill-ups,
new mounts, duel and Mak'gora wins, and battleground wins) and announces the
ones you choose in guild, officer, party or raid chat the moment they
happen, with real item links:

Discord too. The free, open-source
DOINK companion mirrors the
same events to a Discord channel of your choice as class-coloured embeds
with Wowhead links, so your guild's Discord sees every ding, epic and boss
kill even when nobody is online. See
Discord mirroring.

> Two parts, one optional. The addon alone does all the guild chat
> announcements. Discord posting requires the companion, a separate
> program (Windows, or Linux) you download from the GitHub releases page and run
> alongside the game: WoW addons cannot reach the internet, so without the
> companion nothing goes to Discord. Install the addon from here; get the
> companion from GitHub if you want Discord.

No dependencies and no libraries: install it and it works. Settings are on
a normal options page (Esc → Options → AddOns → DOINK) and can also be set
with /doink commands.

Guild already linked to Discord? Blizzard's guild chat link shows DOINK's
lines in your Discord channel with no companion at all; see
below.
Credit: Dink
DOINK is heavily inspired by Dink,
the RuneLite plugin by pajlads that posts your
Old School RuneScape achievements to Discord. The idea of an addon that
notices your milestones and tells your friends, the Discord embeds, the
per-event toggles and the name all come from Dink. DOINK is not affiliated
with the Dink project; it's a from-scratch WoW take on the same idea, built
within what a WoW addon is allowed to do. If you play OSRS, go use Dink.

addons.changelog:
Forever Classmate v0.26.0What changed
• Audited all nine classes against Blizzard’s November 3 Forever launch notes. Replaced retired Paladin, Rogue, Druid and Shaman cues with learned launch abilities, including Unsealed Wrath, Shank, Primal Bite and Lightning Mastery. Venom is a temporary proc; it no longer counts as Rogue upkeep.
• Added selected readable effects and cooldowns to existing class slots: Garrote, Death Mark, Rake, Lacerate, Reckless Swings, Slam, Missile Barrage, Penance, Amplify Curse, Stormstrike and Totemic Call. Existing layouts and settings carry forward.
• Corrected the bear, boar, carrion bird and bat family guide entries to match Blizzard’s Forever overview. Pet guide entries remain family guidance, not evidence of an individual pet’s skills.

Use /reload after updating. Checks use mocked APIs; live launch-client aura names and combat restrictions still need validation.

Forever Classmate
One compact, class-aware companion for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Version 0.26.0 supports all nine classes. Forever Classmate detects the player class and starts only that module; other class modules create no frames, events, or polling. Every module has separate saved settings while movement, locking, scale, minimap access, and combat fading remain consistent. Full bars use the same 426-pixel rendered width as Forever's default desktop Main Hand swing timer; Hunters can switch to a 42-pixel range icon.

The interface follows the WoW client language: English and Simplified Chinese (zhCN) labels for bars, settings, warnings, and tooltips. Spell and character names come from the client; curated rare-pet names may remain in English. Other client locales use English.
Class companions
| Class | Live helper |
| --- | --- |
| Hunter | Range brackets and validated yards or an optional red/green range icon; ammo, target of target, facing, Hunter's Mark, aspect, pet care, family guidance, and optional player Inspect |
| Shaman | Four totem slots with live or marked estimated timers, weapon imbue, elemental shield, mana, Totemic Recall, and learned Maelstrom, Riptide, Lightning Mastery, Stormstrike and Totemic Call cues |
| Paladin | Mana, active seal, target judgments, Unsealed Wrath aura, and learned Holy Strike/Holy Shock/Consecration readiness |
| Warrior | Rage, current stance, shout upkeep, Rend/Deep Wounds, and learned cues including Overpower, Slam and Reckless Swings |
| Rogue | Energy, combo points, both weapon coatings, Slice and Dice upkeep, Poised and Venom procs, target poison or bleed, and reactive abilities |
| Druid | Current form and its live power type, Mark/Thorns, target bleeds and DoTs, Poised and other readable procs, plus Primal Bite and Shifting Power |
| Mage | Live mana meter, armor and absorb-shield status, personal target setup, Hot Streak/Fingers of Frost/Arcane Blast/Missile Barrage state, and learned cooldowns |
| Priest | Mana, self buffs, Shadow target effects, Penance and other healing or Shadow abilities, and Forever's race-specific Priest spells |
| Warlock | Mana, health, Soul Shards, armor, demon presence, target DoT/Bane/Curse, and learned abilities including Amplify Curse |

The seven standard class bars discover every learned active racial and surface the one most useful now, while hover details list the others. This includes Forever racials such as Will to Survive, Elune's Light, Eureka!, Shatter Curse, Read Ley Line, and Skysight, plus the twelve race-specific Priest spells. “Context” means the game currently reports the racial unusable; the addon does not guess why.…

addons.description:
Forever GuideMate is a minimalist, free, open-source questing guide for World of Warcraft: Forever. It shows the next quest step and tracks destinations with Blizzard Map Pins or optional TomTom. It reads your quest log.

Blizzard Map Pins is the default waypoint provider. Choose optional TomTom under Navigation in addon settings.

It does not accept quests, choose rewards, move the character, or take protected gameplay actions. A guide the character cannot use says Ineligible. Coordinates in the shipped guides have not been validated in the Forever client.

Opening an authored guide midway resumes a valid saved step or returns to the earliest unfinished eligible route step. After starters, Forever Casual Route (Alliance or Horde) is the 1–60 spine: Casual leveling order with Forever quests woven on top, as one flat guide (no zone chapter title). Use Skip on Casual or dungeon guides to hard-skip a step and its dependents after a confirm; Loremaster cannot skip. Sync resyncs from the quest log and keeps skips; Reset skips on this guide in options clears them. Completed quest history comes from the client, and verified quest prerequisites are followed automatically. If a giver does not offer an expected quest and no verified prerequisite is registered, the tracker stops with a diagnostic instead of silently skipping the quest.

Quest-step rules are in docs/guide-authoring.md. Loremaster weave rules are in docs/zone-loremaster-guides.md.

All guides except Miscellaneous follow their authored action order. Miscellaneous includes exploration and books. Loremaster currently shows Coming Soon!

The leveling route is quest-only. Its reference includes grinding and level-up stops that are intentionally omitted, so matching quest order does not establish sufficient XP at every transition.
Guide Types
• Class Quests
• Dungeon Quests
• Leveling Quests
• Loremaster (Coming Soon!)
• Raid Quests
• Miscellaneous

[2.8.0] - 2026-10-25
Quest History comes to Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic, and the About tab links the new Everything Quests video tutorial.
New Features
• Quest History on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. Every quest you turn in is recorded across your characters, with what it paid and, for a quest you accept from this update on, how long you held it. The Quests page lists them to search, filter by character, date or type, and sort, and the Stats page shows your streak, your activity day by day, your totals, trends over time and this session. Each character's past quests are added the first time it logs in after this update, without dates. The Type filter uses the Quest Browser's groups, and right-clicking a quest opens its Quest Browser page where it has one. Open it with /eqs history or from the History tab in the options window. There is no Chain Timeline page, because it lists the Chain Guide's chains.
Improvements
• A video tutorial. There is now a video tutorial for Everything Quests on YouTube. The About tab's Tutorials card lists it: click YouTube to copy its link.
• Updated Korean. Some of the Korean wording is updated. Translated by labrie75.
Known Issues
• Some past quests in Quest History show as "Quest #12345" on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. A past quest added the first time a character logs in after this update takes its name from the game or from Everything Quests' quest data. When neither has it, the quest keeps its number, because these versions of the game cannot be asked for a quest's name.
addons.description:
A unified replacement for the Blizzard quest experience — objective tracker, world-map overlays, nameplate quest icons, an account-wide quest history, and a quest chain guide. Runs on retail, Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever.

Watch the Everything Quests video tutorial

Overview
Everything Quests replaces Blizzard's quest tracking and builds on the rest of its quest experience for World of Warcraft: Midnight, with limited support for Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever.

1. An on-screen objective tracker that replaces the default ObjectiveTrackerFrame, provided by EQ Objective Tracker and installed automatically alongside this addon
2. Nameplate Quest Icons — a quest icon plus the remaining count or percent on objective mobs in the 3D world
3. Interactive World Quest pins on the world map and zone maps, plus a docked World Quests panel (retail)
4. A standalone Chain Guide window for browsing quest chains: Midnight's on retail, and on WoW Forever every chain your character can take
5. An account-wide Quest History log with a backfill of past completions, on every version Everything Quests runs on
6. Branded Quest POI overlays on zone maps, and on Classic, objective spawn markers on both the world map and the minimap
7. A Quest Browser on Classic, for looking up almost any quest in the game before you accept it, plus shareable quest links in chat on every flavor
8. Quest progress on game tooltips — a bag item names the quest that wants it, how many are still missing, and which group members still need it too
9. Coordinate readouts on the world map and under the minimap, for the cursor and for your own position
10. Optional auto-accept / auto-turn-in for quest dialogs (Alt to pause)
11. Group quest features — quest announcements in party or raid chat, escorts and other group quests joined for you, and your group's quest progress on quest markers and tooltips

Open Options with /eqs, from the minimap button, from the Everything Quests icon on the tracker, or via Game Menu > Options > AddOns > Everything Quests.

Classic support
Everything Quests runs on Classic Era (1.15), Burning Crusade Classic (2.5) and WoW Forever (1.60). On Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic, support is deliberately partial: what ships is what was measured working on a live client, not the whole addon. WoW Forever loads the same feature set plus a Chain Guide of its own, and is still being checked there (see below). Elsewhere in this README, "Classic" covers all three unless a flavor is named.

Era and TBC were measured identical across every game API the addon reads, so one implementation covers both. They differ only in their generated dataset — TBC ships its own, because Era quest data has nothing for Outland or for the Blood Elf and Draenei starting zones. WoW Forever has its own dataset too: the Classic Era data adjusted to Forever's maps, plus quests gathered by playing Forever itself and the WoW Forever quest data of AllTheThings. Each flavor's TOC lists exactly one set. They define the same globals and are alternatives, never companions.

Working on Classic Era and TBC
• Objective markers on the world map and the minimap, drawn from a generated coordinate database rather than from the client, which exposes no quest coordinates at all
• Objective kind icons — a colored badge per kind, red for something to kill, amber for something to loot and green for something to use, each with a dark outline so a busy zone stays readable. An objective inside a dungeon is marked at the dungeon entrance, with an archway of its own
• Turn-in markers at every location a finished quest can be handed in, and markers for quests you can pick up, gated on level, race, class, prerequisites, reputation, completion, and whether a holiday quest's world event is actually running…

Every quest you turn in is recorded across your characters, with what it paid and, for a quest you accept from this update on, how long you held it. The Quests page lists them to search, filter by character, date or type, and sort, and the Stats page shows your streak, your activity day by day, your totals, trends over time and this session. Each character's past quests are added the first time it logs in after this update, without dates. The Type filter uses the Quest Browser's groups, and right-clicking a quest opens its Quest Browser page where it has one. Open it with /eqs history or from the History tab in the options window. There is no Chain Timeline page, because it lists the Chain Guide's chains.
Improvements
• A video tutorial. There is now a video tutorial for Everything Quests on YouTube. The About tab's Tutorials card lists it: click YouTube to copy its link.
• Updated Korean. Some of the Korean wording is updated. Translated by labrie75.
Known Issues
• Some past quests in Quest History show as "Quest #12345" on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. A past quest added the first time a character logs in after this update takes its name from the game or from Everything Quests' quest data. When neither has it, the quest keeps its number, because these versions of the game cannot be asked for a quest's name.

[2.7.0] - 2026-10-18
A search box in the options window finds a setting by name and takes you to it, and on WoW Forever, quests new to Forever that belong to a dungeon and need no earlier quest now count as dungeon quests.
New Features
• Search your settings. The options window has a search box at the top of its sidebar. Type a word and it lists the settings and cards that match it, by name or by the card or tab they sit on, each with where it sits, such as Map > Coordinates. Click a result, or press Enter for the first one, to open its tab, scroll to it and light it up for a moment. It searches names, not tooltips.
Improvements
• Two more hand-in markers. Crocs of the Sky and From the Ashes, in the Wetlands on WoW Forever, now have a marker where you hand them in.
Bug Fixes
• Dungeon quests new to WoW Forever count as dungeon quests. A quest new to Forever that belongs to one of its dungeons and needs no earlier quest now counts as a dungeon quest: "Dungeon and raid quests" under "Hide these quests on the map" hides it, the Quest Browser tags it "Dungeon or raid", and Quest History's Type filter lists it as one. That is about half of the dungeon quests new to Forever that are marked on the map. Before, none of them did.
• The Great Windborne Cat Spirit is for druids. On WoW Forever it was marked for every class at level 20. It is the Skyborne druids' version of The Great Cat Spirit, so it is now marked only for druids.
• No "Races: Alliance, Horde" on Skyborne quests. For ten quests only Skyborne characters can take, nine of them on Zephras Isle, the Quest Browser said "Races: Alliance, Horde", which reads as open to everyone. It now shows no race line for them, as for any quest the data does not limit by race.
Known Issues
• About half of the dungeon quests new to WoW Forever that are marked on the map still do not count as dungeon quests. One that follows an earlier quest and starts outside the dungeon, such as Unending Torment in Undercity or Destruction in Deadmines, is left out, because many quests like that are handed in somewhere else.
• Some Skyborne quests are marked for other characters. Many Zephras Isle quests can only be taken by Skyborne characters, but Everything Quests cannot yet record "Skyborne only" in its quest data, so they are marked for other characters, a character who is not Skyborne can see a Zephras Isle zone in the Chain Guide, and the Quest Browser can say "Races: Alliance" for a quest only the High Order can take.

[2.6.1] - 2026-10-17
On retail, the World Quests tab's reward filters now show the ring color each kind of world quest wears on the map, and the PvP and Pet battles rows finally have their icons.
Improvements
• A legend for the world quest ring colors. In the World Quests tab, each reward filter's icon is now round and sits inside the ring that world quests of that type wear on the world map, so the list of filters is also a guide to the ring colors. Hover the "Filters by reward type" title to read what the rings mean, including the larger yellow ring of the world quest you are following.
Bug Fixes
• PvP and Pet battles icons. The PvP and Pet battles reward filters in the World Quests tab, and their rows in the reward summary of the World Quests panel beside the world map, showed no icon, because they pointed at icons the game does not have. They now show a PvP icon and a pet battle icon.

[2.6.0] - 2026-10-17
WoW Forever's quest data grows from 323 Forever quests to 534, more of them know the level and faction they need, and the second Destruction in Deadmines quest is marked near its own quest giver.
New Features
• 211 more WoW Forever quests. Everything Quests now knows 534 quests new to WoW Forever, up from 323. Most of them come from the WoW Forever quest data of the AllTheThings addon, which it publishes under the MIT License, and the rest were gathered by playing Forever. 530 of them have a marker where you pick them up and a Quest Browser entry, every one of them named, and 501 of those carry the level they need. Tirisfal Glades, the Wetlands, Mulgore, Durotar, Teldrassil, the Barrens, Silverpine Forest and Stormwind City gain the most, and quests for Forever's new dungeons are among them.
Improvements
• More Forever quests know what they need. 26 Forever quests that were marked with no level requirement now carry one, so Show of Force and the others are no longer marked before you are high enough to take them. 23 quests that were marked for both factions, most of them on Zephras Isle, are now marked only for the faction that can take them.
Bug Fixes
• The second Destruction in Deadmines quest was marked at the wrong quest giver. On WoW Forever it was marked at Sentinel Hill, on the Alba Fairmoon who gives the first Destruction in Deadmines, rather than at the Alba Fairmoon who offers it in the south of Westfall. It is now marked where she was seen.
Known Issues
• Some Skyborne quests are marked for other characters. Many Zephras Isle quests can only be taken by Skyborne characters, but Everything Quests cannot yet record "Skyborne only" in its quest data, so they are marked for other characters, a character who is not Skyborne can see a Zephras Isle zone in the Chain Guide, and the Quest Browser can say "Races: Alliance" for a quest only the High Order can take, or "Races: Alliance, Horde" for one only Skyborne characters can take.
• Dungeon quests new to Forever do not count as dungeon quests. This includes every quest for Forever's new dungeons. "Dungeon and raid quests" under "Hide these quests on the map" does not hide them, and the Quest Browser and Quest History do not list them as "Dungeon or raid".
• A few quest chains new to Forever show every step at once. Where the quest data does not say which step comes first, or says it only for some characters, Everything Quests marks them all, so a few quest givers, such as one in Thunder Bluff and one in the Wetlands, show two to four quests with the same name.
• Some Chain Guide zones belong to the other faction. On WoW Forever, Alliance characters see an Orgrimmar zone holding the Horde's Ahn'Qiraj war effort quests, and Horde characters an Ironforge zone holding the Alliance's, because those quests carry no faction in the quest data. Warlock class chains also list the other faction's warlock trainer, because the quest data gives a few of their quests to the wrong faction.
• Many quest givers new to Forever have no name yet. Their markers still show where to go, but the tooltip, the Quest Browser and the Chain Guide cannot say who is standing there.

[2.5.0] - 2026-10-17
On retail and WoW Forever, right-click a quest on the tracker to open the Chain Guide on its chain, and on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic the Quest Browser's search box lets go of the keyboard when you left-click elsewhere. Scroll bars in Everything Quests' windows also drag the right way.
New Features
• Open the Chain Guide from the tracker. On retail and WoW Forever, the right-click menu of a quest on EQ Objective Tracker now has Open Chain Guide, below Open in Map & Quest Log. It opens the Chain Guide on that quest's chain with the quest highlighted, and it is there only for a quest the Chain Guide lists. A quest that sits in two chains opens the one you are following, as the quest log's Chain button does. Thanks to user_2igf1k3nab5s7rpa for the request.
Improvements
• Copy boxes keep their link. Every box in Everything Quests that shows a link to copy, such as the Discord invite or the links on the About tab, now puts the link back if you type over it, so a stray key can no longer change it before you copy it.
Bug Fixes
• Scroll bars drag the right way. In Everything Quests' windows, pressing a scroll bar's thumb made the view jump to the far end, so dragging seemed to run backwards. The thumb now stays where you pressed it and follows the cursor, and a press on the bar away from the thumb moves the thumb there.
• The Quest Browser's search box lets go of the keyboard. On Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic, the search box kept the keyboard after you clicked somewhere else, so the keys you pressed to move typed into it instead. It now lets go as soon as you left-click outside it.

addons.changelog:
Added
• AddOns List: the new AddOn Sets option (off by default) adds a Sets dropdown beside Disable All, to save which addons are on under a name and turn that set back on later.
• Auto Decline: the new Guild Invites and Guild Charters options (off by default) turn down guild invites and requests to sign a guild charter, even from friends and guildmates.
• Comprehend Scrolls: a new module for Mages: right-click a scroll you read with Comprehension in your bags to cast Comprehend Scroll on it, without opening the spellbook. Not in combat. On by default; it does nothing for characters without the spell.
• Combat Alert: the new Play Sound option (off by default) plays the raid warning sound as you enter combat and a soft chime as you leave, for when you're looking somewhere else.
• Fishing Cast: the new Louder Bobber option (off by default) turns sound effects up and music down while you fish, so the splash is easy to hear, and puts your own volumes back after you stop, even after a reload or disconnect mid-cast.
• Item Tooltips: the new Repair Cost line (off by default) shows what repairing damaged gear costs, on gear you wear or carry, without a merchant's repair cursor.
• Flight Timer: the new Sound on Landing option (off by default) plays the ready check sound a few seconds before you land, on a flight you've taken before, so you can tab out on long flights.
• Forever Quest Icons: the new Quest Details option (on by default) puts the icon after the quest's name at the top of its details, in the quest window and on the map.
• Minimap Node Icons: a new module that puts the herb's or ore's own icon on each tracking dot on the minimap while Find Herbs or Find Minerals is on. Off by default. Its Tint Unusable option (off by default) turns an icon red while your skill is too low to gather it, and Gray Out Trivial (off by default) turns it gray once gathering it no longer raises your skill.
• NPC Nameplates: the new Skip Pets, Skip Totems, and Skip Companions options (off by default) leave players' pets and minions, totems, or companions with Blizzard's own nameplate instead of a name and title.
• Profiler: a new page in Settings (/fpp profile) that records how much CPU each module takes, heaviest first, beside Forever++'s total CPU and memory. A module made of parts folds open to show what each part takes. Nothing is timed until you press Record.
• Quest Levels: a new module that shows a quest's level before its name, like the quest log's [12], in a quest giver's list and at the top of the quest's details. On by default. Its Color by Difficulty option (off by default) colors the level gray through red by how it compares with yours.
• Quest Tracker: the new Current Zone Only option (off by default) tracks only the quests of the zone you're in, and tracks the others again when you get there. The quest your map follows always shows.
• Talent Planner: the new Level-Up Reminder option (off by default) says in chat which talent your plan takes next when you gain a talent point.
• Tooltips: the new Hide Health Bar option (off by default) hides the green health bar under player and NPC tooltips.
• Unusable Items Tint: the new Auction House and Loot options (off by default) tint red the items you can't use in the auction house's search results, and in the loot window and on loot rolls.
• Waylaid Crates: a new module for filling Waylaid Crates. Its Waylaid Crates entry in the auction house's categories lists every item your crates still need, less what's already in your bags and bank.
• Waypoints: the new Follow Selected Quest option (on by default) points the arrow to the quest selected on the map instead of your map pin, and back to the pin when no quest is selected. Its Show Quest Name option (on by default) shows the quest's name under the distance.
• Waypoints: the new Point to Corpse option (on by default) points the arrow to your corpse while you're a ghost, ahead of a quest or your map pin, and back to them once you're alive.…
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for WoW: Forever that adds to and changes the default UI in small, separate modules. It doesn't replace the UI: every change is meant to look like Blizzard shipped it, needs no setup, and can be turned off on its own.

Download it from CurseForge or Wago.
Modules
Everything is on by default except where noted. Each module can be turned off, and most have options.

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| Automation | |
| Auto Decline | Turns down duel requests, and optionally party invites, guild invites, and guild charters, and says in chat who asked. Can let friends and guildmates through for duels and party invites. Off by default. |
| Auto Dismount | Gets you off your mount or stands you up when a spell, flight, loot, or attack fails because you're mounted or sitting. Can also leave shapeshift forms (off by default). |
| Auto Gossip | When an NPC has only one thing to say, or one service beside small talk, and no quests, picks it for you, so the bank, shop, trainer, or flight map opens straight away. Hold the Skip Key (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or none) to choose yourself. Off by default, and so is its Other NPCs option. |
| Auto Release | Releases your spirit when you die in a battleground, unless you can resurrect yourself or someone is resurrecting you. Hold the Skip Key (an option, None by default) to stay where you fell. Off by default. |
| Auto Screenshot | Takes a screenshot when you level up, earn an achievement, or defeat a boss, and can for good loot, reputation, PvP ranks, titles, battlegrounds, and deaths. Can hide the interface for the shot, and for the ones you take with the Screenshot key too, and can show your /played time when you level up. Off by default. |
| Auto Repair | Repairs your gear at any merchant who repairs and says in chat what it cost. Hold the Skip Key (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or none) to skip it. |
| Auto Sell Junk | Sells the gray items in your bags when a merchant opens and says in chat what they sold for. Can stop at what the buyback list has room for, so anything you sold yourself stays buyable. Hold the Skip Key (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or none) to skip it. Off by default. |
| Auto Stow | Puts your weapons away once they've been out for a few seconds out of combat, whether a fight left them out or you drew them yourself (pressing Sheath starts the delay again). Melee and ranged alike. |
| Auto Weapon Buff | Right-clicking a sharpening stone, weightstone, oil, poison, or fishing lure in Blizzard's bags, or using one from an action bar, puts it straight onto your weapon, without clicking the weapon. Anything else you put on a weapon by hand works this way from then on. Not in combat, when the bags and bars work as usual. Main hand first; the off hand when only it can take it, or when the main hand already has a buff and the off hand doesn't (or its buff runs out sooner). When no equipped weapon can take it, a right-click in the bags says so in red instead (Warn When No Weapon Fits, on). Off by default. |
| Comprehend Scrolls | For Mages: right-clicking a scroll you read with Comprehension ("Scroll: CHAP BALK WELLES") in Blizzard's bags casts Comprehend Scroll on it, without opening the spellbook. Not in combat, when the bags work as usual. Does nothing for characters without the spell. |
| Fishing Cast | Double right-click in the world with a fishing pole equipped to cast Fishing, and the click after that loots as usual. Never while in combat, and it warns you once when combat starts with the pole still equipped. Off by default. Its Louder Bobber option (off by default) turns sound effects up and music down while you fish, and puts your volumes back after. |
| Fast Loot | With auto loot on, takes everything at once instead of waiting for the loot window. |
| Gathering Tracking | Keeps Find Minerals or Find Herbs on after logging in, zoning, or dying, and can swap between the two. |…

releases.changelog:
Added
• Chat Levels: a new module that shows each player's level before their name in chat, colored like a quest of that level. Forever++ remembers players you group with, your guild and friends, your /who results, and players you see nearby, so the level shows for players far away too. Off by default.
• Class Colors: the new Offline Friends option (on by default) colors offline friends in the friends list by the class Forever++ last saw them as.
• Gear Probe: a new Run button under Testing in the Debug module's settings (and /fpp gearprobe) that saves what the client says about your gear, its item comparison, your talents, and your stats, for the developers.
• Item Tooltips: the new Disenchant line (off by default) shows what disenchanting green, blue, and purple gear gives on average, priced from Auction Prices while that's on, or else the material it most likely gives. Hold Shift for every outcome and its chance.
• Item Tooltips: the new Color Stats option (on by default) shows each stat on gear in its own color, including Equip: bonuses like hit and spell power.
• Item Tooltips: Auction Prices can use Auctionator's prices instead of scanning: turn on Use Auctionator's Prices. Your own saved prices are kept for when you turn it off.
• Macros: a new module that makes macros shared by your characters, each with its own checkbox, and deletes them when they're turned off. The first is Smart Buff: it casts the buff your friendly target (or you) should get from you at the best rank you know, skips buffs they already have or a stronger one, buffs you instead when they can't get anything from you and says why, and warns in combat when it can't change to fit a new target. Off by default.
• Minimap Button: the new Swap Clicks option (on by default) opens the quick toggles with a click and settings with a right-click, and Error Keys on Left-Click picks which click the error keys go on. Menu Side opens the quick toggles to the left or right of the cursor.
• Upgrade Arrows: a new module that puts Blizzard's green arrow on gear that beats what you wear, judged by stat weights for your class and main talent tree (or one you pick, with a Feral Bear profile for Druids). It marks your bags and bank, merchants, loot and loot rolls, the best quest reward, and the auction house, each with its own checkbox. A ring is judged against your weaker ring and a two-hander against both hands. Pick the arrow's corner, size, and padding, and show the percentage beside it or in the tooltip. Options show every item's score, mark worse gear with a red arrow, judge gear up to 5 levels above yours, leave profession tools and the reagent bag unmarked, and hide small differences. The weights start from a template per talent tree, and the Stat Weights page (/fpp weights) has a slider per stat, per profile, with Import and Export of Pawn strings. Off by default.

• Chat Copy: the window looks like Forever++'s other windows.
• Item Tooltips: Sell Price also shows on quest reward tooltips, so you can see what each choice sells for.
• Minimap Node Icons: costs much less while you play: it checks the minimap about once a second instead of ten times, and does nothing while Find Herbs and Find Minerals are off. A new dot may take a moment longer to get its icon.
• Profiler: also times work modules put off for a moment, like redrawing bag marks.
• Quest Tracker: the background is a little darker by default, 40% instead of 30%, unless you set its Opacity yourself.
• Settings: a module's warnings and limits sit in a gray line under its description on the Modules page.…
