addons.changelog:
Mana potion timing, the five-second rule and live mana regen for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Potions, runes, gems and your own mana spells light up the moment they fit your missing mana.

Install: CurseForge app, or unzip into Interface/AddOns.

Full Mana Forever 0.9.0

Works together with unit frame addons (asked for in the comments):
• Only markers (under Mana bar): hides the bar's fill, background and border. The potion markers, the five-second strip and the texts stay, so you can lay them over the mana bar of your unit frame; match length and thickness to that bar
• Move the bar separately (under Move texts freely): the bar gets its own place, apart from the icons; unlock the frame and drag it. Reset position puts it back next to the icons
• Above other frames: icons, bar and texts are drawn above other addons' frames
• Bar length goes in steps of 10 (was 20), to match a unit frame exactly
• The texts (mana numbers, seconds, regen) always lie above the bar; dragged onto the bar they no longer go under it
• Seconds (under Five-second rule): the countdown number can be switched off, the gold strip alone shows the rule
• The five-second strip runs down smoothly instead of in steps; the mana fill eases to its new value where the game supports it
• Item list cleaned up: Diet McWeaksauce (a test realm item that never reached the live game), Tessa's Tonic, Restored Mana Potion, Full Moonshine (unclear where they come from), Mug of Shimmer Stout and Tea with Sugar (quest rewards that share the potion or rune cooldown with better items) are no longer listed. You can still add any item yourself
• Read Leyline (Skyborne, renamed by the game from "Ley Line reading"): in combat the regen now stays green for 30 seconds after the cast, as the spell's own text says since the 17 October patch (was 15). The items and spells of the addon were checked again after the patch: all unchanged; the new fourth rank of Mana Tide Totem is found by itself

Bug reports: https://github.com/KesaObscura/FullManaForever/issues
addons.description:
Full Mana Forever – mana potion, five-second rule and mana regen addon for WoW Forever
An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW Forever, "Classic+", client 1.60.1) for healers
and every other mana user. It lights up your mana potion, Demonic/Dark Rune, mage mana gem,
mana item or own mana spell (Evocation, Innervate, Mana Tide Totem, Inner Focus, Life Tap,
Eureka!, Read Leyline) the moment it is ready and fits into your missing mana, so nothing
is wasted: drink on cooldown, stay near full mana, and never panic-chug at 5 %. A compact mana bar
shows the five-second rule (5SR) and your live mana regen per second, also in combat.

| Right potion for the missing mana | Live regen and five-second rule | Own mana spells |
|---|---|---|
| | | |

| See it coming: grey with a countdown, then it lights up | Five-second rule: 5 to 1 at 0.0/s, then the regen runs again |
|---|---|
| | |
How it works with Forever's addon rules
In Forever your current mana is a secret value: addons cannot read or compare it.
Full Mana Forever never tries to. It gives the game a step curve
(C_CurveUtil + UnitPowerPercent), the game evaluates it and returns a secret alpha,
and that alpha is applied straight to the icon. Nested frames multiply their alpha, which
gives "ready and deficit big enough (and enough health for runes)".
Item cooldowns, item counts and maximum mana are readable and handled normally.

The addon never uses an item for you. Put your potions on the action bar and press them
when the icon lights up.
Features
• One icon per cooldown group: mana potions, Demonic/Dark Rune, mage mana gems, other
mana consumables, and use effects of equipped gear.
• Right potion for the deficit: with several potions in your bags the icon shows the
strongest one that will not overflow.
• When to light up setting: No waste (default) waits until the whole potion fits;
More per fight uses the average restore (earlier, sometimes a small overflow);
Strongest only.
• Runes are safe: shown only if you keep a set share of health after the rune
(30 % by default).
• Own mana spells: Evocation, Innervate, Mana Tide Totem, Inner Focus, Life Tap and the
racials Eureka! (gnome) and Read Leyline (Skyborne): every ready spell gets its own icon
when your mana is at or below its own threshold (sensible defaults per spell, set in the list
below); Life Tap when its mana fits.
• Mana bar with markers: a thick marker where an icon lights up, thin ones where a
stronger potion becomes the best fit. Icons stand in the order they light up (highest
threshold first), so lit icons never leave a gap. Icons in a row or a column, bar on any side;
color, thickness, length, icon size and spacing are adjustable. For unit frame addons: *Only
markers* (no fill, background or border: lay the markers and the five-second strip over your
unit frame's mana bar), Move the bar separately (its own place, apart from the icons) and
Above other frames.
• Five-second rule and mana regen on the bar: a gold strip (and the seconds, can be switched off) after a spell
that costs mana, and the regen running right now ("14.8/s"), also in combat. The regen turns
green when it is above your normal rate, red while Resurrection Sickness holds it down. The
mana numbers, the seconds and the regen also show without the bar, and each can be dragged anywhere ("Move texts freely").
• Mana text like the game's status text: number, percentage or both, with its own switch
and text size.
• Show: solo / in a party / in a raid, optionally only in combat.
• See it coming: icons already show in the last seconds of their cooldown (5 s by default,
up to 60), grey and counting down like the action bar; at 0 only when ready.
• Sound when your potion is ready again (optional, off by default): three sounds of the addon's own.
• Items and spells (/fmf items): every supported item, on/off per item, add your own;
your class's mana spells with their threshold and, if you lack one, why (level, talent,
trainer).…

Full Mana Forever 0.8.11

Full Mana Forever 0.8.9
• Regen colour after death: the lowered regen under Resurrection Sickness (or anything else that takes at least half of your Spirit or Intellect) is no longer taken as your normal regen, so your normal regen no longer turns green with the up arrow once the debuff ends. Gear with a few points less Spirit still counts as normal
• While such a debuff lasts, the regen is shown red with a small down arrow
• Major and Superior Mana Draught (battlegrounds) share the potion cooldown, as the game shows: in battlegrounds they now use the potion icon (the strongest that fits) instead of a second icon that always went on cooldown together with it
• More potions in the potion slot, all with the shared potion cooldown read from the game: Forever's Restored Mana Potion (20 % of your max mana, so it fits at every level), Tessa's Tonic, Diet McWeaksauce, Mug of Shimmer Stout, Full Moonshine and Forever's second item IDs of the Minor and Lesser Mana Potion (usable from level 1; one row in the list with the original, counted and switched together). Wildvine Potion is listed but off by default (it may restore nothing)

addons.description:
This addon provides a button that can be used with a variety of hearthstones including a unique skin made of the Hearthstone game cardback textures.
Commands
Commands can be accessed via /hearthbag or /hb. Subcommands include:
• /hb combat
• Toggle the moveable combat frame
• /hb anchor
• Set the Hearthbag Parent to the frame under your mouse or to the specified frame name (BagItemSearchBox, Minimap, PlayerFrame)
• /hb reset
• Reset to your Hearthbag to centered position
Limitations
The Hearthbag frame won't be displayed on certain frames during combat due to limitations, as the frame will become "Protected". The Combat Frame is an optional frame for Hearthbag to still remain accessible during combat.
Missing Hearthstones
I may be a bit slow to update some of the current missing hearthstones and add skins for them. I'll eventually get to them, but keep in mind they're all manually done by hand in my free time.

1.0.0
Large redesign to addon functionality and efficiency for retail

Reworked how saved data is handled:
• Position / anchor data is now account-wide data
• Chosen hearthstone style remains as character-specific data

As a result, the previous addon data format is now incompatible and will no longer be used (you will have to set up the addon again).

Certain hearthstones are now flagged as "Temporary Teleports", where your primary hearthstone will be chosen once the cast is finished.

Added 2 new buttons to select from:
• Random Hearthstone: Randomly selects from your collection of hearthstones that you've collected. Does not include temporary teleports.
• Housing Teleport: Allows teleporting to your house in your respective neighborhood. This acts as a temporary teleport.

Garrison and Dalaran hearthstones are now temporary teleports.

The settings menu is now accessible via right clicking the Hearthbag button:
• Nudge buttons have been moved to each side of the Hearthbag frame, and will now only display when the menu is open.
• 3 Settings are now accessible:
• Shows combat frame during combat (necessary to display Hearthbag in combat, attempting to prevent taint on frames that it's anchored to such as as the bag frame)
• Unlock Combat Anchor Frame (move the combat frame, only when outside of combat)
• Display chat commands in Hearthbag tooltip

The Hearthbag button may now be resized via Shift+Scroll.

The Hearthbag button may now be moved via Shift+Drag.

New chat commands are now available, via /hearthbag anchor:
• /hearthbag anchor [FrameName] - allows you to choose a specified frame, such as /hearthbag anchor Minimap. This will keep the button tied to the specified frame (for example, BagItemSearchBox for the bag frame, which will hide if you close your bags, and show when the bags are open.)
• /hearthbag anchor - Will attempt to choose the frame under your current mouse focus location. Not all frames are eligible, and some may break, so this is a bit experimental. Any problematic frames can be reported to add to a list of forbidden frames.

Some chat commands are now reworked:
• /hearthbag reset - No longer clears the appearance of your chosen hearthstone. It only resets the positioning to the screen center.
• /hearthbag combat - Functions the same as the menu settings button to temporarily display the movable combat button location.

The checkbox setting to inherit right click functions of certain bag addon frames has been removed for now, as this is no longer a current functionality and interferes with the left / right click functionality of the addon. This may be added back in at a later date.

The checkbox setting to allow rescaling the Hearthbag button frame has been removed, as this is now handled by the Shift+Scroll functionality.

An update to the rest of the newer hearthstones is planned for a later update.

addons.changelog:
Guild-tabard consistency for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Install: unzip Livery-1.0.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ so that Livery/Livery.toc is inside Livery/, restart or /reload, then type /livery.
• Two buttons: Use my guild / Use target set the reference tabard.
• A MATCH / NO MATCH frame beside your target, naming what differs.
• A list of every sister guild you have targeted, in hierarchy order (OLYMPUS, OLYMPUS II, III, IX...).
• More: a share code so other officers check against the same reference, sister-guild name rules, frame options.
• ? in the window explains the three steps.

Known beta issue: the current client does not read saved variables back at login (Blizzard bug), so keep your share code handy and re-import it after logging in. Livery-1.0.0.zip.sha256 is the checksum of the zip.

seen and how it compared.

Local-only: no network calls, no chat, whisper, guild or addon messages,
nothing posted anywhere on your behalf.

addons.changelog:
Changelog1.4.3
• Data: the quests, as the public databases have them now.
• New: the quests of the books lying around the world (the ones you hand in to the librarians of Stormwind and Undercity) have a "Books" entry under Miscellaneous. They used to be in no entry at all.
• Fixed: the names of the entries under Events and Miscellaneous (Seasonal, Lunar Festival, Epic...) are now translated.
1.4.2
• Data: the rewards of a few more quests, as the public databases have them now.
1.4.1
• New: each quest box in the chain view also shows, at its bottom left, the money the quest gives and small icons of the items it gives (up to five, as many as fit; hover one to see the item), without making the boxes any bigger.
• Fixed: the quests of another class (a shaman quest for a hunter) no longer show up as available in the search.
1.4.0
• New: each quest box in the chain view shows the experience the quest gives, in its bottom-right corner, so you no longer have to open the quest and scroll down to read it. The boxes are a little taller to make room for it.
1.3.0
• New: the focus window now lists, under "Also here:", the other tracked quests with something to do near the step you are working on (the miniboss's quest and the 10 critters beside it), with their objectives. Clicking one sets the waypoint on it. When you are away from that spot it says "Also there:" instead, and switches by itself as you walk to or from it.
• New: a key to target the quest's creatures (Key Bindings, "Target quest creatures and turn-in NPCs"), and the preferences option "Tab targets quest creatures and turn-in NPCs first" (off by default) to use Tab for it. With no target and out of combat it targets by name the NPC who takes a quest that is ready to turn in once you are close to him, and otherwise the creatures of the unfinished objectives of the focused quest (the ones to kill, and the ones that drop the item asked for; also for the quests listed under "Also here:"). With a target, in combat, or with nothing to target around, it is the normal "target the nearest enemy". The game does not let addons change the target by themselves, so it takes a key press.
• The preferences window is wider and shorter: two columns, with the related options grouped under headings (general, main window, quest log, focus).
1.2.4
• Data: new quests and the rewards of more quests, as the public databases have them now.
1.2.3
• New: "Hide Blizzard's objective tracker" in the preferences (off by default). The game puts the tracker back on every login and reload; with the option on, it is hidden again each time.
1.2.2
• Data: new quests and the rewards of more quests, as the public databases have them now.
1.2.1
• Fix: the welcome windows of several addons no longer show their text, buttons and links through each other when they open together: each one opens in front, with all its content, and a click brings it forward.
1.2.0
• Fixed: a reward that the data lists both as a choice and as a fixed reward (Deviate Hides, for one) showed twice in the quest details, under "choose one" and again under "you will also receive". It now shows once, among the choices.
• New: "Untrack" in the right click menu of a quest that is on the objective tracker, to take it off without leaving the window.
1.1.1
• Fixed: no waypoint for the quests of Zephras Isle (and any other zone whose map id is past 2500).
• Fixed: quests that start or end at a world object or an item had no spot on the map; they now take the object's place, or where the item is found.
• Fixed: a quest ready to turn in with no turn-in spot in the data (a Craftsman's Writ, for one) now takes the place the game marks for it, so the focus window sets its waypoint.
1.1.0
• New: a click on the focus window opens the tracked quests with the details of the focused quest open under the table, as after a click on its row.…
addons.description:
World of Warcraft addon for Classic that shows quests as a
chain tree: which quests exist, what each one requires, where it starts, and
which ones you have already done. Pick a dungeon, raid, zone or class on the
left, read the tree on the right, click a quest for the details.

Inspired by BtWQuests.
What it does
• **Dungeons, Raids, Battlegrounds, Zones, Class Quests, Professions, Races,
Events and Miscellaneous** sections in a collapsible side panel, each one
sorted alphabetically (dungeons and raids by level). Each entry lists its
level range, progress (done/total) and a NEW tag for the content a client
adds on top of Classic (today, Forever's). Everything but dungeons and raids only lists what you can do: entries
with no quest for your faction and race are hidden. Zone, class, race and
profession names follow the client's language. Events holds the holiday and
world events (Lunar Festival, Darkmoon Faire, the Ahn'Qiraj war effort,
Scourge Invasion...); Miscellaneous the reputation and legendary quests.
• Only what applies to you: quests of another class, race or faction are
hidden, unless you look at that class or race in particular (its own entry in
the panel). A "Show other faction" checkbox lifts it for the opposite faction.
• Quest chain tree: quests laid out left to right by prerequisite, colored
by state (completed, in progress, available, locked). Long columns are split
(12 rows at most), so a zone with a hundred loose quests reads as a grid.
Drag the background to pan and use the wheel to zoom (Shift+wheel scrolls
sideways, Ctrl+wheel vertically); the zoom is remembered (per character or shared, see Preferences).
• Search quests... at the top of the side panel opens a search form in the
main area, across every section at once, among the quests meant for your
character: quest title; include low-level, too-high and completed quests
(off by default); and the reward's item type and subtype as the game names
them (Weapon > Wands...), or only quests that give an item. Results are a
table -- title in its state color, level, where it is, money, reward icons
with their tooltips -- sortable by title, level or money from its header,
and clicking one opens its tree with the quest selected and centered
(Search.lua). Quest Log, right below, shows the quests in your log in
the same table.
• The window can be made small: filters, the search form and the quest
panel's buttons wrap onto new rows as it narrows, and the results table
narrows its columns (ns.FlowLayout).
• Filters above the tree, remembered like the zoom: a search box by title, and
three checkboxes -- hide low-level (grey) quests, hide quests that are too
high (you cannot take them yet: their minimum level is above yours), hide
completed quests. "Completed" hides every quest you have done, also the done
steps of a chain you are still on. By level, chains are shown or hidden
as a whole, so they are never cut in half: "too high" hides a chain when
everything it starts with is above your level (if you can start it, all its
steps stay, even higher ones); "low level" hides a chain only when all its
quests are grey. A chain you
have already started, and anything in your quest log, is never hidden by
level; loose quests are hidden by their own level. What stays visible is
drawn translucent -- more the quests too high for you, less the low-level
ones, which stay readable. "Low level" means the title would be grey in your
quest log, as the game itself decides.
• Done inside the instance: quests that take place inside a dungeon or raid
carry a small doorway icon on the top-left corner of their box (and a line in
the tooltip and the quest panel), so you can tell them apart from the ones you
do outside on the way there. A dungeon quest is marked when it starts or ends
inside or has something to do there; the ones of a dungeon's quest line that
never go in (only talking, or targets all outside) are not. Everything in a
raid or battleground is marked.…

addons.description:
BindPad is a keybinding UI for spells, items and macros. Drag anything onto one of its slots, click the slot, and press a key to bind it. You don't need a free action bar slot for it.

This is a re-release of BindPad for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.x, Interface 16001).

> [!NOTE]
> This is a fork of BindPad by Tageshi, which is maintained by the BindPad team on CurseForge. All credit for the original addon goes to them. This fork only ports it to the WoW Forever client and packages it. Please report problems with this version on this repository's issue tracker, not to the original authors.
Features
• Bind keys to spells, items, macros, mounts, battle pets and equipment sets without putting them on an action bar.
• BindPad Macros: create as many virtual macros as you want, without using the limited slots in Blizzard's macro panel. Names and icons are picked with the same icon selector as Blizzard's macro panel.
• General slots are shared by all your characters. Character Specific slots (three tabs) belong to one character. Tick For all characters on a General slot's key binding to carry that key over to your other characters.
• Up to five profiles per character. BindPad remembers which profile goes with which talent group (shown with the talent tree you spent the most points in) and switches automatically.
• Spell ranks: bind a specific rank of a spell without writing a macro. Drop a lower rank from the spellbook (or pick a rank from the slot's right-click menu) and its key casts exactly that rank. A slot left on Highest Rank keeps casting your newest rank as you learn more.
• Optionally saves and restores all of Blizzard's key bindings per profile ("Save All Keys").
• Optionally shows BindPad hotkeys on action bar buttons and in tooltips ("Show Hotkeys").
• A native WoW Forever look: the same window frame, tabs, side tabs, action button art and menus as the game's own panels.
• Listed in the minimap's addon compartment menu.
addons.name: bindpad-forever

addons.description:
===========
A story telling addon for World of Warcraft.

This addon is designed to tell long stories for roleplaying, including emotes and macros.

How to use

Left click on the minimap button or type /story to open the main window then paste your text in the edit box.

Click the Read button to read the selected line and jump to the next one.

You can navigate through the text lines using the buttons >.

To start over with a new text, click Clear to reset then paste a new text.

Click Edit to modify the current text using the in-game editor.

Tips and tricks

• Lines longer than 256 characters are automatically split into multiple lines.
• The text can contain emotes and macros as long as you don't use secure functions. In this case, secure function calls will be automatically commented out and ignored.
• Click Edit to modify the text directly in game.
• Blank lines and lines that starts with a comment code --, // or # are ignored.
• Text lines are sent using the chat window. Add a /s or /party to the first line to be sure to send the text to the right place.

addons.description:
Chatify is a lightweight, modular addon for World of Warcraft written in Lua. It cleans up the standard chat interface, adds message history, safer chat copying, spam filtering, mention controls, sound alerts, and quick channel buttons.
✨ Features
• 🎨 Visual Customization: Configurable fonts and shadows.
• 📜 Chat History: Saves chat messages between sessions for a dedicated selectable History window. It never replays old lines into the live chat frame.
• 🔗 Utilities: Clickable URLs (discord.gg, youtube.com) and ChatCopy 2.0 with selectable chat-window tabs.
• 🛡 Spam Filter 2.0: Blocks spam keywords and repeated messages with channel rules, whitelists, counters, and a log-only tuning mode.
• 🔔 Mention Manager: The single place for name/text highlights and mention sounds, with custom color, sound, channel scope, case sensitivity, whole-word matching, and sound cooldown.
• ⚙️ Settings GUI: Built-in configuration menu (no code editing required).
📂 Project Structure
The addon is split into logical modules for better maintainability:
• Chatify.toc — Addon manifest (metadata and file list).
• Config.lua — Default settings and variable initialization.
• Settings.lua — GUI code (Options panel).
• ChatFilters.lua — Safe text processing logic (URLs, spam rules, mention highlights).
• ChatHistory.lua — Per-frame history store and History window data provider.
• ChatVisuals.lua — Visual tweaks (fonts, hiding elements).
• ChatCopy.lua — ChatCopy 2.0 popup, shared tabbed copy/history window, safe copy cache, native selection guard, and configurable chat-window tabs.
Fonts
Chatify registers its known chat fonts through LibSharedMedia and also keeps a built-in fallback list for clients where the LSM widget is unavailable. The settings dropdown supports Blizzard fonts plus Chatify internal font paths for Exo 2, Inter, and Inter Display variants.

Supported internal filenames under assets/Fonts/:
• Exo2.ttf
• Exo2-Regular.ttf, Exo2-Medium.ttf, Exo2-SemiBold.ttf, Exo2-Bold.ttf, Exo2-Italic.ttf
• Inter-Regular.ttf, Inter-Medium.ttf, Inter-SemiBold.ttf, Inter-Bold.ttf
• InterDisplay-Regular.ttf, InterDisplay-Medium.ttf, InterDisplay-SemiBold.ttf, InterDisplay-Bold.ttf

If a selected font file is absent or cannot be loaded by the current WoW client, Chatify falls back to the active Blizzard chat font instead of breaking chat rendering.

addons.description:
Lootifications is an addon for World of Warcraft that shows notifications for loot and money, and keeps a log of them.
Features
• Notifications for items and money, with the item's icon and quantity
• Optional vendor price and bag count in item notifications
• Choose which way the notifications grow and how they line up, and drag them anywhere on the screen
• A log of the items and money looted this session, with totals
• A minimap icon and chat commands
Options
The options are on the Settings tab of the main window. The window remembers where you move it, and Shift and right-click on it resets its position.
• Money — Show a notification when money is looted or received
• Item Prices — Include the vendor price of items in loot notifications
• Bag Counts — Include how many of the item are in your bags in loot notifications
• Text Size — The size of the notification text, from 8 to 32 pixels
• Background — The background and border of the notifications:
• None: no background or border
• Subtle: a faint background and border, both 30% opaque
• High Contrast: a 95% opaque background, and a solid border in the item's quality color, or the color of the largest coin for money
• Direction — Grow down from the anchor's top or up from its bottom
• Alignment — Line the notifications up to the left, center, or right
• Minimap Icon — Show an icon on the minimap

Reset to Defaults resets every option and the anchor's position.
Anchor
The anchor is where the notifications appear. While the Settings tab is open, it plays sample notifications in a loop. Drag it to move the notifications, and right-click it to reset its position. Loot notifications are not shown meanwhile, but the loot is still recorded in the log.
Log
The Log tab, which the main window starts on, lists the items and money looted this session, newest first.
• Each item shows its icon, link, quantity, and how long ago it was looted, and hovering it shows its tooltip
• A bar under the list shows the total number of items, counting each item in a stack, and the total money
• Clear Log empties the list and the totals, and clears the notifications on screen or waiting
• The log is not saved between sessions
Minimap Icon
• Left-click toggles the Log
• Right-click toggles the Settings

The Minimap Icon option hides it.
Chat Commands
/lootifications can be used in place of /lootif.

• CallbackHandler-1.0
• LibDataBroker-1.1
• LibDBIcon-1.0
• LibStub

addons.description:
Lights up the action buttons of reactive abilities with the game's own spell alert glow. An addon
written for WoW: Forever.

| Class | Abilities |
|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Warrior | Overpower, Revenge, Execute |
| Rogue | Riposte |
| Hunter | Counterattack, Mongoose Bite |
| Paladin | Exorcism (undead or demon target), Hammer of Wrath |
| Warlock | Shadow Bolt while Shadow Trance (Nightfall) is up |
How it detects the moment
Addons cannot read the combat log in WoW: Forever, which is what addons of this kind use on Classic
Era. Instead:
• Usable state (default): the server marks a reactive ability usable only while its condition holds
(that is why the button is dimmed until a dodge happens). The glow follows that flag exactly, and goes off
when the ability is used. "Glow without enough rage/energy/mana" also lights it when power is the only
thing missing.
• Combat events: the client still reports dodges, parries and blocks for you and your target
(UNIT_COMBAT). Those open a 5 second window like the original addon did; using the ability closes it.
A dodge of a group member's attack on your target counts as well, since the event does not say whose
attack it was.
• Either: both.

Execute and Hammer of Wrath additionally glow while the target is below 20% health, Exorcism while the
target is undead or demon and the spell is off cooldown, Shadow Bolt while Shadow Trance is on you.

The glow is the game's ActionButtonSpellAlertManager animation on the default action bars (including
macros that cast the ability), on Bartender/Dominos buttons through LibActionButton, and on the icons of
the game's Cooldown Manager (Essential and Utility bars).
Relation to other addons
ClassicSpellActivations by d87 does the
same job on Classic Era, and is where the idea comes from. SpellActivationsForever is an independent
implementation written from scratch and shares no code with it: it cannot use the combat log (forbidden
for addons in WoW: Forever), so it detects the moment through the server's usable state and the client's
UNIT_COMBAT events, draws the glow with the game's spell alert manager instead of hooking the old
overlay functions, finds spells by name so changed spell IDs in Forever still work, and has its own
settings panel, slash commands and offline tests. The only data in common is the list of reactive
abilities, which is a fact of the game.
Settings
/saf opens Options → AddOns → SpellActivationsForever: detection mode, glow without power, per-ability
switches, debug messages.

Slash commands: /saf mode usable|events|both, /saf on|off , /saf nopower, /saf test
(every tracked ability glows for a moment), /saf status (what each ability currently sees), /saf debug.

addons.description:
Live 3D animated portraits for World of Warcraft unit frames. Your character breathes and idles like on the character screen. A companion addon for BetterBlizzFrames.

> Formerly BBF Animated Portraits. Upgrading? Delete the old BBF_AnimatedPortraits folder from AddOns (if it's still enabled, Living Portraits offers to disable it for you); settings start fresh under the new name. /bap still works as an alias for /lp.

> Status: v0.10.0, public test release. Tested in game on the WoW Forever beta, with and without BetterBlizzFrames. See CHANGELOG.
Best with BetterBlizzFrames
Living Portraits works on its own, but it's built to be used with BetterBlizzFrames (BBF), and that's how it looks best.

| | Without BBF | With BBF |
|---|---|---|
| Style | Circle: the model inside Blizzard's round portrait | Box: a pixel-bordered box beside the bars (shown below), or circle if you keep BBF's portraits |
| Bars and names | Blizzard's default layout | Resized so the box and bars line up, name and level in one row |
| Extras | Bar text (350 (462) or 350 (76%)) | Also talent builds, tall portraits, mirrored target text, gold/silver elite and rare borders, combo points under the bars and Edit Mode outlines that fit the portrait (box style only) |
| Setup | Nothing to do | One click: load a profile (Starter, Naut or BlizzFrames; offered on first login), or just turn on BBF's Pixel Border mode |
Screenshots
Switching targets: the bars grow from empty, each player's talent build appears above their name, and every portrait is a live 3D model.

Tall portraits with Mirror Target Text, on BetterBlizzFrames' Pixel Border mode. The player and target frames mirror each other, and party frames get living portraits too:

| Player | Target and focus | Party |
|---|---|---|
| | | |
Elite and rare targets
Elite and boss targets get a gold portrait and bar border, rares a silver one (both colors are adjustable). The elite icon takes the same color and sits on the portrait; the "??" skull takes the level's spot. Health and mana show as full numbers with the bar text option:
Class resource
Combo points sit under the player's bars as pixel-bordered circles in the border color (or BetterBlizzFrames' own art, or hidden), lined up left, center or right of the mana bar, with your choice of size and color. The resting Zzz can sit after your name, as here, or over the portrait's top-right corner (the default):
Profiles
A profile is a whole look in one click: Living Portraits' settings and the BetterBlizzFrames settings that go with it. Pick one on the Profiles page (Options → AddOns → LivingPortraits → Profiles), from the welcome popup on your first login, or with /lp profile .

| Profile | Look | BetterBlizzFrames base |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | A clean starting point: square box portraits with the gold/silver elite border, full names, no talent builds, Blizzard's bar text | BBF's own Starter profile, with Pixel Border mode |
| Naut | The author's setup: tall box portraits with talent builds and 350 (462) bar text, target and focus turned toward the player, class resource circles, and his fonts, textures, class colors and target-of-target placement (the screenshots above) | BBF's Bodify profile, with Pixel Border mode |
| BlizzFrames | Living portraits in the round portrait, with bigger player, target and focus models | BBF's Forever profile (its Classic Frames look) |

BlizzFrames, the round portraits on BetterBlizzFrames' Classic Frames:

| Player | Target |
|---|---|
| | |

Loading a profile overwrites all of your Living Portraits and BetterBlizzFrames settings with the profile's, then reloads the UI. It asks first, and Undo on the Profiles page puts your previous settings back.

Share your own: Export turns your Living Portraits and BetterBlizzFrames settings into a text string; Import loads one, on another PC or from a friend (needs BetterBlizzFrames).

ItemWatchv2.3.5Added
• New "Only show what I still need to buy" checkbox at the top of the Shopping List. Turn it on and reagents you already have enough of are hidden, leaving just what's left to buy. Raise a recipe's quantity and a hidden reagent comes back as soon as you're short on it. It's off by default.
v2.3.4Fixed
• A rare repeat of the "goal reached" sound: the check that a goal is no longer met now only counts real bag changes, not item-info updates from the game.
• The Add to Shopping List button on the crafting window now always appears, even if the crafting window loaded before ItemWatch.
• Reloading during combat or a pet battle now starts the box in the right state.
• Shopping List icons now fill in on their own instead of staying as question marks.
• A custom sound ID now shows as selected (and refills its box) when you reopen settings.
Changed
• Updated the help text about bank counting.
• Removed leftover debug messages and the /iw craftdebug developer command.
v2.3.3Fixed
• The little silver/gold star on tracked crafting materials showed one level too high (a 2-star silver material showed as gold). It now matches the real rank.
v2.3.2Fixed
• The box no longer pops back up after combat or a pet battle when you had hidden it yourself. A box you hide stays hidden until you show it again, and that now survives /reload and logging out.
New
• "Reset box position and show it" button under Visibility in the settings (or type /iw reset). It puts the box back in the center of the screen and unhides it, which helps if the minimap button is hidden.
• Alt-click a vendor item that is bought with items (cloth, ore, gems) and ItemWatch tracks those items for you, with the goal set to the amount needed. Alt-click again for a second purchase and the goals add up.
• Items added from a vendor also count your bank and warband bank. Any item can switch this on or off in its edit popup (left-click the icon). The rest of the box still counts bags only.
• Added "HandyNotes: Seeking the Soulstones" to the list of other NerdyBertie addons on the workshop page.
• "Hide the item box" checkbox under Visibility, plus /iw show and /iw hide commands.
• "Show Shopping List" button in the settings to reopen a list you closed (same as /iw shopping).
• "Hide Shopping List during combat" checkbox. The list comes right back when combat ends and nothing is lost.
v2.3.1Fixed
• Fixed an error ("attempt to call a nil value") that appeared after WoW patch 12.1.5. Blizzard removed the old item lookup function the item box relied on, so tracked items could be added but not drawn or refreshed until a /reload. The box now draws and updates normally again.
• Adding items from other addons, such as Ctrl-clicking a holiday's shopping list in Holiday Herald, works right away.
Changed
• Added support for patch 12.1.5.
• The addon is now listed as "ItemWatch & Shopping List". Your tracked items and shopping lists are unchanged.
v2.3.0New
• The Shopping List now holds more than one recipe at a time. Leveling a profession? Add the wrist guards, the chest and the legs, and ItemWatch adds up the materials they share, so three recipes that all use metal bars show one combined bar total.
• Each recipe on the list has its own "how many" box and an x to remove just that recipe. Clicking "Add to Shopping List" on a recipe that's already there adds one more.
• New "Clear all" button (it asks first) to start over.
• Hover Practically Pork, Plant Protein or Thalassian Fillet in the list to see where it comes from (looting and/or salvaging). Thalassian Fillet, which can only be made by salvaging, gets a small [salvage only] tag.
• The list scrolls with the mouse wheel when it gets long.
Changed
• The X on the Shopping List window now just hides it and keeps your list. Type /iw shopping to bring it back.
• A Shopping List you had open when you updated carries over automatically.

addons.description:
=========

A World of Warcraft addon for tracking specific item counts — a movable,
resizable box you drag items into, with goals, per-item sounds, and a
minimap button. Also builds a shopping list straight from any
crafting recipe, and can track the items a vendor wants in trade.

Built for farming, collecting, or any situation where you need to keep an
eye on an exact item count without repeatedly opening your bags.
Features
• Item Box — a movable, resizable container for everything you're
tracking. Drag items from your bags straight onto it, right-click an
icon inside to remove it.
• Recipe Shopping List — click "Add to Shopping List" on any recipe
in the Professions Recipes tab, and ItemWatch reads its full reagent
list and builds a shopping list for you automatically. It holds as
many recipes as you like, so leveling a profession is easy: add the
wrist guards, the chest and the legs, and any materials they share
(like metal bars) are added together into one row with the combined
total. Each recipe has its own "how many" box and an x to remove it,
and clicking "Add to Shopping List" on a recipe that's already there
adds one more. Required reagents track live progress (counting bank
and warband bank, not just bags) and show a "Need: X" line for
anything you're still short on, so there's no mental math while
you're standing at the Auction House. Optional/finishing reagents
show as a plain reminder, and reagents you can't buy on the Auction
House are flagged "[vendor/earned only]" instead of silently
vanishing. The window is movable, resizable, lockable, scrolls with
the mouse wheel, persists across logout/reload, and has a "Clear all"
button (it asks first) to start over. Pulled away by a dungeon queue?
Close it and your list is kept - a "Show Shopping List" button in the
settings (or /iw shopping) brings it right back. Tick "Only show what
I need to buy" to hide the reagents you already have enough of, so the
list shows just what's left to shop for. A hidden reagent comes back
the moment you're short on it, like when you raise a recipe's quantity.
• Quick-Add popup — track items you don't have yet by pasting a
Wowhead link, typing an item ID, or shift-clicking an item straight
into the field. Set a goal and sound in one step.
• Per-item edit popup — left-click any tracked icon to change its
goal or pick its own custom "goal reached" sound (or mute it).
• Per-item ding sounds — no more one generic sound for everything;
give each tracked item its own, so you know what just hit its goal
without looking. A growing collection of fun/thematic presets alongside
the practical ones - see the Sound Presets section below for the full
list.
• Shift-click to link, Ctrl-click to preview — tracked icons behave
like real item icons for chat links and equippable-gear previews.
• Vendor purchase tracking — some vendors sell things for items
(cloth, ore, gems) instead of gold. Alt-click the vendor item and
ItemWatch tracks the items it costs, with each goal set to the amount
needed. Alt-click again for a second purchase and the goals add up.
Hover a vendor item and the tooltip tells you if Alt-click is
available for it.
• Character-specific tracking — each character keeps its own list.
The main Item Box counts bags and the reagent bag, real-time, so
counts are exactly what you're carrying. Any item can also be set to
count your bank and warband bank (a checkbox in its edit popup), and
items added from a vendor start that way. The Shopping List always
checks your bank and warband, since it's answering a different
question - "do I still need to go buy this."
• Blizzard Edit Mode support for the box.
• Hide it when you want to — hide the box with the minimap button,
a checkbox in the settings, or /iw hide. It stays hidden through
combat, reloads and logging out. There are also combat and pet battle
toggles to hide it automatically, and the Shopping List can hide…

addons.changelog:
WoW Forever (beta)
• Auto Shot wind-up mark: the mark drifted (reported as marks sitting about a third of the way into each half of a converge bar). The band behind it was a running maximum of interrupt reads, and one read taken from a fresh Auto Shot press on a new target set the mark a second and a half early for good. A dummy session settled the model: the wind-up scales with your reload, and the server retries a held shot every half second. Nock now reads the wind-up from your own pulls, as a share of the bar: Auto Shot pressed on an idle bar while standing still, and the time to the first shot. The share is kept per character and per ranged weapon and only moves when your pulls say so, so a new weapon steps it once and nothing creeps. The mark, the inverse auto bar's second phase and the cast-bar wind-up are there from the first frame, with a stand-in until your first pull. Reads saved by 2.1.3 are dropped at login. /nock probe windup script walks a five-leg dummy run for bug reports, and /nock probe windup now reads it back with a haste verdict.
• Sting tiles: grey until applied: a new Grid option (off by default). Your sting's tile is greyed out while the sting is not on the target and lights in full colour the moment it lands, so the grid tells you what is missing rather than what you have. Its swipe then drains as the sting runs out instead of filling like a cooldown. The timer stays the client's own. By request.
• Range colours: a new option under Range text on the strip (off by default): Text colours the bracket on the weave strip the way the Range Finder colours its segments (8-20 teal, 20-30 blue, 30-35 indigo, 35-40 purple, out of range red); Bar background puts that colour behind the whole bar instead. The weave words and the sweet spot's green keep their own look. The five colours are pickers under Skin → Range colours (Advanced), and the Range Finder reads the same ones. By request.
• Melee bar with the weave cue off: with Weave cue takes over the melee bar off, the melee bar no longer shows the stage words in small text; the weave strip is the cue, and the Weave helper switch owns the strip and the leg learning only. The weaving quickstart says NO CUE when both the melee-bar cue and the strip are off.
addons.description:
A combat HUD for Hunters on TBC Classic Anniversary realms (Burning Crusade
2.5.x). Nock measures your Auto Shot live, tells you exactly when a cast will
clip it and when it is free, and turns the whole ranged/melee weave into
something you can see — and practise out of combat against your own rotation.
What it does
• Swing timer that knows the wind-up. Auto Shot has a haste-scaled wind-up
that sits inside the weapon cycle; Nock measures it from the combat log
instead of assuming 0.5 s, and draws the clip band as what it really is — a
band, with a free queue window at the end of every cycle.
• Rotation advice for the Steady / Multi / Arcane cadences (1:1,
5:5:1:1, the French rotations, weaves) with one clip deadline shared by
every view, plus scrolling Shot Bars in the style of Fluffy Hunter Bars.
• Weave bind and coach. A press/release weave key (importable from
Grounded), a range finder with reach-aware zones, a retry grid for the
re-arm, and a live weave log (A-W / W-A / T).
• Weave practice. A workbench with a stage, lessons, a drill ladder, a
scenario catalog, a replay you can scrub, and an expert combat log — graded
against the rotation notation, at your own haste.
• Cooldowns, procs, pet, Misdirection, buff and debuff trackers, totem and
mana bars, a React-style compact HUD mode, and a Classic layout — every frame
movable, every panel skinnable through SharedMedia.
• Warnings that are worth a sound: quiver low, wrong trinket, pet training
points, keybind conflicts, and boss-specific ones (Anetheron Sleep vs the
Slammer, Teron's ghosts, the teleporter ALT-F4 countdown, Steam Tonk guard).
• Setup wizard (/nock wizard) and a setup check that catches the common
misconfigurations, plus a shopping list for consumables before a raid.

releases.changelog:
WoW Forever (beta)
• Auto Shot wind-up mark: the mark drifted (reported as marks sitting about a third of the way into each half of a converge bar). The band behind it was a running maximum of interrupt reads, and one read taken from a fresh Auto Shot press on a new target set the mark a second and a half early for good. • Sting tiles: grey until applied: a new Grid option (off by default). Its swipe then drains as the sting runs out instead of filling like a cooldown. The timer stays the client's own. By request.

The weave words and the sweet spot's green keep their own look. The five colours are pickers under Skin → Range colours (Advanced), and the Range Finder reads the same ones. By request.

The weaving quickstart says NO CUE when both the melee-bar cue and the strip are off.

Both clients
• Settings: Step aside: a new footer button hides the settings window without closing it, so you can drag the HUD into place and come straight back to the page, tab and search you were on. A pill at the top of the screen brings the window back and carries a Lock / Unlock frames toggle of its own; the lock is otherwise left as you had it. The same cycle (open, step aside, back) is on a keybinding, Settings: open / step aside / back, under Key Bindings → Nock.
WoW Forever (beta)
• Auto Shot wind-up: the client now has a wind-up before each Auto Shot, and the game reports nothing about it, so Nock measures it from your own shots: a move that begins inside the wind-up interrupts it, and from those interrupts Nock learns where the wind-up starts (the game's 0.5 s plus your latency, so about 0.6 s). The wind-up mark on the Auto Shot bar and the inverse auto bar's second phase move to the measured spot (the spell-queue window stands in until the first measurement), and the React cast bar shows the wind-up the way it does on TBC: standing still it runs up to the shot; after a late stop it runs from the stop. Moving before the mark is free; moving past it holds the shot until about a second after you stand still again. The measurement is kept per character. Auto Shot wind-up on cast bar (Nock HUD → Size & Elements) switches the cast-bar part off, which you will want with the inverse auto bar, since the two would show the same window twice; the switch now sits in Simple mode. /nock probe windup shows what Nock measured, for bug reports.
• Learned spells only: a new Grid option (off by default) leaves a cooldown tile out of the grid while you have not trained its spell, instead of showing it greyed; the row closes up, and the tile returns the moment you learn the spell. The cooldown board still lists the spell, greyed, so it can be placed ahead of time. By request.

Both clients
• OmniCC GODMODE: Nock's own timer digits now stand down when OmniCC GODMODE is loaded, as they already did for OmniCC, tullaCC and ncCooldown, so you no longer get two countdowns on the same icon.
WoW Forever (beta)
• Eyes of the Beast pulse, out of combat: a new option, Also out of combat (Alerts → Eyes of the Beast pulse, off by default), shows the pulse bar while you channel Eyes of the Beast outside combat too.
• Eyes of the Beast pulse follows the pet's beat: the countdown now starts when you begin the channel and keeps running through the pull and after combat ends, which is what in-game measurements showed. If your bar falls out of step right after a pull, the new Restart at the pull option brings back the old behaviour. A /reload mid-fight no longer leaves the bar empty until a resync, and /nock pulse log shows what the timer saw for bug reports.
• Fix: Lua error after leaving Eyes of the Beast: with a sting timer on the cooldown grid, exiting Eyes of the Beast after a kill could throw "calling 'SetFont' on bad self". The sting countdown is now left alone once the game has taken it over.

WoW Forever (beta)
• Pet abilities in the cooldown grid: a new Pet tab on the cooldown board lists the abilities of all your pets, active and stabled: Bite, Claw, Dash, Prowl, Growl, Swipe and the rest, one chip per ability whatever its rank, with its cooldown and which of your pets have it. Abilities the pet you have out has not learned yet are greyed and marked "not learned", but can still be placed. A placed pet tile shows on the HUD only while your summoned pet knows that ability: swap to a pet without it, or dismiss your pet, and the tile hides and the row closes up; call it back and the tile returns. Timers work in combat, in the open world and in dungeons. /nock petcd shows what Nock reads from your pet, for bug reports.
• Range text on the weave strip: a new option, Range text on the strip (Nock HUD → Size & Elements, and the Weaving quickstart), hides the Range Finder and puts its text on the weave strip's bar instead. Out of range it reads OUT OF RANGE, in range it names your bracket (8-20, 20-25, ...), and the weave words (dead zone, melee, sweet spot, the stages) take over as soon as a weave starts. Off by default.

Both clients
• Cooldown grid tile size: the Icons card on the Grid tab (Advanced) now sets the size of the tiles. Top row height, whether the top row fills the HUD width or keeps a tile width of your choice (centred), and the height and tile width of the rows under it; FluffyHUD's row gets its own height. Unset, the grid looks as before. A width the HUD cannot fit fills it instead, icon zoom crops the art to any shape, and the HUD below moves to make room. By request.
• Cast bar, pixel-exact: the React cast bar is laid out in whole screen pixels, like the rest of the HUD, so its fill now meets the right border at any UI scale and its seams stay one pixel.
WoW Forever (beta)
• Eyes of the Beast pulse timer: while you control your pet with Eyes of the Beast, it pulls nearby mobs on a fixed beat counted from the pull. A new row stacked on the React cast bar counts that beat down in combat while Eyes of the Beast is channelled, so you can time your moves between pulses. Right-click it, or type /nock pulse, to resync when the pet's pulse drifts. The interval is 5.6 s by default and adjustable. Off by default: Alerts → Eyes of the Beast pulse. After the "EotB Pet Combat Pulse" WeakAura by Rubot; by request.
• Trueshot Aura warning: an amber TSA square when Trueshot Aura is talented but not on you, or has under a minute left on its 30 minutes (the square then counts it down; the lead is a slider, 0 turns it off). In and out of combat, so it shows before the pull; a Where setting limits it to dungeons and raids, or raids only. The game hides your auras in combat, so there Nock goes by your own casts and the buff's 30 minutes: casting it clears the square, /cancelaura Trueshot Aura brings it back, and a right-click on the buff is seen when combat ends. Alerts → Warnings → Combat. By request.
• Active timers on Rapid Fire, Bestial Wrath and Deterrence: like the racials, these cooldown tiles now light up with their buff's countdown before the cooldown takes over. Bestial Wrath's is read from your pet.
• Aspect after /cancelaura: cancelling your aspect with /cancelaura in combat now clears it from the HUD at once, instead of when combat ends.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for WoW Forever that counts the footsteps your character takes and how far you travel by every other means.
Features
• Step counting from your actual movement, using stride lengths measured for every Forever race and sex. Running, walking, backpedaling and strafing are tracked separately.
• Distance by travel mode: on foot, mounted, shapeshifted (druid forms, Ghost Wolf), swimming, jumping and falling, flight paths (with the fares you paid), boats, zeppelins and trams, and corpse runs as a ghost.
• A small panel with today's steps or distance, the session so far and what you're doing. Hover it for the full breakdown.
• Broker and minimap button: the same headline in any LibDataBroker display (Titan Panel, ChocolateBar, data bars), plus a minimap button and an entry in the minimap's addons menu.
• History: week, month and year charts of steps or distance for one character or all of them, stacked by character (in class colours) or by travel mode, with a filterable legend.
• Milestones: travel achievements in Bronze, Silver, Gold and Legendary tiers, with points, per character and account-wide.
• Sync between PCs: export your travel as a text string and import it on another PC, so a desktop and a laptop show the same combined totals, history and milestones. Nothing is counted twice, however often you sync.
• Stride calibration: measure your own stride lengths if the built-in ones don't suit your character.
Screenshots

Translates World of Warcraft terms, acronyms and slang right in your chat

🇪🇸 Español

📸 Screenshots
▶️ How to use WoW Translator v2.00

All languages in chat, in real time

What it does
WoW Translator reads incoming chat messages and adds the meaning of WoW jargon next to each term, in the colour you choose. A message like LFM ICC HC 25m Need Tank and Healer keeps its original text, with the translation of every recognised acronym or word added in brackets. Nothing is sent for you: it only annotates what you receive.
Features
• Translates dungeon and raid acronyms, slang, classes, roles, stats, professions, combat, trade, group, guild and status terms.
• 44 target languages; defaults to your game client's language.
• Whole sentences: typical messages (looking for group, recruiting, trade, crafters, portals, guild recruiting) also get the full sentence on a line below, in the speaker's voice, in 20 languages.
• Zone, item set and race names from LibBabble, in your client's language, each with its own colour.
• Turn each category and the instance names of each expansion (Classic to Midnight) on or off.
• Pick which chat channels are translated: say, yell, emote, global channels, whispers, Battle.net, guild, party, raid, instance, battleground and communities.
• Ignore list for words you never want translated.
• /wt en turns text written in your target language back into English WoW terms and leaves it in the chat box for you to review and send.
• Beta: also recognises WoW slang written in Korean and Simplified Chinese (off by default).
• Minimap button and options panel translated into 20 languages.

0.13.0
A small feature release since 0.12.0: Modern chat can now keep its tabs above the chat.
Added
• Tabs: Bottom or Top (Modern chat, /quiet setup → Misc.): a new Tabs choice next to Fade after. Bottom (the default) keeps the 0.12.0 behavior, with the tab row below the chat. Top leaves the tabs at Blizzard's own place above the chat. Either way, the tabs stay hidden until you hover the chat or the tab row, and a tab with new messages still glows until you read it. The choice is saved with your presets.
Fixed
• The Tabs stepper switches between Bottom and Top from either arrow, and its value lines up with Fade after.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.13.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. /reload is enough; this release adds no new files. Keep your existing SavedVariables.

3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.12.0...0.13.0
addons.description:
Less UI. More world. A quiet interface for the WoW Forever beta (Interface 16001).

QuietUI fades the Blizzard HUD while you explore and brings back the parts you
need through hover, combat, and your current situation. It works out of the box;
one setup window lets you tweak what stays visible.
What you get
• Bars when you need them. Hover reveals a group of action bars; combat and
instances bring all bars back.
• A quieter HUD. Quests appear on hover. Cooldowns and the damage meter appear
when fighting or grouped. Health and resources appear when they need attention.
• One bag button. Left click opens bags, right click reveals bag slots, and
dragging moves the button.
• Glance. Press ` to reveal the faded HUD at once. Press again to return
to your usual visibility rules.
• Small extras. Chat without the chrome, short quest update notices, a glow on
the herb, ore, or object you can interact with, and an icon on mobs your quests need.

releases.changelog:
0.13.0
A small feature release since 0.12.0: Modern chat can now keep its tabs above the chat.
Added
• Tabs: Bottom or Top (Modern chat, /quiet setup → Misc.): a new Tabs choice next to Fade after. Bottom (the default) keeps the 0.12.0 behavior, with the tab row below the chat. Top leaves the tabs at Blizzard's own place above the chat. Either way, the tabs stay hidden until you hover the chat or the tab row, and a tab with new messages still glows until you read it. The choice is saved with your presets.
Fixed
• The Tabs stepper switches between Bottom and Top from either arrow, and its value lines up with Fade after.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.13.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. /reload is enough; this release adds no new files. Keep your existing SavedVariables.
2. No settings change; your presets and per-character settings carry over, and the tabs stay below the chat until you pick Top.
3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.12.0...0.13.0

0.12.0
A feature release since 0.11.1: Modern chat now keeps its tabs quiet below the chat, and whisper windows get the same look.
Added
• Chat tabs below the chat (Modern chat, /quiet setup → Misc.): the tab row moves below the chat, under the strip where the input appears. When there is no room above the screen bottom, the tabs sit at the bottom edge.
• Tabs on demand: the tabs stay hidden until you hover the chat or the tab row. A tab with new messages, such as a whisper, glows until you read it.
• Click a tab, see its messages: hovering the tab row counts as hovering the chat, so clicking a tab shows that window's lines at once, including ones that already faded.
• Whisper windows: whisper tabs that open their own window get Modern chat too: line bubbles, the flat input, and the hidden tab.
Changed
• QuietUI layout: the durability frame has a new position. If you use the bundled layout, QuietUI offers the update once after you install.
• The unfocused chat input no longer takes clicks, so a click on a tab never opens the last whisper by mistake. Press Enter to type.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.12.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. Restart the game; this release adds a new file (Settings.lua), which /reload does not load. Keep your existing SavedVariables.
2. No settings change; your presets and per-character settings carry over as they are. Turning off Modern chat or QuietUI puts the tabs back above the chat.
3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.11.1...0.12.0

0.11.1
A small fix release since 0.11.0: Glance now works on dead targets, and the Highlights glow is easier to see.
Changed
• Highlights (/quiet setup → Misc.): the soft-interact glow sits lower and reads larger. The halo and aura grow, herbs get a stronger glow, ore moves up slightly, and the glow now carries five glints and six motes.
Fixed
• Glance now shows the player, pet, and target frames even when Require a living target would fade them for a dead target, matching how Glance already bypasses the death and ghost-form rule.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.11.1.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. Restart the game or type /reload. Keep your existing SavedVariables.
2. No settings change; your presets and per-character settings carry over as they are.
3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.11.0...0.11.1

0.11.0
Two new world helpers since 0.10.1: Highlights make herbs, ore, and interactable objects easy to spot, and Quest mobs mark the enemies your active quests need.
Added
• Highlights (/quiet setup → Misc.) put a soft pulsing glow with small glints and rising motes on the object picked for the Interact key: herbs in muted green, ore in gold, and other interactable objects (chests, doors, mailboxes and similar gear-icon interactions) in warm white. Each category has its own check, and all are off by default.
• Quest mobs (/quiet setup → Misc.) place a small icon left of the health bar on the nameplate of an attackable mob tied to an active quest: an exclamation mark for a mob to kill, or a leather pouch when it only drops quest items. On by default.
• Both settings are shared through presets, and Reset default restores them.
Changed
• While Highlights are active, QuietUI turns on soft targeting for the Interact key so the glow can follow the object. Nearby NPCs then show their names (drawn by the client). The original soft-target settings are saved and written back when Highlights turn off, QuietUI turns off, or an instance begins.
Fixed
• Highlights keep working in combat and across target and nameplate changes, restore the original soft-target settings even after a failed write, and leave the soft-target icon as it was for categories you did not check.
• Quest mob icons size to the health bar, stay off the bar itself, and fall back to the exclamation mark when quest data from the tooltip cannot be read.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.11.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. Restart the game or type /reload. Keep your existing SavedVariables.
2. Quest mobs are on by default; Highlights are off until you check Herbs, Ore, or Interact objects under /quiet setup → Misc. Highlights are suppressed in instances.
3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.10.1...0.11.0

0.10.1
Performance and reliability patch since 0.10.0: fewer idle scans on the HUD and in chat, plus fixes for stale state after disabling and re-enabling QuietUI.
Changed
• Reduced per-frame and idle work across the HUD. Visibility settings migrate once instead of on every read, event-driven rescans are coalesced into one per frame, and party frames are rescanned only when the roster or frame layout changes.
• Range gradient, micro menu buttons, quest notice layout, the quest tracker hover catcher, and action bar hosting are now cached and refreshed only when relevant events fire.
• Chat skips re-walking message text when the frame structure has not changed, and restyles only the chat window that actually changed.
• The swing timer lookup no longer scans every UI frame each second when no swing timer exists.
Fixed
• Re-enabling QuietUI now rescans frames that changed while it was off, and disabling clears cached range and party state.
• Quest notices restyle correctly when the quest tracker font size changes in place.
• Re-enabling Modern chat hides the native chat text again, and chat restyling no longer touches windows outside the regular chat frames.
• Only the leading channel tag is shortened; tags that appear inside message text are left unchanged.
• Textures with an unreadable (secret) alpha are hidden safely without comparing the value.
Upgrade notes
1. Extract QuietUI-0.10.1.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the existing QuietUI folder's addon files. Restart the game or type /reload. Keep your existing SavedVariables.
2. No settings changed; existing setup and presets carry over as they are.
3. This release targets the WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/rdurica/quiet-ui/compare/0.10.0...0.10.1

addons.changelog:
Changelog
All notable changes to Craft Compass. The text of this file goes into each release's notes.
0.5.0 — 2026-11-03
• A click on a quest (or Alt over it, or a right click) opens its window: level and zone, whether it's done or in your
log, what it says to do, who gives it and who takes it back, the items to bring with how many you have, the quests
before and after it in the chain (they open too) and its Wowhead page. Shift-click still links it in chat.
• With Questie itself loaded, hovering a quest shows Questie's tooltip of it, and the quest's window has an "Open in
Questie" row for Questie's own window of the quest.
• The Wowhead address dialog keeps its size: it used to grow wider each time it was opened, until it ran off the
screen, and a long address stuck out of its box.
0.4.0 — 2026-11-03
• Drag a nested window away and it stays on its own: closing the window it came from no longer closes it, and that
window opens its rows in a new nested one.
• No more "Drops from", "Found in" and "Contained in" lines. Outside quest items, the data behind them comes from
private-server databases and was too often wrong (rogue quest mobs "dropping" herbs). Where to get an item now
shows the gathering profession and zones, vendors and quest rewards.
• No more "Not used in any recipe or quest" line and its setting: the sources don't know every use, so it was a
guess.
• Instead of drops, the last row of a pinned window is the item's Wowhead page: click it and press Ctrl+C to copy
the address, on the site of your game version and in your client's language. The dialog closes by itself.
• Enchants open in pinned windows too: Alt over an enchant row (or Alt-click, or a right click) shows what it does,
what it takes, where its formula comes from and its Wowhead page. Hovering an enchant row shows its tooltip.
• Herbs and ores show every zone they grow in. Questie clears the spawn points of the most common herbs and veins
(Peacebloom, Briarthorn, copper, tin, iron...), so only a zone or two used to show.
• The list of zones no longer shows how many spawn points each has: the numbers come from private-server data and
don't match the live realms. The richest zones still come first.
0.3.0 — 2026-11-01
• Where an item comes from, with Shift, in pinned windows and in the item window: herbs, ore, stone, leather and
hides show the gathering profession and the skill they need, and herbs and ore the zones they grow in. Any item
shows who sells it, which creatures drop it, what it is found or contained in and which quest rewards it.
• In a pinned window every source line opens the whole list in a nested window: all vendors (the other
faction's greyed out), all creatures with their level and zones, all objects, containers and quests, and every
zone with how many spawn points it has.
• Long source lines wrap in pinned windows instead of making them wider and wider.
• NPCs and objects show every zone they appear in, so the Darkmoon Faire's vendors show both of theirs.
• Long drop lists no longer slow tooltips down: only the names shown are looked up.
• The source lines of a recipe are no longer indented, which pushed them to the right.
0.2.0 — 2026-10-31
• Alt-click on an item link in chat (or anywhere else a link opens the item window) pins it into a window.
Alt-click on a row of a pinned window opens it nested, like a right click.
• A pinned window of a crafted item starts with what its craft takes, and the reagents are rows like the rest:
hover one for its tooltip, Alt or right click it for its own window — where it comes from and how it is made.
The item window a link opens says so.
• The close button of a pinned window works in combat too.
0.1.0 — 2026-10-29
First version.
• Shift (or Ctrl) over an item: the recipes it goes into, by profession and skill with how many each takes, and the
quests that ask for it, filtered to the character's race and class, completed ones marked.…
addons.description:
**What is this item for, and what does it take to make that? A tooltip and pinned windows for World of Warcraft
Classic.**

English · Русский · Architecture

Hover a herb, an ore or a piece of cloth and see every recipe and quest that uses it. Pin that list into a window,
follow a potion into what it is used for, and see for any craftable item which profession makes it, which
reagents it needs and how many of them you already carry, and where its recipe comes from — so you know what to
gather before you ask a crafter.

*Someone offers to craft a piece of armour: Alt-click its link in chat, see the reagents, and hover the one you don't
know where to get. Screenshots are from a Russian client.*
What does it do?What an item is used for
Hold Shift (or Ctrl) over an item: the recipes it goes into, by profession and skill with how many of it each
takes, and the quests that ask for it, the completed ones marked.
Pinned windows
Hold Alt over an item to pin that list into a window that stays on screen. Hover a row for its tooltip, click it
for the item window, Shift-click to link it in chat. Long lists scroll; Escape closes them all.

Alt over a row (or Alt-click, or a right click) opens a nested window beside it, as deep as you like: from a herb to
the elixir made of it to the belt made of that. An enchant opens the same way: what it does, what it takes and where
its formula comes from. A nested window closes with the one it came from, unless you drag it away: then it stays on
its own.
Items from chat
Alt-click an item link in chat to pin it instead of opening the item window. A plain click opens the item window
as usual, with what the craft takes added and a reminder that Alt-click lets you open the reagents.

| Alt-click a link | A plain click |
| --- | --- |
| | |
What a craft takes
Pin a crafted item, hover it in a pinned window, click it, or hold Shift over it anywhere: the profession and skill
that make it, every reagent with how many you have (bags and bank) against how many it needs, and its recipe:
taught by the trainer, or the recipe item with who sells it and which quest rewards it. In a pinned window the
reagents open in nested windows like any other row, so you can follow an oil or a thread back to where it comes from.
Where to get it
The same places show where an item comes from. A herb, an ore or a stone shows the profession that gathers it with
the skill it needs and the zones where it grows most; leather and hides show the skinning skill they start at. Then
who sells the item and which quest rewards it. In a pinned window each of these lines is clickable and opens the
whole list: every vendor with their level and zone, every zone, the richest first.

Craft Compass is a compass: it points you the right way, it isn't a database. It doesn't say which creatures drop an
item or which chests it is found in: the data addons have on that comes from private-server databases and is too
often wrong. For that, the last row of a pinned window is the item's (or the enchant's) Wowhead page: click it and
press Ctrl+C: the address is copied and the dialog closes (addons can't open a browser or copy by themselves). The page
is in your client's language where Wowhead has it (German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Korean,
Simplified Chinese), in English otherwise, and on Wowhead's Classic or TBC site to match your game.
And also
• Quest windows. Click a quest in a pinned window (or Alt over it) for its own window: level, zone and whether
it's done, what it says to do, who gives it and who takes it back, the items to bring, the quests before and after
it, and its Wowhead page. With Questie itself loaded, hovering a quest shows Questie's tooltip, and an "Open in
Questie" row opens Questie's window of it.
• Quests in chat. Shift-click a quest in a pinned window to link it in chat, in the [Name (id)] form Questie
turns into a clickable quest link.…

RGX-Framework v2.11.0
Package: RGX-Framework-v2.11.0.zip, 106 runtime files, plus release.json.
• New RGXTriggers module: a trigger state store for the trigger evaluation
engine (rgx-mod substrate). Trigger authors mutate clone-keyed state and the
engine diffs every field write — state.changed only flips when a value
actually changed or the clone is new, so consumers react to real changes
and identical writes cost nothing.
• Stale clones cannot survive: Sweep(keepIds) removes every clone the author
did not keep alive in one coalesced notification; Remove and Clear
cover the single-clone and all-clone cases.
• Guaranteed progress shapes: UpdateProgress applies the timed form
(duration/expirationTime/autoHide) or the static form
(value/total/inverse) with progressType on every state, and
switching forms clears the other form's fields in the same diff, giving
conditions and displays one stable shape to read.
• Change notifications (Triggers:OnChanged(id, fn)) are failure-isolated:
one handler error cannot break dispatch or other handlers.
• Design provenance: AddonLearner curated pass 5 (weakauras @ 37c3950c) —
the clone-keyed, engine-diffed state contract.
• Current public APIs and client Interfaces are unchanged. No SavedVariables
change is required.

Update RGX-Framework, then fully restart WoW.
addons.description:
The v2.11.0 release adds RGXTriggers, the clone-keyed trigger state
store behind the upcoming trigger evaluation engine. See the release notes.

One dependency. Everything your addon suite needs.

RGX-Framework is a modern, self-contained WoW addon framework for Retail,
WoW Forever (beta), Classic Era, TBC, Wrath/Titan, Cataclysm, and Mists. One shared dependency
provides events, timers, hooks, slash commands, minimap buttons, options panels,
database profiles, DataBroker, media, dropdowns, UI controls, and a visual design
system. It is not a player-facing addon; it loads silently and exposes an API.

Quick Start
Latest published release: v2.11.0

1. Declare the dependency:

2. Declare your addon — one call:

That is a complete addon: profile-aware saved settings, a tabbed options
panel with db-bound controls, a slash command, a minimap button, branded chat
output, and lifecycle work routed through scoped framework methods. The addon
object carries RegisterEvent, RegisterUnitEvent, RegisterMessage, After,
Every, Print, Warn, and Error, so consumers do not need raw WoW plumbing.

> Human on triggers remain frozen future contract forms. One-line controls
> ship in v2.7.15-beta.2; named every timers are implemented. Local
> options.columns work adds column flows, not the full declarative card/page model.
> Use scoped methods for events and other behavior that is not yet
> declarative.

3. À la carte — individual systems when you need them:

For module-dependent code, wrap in OnReady:

Core-only APIs (events, timers, hooks, slash commands) are available immediately — no OnReady needed.

What It Provides
| Category | Details |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | OnReady, OnLogin, module readiness tracking |
| Events & Messages | Blizzard event registration + internal message bus + module-local emitters |
| Timers | After, Every, CancelTimer — native OnUpdate driver, no C_Timer |
| Hooks | Post-hooks via hooksecurefunc — safe for Blizzard UI functions |
| Slash Commands | RegisterSlashCommand — no raw SLASH_X boilerplate |
| Combat Queue | QueueForCombat, SafeShow, SafeHide, SafeSetPoint, and more |
| Fonts | 40 bundled + 4 WoW defaults (44 total), 10 blocked in unavailableFonts, grouped dropdowns, style objects |
| Colors | Named palette, class/quality/power colors, color math, wrapping, picker integration |
| Textures | Statusbar registry, LibSharedMedia import, dropdown controls |
| Dropdowns | Nested UIDropDownMenu with auto-width, inline buttons, dual-schema items |
| UI Controls | Slider, toggle, label, dropdown, color picker, section, preview, reset button |
| Options Panels | Tabbed settings windows registered with WoW Settings |
| Minimap | Circular-drag buttons with persistent angle, tooltip, show/hide |
| Design | Static brand palette (primary, accent, border, etc.) + visual building blocks |
| DataBroker | LibDataBroker-compatible proxy data sources |
| Sound | Level-up sound system with variant playback and SavedVar integration |

| SharedMedia | RGXSharedMedia | GetSharedMedia() | Active |

| Combat | RGXCombat | GetCombat() | Active |

| Achievement | RGXAchievement | GetAchievement() | Active |
| LevelUp | RGXLevelUp | GetLevelUp() | Active |
