addons.changelog:
Changelog
All notable changes to this addon are documented in this file.
[0.1.3] - 2026-10-25Added
• 141 more recipes show where to get them.
Changed
• 65 recipes show updated information on where to get them.
• Recipe data from game build 1.60.1.70532. 43 recipes changed, and 5
that are no longer in the game are no longer listed as missing.
• Each guild keeps its own crafters. An alt outside your guild, or in
another guild, no longer sees your guildmates' recipes, and a character with
no guild sees only itself. Existing data moves to its guild the first time
one of your characters logs in there.
[0.1.2] - 2026-10-04Added
• The window tells you when you are out of date. When a guildmate runs a
newer Recipe Registry, a yellow "Update available" appears next to the Sync
light, and stays there until you update. Before, the only hint was one line
in chat that was easy to miss. Thanks to Juliette for the idea.
Changed
• Recipe data from the latest beta build (1.60.1.70205). Ten more recipes
now tell you where they drop, among them the Filigreed tailoring patterns
from Deadmines, Wailing Caverns and Blackfathom Deeps, Royal Tea, Bear
Brisket and Sterling Silver Boots. Fifteen camp crafts no longer show a
difficulty range, because this build no longer gives them one.
[0.1.1] - 2026-09-26Fixed
• The favourites star is back. It was looked up in the folder of the TBC
addon, which a Forever install does not have, so it showed nowhere.
Changed
• Sorting by skill level goes both ways. The sort button now cycles through
alphabetical, rarity, skill from lowest and skill from highest -- the last one
being what you want when you are looking for something worth crafting now.
Recipes with no known level stay at the bottom either way.
• Your character is read the way the game names it. First name and surname
now come from the game's own name API instead of being pieced together, so a
client update that changes how names are reported can no longer split you
into two crafters.
• Settings stay with your character. The bundled AceDB library is updated to
its WoW: Forever release, which files your settings under your full name
rather than under the ruleset.
[0.1.0] - 2026-09-25
The first release of Recipe Registry for WoW: Forever.
Added
• A recipe directory for the whole guild. Search any recipe and see which of
your guildmates can make it, without asking in chat. Everyone running the
addon shares what their characters know, so the directory fills itself in and
keeps up as people learn things.
• Your professions are read and shared on their own. Open a profession once
and it is recorded. You never have to press a button to publish anything.
• A recipe you learn appears by itself. Learn a pattern in a dungeon and it
is in the directory within seconds, wherever you are -- there is no need to go
back to town and open the profession window for it to count.
• All twelve professions, gathering ones included. Alchemy, Blacksmithing,
Cooking, Enchanting, Engineering, First Aid, Fishing, Herbalism,
Leatherworking, Mining, Skinning and Tailoring. Fishing, Herbalism and
Skinning have recipes of their own on this game, so they get a tab like
everything else instead of being treated as professions with nothing in them.
• A recipe database for this game's content. 2519 recipes with their
materials, what they produce, the skill level they are learned at and the
point where they stop giving skill-ups. It is built from the game itself, so
recipes added by a patch are in it rather than missing until someone updates
the addon.
• A Collection tab: your own professions' book. Every recipe your
professions can learn, with the ones you already know ticked off and the rest
showing the skill they ask for against the skill you have. Each profession is
a section you can fold away, headed with how far along you are.
• Where to learn it. The Collection tells you who teaches or sells each
recipe, or where it drops -- with the zone, the map coordinates in a column of…
addons.description:
Your guild already knows how to make it. Recipe Registry tells you who.

Stop asking "can anyone craft this?" in guild chat and waiting. Recipe Registry
builds a searchable directory of every recipe your guildmates know, keeps it up
to date by itself, and tells you who to whisper — who is online right now, and
who can help when they log back in.

Available for WoW: The Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary and **WoW:
Forever**.
At a glance
• Find a crafter in seconds — search a recipe, or a material you are
holding, and see who in the guild can make it, online ones first.
• Zero upkeep — open your professions once; the directory fills and syncs
itself between everyone running the addon.
• Your whole book in one table — every recipe your professions can learn,
what you already know, and where to go for the rest.
• Tooltips that answer the question — hover almost any craftable item and
see who can make it.
• Know the margin — material cost, sale price and profit, with
TradeSkillMaster or Auctionator.

Search it like you think about it
Type the name of what you want. Or type a material you are sitting on and see
what it turns into. Filter to one profession, sort by rarity — or, on Forever,
by the skill level a recipe is learned at — star the crafts you ask about most
and keep them on top. Categories and subcategories drill
down through big professions without scrolling through hundreds of rows.
Know who to ask, and when
Every recipe lists the guildmates who know it, online ones first. One button
whispers them. Another links the recipe to guild, party, raid or say — and hover
almost any craftable item in the game and the tooltip quietly tells you who can
make it, without opening anything.
See the whole book, not just what you know
The Collection tab is your own professions laid out end to end: every recipe
they can learn, the ones you already know ticked off, and the rest showing the
skill they ask against the skill you have. Each profession is headed with how
far along you are — "Blacksmithing (185/385)" — so you can see the holes at a
glance, and narrow the list to what you could go and learn today.

For the ones you are missing it tells you where to go: the trainer, the vendor,
the drop or the quest, the zone, and on Forever the map coordinates too.
Know what a craft is worth before you make it
With TradeSkillMaster or Auctionator installed, the details panel adds what the
materials cost, what the result sells for, and what is left over. Vendor prices
are learned from merchants you visit, so vials, thread and spices are priced at
what you actually pay instead of whatever the auction house is asking. One
switch hides everything that comes out at a loss.
It keeps itself current
Open a profession once and it is recorded. From then on the addon shares with
guildmates running it and takes their data in return, quietly, pacing itself so
the game stays smooth and holding off during combat and instances. Learn a new
recipe and it is in the directory within seconds — on Forever, without even
opening the profession window.

A Guild members tab shows who else is running the addon and on which version, so
you can tell someone out of date from someone who simply has not installed it.

Getting started
1. Install it, and open each of your profession windows once.
2. Open the window from the minimap button or with /rr.
3. Ask a couple of guildmates to install it too — that is when it gets good.

The first sync takes a moment in a large guild. After that you can forget it is
there.
Commands
Most people only ever need /rr. The rest is there when you want it:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /rr | Opens the main window |
| /rr options | Settings |
| /rr rescan | Queues a fresh profession scan |
| /rr share guild | Shares the selected recipe (also party, raid, say, reply) |
| /rr prices | Checks market data for an item |
| /rr adoption | Prints who in the guild is running the addon |
Which game you are on…

addons.changelog:
Fixed
• Show lockout debuffs on WoW Forever now times Forbearance at 1 minute
instead of 30 seconds. It also follows every rank of Blessing of Protection
and Divine Shield, plus Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark, and no
longer starts from Lay on Hands. Sacred Duty's reduction isn't read, so the
icon can stay up to 10 seconds longer than the debuff.
addons.description:
Decursive-style dispelling, one click per party member.

One click to cleanse them all, and in the options bind them.

Questions, bugs or ideas? Come say hi on the Consecrated Hammer Discord. Bug reports go in #bug-reports, or you can open a GitHub issue.

Salve gives you one box per group member. When someone picks up a debuff you can remove, their box lights up with that debuff type's colour and icon, and you click it to cleanse them. As a long-time Decursive user, I wanted to keep that simple rhythm: see the colour, click the box, cleanse the party.
What it does
• One box per group member, in a small grid you can size and place anywhere.
• It lights up straight away. A box shows the dispel type's colour and icon (Magic, Curse, Poison or Disease) the moment that member catches something you can remove, and dims when they're clean. Stack counts are drawn by the game itself.
• One click to cleanse. Left click uses your primary dispel. If your spec has a second dispel covering other schools, it goes on right click automatically. Every detected action can be rebound.
• Every dispelling class: Paladin, Priest, Druid, Shaman, Monk, Evoker, Mage and Warlock. Your spells are picked up automatically when you change spec or, for Warlocks, when your demon changes.
• Movement removal for you. Enable a spell like Blessing of Freedom on the Actions page and your own box lights orange when Blizzard reports a root or snare on you, with optional on-screen or chat text. These movement alerts are in beta and live on the Movement (beta) page.
• Optional sound alerts for known dispellable debuffs in the current dungeon or raid.
Getting started
Install, then type /salve for settings.

The panel starts in the centre of your screen with a small gold grip above it. Drag the grip to move it (the boxes themselves are buttons, so the panel can't be dragged directly). Use /salve lock or right-click the minimap button to hide the grip once you're happy with it.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /salve | Open settings |
| /salve toggle | Show or hide the panel |
| /salve lock / unlock | Hide or show the drag grip |
| /salve reset position | Put the panel back in the centre |
| /salve forever | Copy a WoW Forever cure and spellbook report, handy for bug reports |
| /salve whatsnew | Show what's new in recent releases |
| /salve cooldowns | Show how the cooldown icons read each spell; works in combat |
| /salve snares | List the root and snare spell IDs Salve has captured |
| /salve learned / learned clear | Show or clear the learned spell catalogue |

Every Consecrated Hammer addon also has help, version, about, debug, startup, minimap, reset settings and quiz.
Detected actions
The Actions page only lists spells your character knows. Movement actions stay off until you turn them on and bind them. "Area movement" is a ground-placed spell, so drop it where the affected players can reach it.

| Class | Dispels | Frees movement (ally) | Area movement | Self only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paladin | Cleanse: Magic, Poison, Disease; Cleanse Toxins: Poison, Disease | Blessing of Freedom; Blessing of Protection | None | Divine Shield |
| Priest | Purify: Magic, plus Disease with Improved Purify; Purify Disease: Disease | None | None | None |
| Druid | Nature's Cure: Magic, plus Poison/Curse with Improved Nature's Cure; Remove Corruption: Poison, Curse | None | None | Travel Form; Cat Form |
| Shaman | Purify Spirit: Magic, plus Curse with Improved Purify Spirit; Cleanse Spirit: Curse | None | Wind Rush Totem (Jet Stream only) | Spirit Walk; Ghost Wolf |
| Monk | Detox (Mistweaver): Magic, plus Poison/Disease with Improved Detox; Detox: Poison, Disease | Tiger's Lust | None | None |
| Evoker | Naturalize: Magic, Poison; Expunge: Poison; Cauterizing Flame: Poison, Curse, Disease | None | None | Hover |
| Mage | Remove Curse: Curse | None | None | Blink; Shimmer; Ice Block; barriers with Energized Barriers (snares only) |…
addons.name: Salve (WoW Forever)

releases.changelog:
Fixed
• Show lockout debuffs on WoW Forever now times Forbearance at 1 minute
instead of 30 seconds. It also follows every rank of Blessing of Protection
and Divine Shield, plus Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark, and no
longer starts from Lay on Hands. Sacred Duty's reduction isn't read, so the
icon can stay up to 10 seconds longer than the debuff.

Added
• A Cooldowns settings page. The cooldown bar and lockouts are off by
default.
• Sweep style on the cells: Auto (the default), Whole cell or
Icon. Icon shows each spell's icon on the cell only while it's on
cooldown, with its sweep and countdown, so names stay readable. Movement
sweeps such as Freedom get their own icon beside it. Auto uses Icon when
names are on and the whole-cell sweep when they're off, so cells without
names look as before. Icon size and Icon position set where they
sit.
• A cooldown bar beside the grid for the spells bound on Actions, such as
Cleanse, Freedom and Blessing of Protection. Each spell shows only while
it's on cooldown, or dimmed when ready with Show when ready. Pick its
side, gap, icon size and spacing, run it horizontally (the default) or
vertically, and switch individual spells off. Match Salve panel, on by
default, uses the cell height, cell spacing and box borders so icons line up
with the cells.
It moves with Salve, including when attached.
• Show lockout debuffs shows Forbearance, with its timer, after you cast
Blessing of Protection, Blessing of Spellwarding or Lay on Hands on someone,
or Divine Shield on yourself. Show on puts it on the cooldown bar with
the member's name (the default, and the bar appears for it even with the
spells off), on their cell, or both. It only shows while it lasts. It
follows your own casts, from a Salve cell or anywhere else, so another
paladin's Forbearance isn't shown. Off by default.
• /salve cooldowns shows how the cooldown icons read each spell. It works
in combat, which is where it matters.
• A What's new window after updates, listing new features with one button
per settings page. News from your other Consecrated Hammer addons shares the
same window. It never opens on a fresh install or in combat.
Turn it off with Show what's new after updates on Visibility, and reopen
it with /salve whatsnew or the About page.
Changed
• Updated the bundled HammerCore library, which adds the What's new window,
quiz questions grouped by category and a minimap click fix.

Added
• A Sorting settings page. Sort by keeps the game's group order
(the default), or sorts by role or by name. Role order picks any order of
tank, healer and DPS, with members who have no role last. Your cell pins
your own box first or last, and Reverse order flips the rest. The preview
follows the same settings.
• Boxes re-sort when roles change, while in Role mode.
• An Attach settings page. Attach to DandersFrames or EllesmereUI group
frames, whichever are loaded. Left and Right line each cell up with
its member's frame at the host's spacing, in the host's order, with raid
groups kept in their own columns or rows. Top and Bottom keep Salve's
grid together above or below the host. Gap sets the distance, and for
Left and Right, Align (top, centre or bottom of each frame) and
Up / down fine-tune where the cells sit. Salve moves when the host's
frames move, and uses its saved position whenever the host's frames aren't
on screen.
Fixed
• When someone joins or leaves mid-fight, box names now update straight away.
The boxes themselves still wait until combat ends to rebuild.

Added
• A Movement (beta) settings page for root, snare and slow alerts. The
movement sound, movement text, destination and preview controls moved there
from Alerts, with a link to Actions for binding movement spells.
• Enable movement alerts (beta) turns off all automatic movement text,
sounds and the orange player-cell cue. Movement-spell bindings and dispel
alerts keep working. It stays on by default, so existing behaviour doesn't
change until you switch it off.
• Include inferred slows (beta), off by default. When on, a sharp drop in
your run speed shows movement text and lights your box orange, pointing at
your existing movement-spell mouse binding. Inferred slows stay silent.
Enabling either beta option prints a warning that it may not work correctly.
• Dispel sound coverage for Living Bomb in Ruby Life Pools and Venomfang,
Icebound Flames, Essence Rend, Tempest and Congealing Bolt in The Venomous
Abyss.
• Coverage for both Curse of Darkness effects in Windrunner Spire and Energy
Bomb in Algeth'ar Academy.
• Instance-scoped sound data for Devouring Essence and Curse of Hesitation in
Torment's Rise, and Void Toxin in Venomfall Deeps.

These 12 entries use reviewed current boss-addon dispel metadata. Sounds still
require the matching cure school and the relevant instance, with dispel sound
alerts enabled. Actual playback of the added entries remains to be checked in
game.
Changed
• Inferred speed drops no longer show movement text unless **Include inferred
slows (beta)** is on. Reported roots and snares are unaffected.

Added
• Separate Alerts options for learning scope-change and newly learned-spell chat
messages, including captured roots and snares. Muting messages keeps learning
active. Existing message behaviour is retained until the options are changed.
• Orc Shatter Curse as an optional personal dispel on WoW Forever build 70425
or later. Bind it on Actions to arm only your own cell, leaving ordinary
class dispels unchanged. A small R cue uses the native Curse filter and
disappears while its cooldown is active or unreadable. It adds no sound
alerts. Actual Forever cue behaviour and Bane classification still need a
client check.

addons.description:
Cooldown Manager Utils adds missing-buff and reactive-proc reminders to World of Warcraft's built-in Cooldown Manager.
Features
• Adds a Buff Reminders tab to the side tabs of Blizzard's Cooldown Manager settings.
• Adds a separate Proc Reminders tab. On Retail it lists the Essential and Utility spells of the Cooldown Manager; on WoW Forever Warriors, Rogues, and Hunters it lists their reactive abilities (Overpower, Revenge, Riposte, Mongoose Bite, Counterattack). Selected abilities appear on the Proc Reminder bar only while Blizzard marks their reactive combat window active.
• Lists active spells from all class spellbook tabs (on Retail: class and current specialization) that apply a buff to your character, independently of Blizzard's Auras tab.
• Includes the gathering tracking abilities Find Herbs, Find Minerals, and Find Fish when they are available to your character. Their reminders disappear while the matching minimap tracking is active.
• Also covers temporary weapon enchants cast by you, such as the Shaman weapon imbues (Rockbiter, Flametongue, Frostbrand, Windfury, Earthliving) and the Paladin rites. Tracked weapon enchants are checked together against every equipped weapon (main hand and, when dual wielding, off hand; shields only if a shield imbue is tracked): they stay hidden while every weapon carries one of them, otherwise the tracked enchants that are not active on any weapon are shown (or all of them, if each one is already active on another weapon).
• Add Buff at the top of the Buff Reminders tab opens a search window: find a spell of your class by name or spell ID and click it to add it as a Buff Reminder. Spells added this way are marked with a warning triangle, may not work correctly, and can be removed with a right-click. Contact D4KiR on Discord to get a missing buff or proc added properly; the link is shown below the contact note and can be copied there.
• Sorts available entries into Tracked Buffs/Abilities, Not Displayed, and Not Learned. Learned entries can be moved by drag and drop; unlearned or currently unselected talent spells are shown disabled but retain their spell tooltip.
• The Buff Reminder bar shows an icon for every tracked buff that is currently missing on your character. The bar is hidden while nothing is missing.
• The separate Expiring Buffs bar shows selected buffs when they are missing or approaching expiration. Seconds before expiry controls the warning window (1–60 seconds) and is available in both the add-on options and the bar's Edit Mode settings. Both controls use the same value.
• Group buffs (Blizzard's Group Buffs list, plus Mark of the Wild, Blessing of the Bronze, Arcane Intellect, Power Word: Fortitude, Skyfury, and Battle Shout) are also checked on every eligible party or raid member. Their reminder appears as soon as one living, connected, visible member in range is missing the buff, and the icon shows how many eligible members have it, for example 2/5 or 3/40. Offline, dead, invisible, and out-of-range members are excluded from both numbers. Disable Check buffs on the group in a bar's Edit Mode settings to check only your own buffs instead. Group checking is enabled by default.
• Paladin Blessing reminders work as one group: every eligible party or raid member needs any recognized Blessing cast by you. If one member is missing your Blessing, all selected Blessing reminders are shown; Blessings from another Paladin do not count. Blessing of Freedom and Blessing of Protection are separate personal reminders that only check your own character.
• On WoW Forever, Paladin Seal reminders also work as one group. Any active recognized Seal hides all selected Seal reminders; when no Seal is active, they are all shown.…

addons.description:
ExpansionUtils by D4KiR combines a character overview with shortcuts and small improvements for World of Warcraft expansion features. Track your alts, weekly progress, professions, money, and played time in one place.
Character overview
The overview stores data from characters you log into with the addon enabled. It includes the following columns where the corresponding game systems are available:
• Character: class-colored name, level, specialization, and equipped item level.
• Mythic+: rating, best runs for the current season's dungeons, and current keystone.
• Raids: weekly progress and expansion-wide boss progress, separated by supported difficulty.
• Professions: both primary professions, skill levels, and unspent knowledge points where supported.
• Great Vault: raid, dungeon, and world activity progress. Unclaimed rewards appear as a green "Rewards waiting" message across the visible vault columns.
• Played time: total time played and time played at the current level.
• Money: gold, silver, and copper for each character.

Click column headers to sort the list and hover over cells for additional details. The footer shows total money and played time for the stored characters, including recorded Warband bank money where supported.

Customize the overview through its footer and settings:
• Filter the list to max-level characters.
• Adjust the font size from 8 to 18.
• Show, hide, and reorder column groups and their subcolumns.
• Resize the window and open settings with the footer's gear button.

Alt data reflects the last time each character was updated; log into an alt to refresh it. Missing values appear as ?, and weekly data is marked as outdated after a reset. Account totals use the characters already recorded by the addon.
Great Vault
On Retail, the Great Vault minimap button provides quick access to the overview and the vault. Its tooltip shows activity progress, example reward item levels when available, and whether rewards are waiting.

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Toggle the character overview |
| Right-click | Toggle the Great Vault outside combat |

The button can be shown or hidden in settings and is omitted where the Great Vault system is unavailable.
Valeera XP bar
On Retail, a movable XP bar tracks Valeera's Delve companion level and progress toward her next level. It appears while she is an active companion and has XP left to earn.

The bar and its tooltip show current XP, remaining XP, XP gained during the current Delve, and saved XP highscores by Delve and tier. Drag the unlocked bar outside combat to move it; its position is saved account-wide.

Other conveniences
• Reshii Wraps: on Retail, a shortcut beside the back slot in the character window opens the upgrade interface while Reshii Wraps are equipped.
• Mythic+ preparation: the keystone window gains a ready-check button with group readiness feedback and countdown buttons for 10, 5, and 3 seconds. Countdowns use DBM, BigWigs, or the built-in party countdown when available.
• Non-interruptible casts: on non-Retail clients, target and focus cast bars gain a shield indicator and gray coloring for non-interruptible casts, including support for DragonflightUI cast bars.
Settings and access
On Retail, use the main ExpansionUtils minimap button:

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Toggle settings |
| Shift + left-click | Toggle the character overview |
| Right-click | Hide the main minimap button |

Open settings with either command:

Use the language selector in the top-left corner of settings to choose between the eleven supported languages. The selection is saved account-wide and updates addon labels immediately; game-provided names follow the client language.…

Changelog4.1.2 (2026-10-31)
Voices similar to the in-game characters. Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment.

Version 4.1.2 covers the base add-ons, every retail sound pack and every WoW Forever pack.
What's new
• About 1,300 more lines re-recorded after player and owner reports, mostly Kul Tiran, Tauren, Goblin and Dracthyr characters.
• 51 characters who had lines waiting without a voice now speak, including Breem, Ba'kel, Katy Stampwhistle, One-Eyed Thak and the Mnemis keepers in Bastion.
• Nine characters the game shows as either a man or a woman now have a voice for each, and you hear the one that matches the character in front of you (for example Alliance Worker, Dark Iron Grenadier, Forsaken Dreadmage, Zandalari Vagrant and Tortollan Seeker).
• Colonel Troteman (Redridge Mountains) has a new voice that fits him.
• Goblin voices were shared out more evenly, so fewer goblins sound alike.
• Quest titles, character names, books and greetings in the Audio Library updated to match the new lines.
Thank you
Thank you to everyone who sent in quest text, flagged a line or reported a problem. Want to help? Send in quest text, report a line or flag a voice at https://speakstone.beanw.co.uk.
4.1.0 (October 2026)

Version 4.1.0 covers the base add-ons, every retail sound pack and every WoW Forever pack. All of them are now on 4.1.0.
Thank you to everyone who helped
A huge thank you to everyone who sent in quest text and game data through the website, flagged lines that sounded wrong, and reported problems on GitHub. This release exists because of you.
• Cliff, Fiz, Nerf, Klebster, Zen, AuthenticSenpai, silvy, Pappnase, illset, Benny McBackstab, Vanadan
• Everyone who contributed anonymously
• Everyone who reported a voice that did not fit its character

Fixes
• Narration now finishes after you close the quest or gossip window when "Stop narration when the window closes" is off. It plays at your Master volume, because the game cuts the Dialog volume channel when a window closes.
• The SpeakStone Guide names the character you hear giving each quest. Quests that start from a board, poster or note still show that.
• What's new lists these changes and the optional Dialogue UI follow-along.

Voices (arrive with the voice packs)
• Corrected pronunciation of Primalists, Nozdormu, Murozond, Khadgar, Kel'Thuzad and Runecarver.
• Jesper (Hallow's End) has a child's voice; new takes for Archmage Khadgar and Chromie.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment. The voices are similar to the in-game characters.

• Dialogue UI: quest text can follow the voice inside Dialogue UI's own window (optional).
• A redesigned SpeakStone Guide and settings window, with themes and font choices.
• The Guide shows each quest's zone and who gives it, and can group by NPC.

Voices (arrive with the voice packs)
• Corrected pronunciation of Primalists, Nozdormu, Murozond, Khadgar, Kel'Thuzad and Runecarver.
• Jesper (Hallow's End) now has a child's voice.
• New takes for Archmage Khadgar and Chromie.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment. The voices are similar to the in-game characters.

• Greetings for about 250 more lines are recognised, among them all nine of Orweyna's.
What's new
• A new What's new button in the settings window (beside Profiles, or /ss whatsnew) lists the changes in each release, newest first, with dates.
Fixes
• Fixed a rare error in the speech frame on WoW 12.x.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment.
3.2.3
Settings
• The settings window has tabs: Playback, Sound, Speech frame and Interface. The status cards stay on the left.
Playback
• New: Skip quests I've already heard. Autoplay leaves a quest passage alone once you have heard it, on any character. Read Quest still plays it, and /ss forget clears the list. Off by default.
• New: Stay quiet in combat, and in dungeons, raids and battlegrounds. Two separate options, both off by default. Read Quest and the keybind still work.
Sound
• New: Lower music and ambience while speaking, with a slider for how far. WoW cannot set a volume for one sound, so this turns the others down instead and puts them back when the line ends. Off by default.
Missing voices
• A small muted-speaker icon beside Read Quest shows when the quest text on screen has no voice yet. Hover it for how to send the text in. Can be turned off under Interface.
Audio Library
• New Favourites and Recent tabs. Click the star on any row, or on the speech frame while a line plays, to keep it in Favourites. Recent lists the last 50 things played.

Lodestarv2.8.0 (2026-11-03)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• chore(release): v2.8.0
• Merge pull request #64 from danielcosta42/feat/questiedb-110
feat(guias): biblioteca regerada do QuestieDB 1.0.10
• docs(guias): números da rodada e o que ficou aberto
• fix(guias): aceite de drop depois do último passo que mata quem dá o item
O portão hasitem era avaliado antes de o jogador matar os mobs: o guia passava reto e a cadeia
sumia, como as nove quests do Nibbled-On Book em Elwynn. O aceite agora vai para depois do último
passo que mata quem dá o item, sem passar do primeiro que depende da quest, e pede para usar o
item, sem coordenada: ele já está na bolsa.
Drop incerto passa a contar mob comum com muitos spawns (Lost Stalker), e The Damp Note, drop de
elite dentro de Blackfathom Deeps, fica só no guia da masmorra.
• fix(guias): passo que esperava drop raro ou conteúdo do Season of Discovery
O guia parava em dois lugares que os validadores aprovam. A caça de ladino do Season of Discovery
(Stepping Stones, Scramble), sem classe no banco, mandava todo mundo clicar num objeto que não dá
nada em Stonetalon, na Barrens e em Arathi: a faixa 76000-85999 sem classe sai do leveling. E a
quest que começa por item que cai de vários mobs esperava o drop, como Crystal in the Mountains,
de 287 mobs: agora só aparece para quem já tem o item, e a entrega para quem a pegou.
Starving Arcane volta a ser só de masmorra, e as cadeias de paladino e ladino do Season of
Discovery que terminam em objeto saem também dos guias de classe.
• feat(guias): biblioteca regerada do QuestieDB 1.0.10
Os 31 bloqueios de ordem que os guias tinham sob os dados novos somem, e os saltos caem de 237
para 233, com as oito cadeias chegando ao fim.
Dois dados novos quebrariam guias sem nenhum validador acusar. O minLevel 9999 é o sentinela de
nível que escala, e com os ranks novos a elite amiga de Zephras Isle virava elite acima do nível
máximo, tirando Desperate Times do leveling e, com ela, toda a saída da ilha. E os Library Books:
o banco lista o objeto como quem dá a quest, mas ela só abre no bibliotecário com o livro na
bolsa, então o accept nunca completava e Silverpine parava ali. Os livros ficam fora de todo
guia, junto com as duas quests de ladino do Season of Discovery sem classe no banco.
addons.description:
Free & open leveling guides for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Lodestar is an in-game, step-by-step guide engine — a community-built alternative to paid guide addons. It routes you (Alliance & Horde), automates the tedious quest clicks, and points an arrow at your next objective. No gating, no nag screens, no telemetry — 100% MIT-licensed.

Install it, log in, and Lodestar automatically loads the best guide for your level and zone. That's it.
Why this addon exists
Forever keeps its quest text, objectives and coordinates on the server — the client ships
bare quest IDs and nothing else. Lodestar's routes are generated from the open QuestieDB
(Forever flavor), which now carries Forever's own content — the new Skyborne starting zone,
Zephras Isle, included. For what no database has yet, the only way to get it is by being there,
so Lodestar collects it while you play and gives it back, open.

See docs/forever.md for the measurements and what is still open.

FeaturesGuidance
• Clean step window with your current objective, checkboxes, and a preview of what's next.
• On-screen waypoint arrow, a compass strip at the top of the screen, and the route drawn as
dots on the minimap and the world map — flights along their real track, boats and zeppelins
along their crossing.
• Travel planner — the fastest trip by travel time, leg by leg: walking, the flight paths you know
(and new ones you pick up on the way), boats, zeppelins, the Deeprun Tram, your hearthstone and
class teleports. It replans as you go, and the flight map highlights where to fly.
• Walks follow the terrain — the walking part of a route goes around mountains, cliffs and
lakes instead of a straight line (from the game client's own terrain; enclosed cities still
fall back to a straight line).
• Boat and zeppelin times — once Lodestar hears a zeppelin master or shipmaster announce an
arrival (or you ride one), it learns that transport's schedule: the route uses the real wait, the
arrow counts down ("leaves in 1m20s", "board now") and an alert sounds 30 s before it docks.
• Goes where you need — your guide step, your corpse while you're a ghost, a Shift+click on the
map or minimap, a typed coordinate, or the nearest class/profession trainer, repair, vendor, inn,
bank, auction house, flight master or stable (nearest by travel time, not straight line). All in the
Travel panel — the compass button in the guide header.
• Multiple guides open at once as tabs — switch, add, or close routes on the fly, with a clean empty state when none is loaded.
Automation (never get stuck)
• Auto-accept, auto-turn-in, and optional auto-reward (off by default; picks the best reward using a class-aware gear score).
• Auto-selects the right gossip/quest option and auto-shares quests with your party.
• Auto-skips a step whose NPC no longer offers its quest — imperfect data never stalls you.
Leveling companions
• XP/hour pace HUD with ETA-to-level and ahead/behind tracking.
• Gear Advisor — pings you when a bag item is an upgrade.
• Target markers on tooltips & nameplates; player coordinates on minimap and map.
• Death counter and a shareable end-of-run Report Card (with "ghost racing").
⭐ Quest collection — /ls scan
Part of Forever's new content is not in any public database yet, so Lodestar harvests it as you play: who gives
and who ends each quest, with NPC ID and coordinates, the objectives, and the waypoint the server
itself points at. It goes to LodestarDB.scan, and tools/ turns it into routes.

Nothing personal is collected. Nothing leaves your machine unless you turn on **Share quest
locations with the family** (off by default), which whispers only the where — quest ID, NPC ID, map
and coordinate — to guildmates running the companion, so the guides grow. Nothing about your character
goes in the message, and the addon on the other side drops who sent it. Off, sharing a harvest stays
what it always was: a file you hand over on purpose.
For contributors…

nada em Stonetalon, na Barrens e em Arathi: a faixa 76000-85999 sem classe sai do leveling. E a

addons.description:
Not everyone has a beastmode PC. ForeverSettings finds the graphics settings that fit yours.

The graphics menu is a wall of sliders with names like "Compute effects" and "SSAO". Most of us either crank everything up and stutter in the busy places, or drop it all to Low and lose a beautiful game.

ForeverSettings measures your PC, tells you in plain words what each setting costs in frames per second, and picks settings for the frame rate you want. It shows you what you're giving up, so it's your call.

An addon for WoW Forever.
Get it
• Wago: addons.wago.io/addons/foreversettings
• GitHub: the zip on the Releases page.
• Install by hand: unzip into the game's Interface/AddOns folder so you have one ForeverSettings folder (for Forever: World of Warcraft/forever/Interface/AddOns/ForeverSettings), then start the game or /reload. The details are in INSTALL.md.
Try it in four steps
1. Stand somewhere quiet and click the minimap button, then Find my best settings.
2. Pick the frame rate you're aiming for (your monitor's refresh rate is a good choice) and press Start. It takes roughly 5 to 10 minutes and runs on its own. Don't move or open windows while it runs.
3. See what each change does, then Save. Your own settings are put back after the test.
4. Later, in a busy place (a city, a raid): Find my crowded settings.

See the price of every level
My settings (minimap menu, or /fset settings) has a page list on the left. The settings pages list every setting with what each level costs in frames per second against the level you have, how much it matters to the picture, a total for your choices, and what everything at the highest would give. Save as Everyday and Save as Crowded, at the bottom of the page list, keep the settings you have in the game now.

The Home page switches profile and starts the tests. The Picture size page has a slider for picture sharpness, up to 200% for this session only, with a warning that high values can crash some graphics cards.

Profiles
| Profile | What it is |
|---|---|
| Original | Your own settings, hands off. The addon records them before it first changes anything. Choose it to put everything back. |
| Everyday | The settings you saved for normal play. |
| Crowded | The settings you saved for raids and busy cities. |
| Maximum | Everything at the highest level the addon has learned. It needs plenty of graphics memory. |

Switch from the minimap button, or type /fset profile everyday (also crowded, maximum, original).

Good to know
• Nothing is forced on a first install.
• It never changes a setting during combat or while a test is running.
• It doesn't collect or send anything.
• /fset reset puts back everything the addon changed. /fset settings opens My settings, /fset size 50 to /fset size 200 sets the picture sharpness for this session, and /fset minimap hides or shows the button.
• Built for and tried on WoW Forever. Retail is untested.
Problems and ideas
Open an issue with a screenshot and what you clicked. If a test stopped, the window says why; include that.
For developers
The addon is Lua 5.1. The tests run under Node with fengari against a simulated game (tests/harness.lua):

tests/run.js also holds the mutation table: each rule in the code has a deliberate breakage that a named test must catch. docs/specs/ holds the design specs. Releases are made by pushing a version tag; see RELEASING.md.

addons.changelog:
Changelog1
• This is a work in progress. In groups and busy fights, the addon can still mistake other players' hits for yours, so some of your numbers can be wrong or missing, mostly melee hits and misses. If you see it happen, a recording of that fight (/nsctr record) helps a lot.
• Type /nsctr record to record your combat events, then type it again to stop. Attach the recording to a bug report, so problems in groups, raids, and battlegrounds can be fixed.
• Your damage and your pet's damage now show above enemy nameplates, and so do misses and dodges. Your combat log filter needs to show them.
• Your numbers show the icon of the spell that made them when the addon is sure which spell it was. Your melee hits and misses show the Auto Attack icon, and your pet's show the pet Attack icon. Most procs such as poisons, and your pet's spells, have no icon. A wand's Shoot gets its icon from its second hit, once the addon learns your wand's school, and again from the second hit after you change wands. With "Display Icon Only" on, a hit with no known spell shows its number. To clear what the addon learned, type /nsctr forget or press "Forget learned spells" in the Icons options.
• Your and your pet's melee hits use the "Auto Attacks" animations. With "Use Damage Type Color" on, yours show in white and your pet's in orange, as in NameplateSCT, so they no longer look like physical abilities. Once in a while, when you and your pet swing close together, your pet's number can show your colour and icon, or the two numbers can swap them.
• To hide the numbers of some spells, list them in the Filters options, one name or spell ID on each line, and turn on "Enable". Turn on "Inverse Spell Filter" to show only those spells. A spell's name covers all of its ranks. You can also list melee for your and your pet's melee hits and misses, missed for every miss, or unknown for hits whose spell the addon isn't sure of (melee never counts as unknown). Each character keeps its own list.
• In the Filters options, you can also hide numbers on some kinds of enemies: Boss, Rare, Elite, Normal, or Minor (totems and critters). Turn on "Inverse NPC Filter" to show numbers only on the kinds you check. "Enable" turns on both filters, and a number shows only when both let it through. This filter never hides numbers on enemy players. Your NPC choices count for all your characters. Unlike NameplateSCT, there's no list of NPC IDs, since the game hides which NPC is which in instances.
• The game's own damage numbers over the unit you hit are hidden while the addon is on. Turn off "Hide Blizzard Target Text", or the addon, to get them back the way you had them.
• Your numbers no longer go missing when a mob hits a friendly player near you.
• Numbers finish their animation when an enemy's nameplate disappears, so you see your killing blow, even when the game reports it just after the nameplate goes.
• The bottom of the main options page credits NameplateSCT, which this addon is based on.
• If your enemy nameplates are off when you hit something, a chat message tells you which key turns them on, once each time you log in.
• If your combat log filter doesn't send your and your pet's damage and misses, each kind of line in its own colour, or mixes in other players' lines that look like yours, a window offers to fix it with one click and a reload. The fix gives each kind of line in your Combat Log tab its own colour (spells, ticks, melee, shots, misses, heals), so the addon can tell them apart, and it stops the filter showing what others do to you, since those lines would look like yours. Since every filter lacks these colours before the fix, the window shows once for everyone. Until then, the numbers that can show still do.
addons.description:
NameplateSCT's scrolling combat text, drawn above enemy nameplates, for WoW: Forever.

Forever closes the combat log to addons, so the original NameplateSCT can't tell which hits are yours. This version works it out from what the game still sends. Your damage, misses, and your pet's damage show above the enemy you hit, with the original's animations and options.
Work in progress
Solo, the addon tells your hits apart well. In groups and busy fights, it can still mistake other players' hits for yours, so some of your numbers can be wrong or missing. Melee hits and misses get mixed up the most.

I'm still working on this. If you see it happen, a recording of that fight (/nsctr record, see below) helps a lot.

Turn on "Inverse NPC Filter" to show numbers only on the kinds you check. "Enable" turns on both filters, and a number shows only when both let it through. This filter never hides numbers on enemy players. Your NPC choices count for all your characters. Unlike NameplateSCT, there's no list of NPC IDs, since the game hides which NPC is which in instances.
• The game's own damage numbers over the unit you hit are hidden while the addon is on. Turn off "Hide Blizzard Target Text", or the addon, to get them back the way you had them.
• Your numbers no longer go missing when a mob hits a friendly player near you.
• Numbers finish their animation when an enemy's nameplate disappears, so you see your killing blow, even when the game reports it just after the nameplate goes.
• The bottom of the main options page credits NameplateSCT, which this addon is based on.
• If your enemy nameplates are off when you hit something, a chat message tells you which key turns them on, once each time you log in.
• If your combat log filter doesn't send your and your pet's damage and misses, each kind of line in its own colour, or mixes in other players' lines that look like yours, a window offers to fix it with one click and a reload. The fix gives each kind of line in your Combat Log tab its own colour (spells, ticks, melee, shots, misses, heals), so the addon can tell them apart, and it stops the filter showing what others do to you, since those lines would look like yours. Since every filter lacks these colours before the fix, the window shows once for everyone. Until then, the numbers that can show still do.

Interface and quality-of-life for WoW Forever (client 1.60, engine 12.x, Interface 16001).
Modules you can enable one by one, no library to install (LibStub and LibDeflate are bundled).
The CurseForge app also installs ForeverMeter, the damage meter, as a required dependency.
Built for this client, within the limits of its engine.

Unofficial addon, not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment. World of Warcraft and WoW Forever are trademarks of Blizzard Entertainment.
Modules
| Module | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Top bar | Friends and guild online (lists, AFK/DND), 12/24h clock + date + "zzz" while resting, gold, durability, bags, colored FPS/latency + addon memory (Shift-click: free), Travel menu (mage teleports and portals, Moonglade, Astral Recall), hearthstone. Can hide in combat (FPS/latency can stay visible). Position: top, bottom or free (fitted width, movable via /musca unlock). Moves the minimap down so it isn't covered (clients without Edit Mode; on Forever, place it via Edit Mode). Two free slots (left, right) for any info text. | on |
| Bags | One window for the backpack and equipped bags, on its own mover: search, client sort, item level on gear, gray items flagged, quality border, cooldowns, free slots and gold. Blizzard bank. | off |
| Raid utility | "Raid" button on its own mover, visible in a group: ready check, role check, countdown, target markers, ground markers (secure buttons, usable in combat). | off |

| Reminders | Out of combat: missing class buff (only if you know the spell), expected stance/form (warrior, druid), no pet out, not "Well Fed" in an instance, Shadowform / Righteous Fury (option), low durability, full bags, forgotten stealth (dungeons/raids or everywhere). Stealth and stance: customizable text and color, sound repeated at a chosen interval. | on |

| MuscaUI group and raid frames | Party and raid grids: health, power, name, role, leader, marker, aggro border and border for debuffs dispellable by your class, out-of-range dimming; sort by group, class, role or name; truncated name; raid threshold 5 to 40; on-screen preview of 5 to 40 members; click to target. | off |

Micro menu and bags: hidden, Blizzard style (Edit Mode or mover) or MuscaUI style (on their own mover or in the top bar). | off |

addons.description:
Advanced graphics settings for World of Warcraft, in one panel.

Many graphics options are only available through /console commands. Panorama puts them in a
window of its own with sliders, checkboxes and dropdowns. It reapplies your values every time
you log in.
Features
• 58 settings grouped by theme: view distance, vegetation, shadows and lighting, environment,
image, camera and interface, nameplates, advanced, floating combat text.
• Your values are kept: a value set with /console beyond a slider's range is kept and written
again at login. The game itself limits what it accepts.
• Safe on your client: a setting that your client does not support is hidden and never
written.
• Starts from your current values: on first install, the panel reads your current game
settings. Nothing changes until you move a control.
• Stays in sync: a change made in the game's Graphics menu or with /console shows in the panel.
• Reapply on login: your values from the last session are written again at login, in case the
game changed them between sessions (Config.wtf, automatic detection). You can turn it off.
• Combat safe: changes made during combat are applied when combat ends.
• Graphics restart button: it applies settings such as anti-aliasing without leaving the game.
• Presets: Low, Medium, High and Extra set every graphics setting at once. They do not change
camera, mouse or comfort settings.
• Default button on every line: it puts that setting back to its default. Advanced settings,
nameplate class colors, size, pets and totems, zoom speed, text size and combat text use the
game's own default.
Settings
| Section | Settings |
|---|---|
| View distance | Scenery distance, horizon distance, volumetric fog |
| Vegetation and details | Ground details, grass density, grass distance |
| Shadows and lighting | Shadow quality, soft shadows, shadow resolution, sun shafts, SSAO, screen space effects |
| Environment | Water detail, sky detail, weather intensity, physics |
| Image | MSAA, sharpening filter, sharpening strength, full-screen glow, death grey screen, violence level, projected textures, spell clutter |
| Camera, mouse and interface | Max camera distance, raw mouse input, screenshot quality, zoom speed, text size |
| Nameplates | Nameplate distance, enemy and friendly class colors, far, near and target nameplate size, enemy pets, enemy totems |
Commands
| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| /pano | Open the settings panel |
| /pano apply | Reapply all settings |
| /pano restart | Restart the graphics engine |
| /pano low, /pano medium, /pano high, /pano extra | Apply a preset |
| /pano undo | Restore the settings from before the last preset |
| /pano minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |

The panel opens in its own window, which you can move and close with Escape. Options > AddOns >
Panorama has a button that opens it.

addons.description:
Local, transparent and reversible noise control for public chat in
WoW Forever. It hides close repeats, optional bursts from one author and
literal terms that you choose, while keeping normal conversation, group
calls and legitimate trading visible.

Version 1.0.0 for WoW Forever 1.60.1 (Interface 16001).
What it does
• Observe first. On first start nothing is hidden: ChatGuard lists what
it would have hidden so you can judge its rules.
• Repeated text. Same author, same channel, same text within 30 s
(5–120 s). Exact match after harmless normalization: colours removed, spaces
collapsed, A–Z lowercased. Prices, digits and item links are kept, so
10g ≠ 100g and two different items with the same name are different.
• Bursts (off by default). More than 5 messages from one author in one
channel within 10 s (both adjustable).
• Your terms (off by default). Literal words or phrases, case-insensitive
for A–Z. There is no built-in word list: words such as WTS, LFG or gold are
never filtered unless you add them. A short term also matches inside longer
words.
• Allow and block lists of authors (Name-Realm); the allow list wins.
• Quarantine. Hidden or would-be-hidden messages stay viewable for the
session with time, channel, author and reason. Nothing is ever re-sent.
• Only the channels you select (none at first start). Whispers, party,
raid, guild, system and combat messages are never filtered.

Nothing leaves your computer: no network, telemetry, shared blacklists,
automatic reports or messages. Chat text is never saved to disk.

addons.description:
Guild bank and guild helper tools for E Pluribus Unum on WoW: Forever.

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| EPUGuild/ | The WoW addon. Everyone in the guild installs it. See its README. |
| epu-discord/ | Discord companion bot. One officer runs it. See its README. |
| updater/ | One-click updater for guildmates (Windows). Ships as EPU-Updater-x.y.z.zip on each release. |
| tests/ | Simulators that run the addon outside WoW, with stubbed game functions, plus the Discord file round trip. |
Getting the addon (guildmates)
• Easiest: download EPU-Updater-x.y.z.zip from the latest Release, unzip it somewhere you'll keep it, and double-click Update EPU Guild Tools. It finds WoW: Forever, installs the addon, and updates it whenever you run it. Double-click Update automatically at startup once and it keeps itself current.
• WowUp: pick your Forever install from the dropdown at the top, then Get Addons > Install from URL, paste https://github.com/Donaga/epu-guild-tools and click Install. WowUp updates it like any other addon.
• By hand: unzip EPUGuild-x.y.z.zip into World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns\, then /reload.

In game, the addon tells you when a guildmate has a newer version. On Discord, the bot announces each release and /download gives the links.
Making a release
1. Commit changes to main. The Tests workflow runs on every push.
2. Add a line to CHANGELOG.md.
3. On GitHub: Releases → Draft a new release. Type a new tag such as v0.4.0 (target main), paste the changelog lines, then Publish release.

The Release workflow then runs the tests, stamps the version into the .toc, and attaches EPUGuild-0.4.0.zip, EPU-Updater-0.4.0.zip, epu-discord-0.4.0.zip and WowUp's release.json to the release. It takes about a minute. Within 30 minutes the Discord bot announces it, and guildmates' updaters pick it up the next time they run.

The repo must be public for the updater and WowUp to download releases.

addons.description:
Context-Aware Lore Codex, Investigative Dossiers & Field Journal for World of Warcraft: Forever

ChronicleWeaver transforms your journey across Azeroth in World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface: 16001) into an interactive, spoiler-safe archivist's investigation.

Unlike static lore databases, ChronicleWeaver observes what you actually discover in-game—zones and dungeons you step into, notable figures you target, quests you complete, multi-page books and plaques you read, NPC dialogue you archive, and item flavor text you inspect—and weaves them together into a living Lore Web and 18 Grand Archivist Case Files (Dossiers).

✨ Key Features🕵️ Grand Archivist Investigative Dossiers (ARCH-01 – ARCH-18)
• Cross-Zone Case Files: 18 handcrafted investigative dossiers connecting WoW: Forever custom zones/dungeons (Zephras Isle, The Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands, City of Dalaran, The Drowned City, Riverglades & Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison, Shen'Dralas, Blackmaw Hold, Shaper's Terrace, Mount Hyjal) with classic Warcraft history.
• Live Investigation Progress Bar: Tracks Uncovered Evidence: X / Y Clues (Z%) across linked Zones, Dungeons, NPCs, Quests, Books, and Relics.
• The Archivist's Synthesis & Field Directives: Each Dossier contains a hidden Archivist's Synthesis deduction that remains sealed under Spoiler-Safe protection until you uncover field clues in Azeroth, plus actionable Field Directives pointing you toward the zones and dungeons that hold the next piece of the mystery.
📖 Automatic Multi-Page Book, Quest & Relic Harvesting
• Multi-Page Book & Plaque Harvester: Automatically archives every page of in-game books, monuments, and plaques you read, complete with origin zone, coordinates, and a live [OK] ChronicleWeaver: Page Archived HUD badge on ItemTextFrame.
• Pure-Story Quest & Gossip Archiver: Records narrative quest descriptions and completion resolutions (automatically stripping out kill counters like 0/10 Slain), plus a 1-click [+] Archive Lore button on GossipFrame to preserve NPC story dialogue.
• Dynamic Relic Flavor Harvester: Automatically detects and archives items with quoted lore flavor text when inspected in your bags or tooltips.
🕸️ Bi-Directional Lore Weaving & Strict Category Navigation
• Automatic Keyword & Entity Weaving: Dynamically highlights known entities, zones, dungeons, and dossier keywords inside every chronicle you read, generating clickable Connected Lore & Mentioned In backlink pills.
• Strict Per-Category Top Tabs: Dedicated tabs for Zone, Dungeon, NPC, Relic, Book, Quest, and Dossier.
• Dungeon, NPC, Relic, Book, and Quest tabs organize entries into collapsible Zone folders (with * Favorites pinned at the top), or toggle to a flat list.
• Zone and Dossier tabs present clean, scannable direct lists.
• Dual-Theme Engine: Switch seamlessly between Royal Archivist Parchment and Midnight Obsidian (Theme: Parchment / Dark).
• Strict Spoiler-Safe Mode: Undiscovered entries stay hidden from your index and redacted on Dossier Evidence Boards until you encounter them in Azeroth (with an optional manual reveal button).
• World Map Waypoints & Personal Field Notes: Pin any location-tagged entry directly to your World Map with UiMapPoint super-tracking, and jot down auto-saving personal field notes on every entry.

⌨️ Slash Commands & Controls
| Command / Input | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| /cw or /lorecodex | Open / Close the ChronicleWeaver Tome |
| /cw theme | Toggle between Parchment and Dark themes |
| /cw spoilers | Toggle Spoiler-Safe Mode (Hidden / Shown) |
| /cw toast | Toggle animated Discovery Toast fanfare banners |
| /cw scan or /cw quests | Backfill narrative lore from your active Quest Log |
| /cw help | Print command reference in chat |
| Minimap Addon Compartment | Left-Click: Toggle Tome \| Right-Click: Toggle Spoiler-Safe Mode |
| Sidebar Entry Row | Left-Click: Read Chronicle \| Right-Click: Toggle * Favorite |

🗂️ Project Architecture

addons.description:
One bag window for WoW: Forever where you choose where items sit.

Your backpack and bags open in a single window. Save an item to a spot and it stays in that spot: when you use it up, the spot stays reserved (shown as a faded icon), and the next one you pick up goes right back to it.
Saving an item to a spot
• Alt+click an item to save it to the spot it is in. Alt+click it again to free the spot.
• Dropping an item on a faded spot puts it in your first empty bag slot, and it shows up in the saved spot.
• A small gold mark on an item means it has a saved spot. Spots are saved per character, by item (so every stack of Hearthstone lands in the same cell).

Spots are virtual. Baggie never moves anything in your real bags, so it is instant and safe. If saved spots would push a real item off the bottom of the window, the window grows by a row so nothing is ever hidden.
Bank
The bank and guild bank open as Baggie windows too, with the same saved spots. A Deposit button opens a menu of quick deposits from your bags (or Ctrl+Alt+click an item). On a character that has not bought a bank tab yet, the window says so and shows a Buy tab button with the price. Escape closes the bank and ends the banker conversation properly.
Quest item cleanup
Shift+Alt+click a quest item to mark it with a small red cross. Alt+click the minimap button (or type /baggie toss) to destroy the marked items. Baggie reads the game's own quest log and keeps anything a quest you have could still want (Questie, if installed, adds a second check). If it cannot read the log it keeps everything, it checks again just before each item goes, and it asks you to confirm first. /baggie toss list shows the marks and /baggie toss clear removes them.
Glows
New items, quest items, quest starters and currencies each have their own glow switch and color under /baggie options. Currencies that the game files as quest items (Blood Shard and the like) only glow if you turn that on. New-item glow only marks items that came in from outside (loot, mail, bank, vendor, trade). Items that start a quest also get a yellow ! in the middle of the slot until you accept the quest (optional). Quality glows have their own brightness slider, and one more sets how far all the glows reach past the slot.
Also
• Search box: dims everything that does not match a name or item type.
• Quality borders, dimmed grey junk, cooldowns, free slot counter, money.
• Sort button (manual only, uses the game's own bag sort). Bags never rearrange on their own.
• Options window (/baggie options): themes and color pickers for the window, title bar, slots and borders; border style and thickness; slot size, spacing and padding; gold and slot-counter display; item level; vendor helpers and more. Backgrounds, borders, fonts, glows and text positions are all adjustable. Right-click the minimap button for the options. The bank and guild bank open as Baggie windows too. Window backgrounds include textures and a custom texture path, every color can be copied and pasted as a hex code, and opacity is adjustable for the window, border and title bar.
• When Follow GreedUI is enabled, its look is applied only while Baggie draws its windows. Your Baggie settings and profiles are not rewritten; turn sync off to immediately restore Baggie's saved appearance.
• Replaces the default bag windows and the bag keys (B, F12 etc.). /baggie default gives the default bags back.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /baggie | Open or close the bags |
| /baggie pins | List saved spots |
| /baggie unpin all | Free every saved spot |
| /baggie cols 4-24 | Cells per row |
| /baggie scale 0.6-1.6 | Window size |
| /baggie borders | Quality borders on or off |
| /baggie keyring | Show or hide the keyring |
| /baggie default | Switch between Baggie and the default bags |
| /baggie toss [list|clear] | Destroy marked quest items, list or clear the marks |
| /baggie reset | Put the window back at its default position |

MIT licensed.

addons.description:
A fishing helper for WoW: Forever, in the spirit of Fishing Buddy.
• Right-click to cast, right-click to catch. With a pole in hand, a single right-click on the world
casts Fishing. When the bobber splashes, right-click again and the fish is looted without aiming at the
bobber. Both are plain right-clicks; the game needs a real click for each. Prefer a double-click to cast?
Switch "Cast with" to double-click in Setup. With no pole in hand, a double-click equips one.
• Automatic lures. When your pole has no lure, the double-click applies the best one in your bags
(Aquadynamic Fish Attractor, Flesh Eating Worm, Bright Baubles, Nightcrawlers, Shiny Bauble ...).
Click again to cast.
• Fishing outfit. Put on your fishing gear, type /fishie save, and from then on /fishie switch (or
right-click the minimap button) swaps between it and your normal gear.
• Catch log. Everything you fish up is counted per zone and per session, with catches per hour.
• Sound boost. Effects up, music and ambience down while your line is out, restored afterwards.
• Options like Fishing Buddy: double-click speed, an optional Shift/Ctrl/Alt to hold, strongest or weakest lure first, replace a lure that is about to run out (with a chat warning), auto-loot while fishing, go back to your normal gear after a quiet spell, a minimap button you can hide, and a key binding (Options > Key Bindings > Fishie).
• On-screen box (/fishie hud): time since your cast, lure time left and this session's catches.
• Skill display and a small window (/fishie) with session stats, catches by zone and settings.

The game needs a real click for every cast, so casting is never fully automatic.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /fishie | Open the window |
| /fishie switch | Fishing outfit on or off |
| /fishie save | Remember what you're wearing as your fishing outfit |
| /fishie stats / reset | Print or reset this session |
| /fishie doubleclick, lure, pole, sound, announce, refreshlure, warnlure, autoloot, hud | Toggle a feature (add on or off) |
| /fishie minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |
| /fishie debug | Explain every click, cast and catch in chat |
| /fishie probe | Show what the game reports about your pole and lures |
Notes
If something doesn't work, run /fishie probe and /fishie debug on, and report what they say.

addons.description:
Recruit on autopilot. Players whisper you a phrase, Guildie sends the guild invite, and when they join it posts your custom welcome in guild chat.

Built for WoW: Forever.
Features
• Whisper-to-invite: set a phrase like guild inv. Anyone who whispers it gets an invite.
• Exact or loose matching: require the exact phrase, or catch it anywhere in a whisper.
• Custom welcome message: posted in guild chat when a new member joins. Use {name} and {guild}.
• No double welcomes: by default Guildie only welcomes players it invited, so several officers can run it at once.
• Reply whisper: optionally tell the player their invite is on the way.
• Spam protection: per-player cooldown.
• Confirm mode: the game blocks addons from sending guild invites on their own, so Guildie shows a popup; its Invite button puts /ginvite Name in your chat box and you press Enter to send it. Guildie only marks the player as invited once that command goes out.
• Activity log and stats right in the settings window.
• Guild Armory (/guildie armory): gear, talents, professions and gold of guildmates who run Guildie, with alts grouped under their main and their gold added up.
• Zone tab (/guildie zone): who's in your zone and who else has quests from it.
• Dates tab: join dates and birthdays, logged and shared automatically, with anniversary and birthday shout-outs.
• Crafters, recruit tracking, loot help and a raid-time schedule.
How to use
Open settings with /guildie, the AddOns button next to the minimap, or Options → AddOns → Guildie.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /guildie | Open settings |
| /guildie on / off | Toggle auto-invite |
| /guildie phrase | Set the invite phrase |
| /guildie welcome | Set the welcome message |
| /guildie preview | Preview the welcome in your chat |

Your guild rank needs permission to invite.
Notes
• Guild chat messages wait until chat is unlocked (for example, after a boss encounter) and then send.
• Some Forever beta builds don't reload saved settings reliably. Guildie keeps a per-character copy as a backup.

Bug reports and ideas welcome!

addons.description:
A gear advisor for WoW: Forever. Tell it your class and spec and it rates the gear in your bags against what you wear, tells you where to get better gear for your level, and shows the best buys in the Auction House.

Open it with /outfit, the minimap button, or the addon list.
What it does
• Inventory. Every piece of gear in your bags is read from its real tooltip, scored for your spec, and compared with the item you would replace. Only the best upgrade per slot is listed (two for rings and trinkets). An empty slot always gets the best item you can use.
• Equipped. Every equipped item with its score, and which slots are empty.
• What to get. Known quest rewards, dungeon drops, vendor and crafted items for your level, scored the same way, with where to get each one. For every class it also lists gear your other characters carry in their bags or bank, and gear one of your characters can craft (this part reads Profiteer's saved data, so install Profiteer). Built-in lists of quest, dungeon and vendor gear cover Mage, Warlock and Priest so far; the Auction tab works for every class. Tick boxes along the bottom pick which kinds (Quest, Dungeon, Battleground, Vendor) each character sees.
• Auction. Reads the prices Profiteer saved from your last Auction House scan and shows the best gear for sale per slot, with its price (red when you cannot afford it yet). Needs Profiteer.
• Tooltips. Hover any item for a line saying whether it is an upgrade, worse or about the same compared with what you wear.
• Minimap button (left click opens, right click opens What to get, drag to move) and a chat alert when a new upgrade lands in your bags.

Everything is limited to what you can use now: items above your level or that your class cannot wear are never suggested.
Spec and weights
Outfitter guesses your spec from your talents. Pick a different one from the drop-down in the window, or /outfit spec to cycle. Each spec has its own stat weights (/outfit weights prints them).
Commands
| | |
|---|---|
| /outfit | Open or close the window |
| /outfit spec | Next spec |
| /outfit weights | The numbers the current spec uses |
| /outfit tip | Tooltip line on/off |
| /outfit minimap | Minimap button show/hide |
| /outfit alert | Chat alert for new bag upgrades on/off |
| /outfit gain N | Only suggest items at least N% better |
| /outfit debug | Print what the game reports about your bags |

The item text is read in English. MIT licensed.

What to get uses the quest database from Questie (QuestieDB) when it is installed, so every class gets quest, vendor and dungeon suggestions.

addons.description:
A mailbox upgrade for WoW: Forever.

Everything Postage adds lives inside the normal mailbox, so it looks and works like part of the game.
Inbox
• Select. A checkbox on every mail. Shift-click a checkbox to select a range, ctrl-click to
select everything from that sender. Then Open or Return the checked mail.
• Open All. Opens every mail with gold or items attached, of the kinds you choose
(right-click the button: auction sold/won/expired/cancelled/outbid, Postmaster, players).
COD mail is always skipped and reported. It keeps bag slots free if you ask it to, and tells
you how much gold it collected.
• Express. Shift-click a mail to take it, ctrl-click to return it. Scroll the mouse wheel
over the inbox to change pages.
• DoNotWant. Each mail shows how long it has left: yellow means it goes back to the sender,
red means it will be deleted.
• Pending auction gold. A readout at the top of the inbox totals auction sales whose gold
hasn't arrived yet, and when the next one lands. Hover it for each sale.
Sending
• BlackBook. A contacts button next to the To: box with your alts, people you've mailed,
friends and guild. Names autocomplete as you type. Your alts are listed once you've logged in
on each with Postage, or add one by typing its name and choosing "Add ... to Alts". Each alt shows its professions in shorthand (LW, ECH, ALC...; main professions only).
• Keep recipient. Tick it to keep the name in the To: box after sending, so you can send
several mails to the same person.
• Alt-click an item in your bags to attach it; shift-alt-click attaches every stack of it.
• QuickAttach. Buttons beside the Send Mail frame attach everything for a profession in one click (tailoring, skinning, leatherworking, mining, blacksmithing, cooking, herbalism, alchemy, enchanting, engineering, first aid and more: cloth, leather, ore, herbs,
cooking, elemental, enchanting or engineering materials in one click.
• Wire. Leave the subject empty when sending gold and it is filled in with the amount as soon as you type the gold, so Send is never greyed out.
Reading
• Copy shows a mail's text in a box you can copy from.
• Forward starts a new mail with the same subject and text (attachments aren't forwarded).
Other
• TradeBlock declines trades and guild charters while the mailbox is open.
• Themes. Pick a look (colors, opacity, list size) for Postage's windows, and optionally paint the
game's inbox, send mail and open mail windows to match.
• A minimap button, the game's Settings > AddOns panel and the addon list entry open the options,
where every feature can be turned off.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /postage | Options |
| /postage help | List commands and shortcuts |
| /postage minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |
| /postage freeslots | Keep n bag slots free when opening mail |
| /postage probe | Check which mailbox parts Postage found on your client |
Notes on WoW: Forever
Postage attaches itself to Blizzard's mailbox frames. If a feature doesn't appear, run
/postage probe and report what it says is missing. QuickAttach's material categories use the
standard item subclass numbers, which haven't been checked on a Forever client yet; the
"All trade goods" button works either way.
Mailbox look
Alt-click the minimap button to restyle the mailbox: letter paper (original, plain, dark or none), and the quick-attach tray (side, size, columns, spacing, panel, counts, which professions to show). Buttons dim when you have nothing of that kind.

addons.description:
Find out which crafts actually make money. Profiteer reads the recipes your characters know, prices the materials and the finished item from the Auction House, and ranks every craft by profit and return on investment, across all of your characters.

Built for WoW Forever (beta client 1.60.x).
What it does
• Ranks your crafts. For every recipe any of your characters knows: material cost (auction price, or the vendor price if that's cheaper) against what the finished item sells for after the auction cut. Shows profit, ROI, how many are listed, and how many you can craft right now from your bags and bank.
• Click through to the materials. In the results window, click a craft to search the Auction House for its materials (through Auctionator's Shopping list if you have it), shift-click to search for the finished item, and right-click to track a craft so it stays pinned at the top.
• Works across your whole account. One window lists each craft once, with every character who can make it.
• Scans automatically. Opens the Auction House, takes one full scan in the background without hitching the game, and refreshes whenever the data is stale.
• Price history and sales estimates. Every scan adds a snapshot, so you get a market median, a trend, and an estimated sales-per-day figure for the items you craft.
• Recipe tracker. A recipe item's tooltip (Recipe, Pattern, Formula, Plans...) tells you which of your characters already know it, which could still learn it, and which have no such profession. Open each character's profession windows once to fill it in.
• Auction House tabs. Shopping, selling and cancelling pages with price gaps, relist prices and totals.
• Item tooltips. Lowest auction price, listing count, market median and trend, and vendor price on any scanned item.
• Lives in the Auction House. A Profiteer button on the Auction House window opens the ranking over it. There is also a minimap button.

addons.description:
A character showcase for WoW: Forever. Your character on a full-screen stage, your gear around them, and a photo studio.

Open it with /vanity, the minimap button, the addon list, or a key (Options > Key Bindings > AddOns > Vanity). A button on the character window is available in Settings.
What it does
• Full-screen rotatable model. Drag to turn, right-drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom, slow turntable (/vanity spin).
• Item cards. Every equipped item shows its details beside its slot, no hovering needed: name in quality color, item level, main stats, enchant, equip/use effects and any problems. Hover for the full tooltip, shift-click to link in chat.
• Warnings that matter. A red ! on any item that is missing an enchant (from level 40) or has an empty gem socket, with a summary list on screen.
• Average item level and durability (average and lowest).
• Stats panel: attributes, armor, attack power, crit, dodge, parry, block, haste, health, power.
• Pose picker. The Pose button opens a menu of 22 poses and emotes (salute, wave, bow, cheer, applaud, laugh, cry, flex, point, dance, sit, sleep, kneel ...). One-shot emotes repeat until you pick another.
• Photo mode (/vanity photo): hides the interface, then a studio bar with backgrounds, the same pose picker, turntable, and a screenshot button that hides the controls first.
• 14 backgrounds: Midnight, Class color, Faction, Ember, Frost, Forest, Void, Gilded, Sunset, Slate, Pure black, Studio white, Green screen and The world.
• AFK screen. Go AFK (or /vanity afk to preview) and Vanity fills the screen with your character, a big timer, a clock and your gear and stats, cycling poses. Your active buffs show with tooltips. Move or press a key to return.
• View target: look at another player's model.
Settings
/vanity settings: background, brightness, camera framing (full body, waist up, bust, portrait), turntable, panels, item cards, game-interface hiding and AFK options.
Commands
| | |
|---|---|
| /vanity | Open or close the showcase |
| /vanity photo | Photo mode |
| /vanity afk | Preview the AFK screen |
| /vanity bg | Cycle the background |
| /vanity spin | Turntable on/off |
| /vanity settings | Settings |
| /vanity reset | Reset the camera |
| /vanity minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |

Vanity is built from scratch (it shares no code or art with any other addon). MIT licensed.
