addons.changelog:
Forever Suite 2.0 – beta10

> 🧪 Beta für Retail: Bis WoW Forever startet, wird die Suite in Retail (Midnight) getestet. Dies ist eine Testversion, die Daten darin sind Testdaten.

Spiel ganz beenden, die Forever…-Ordner unter Interface\AddOns löschen, die neuen aus dem ZIP hineinkopieren, Spiel starten. Eure Daten bleiben erhalten.
Wichtig bei diesem Update
• Vorher sichern: Bitte den Ordner WTF kopieren, bevor ihr das Spiel mit der neuen Fassung startet.
• Alle möglichst gemeinsam aktualisieren: beta10 tauscht über einen eigenen Kanal (Protokoll 6). beta9 und beta10 tauschen keine Daten miteinander, ein Hinweis im Chat nennt ältere Fassungen.
Bekannte Einschränkungen
• Die erste Reisesuche nach dem Login kann 9–11 Sekunden dauern, danach geht es deutlich schneller. Das Spiel läuft währenddessen weiter.
• Bei Wegsuchen kann es vereinzelt kurz ruckeln.
• In einem unbekannten Haus reicht eine neue Route manchmal zunächst nur ein kurzes Stück. Sie wird neu gesucht, sobald ihr eine Tür benutzt oder die Seite wechselt.
• Die Zwei-Client-Prüfung lief gegen eine ältere Austausch-Fassung, nicht gegen ein echtes beta9-Paket. Meldet bitte, wenn der Austausch mit Mitspielern hängt.

Neu seit v2.0-beta9:
Basis (Core) 0.4.56 (vorher 0.4.52)
• Suche: Lange Ergebnislisten lassen sich mit dem Mausrad und den Pfeiltasten durchgehen
• Suche: Rechts neben der Liste ein Scrollbalken zum Ziehen
• Kartenpunkte: Lernt das Spiel die Größe einer Karte erst nach dem Login, gehen abgelegte Punkte nicht mehr verloren
• Protokoll: Kein Lua-Fehler mehr beim Laden, wenn BugSack aktiv ist
Navigation 0.5.96 (vorher 0.5.83)
• Route: Eine Suche, die wiederholt von Datenänderungen überholt wird, liefert keinen veralteten Weg mehr
• Route: Ohne Tür aus einem Haus keine lange rote Linie mehr
• Route: Beim Betreten eines Hauses verschwindet eine gute Route nicht mehr
• Route: Eine an bekannten Boden endende Route wird beim Verlassen des Hauses sofort neu gesucht
• Route: Aus einem unbekannten Haus führt der Weg sofort durch die eben benutzte Tür
• Route: Ohne bekannte Tür keine rote Linie mehr durch die Wände zum nächsten Haus
• Route: Eine beschädigte Route, die kürzer als die Luftlinie zum Ziel ist, wird beim nächsten Nachschauen ersetzt
• Route: Die Suche gibt den Frame nach Zeit zurück, das kappt lange Scheiben
• Route: Eine Suche übernimmt keinen Weg über eine inzwischen geänderte Tür mehr, sondern sucht neu
• Reisen: Ein selbst gelaufener neuer Zugang zählt sofort
• Protokoll: Der längste Frame einer Suche wird aufgeschlüsselt
• Route: Die Türen einer Karte werden nur noch nach einer Änderung neu berechnet, das verkürzt Suchen und Ruckler
• Protokoll: Jede Wegsuche nennt Wartezeit, Rechenzeit und längsten Frame, bei laufender Messung im Protokoll
• Route: Findet nach dem Abweichen schneller einen neuen Weg, auch wenn du weiterläufst; die Reisehilfe sagt, dass gesucht wird
• Route: Die Meldung nennt jetzt die unbestätigte Tür
• Route: Weniger Ruckler beim Suchen einer neuen Route, die Türen werden pro Suche nur noch einmal berechnet
• Reisen: Ein Ziel in einer Unterkarte (Nordhain) führt über den gelaufenen Grenzübergang statt in gerader Linie durchs Gelände
• Reisen: Liegt das Ziel auf einer anderen Karte als das Ende des bekannten Wegs (Nordhain vom Wald von Elwynn aus), führt die Route nach dem Grenzübertritt nicht mehr zurück
• Reisen: Die nächste Etappe wird über mehrere Frames berechnet – kein Ruckler mehr bis zu zwei Sekunden
• Reisen: Bist du während der Suche weitergelaufen, wird von dort neu gesucht
• Route: Keine Linie mehr quer durch die Stadt, wenn die Suche ihre Grenze erreicht – der schon gefundene Weg bleibt, jede Strecke wird nur einmal gesucht
• Route: Drinnen kein Sprung mehr von Raum zu Raum durch die Wand, der Weg geht über die Tür; ohne bekannte Verbindung zwischen zwei Räumen gibt es keine Linie
• Route: Zerfällt nicht mehr beim Teleport hin und zurück; der Stopp an der Tür bleibt auch nach einem Umweg…

• Weltsuche: Das Feld blendet nicht mehr aus, während du in der Liste auswählst – ein Klick auf eine Kategorie gibt die Tasten ans Feld zurück, solange die Maus über Feld oder Liste ist, bleibt es stehen
Navigation 0.5.83 (vorher 0.5.81)
• Route: Die erste Berechnung nach der Zielwahl läuft verteilt über mehrere Bilder – kein Ruckeln mehr bei langen Wegen (vorher bis 0,9 s Stillstand); solange steht „Route zu … wird berechnet …“ in der Reisehilfe
• Reise: Alle Etappen auf der Weltkarte – Fahrten (Schiff, Portal, Flug …) als lila Linie von–bis, Fußwege orange; auf der Azeroth-Karte auch zwischen den Kontinenten
• Reise: Das Endziel blinkt auf der Weltkarte als drehender, pulsierender Stern – auf seiner Karte, seinem Kontinent und der Azeroth-Karte
• Reise: Am Hafen, Portal oder Flugmeister bleibt das Zielsymbol stehen, bis man hindurch ist; wer sich entfernt, wird wieder hingeführt

addons.changelog:
v0.1.5 (2026-10-09)
Everything in v0.1.5-beta1, plus the fixes from a code review of the protocol and persistence:
• A character whose name merely extends ours ("Dea Onex", "Deaone", or our first name alone) can no longer replay our hello and become our identity, taking our hosted games' ownership with it (#62, #72). On classic realms the realm is part of the identity too (#76).
• Another host can no longer poison a game's squares by announcing a set under that game's hash: a set is trusted only when its hash comes out of its content and it came from the game's own host, in memory and in the saved library (#63, #73).
• A snapshot that arrives after newer calls no longer rolls the game back and erases them (#64).
• A follower that missed the last call before a game closed now recovers it: the host stays around to answer, keeps answering until the final state is through, and History ends up with the full result (#65, #74).
• Handing a game over is reliable: a recipient that missed a call before the handoff, or the handoff message itself, still takes over; the old host resends until the new host's first card and refuses to call meanwhile (#66, #75).
• Logging in on an alt no longer rejoins the main's games; joined games are saved per character (#67).
• A join whose request or welcome was lost is asked again, a few times, before the addon says it could not join (#68).
• /dea undo on a square that was never called no longer calls it (#69).
• The chip and the toast anchor come back where they were dragged after a reload (#71).
• CI fails when the headless client smoke fails (#70).
addons.description:
Raid Bingo, played inside World of Warcraft: Forever. One person starts a game and calls the
squares, everyone gets the same 24 squares in a different order, and every board ticks over
live. The same rules as raidbingo.com, without leaving the game.

Made for the Drip Enforcement Agency, and it works for any guild or group.
Playing
• Open the window with the minimap button, /dea, or the addon compartment.
• Start a game from the Games tab: give it a title, pick who can join (your guild
anywhere, or whoever is grouped with you), fill the 24 squares by pasting a list or
starting from a previous game, and open it.
• Join a game from the toast that appears when someone opens one, or from the Games tab.
• Calling: the host, and anyone the host lets call, clicks a square to call it. Clicking
a called square undoes it, and an undo leaves no trace; nothing asks for confirmation,
since any call can be undone and redone. There is also an alphabetical caller list with
a filter under the calls panel.
• Five in a row wins. The night continues past the first bingo; winners are ranked by time.
• The chip at the top of the screen keeps the score while the window is closed. Nothing
pops or makes a sound during combat.
• History keeps the last 20 finished games readable. Options has the theme, sounds,
the chip and the minimap button.
What it shares and keeps
Squares usually name real guildmates, so it is worth knowing where they go.
• Opening a game broadcasts it. The title, all 24 squares and the list of players go to
everyone who can hear the game. In Guild mode, the default, that is every guild member
online, in the raid or not. In Raid mode it is everyone grouped with you, pugs included.
Pick Raid mode only when the squares are fit for strangers.
• Nothing is ever posted to chat. Everything travels on the addon channel, which only
other copies of the addon read. Players without the addon see nothing.
• Kept on this computer, in the game's SavedVariables files in plain text: every set of
squares you have hosted or played, the last 20 finished games with each player's character
name and bingo time, and the games you have been offered. Tools that back up or sync your
WTF folder carry these along. Deleting the addon's SavedVariables file clears them.
addons.name: DEA Bingo

v0.1.5 (2026-10-09)
Everything in v0.1.5-beta1, plus the fixes from a code review of the protocol and persistence:
• A character whose name merely extends ours ("Dea Onex", "Deaone", or our first name alone) can no longer replay our hello and become our identity, taking our hosted games' ownership with it (#62, #72). On classic realms the realm is part of the identity too (#76).
• Another host can no longer poison a game's squares by announcing a set under that game's hash: a set is trusted only when its hash comes out of its content and it came from the game's own host, in memory and in the saved library (#63, #73).
• A snapshot that arrives after newer calls no longer rolls the game back and erases them (#64).
• A follower that missed the last call before a game closed now recovers it: the host stays around to answer, keeps answering until the final state is through, and History ends up with the full result (#65, #74).
• Handing a game over is reliable: a recipient that missed a call before the handoff, or the handoff message itself, still takes over; the old host resends until the new host's first card and refuses to call meanwhile (#66, #75).
• Logging in on an alt no longer rejoins the main's games; joined games are saved per character (#67).
• A join whose request or welcome was lost is asked again, a few times, before the addon says it could not join (#68).
• /dea undo on a square that was never called no longer calls it (#69).
• The chip and the toast anchor come back where they were dragged after a reload (#71).
• CI fails when the headless client smoke fails (#70).

v0.1.5-beta1 (2026-10-09)
• The game tab can also shrink in height, to 440; the other tabs keep the full minimum and the window grows back on leaving the game tab (#61).

v0.1.4 (2026-10-09)
• Addon messages sent while the Forever client is in a chat lockdown (encounters) wait in a queue and go out, in order, when it lifts; only the newest heartbeat per game is kept. /dea status says whether the lockdown is on and how many messages wait (#43).
• A send made in the second after a lockdown lifts no longer overtakes the messages still held (#45).
• The queue keeps the newest heartbeat, hello and sync request per destination, and no longer lets a whispered heartbeat evict the broadcast one (#46).
• One held message failing to send no longer loses the ones behind it (#47).
• A held group message goes out on the channel the group has when it leaves, not the one it had when it was held (#48).
• During a lockdown a follower no longer marks the host away or reports a held call request as lost; the timers restart when it lifts (#44).
• A join request held through a lockdown still gets its welcome accepted when it finally goes out (#49).
• A sender or guild roster name the client hands over as a secret value no longer reaches the debug tap or the roster match (#52).
• The window built by a reload mid-fight comes up dimmed and unclickable, like one that saw the fight start (#53).
• In combat the window's header stays live: the close button and the title-bar drag work while the rest is dimmed (#54).
• A text box that had the keyboard when combat started lets it go, so keys reach the game again (#55).
• A confirmation card closes with the window (Escape, a reload) and when combat starts, instead of staying up with a stale action behind its button (#56).
• Calls that land in a burst after a fight make one tick, not one per call; a bingo always sounds (#57).
• A send the client refuses for a lockdown that began after the check, or that the chat library had already spooled, goes back to the front of the queue; /dea net counts refusals and /dea debug shows the client's result code (#50).
• The queue also drains the moment the client reports the restriction over, not only on the next tick (#51).
• The game tab can shrink to the board alone: below the full width the standings and calls rail hides and the board takes the window; the other tabs keep the full minimum and widen the window back (#59).
• A hello held through a lockdown still teaches the client its own server-side name from the echo when it finally goes out (#60).

v0.1.3 (2026-10-09)
• Standings: each player on two lines, the whole name (Forever names are two words) then the meter and the CALLER flag, so rows no longer collide (#40).
• Hover a player in the standings to see their grid as dots, like the chip's: called squares lit, a winning line brighter. Positions only, never their square text (#41).
• Calling: a caller's click calls the square, a click on a called square undoes it, with no confirmation; any call can be undone and redone. Others still click a square to read its full text (#42).

v0.1.2 (2026-10-09)
• Version shown on the Options tab and in the minimap tooltip, with a note on the Options tab when a newer release is around.
• Resizing the window: the History and Games lists now widen with it, and the Options rows no longer lose their hints and buttons.
• The website's footer one-liners, retold for the addon, in the window footer on the Games, History and Options tabs. A new one every 30 seconds.

addons.description:
Steam Deck presets for World of Warcraft: Forever. Pick a preset, keep it or let it revert
after 15 seconds, done. Every preset was measured on a Steam Deck OLED: frame rate, 1% lows and
battery draw, in the open world and in a capital.

Designed to go with the DeckForever app, which installs
Battle.net and WoW: Forever on the Steam Deck, adds them to the Steam library, and can repair, back
up or uninstall the setup. The app gets the game running; this addon tunes it. The addon also works
on its own if you set up the game another way.
Presets
| Preset | Frame rate | What you get | Deck TDP limit | Battery life* |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Battery | 30 fps | lightest look, steady everywhere, even in cities | 8–10 W | ~4.3 h |
| Balanced | 45 fps | Battery plus real shadows and shading | 10 W | ~3.7 h |
| Max FPS | 60 fps | sharp, longer view, full power (cities ~50 fps) | Off | ~2.8 h |
| Max Quality | 30 fps | everything high: lighting, shadows, reflections. Plug in; not for cities | Off | ~2.5 h |

\*Steam Deck OLED, questing. Capitals are limited by power on any handheld; Battery at 30 fps is
the preset that stays smooth there.
Features
• Controller friendly. D-pad moves a focus ring, A selects, B closes, shoulders switch tabs.
Large buttons, no dropdowns, nothing that needs hovering.
• Safe to try. Your own settings are saved before the first preset; Restore previous puts
them back. Each apply shows a 15-second Keep / Revert dialog. Nothing is changed in combat.
• Customize any preset setting with steppers that use the game's own names. Changes show in
gold; one button resets a preset.
• Steam Deck tab: the Quick Access settings (refresh rate, frame limit, TDP) that go with each
preset. An addon can't change those, so the tab tells you what to set.
• UI scale for the 7-inch screen. The game locks its own UI Scale option in Forever; the addon
scales the interface instead.
• Reload UI button in the window, and a minimap button with a quick menu.
• Raid and battleground settings (a separate set in the game) follow the preset, a notch lower.
Commands
| Command | |
|---|---|
| /deckforever | Open the window |
| /deckforever apply battery\|balanced\|performance\|quality | Apply a preset (performance is Max FPS, quality is Max Quality) |
| /deckforever restore | Back to your own settings from before the first preset |
| /deckforever preview
| List what a preset would change |
| /deckforever customize [preset] / deck [preset] | Open the Customize / Steam Deck tab |
| /deckforever set
/ reset
[setting] | Override or reset preset values |
| /deckforever uiscale \|default | Interface size (about 0.75 suits the Deck) |
| /deckforever minimap on\|off, raid on\|off, reminder on\|off\| | Options |
| /deckforever fps, status, help | Information |

addons.description:
everbuff.gg WoW addon
Gameplay recording for data nerds.

The in-game half of everbuff.gg. It records your WoW run the way a flight
recorder records a flight: every fight with a replay you can scrub, every pickup with where it came from,
every death with what killed you, every quest, standing and skill point, and where your gold went. Nothing
to start or stop. Play, and it fills in.
What you get
Five tabs, one question each. No tab is named after a data type.

| Tab | The question | What is in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | How is my run going? | Level, XP per hour and time to level, gold per hour, time played, the story of this session, and one row per play session with XP and gold bars |
| Combat | What happened when I fought? | Dungeon runs boss by boss, every fight with a scrubber that shows your buffs, your group's buffs, the monsters' buffs, gear and items used at any second, and every death with the corpse run and gear lost |
| Loot | What did I get? | Every pickup with its source (the mob, the node, the object, the mail, the auction) and the map coordinates, a by-item view, gold in and out down to repairs, flights and postage, and your auctions: what you posted at what price, what sold and for how much after the house cut, what you bought, what came back |
| Character | How is my character growing? | Quests done and in progress with where you did them, standing with every faction, professions with skill bars and milestones, and crafting: every item you made with the profession and where you made it, every recipe learned |
| Settings | | The on-screen flag, notifications, capture health, disconnect protection, stored data |

The flag in the corner is the part the everbuff desktop app reads: it marks the moments in your video
recording. Drag it anywhere, right-click to snap it to a corner, size and fade it in Settings.
Why an addon and not just a combat log
The combat log knows damage. It does not know your level, your gold, what you looted or from where, what
you were wearing, which potion you drank, what your party's buffs were at the second the tank died, or
where on the map any of it happened. This addon records all of that, timestamped to the same clock as the
combat log and the video, so the desktop app can put the three together.

It also handles the awkward client. On the Midnight and "WoW Forever" builds most combat values are
Secret Values that addons cannot read, and the client hides your own buffs a few seconds into every fight.
The recorder is built around that: identities that survive hiding, guards that never record a phantom buff
loss, and a replay that bridges any gap. Verified against real fights.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft add-on for the guild's member database and Fellowship roster: who each player is, which characters are their mains and alts, and the alias they choose to be called. It supports WoW Forever and WoW Retail from one source tree.

The add-on groups the guild's characters into players. Each player has one main, any number of alts, and an optional alias. The grouping is seeded from public guild notes, and from then on it's kept in a local database. You change it by hand, and officers' edits reach it through guild sync.

addons.description:
NPC voices and quest narration for WoW Forever.

Website ·
Discord ·
CurseForge ·
What’s new ·
Report a problem

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The addon requires the ForeverDubbed companion app to work. The addon cannot generate or play voices on its own.

Have you always wondered what WoW would be like with full voice acting? Wonder no more! Using text-to-speed models that run locally on your computer, Forever Dubbed generates audio for any quest, conversation, or dialog in the game!

Features unique voices for each race/gender and it will even will say your character's name.

Try it out and experience Azeroth like never before!
Install
| Platform | Download | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Installer | Windows 10/11, 64-bit |
| macOS | DMG | macOS 14+, Apple Silicon |

Windows: run the installer, then launch ForeverDubbed from the Start menu.

macOS: open the disk image and drag ForeverDubbed.app into Applications. Grant Screen Recording permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security, then quit and reopen the app.

The application will install the WoW addon automatically.
Connect to WoW
1. Open ForeverDubbed. It finds WoW Forever in the usual Windows locations or /Applications/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/World of Warcraft Beta.app on macOS and installs or updates its bundled addon automatically. If needed, select your WoW client with Locate WoW…: usually WowB.exe (Windows) or World of Warcraft Beta.app (macOS). Renamed clients are supported; on Windows, switch the picker to All executables. The selected client must be inside its WoW installation, and capture uses that exact path.
2. Follow the narrator and banner: restart WoW for a fresh install, or type /reload for an update. Enable the addon in WoW’s AddOns list and keep WoW in windowed or borderless mode.
3. Type /fdb test in WoW. The companion should show Connected and read the test aloud.
4. Use /fdb unlock to drag the small data square somewhere unobstructed, then /fdb lock to finish.

On Windows 10, the companion uses desktop capture while the game is visible to avoid the yellow capture border. Other windows must not cover the data square. Windows 11 uses game-window capture.

The square passes dialogue to the companion. Keep its entire border visible and your pointer off it; it hides after sending text (after ~15 seconds). While unlocked for positioning, it stays visible until you lock it again.

Use Locate WoW… to change the installation or retry. If access is denied, run the Windows companion as administrator and retry, or manually copy the bundled ForeverDubbed addon folder into the exact Interface/AddOns location shown in the error banner. The bundled folder is beside the Windows executable under addon; on macOS, use Show Package Contents → Contents/Resources/addon in Finder.
Make it yours
• Settings: choose quest dialogue, NPC conversations, and ambient NPC speech. Quest titles and objectives are optional and off by default. The Voice volume slider below Read aloud adjusts playback from 0–100% and remembers your setting. Changes apply during native voice playback; the system speech fallback applies them to the next utterance.
• Voices: choose Default, Narrator, or None for each race and gender. None silences that selection, including speech already playing or queued. Your choices are saved.
• Queue new dialogue: finish each message before starting the next. When off, new dialogue interrupts the current line.
• Open an accepted quest in the quest log and click the play arrow to hear it with the narrator voice. This uses your quest title/objective preferences and works even while automatic reading is paused.…

releases.changelog:
Changed
• Version number: this version has the same content as 0.1.8 and carries the minor number because the experience bar and the mouse cursor ring are two new areas.

Added
• A new experience bar window shows your XP as a bar with texts you place yourself, and percentages count across several levels.
• The experience bar has four presets. A click on it opens a menu, pinning fixes the position, and a pencil button opens the layout editor.
• The experience bar has no title bar or frame. Unpinned, drag the bar itself and scale it with the grip at the bottom right. A click brings the window to the front.
• Pause and reset the session and see the time per level from your played time. Percentages, rested XP and targets end at the highest level your game allows.
• An optional chat message at a level up goes to your own chat window, the group, the guild or Say. The game usually blocks Say for add-ons, so you get a hint and the line in your own window.
• A page in the tools area gathers all experience bar settings. The command /fg xp (also erfahrung, xpbar) takes pause, reset, edit, time and chat, and a key binding and a settings card are included.
• Experience bar layouts can be created, duplicated, renamed and deleted, on the page, in the click menu and in the layout editor.
• Layout editor: set bars, texts and rectangles with colors, font, size and placeholders. A text can have a background, and a warning names too little contrast.
• Layout editor: a slim band under the title bar holds save, undo, redo, reset, export and import, and the layout list sits beside it. A star marks unsaved changes, and a dialog asks before you switch.
• Layout editor: eight handles change width and height in the preview, the border has its own opacity, and Live, info, grid and real values sit in one row.
• Layout editor: add, remove (trash button, Ctrl+Z brings it back) and rename elements (F2). Names survive export and import, and every element type has a short description.
• Mouse cursor ring: a ring, shape or crosshair follows the mouse cursor, with presets and layouts of your own from the layout editor. It is off by default, and while it is off nothing runs for it.
• Mouse cursor ring: color, opacity, rotation, blending, line thickness (1 to 64 pixels) and an inner fill are adjustable, and all eight shapes also exist filled.
• Mouse cursor ring: visibility rules for combat, instances, target, mount and vehicle, the screen layer, and the behavior while the camera turns (hide, keep at the cursor, screen center).
• Mouse cursor ring: the command /fg cursor (also mauszeiger, ring) takes on, off, edit and reset. A key binding, a settings card on the General tab and a page in the tools area are included.
• Mouse cursor ring: the Trail element shows particles or lightning behind the pointer, and the Click effect element a growing ring on left and right click. Reduced motion turns the trail off.
• Mouse cursor ring: timers for the global cooldown, for casting and channeling (with a flash on interrupt) and for the swing of each weapon (main hand, off hand, ranged) as a ring or a bar.
• Mouse cursor ring: when the game's own swing bars are on, the panel of the swing timer points it out and never changes the setting.
• Mouse cursor ring: a health ring and a resource ring with start point, direction and colors, red at low health. The game hides these values from add-ons, so the rings show no numbers.
• Mouse cursor ring: the range element shows whether the target is in range, out of range or unknown, as a ring, a dot, text with the distance band (0-5 up to 35+ yards) or both.
• Mouse cursor ring: the range check asks your spells first, then items and the interact distance, or you choose melee, a distance or a spell. The status line names the source.
• Mouse cursor ring: more presets (ring with trail, ring with click effect, timers, swing timer, health, resource and range, distance text) and an editor preview with simulation.
Changed
• Dropdowns have a little more space between the label and the field.
Fixed
• Pressing keys in combat with a window open no longer adds entries to the error list.…

Added
• The start page, the Help page and the last setup step invite you to the livestream and the community server, each with a button that opens the address for copying.
• The setup shows both addresses below the text, and the livestream button uses the color of the channel.
• The title bar channel field is filled purple and shows the live channel address in a larger font.
• Group Finder: choose the search languages from all the game offers. Your game language is always included, one search shows at most 100 groups.
• Group Finder: the new section "I search as" stays in sync with the roles of the game's listing view, you can switch off all roles, and roles your class cannot play are disabled.
• Group Finder: the switch "Show matching groups" hides groups with no free slot for your role. Single players stay visible.
Changed
• Group Finder: the filter panel stays open on all three tabs. A click on Search shows the Search tab with the results, whichever tab you are on.
• Group Finder: the Show section has three buttons for groups, players or everything. Groups without a free slot are always hidden.
• Group Finder: when you switch the category in the panel, nothing is checked at first. "All" checks everything, the first start still checks all dungeons.
• Group Finder: the text filter ignores case, accents and umlauts and finds Russian, Korean and Chinese names.
• Group Finder: raid groups whose slots the game does not count stay visible.
• Group Finder: the panel check boxes react at once and can be clicked anywhere on their row or icon.
Fixed
• Group Finder: switching "Show all dungeons" in the settings no longer leaves the game's own search blocked. A reload is offered after the change.
• Group Finder: the role choice no longer flickers or jumps back on a fast click.
• Group Finder: the Dungeons category shows in the panel dropdown even when the game delivers the categories late.

Added
• Beta: A small label at the minimap shows the layer of your zone. A left click opens the layer window, a right click reads the layer again.
• Beta: The layer window shows your layer, the zone, when it was last confirmed and the layer before. A button reads it again.
• Beta: Switch your layer with one click. The add-on asks a host on another layer, accepts that host's group invite, waits until your layer changed and leaves the group.
• Beta: The layer window lists the hosts of your zone with their layer. "Pick best host" tries them one after the other.
• Beta: Layer sharing and hosting are off by default. Sharing sends your zone, layer, class and character name to other add-on users in a hidden channel.
• The layer is read from the NPCs you see. Target any NPC or move the mouse over one to find your layer.
• The command /fg layer opens the layer window, /fg layer hosts lists the hosts and /fg layer switch starts a switch.
• A new settings card "Layer" holds the switches and a button to reset the position of the label.
Changed
• Declining invites of strangers no longer declines the invite of the host you asked for a layer switch.

Added
• A filter panel docks to the right side of the Group Finder and opens with it. A tab below the game's tabs shows or hides it.
• The group list can be filtered by role, class, group size, leader level, playstyle, name or dungeon, and how long a listing has been up. Entries that do not match are hidden.
• Choose dungeons in the panel and start the search there, without listing yourself first. All dungeons are checked by default.
• The dungeon list shows every dungeon with its level range and marks those that fit your level. Long names are shortened, the level range always stays readable.
• Show only groups looking for players, only players looking for a group, or only groups with a free slot, with presets for one click.
• A new settings card "Group finder" shows whether the Group Finder lists all dungeons or only those for your level, and switches it.
• The panel can be switched off, shown automatically when the Group Finder opens, and docked to the window.
• With docking on, the game's tabs and ours move to the right edge of the panel.
• The command /fg gruppensuche (also /fg lfg) shows or hides the panel.

addons.description:
The addon for World of Warcraft: Forever, and the small program that runs beside the game.
Together they show you, in game, what your professions still need, less what you already have
(/fwc), and they record what the auction house lists and send it on, which is where the prices
come from.

It is plain Python 3.10+ with nothing to install, and a WoW addon. MIT licence. Questions and
help: the Discord, . What is sent and what is not: The pipe
below, and .
What it does
| | |
|---|---|
| The addon (addon/ForeverWowCraftScanner) | /fwc: the cheapest route for each profession from your skill on, with what you have (bags, bank, mail, your own auctions) taken off, across your characters if you like. A Make button on the game's profession panel crafts that route a step at a time, and says what to buy or learn when it cannot, with an arrow to the nearest trainer, vendor or anvil: the addon comes with the vanilla world's (Seed.lua, data from the VMaNGOS database, GPL-2.0, apart from the addon's MIT code) and notes the ones it sees you at. At the auction house a shopping list buys what the step needs, a click and a confirm an item. And it records the auction house's prices, by itself, whenever you open it and it can (once every 15 minutes): a small button on the auction house frame lights up when there is something to save, and that click is all it asks. Nothing of yours is sent: prices only |
| fwch.py | Finds the game, installs the addon, reads what it saved, sends it through the pipe, and writes the lists and the routes it is given into the addon |
Setting up
1. Download ForeverWowCraft-Helper-.msi and run it. Nothing else needs installing:
Python is inside (python\, python.org's own build). It installs for your own user, under
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ForeverWowCraft Helper, so Windows asks for no administrator; it
may warn that the installer is not signed (SmartScreen: "More info", then "Run anyway").
2. The helper starts when the installer is done, and when you log on to Windows from then on:
an icon by the clock, in the notification area. It finds the game, installs the addon,
fetches the lists to scan and the routes, and waits. If it cannot find the game, right-click
the icon and Choose the game folder: the "World of Warcraft" folder, the one that holds
the client folder (forever).
3. Start the game (restart it if it was running: it only finds a new addon when it starts).
/fwc opens the window. Open the auction house now and then: the prices are recorded by
themselves, the Save Prices button on its frame lights up when there is something to
save, and that click is all it asks; the helper sends them within seconds. (Interface,
AddOns, ForeverWowCraft has the switches, among them the scanner's own bar for running
scans by hand.)

Point at the icon for how things stand: what was last sent, how many auction houses have
routes, or what is wrong. Its menu: Send prices now; Fetch routes now; **Choose the
game folder; Open the log; Start with Windows**, ticked when it does (Windows' own
Settings > Apps > Startup has the same switch); Help; Quit. A balloon comes only when
something needs you: the game not found, the addon not installed, prices that could not be
sent, the game to restart. Everything the helper does is in its log, with the date and time at the start of
every line: %LOCALAPPDATA%\ForeverWowCraft\Helper\helper.log. The same folder holds the
helper's name and token at the pipe (identity.json), what it sent (sent.json), and the
routes, lists and freshness it fetched; an uninstall leaves it, so a reinstall is the same
sender. FWC_STATE names another folder. One instance runs at a time: starting the helper
again while it runs only says so.

Each auction house in the scan file is sent on its own: one the service does not take
(not sent, : ...) does not hold the others back, and is tried again. A scan is sent
once: the helper remembers what it sent by what the scan says, so an update of the helper…

addons.description:
Know your keybinds at a glance.

Long keybinding names can get cut off on your action bars, making binds like
Mouse Wheel Up and Mouse Wheel Down hard to tell apart. Clean Binds lets
you give each button a clear, short label such as MWU or MWD in **World
of Warcraft: Forever**. Your keybindings stay exactly the same.

Download on CurseForge |
Wago |
GitHub releases
Features
• Short labels you choose. Customize each button individually, including
mouse buttons, the mouse wheel, and Shift, Ctrl, or Alt combinations.
• Labels for MMO mice. Use names like N1 or N12 for side-button keybinds
on a Razer Naga or similar mouse, even when those buttons are mapped to
keyboard keys.
• Blizzard's familiar action bars. Change the text without replacing your
bars or changing their layout.
• Adjustable keybind font size. Make labels easier to read without
enlarging your action buttons. Keep Blizzard's font style and colors.
• Optional label and macro-name hiding. Hide keybinding labels (while
keeping the range indicator dot) or macro names on your action buttons without
changing your bindings or renaming your macros.
• Built into Options. Browse buttons by action bar and preview your labels
as you type.
• Shared or character-specific settings. Labels automatically follow WoW's
keybinding setting, with no extra profile selector.
addons.name: cleanbinds

ChangesGoatQuest 1.4.1 (Forever)
• Guides updated to Classic source revision 37349 (was 37145). Five guide files changed;
none were added or removed:

new weaponsmith trainer step.
• Sunken Temple (dungeon and raid versions): the Fetish of Hakkar collection steps are gone.
GoatQuestRetail 1.0.1 (Retail)
• Guides updated to Retail source revision 37370 (was 37179). 17 guide files changed, mostly
Midnight Leveling, Dungeons, Mounts and Pets content, plus Events and the Cataclysm Alliance
leveling guide. None were added or removed.

No viewer or engine code changed in either addon.
Install
• WowUp (2.24.0-beta.6 or later): choose Install from URL, enter

Validation
• py -3 build.py all: tooling tests, both flavors' Lua 5.1 offline suites and package
dependency checks passed.
• py -3 build.py --verify-release dist: checksums and release metadata verified.
• Retail guide sync: no Zygor branding left after renaming.
• Forever: the 208 unchanged upstream files come out byte-identical to the previous import
after renaming, which confirms the renaming step.
Known limitations
• These builds have not been tested in game yet.
• Two changed Retail guides use features the engine doesn't support yet: the step keyword
family in the Midnight achievements guide and GetCurrentTitle in the events guide. Neither
category ships in GoatQuestRetail, so this has no effect in game.
• Retail guides need the user's own subscription data. It is not included in the ZIP; see the
Retail LICENCE-USAGE.md.

addons.description:
GoatWay 1.0.0
In-world waypoints and navigation for WoW Forever (Interface 16001), in the GoatQuest look.
GoatWay marks your destination in the world, points the way when it is off screen, and follows
GoatQuest's guide arrow. It is based on Waypoint UI 1.7.3 by AdaptiveX, rebranded and restyled.
First launch
1. GoatWay lives next to GoatQuest in Interface/AddOns/GoatWay. Fully exit and restart WoW so
the new folder is found, then enable GoatWay (Forever).
2. If Waypoint UI is also installed, disable it. Both draw a marker for the same destination;
GoatWay says so in chat if it finds Waypoint UI enabled.
3. /gw (or /goatway) opens the settings, also under Options → AddOns → GoatWay.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /gw | Opens the settings. |
| /gw clear | Clears the destination. |
| /gw arrow, /gw halo | Picks the Navigator (the same words as GoatQuest's /gqviewer). |
| /way [name] | Sets a destination on your map. /way # [name] for another map. When TomTom is loaded, /way is TomTom's. |
What you see
• Waypoint (far away): a flat diamond in the accent with the destination's icon, a thin beam,
and under it the name in the text colour, the distance in the accent and the arrival time muted.
• Pinpoint (close, within 100 yds on Forever): a GoatQuest card (ink, 1px hairline, the accent
rule along its top) with the objectives or description, and three chevrons flowing down to the spot.
• Navigator: Arrow, a GoatQuest chevron orbiting the destination's icon at the screen edge
when the destination is off screen; or Halo, GoatQuest's ring at your character's feet whose
notch points toward the destination with the distance beside it. On arrival the ring lights up
in the accent and says Here. For waypoints (GoatQuest's, /way, map pins, TomTom) the halo
points by your facing and the true bearing; for other destinations it points along the screen.

Quests take their kind's colour: ready to turn in in the accent, unfinished in soft grey,
repeatable in blue, important in lilac. Every icon is redrawn flat in GoatQuest's style.
With GoatQuest
GoatQuest is an optional dependency, so it loads first.
• Follow GoatQuest's Arrow (Extensions → GoatQuest, on by default): whatever GoatQuest's arrow
points at, the step's waypoint or the next leg of a travel route, becomes GoatWay's destination,
titled from the step and marked with the goat. A new place re-navigates; progress in the title
(3/8 boars) does not, so the marker's intro does not replay on every kill. Corpse arrows are left
to the game, and the mark clears when GoatQuest's arrow hides. Turn off Auto-Replace Waypoint
to be asked before GoatQuest replaces something else you are tracking (once per place).
• Accent (Appearance → Colour): Match GoatQuest, the default, uses the GoatQuest viewer's
accent, its class colour or your custom colour, and follows it when you change it there. Without
GoatQuest it is GoatQuest gold. Also Class Colour, GoatQuest Gold or Custom.
• Halo: uses the ring position you set with GoatQuest's movers (**Use GoatQuest's Ring
Position), or its own Ring Height**. While GoatQuest's own halo is on screen, GoatWay's steps
aside so only one ring shows.
The design
GoatWay uses GoatQuest's tokens (packages/goatway-style, matching GoatQuest's
Skins/Default/GoatQuest/Style.lua): flat surfaces, square corners, 1px hairlines, no bevels or glows
on panels, and one accent.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Ink | #0F1115 | Sidebar, pinpoint card, marker fill |
| Slate | #15181D | Settings content |
| Ridge | #1B1F25 | Dialogs, menus |
| Hairline | white 7% | Borders, dividers |
| Text / Soft / Muted / Dim | #ECEAE6 #C5C8CD #8D939C #6F757E | Text by importance |
| Gold | #F5BF29 | The settings accent, primary buttons, checks |

Type is GoatQuest's: Archivo for text (SemiBold for names and headings), Archivo Narrow for
distances and times, and Atkinson Hyperlegible Bold for the halo's distance. They are the default…

Gold Forever0.16.1 (2026-10-25)
• Text takes the same room in every look. Web and Arcane size their text so a line is as wide as in
Classic, measured in game against Friz Quadrata at login. The Scan tab's "Scan when I open the auction
house" no longer runs out of the panel in Web.
0.16.0 (2026-10-25)
The auction house tools and a new window. Gold Forever gets a panel beside the auction house (scan, post,
shop, cancel undercut, rules and sale profiles), a hub window with pages for your money, characters,
crafting, sessions and rares, three looks to choose from, a session HUD, and more in your tooltips.
The auction house
• A panel beside the auction house (/gf ah hides or brings it back). Its Buy, Sell and Auctions tabs
follow Blizzard's and move them. It opens on Scan when a full scan may start, else on the tab
Blizzard's window shows. Prices show gold and
silver, as the auction house sets them.
• Scan: the full scan made visible: asking, reading N of M, the cooldown and the last result. A
scan starts when you press Scan now, or by itself on opening if you switch "Scan when I open the
auction house" on.
After a scan, one chat line names your list items now listed at or under your price.
• Sell: the items in your bags the auction house takes, each priced by your rule against the
cheapest listing by someone else, with the reason (Undercut, No one else, Normal price, At floor,
Under your floor). The floor and normal price are measured against the item's 7-day average where
the shared prices have one, so a day's dip does not move them. An item held under your floor can be
posted anyway at the undercut price, on a second press. Click Post or press Space; it waits for the
server, then moves to the next item. A price under
vendor value or far under the market asks for a second press. The duration and the quantity you
choose are remembered for each item. Alt-click an item in your bags to choose it; its tooltip says
what Post would ask.
• Buy: a shopping list's items with what can be bought at your price; click one to see its
listings. Buy next asks the auction house for the price and a second press buys; a price more
than 10% above the deal is named first. Edit lists › opens the Shopping lists page.
• Auctions: checks your auctions against other players' listings and cancels the most undercut
one a press, past your tolerance (5% at first), showing the cancel cost. Click one to see its
listings in Blizzard's window.
• Shopping lists, a page of the window (Trading → Shopping lists): make, rename, delete, import and
export lists (GFL1: strings); add an item by dropping it on the slot or shift-clicking it anywhere;
for each, the most you pay (under market, a fixed price, or a share of the market value) and how many
you want in all, bags and bank counted. Lowest, ask over % is for what you need (raid consumables):
Buy next buys the cheapest first, and above your share of the market value it asks before buying, so
you can choose something cheaper instead. The craft queue's list is there too, its prices set the same way.
• Selling rules, a page of the window (Trading → Selling rules; Rule › on the Sell tab opens it
for the item in view): undercut by 1 silver or a percentage, a floor and a normal price as shares of
the market value, and hold or post at the floor, each with a line saying what it does, and beside them
what the rule does to an item worth 10g. Rule for adds a rule for one item or a whole category.
Sale profiles (GFP1: strings, made at gold-forever.app/me/lists or shared by others) price the
items they name: keep this many, undercut, a fixed price or a point in the supply, with a floor; their
buy rules become a list in the Buy tab.
• With the companion app, lists and profiles you keep on gold-forever.app come into the game (the
newer edit wins).
• Prices are whole silver unless the auction house takes copper (the addon asks the game). One or two…

Gold Forever web app, which turns it into prices, ledgers and plans. The
addon only records; /gf export gives you the text to paste at gold-forever.app, or the
companion app uploads it for you.

It records your own characters and what you loot and scan, and never other players: auction
owners and bidders are not read. The web app's privacy page:

Gold Forever0.16.1 (2026-10-25)
• Text takes the same room in every look. Web and Arcane size their text so a line is as wide as in
Classic, measured in game against Friz Quadrata at login. The Scan tab's "Scan when I open the auction
house" no longer runs out of the panel in Web.
0.16.0 (2026-10-25)
The auction house tools and a new window. Gold Forever gets a panel beside the auction house (scan, post,
shop, cancel undercut, rules and sale profiles), a hub window with pages for your money, characters,
crafting, sessions and rares, three looks to choose from, a session HUD, and more in your tooltips.
The auction house
• A panel beside the auction house (/gf ah hides or brings it back). Its Buy, Sell and Auctions tabs
follow Blizzard's and move them. It opens on Scan when a full scan may start, else on the tab
Blizzard's window shows. Prices show gold and
silver, as the auction house sets them.
• Scan: the full scan made visible: asking, reading N of M, the cooldown and the last result. A
scan starts when you press Scan now, or by itself on opening if you switch "Scan when I open the
auction house" on.
After a scan, one chat line names your list items now listed at or under your price.
• Sell: the items in your bags the auction house takes, each priced by your rule against the
cheapest listing by someone else, with the reason (Undercut, No one else, Normal price, At floor,
Under your floor). The floor and normal price are measured against the item's 7-day average where
the shared prices have one, so a day's dip does not move them. An item held under your floor can be
posted anyway at the undercut price, on a second press. Click Post or press Space; it waits for the
server, then moves to the next item. A price under
vendor value or far under the market asks for a second press. The duration and the quantity you
choose are remembered for each item. Alt-click an item in your bags to choose it; its tooltip says
what Post would ask.
• Buy: a shopping list's items with what can be bought at your price; click one to see its
listings. Buy next asks the auction house for the price and a second press buys; a price more
than 10% above the deal is named first. Edit lists › opens the Shopping lists page.
• Auctions: checks your auctions against other players' listings and cancels the most undercut
one a press, past your tolerance (5% at first), showing the cancel cost. Click one to see its
listings in Blizzard's window.
• Shopping lists, a page of the window (Trading → Shopping lists): make, rename, delete, import and
export lists (GFL1: strings); add an item by dropping it on the slot or shift-clicking it anywhere;
for each, the most you pay (under market, a fixed price, or a share of the market value) and how many
you want in all, bags and bank counted. Lowest, ask over % is for what you need (raid consumables):
Buy next buys the cheapest first, and above your share of the market value it asks before buying, so
you can choose something cheaper instead. The craft queue's list is there too, its prices set the same way.
• Selling rules, a page of the window (Trading → Selling rules; Rule › on the Sell tab opens it
for the item in view): undercut by 1 silver or a percentage, a floor and a normal price as shares of
the market value, and hold or post at the floor, each with a line saying what it does, and beside them
what the rule does to an item worth 10g. Rule for adds a rule for one item or a whole category.
Sale profiles (GFP1: strings, made at gold-forever.app/me/lists or shared by others) price the
items they name: keep this many, undercut, a fixed price or a point in the supply, with a floor; their
buy rules become a list in the Buy tab.
• With the companion app, lists and profiles you keep on gold-forever.app come into the game (the
newer edit wins).
• Prices are whole silver unless the auction house takes copper (the addon asks the game). One or two…

addons.description:
Forever Game Suit is a campfire arcade addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001).

It adds four short minigames built around campfire downtime while keeping the presentation close to the native WoW Forever client. The addon deliberately prefers Blizzard/Forever frames, fonts, buttons, icons and UI textures instead of generic custom fantasy artwork.

> Current version: 3.5.0

📦 Download Forever Game Suit v3.5.0
•
Release notes
Interface preview
The hub, highscores and options stay inside the same compact Blizzard-style window so the addon feels like one coherent part of the WoW Forever UI.
GamesPolymorph Chicken Run
Run, jump and survive the campfire timer while the route becomes increasingly chaotic.
• Bombs, rockets and meteors
• Event waves and recognizable hazard patterns
• Near-miss and combo bonuses
• Power-ups
• Layered scrolling scenery
• Final Meltdown phase
Murloc Lotus Hunt
Guide a growing Murloc through the bog while collecting Lotus flowers and avoiding hazards.
• Lotus streak system
• Golden Lotus bonuses
• Connected growing Murloc body
• Bog hazards and warning phases
• Increasing speed and difficulty
• Final Hunt phase
Gnomeregan Block-Matrix
A Gnomeregan-themed falling-block minigame with modern quality-of-life features.
• Ghost piece
• Hard Drop
• Hold piece
• Three-piece preview
• 7-bag generation
• Combos and Back-to-Back bonuses
• Lock delay and wall kicks
• Hold A / D for continuous movement
• Pressure, Overdrive and Meltdown phases
Goblin Circuit Breaker
A Goblin-engineering Arrow Jam puzzle. Remove directional components only when their escape path is clear.
• Solvable randomized boards
• Frozen components
• Repair nodes
• Golden bonus arrows
• Combo scoring
• Increasing puzzle density and difficulty
Campfire Arcade
The default round lasts 60 seconds and can be changed from the built-in Options panel.

While a minigame is active, the addon captures the relevant movement keys so your character remains seated at the campfire. ESC pauses and resumes the current game.
Highscores
Each game keeps its own highscore. Forever Game Suit also supports guild score sharing so guild members can compare results.

Your own highscores can be reset from Options → Maintenance. A confirmation dialog prevents accidental resets.
Options
Options stay directly inside the Forever Game Suit hub and use native WoW-style controls.

Current settings include:
• Game sounds
• Round duration
• Highscore reset
• Addon version/status information
Controls
Controls are shown on each game's start screen. Common controls include:
• A / D — movement
• SPACE — jump / hard drop depending on the game
• E — hold piece in Block-Matrix
• ESC — pause / resume
Opening the addon
Use any of the following:
• /fgs
• Minimap button
• AddOn Compartment

Useful commands:
• /fgs status — show addon/campfire status
• /fgs debug — toggle debug messages

addons.description:
A fast, lightweight macro-icon search and filter addon for WoW: Forever.

Instead of scrolling through thousands of macro icons, Macro Icon Search adds a search field and quick filters directly to the normal macro icon picker.

> Current stable version: 2.10.3
> Embedded Forever icon set: 27,714 icons

Deutsche Beschreibung
Before / AfterBefore
Default WoW: Forever macro icon picker.
After
Macro Icon Search adds a search bar, color filters, class filters, profession filters, and fast browsing directly inside the macro icon picker.
Features
• Fast text search for icon filenames, e.g. fire, sword, shadow, bear
• Real pixel-color filters based on offline icon-image analysis
• 13 color filters: Red, Orange, Yellow, Gold, Green, Cyan, Blue, Purple, Pink, Brown, Black, Gray, White
• Color strength levels: broad, strong (!), dominant (!!)
• Class filters: Warrior, Paladin, Hunter, Rogue, Priest, Shaman, Mage, Warlock, Druid
• Profession filters: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Herbalism, Leatherworking, Mining, Skinning, Tailoring, Cooking, Fishing, First Aid, Jewelcrafting
• Combine filters with AND logic
• Right-click reset for individual quick filters
• Mouse-wheel page navigation through filtered results
• Works with the normal All Icons / Spells / Items selector
• English and German UI
• Optimized to avoid large FPS drops while searching/filtering
How it worksText search
Most normal text searches use a pre-generated 2-/3-character filename index.

Instead of scanning all 27,714 icons for every search, the addon first narrows the search to a much smaller candidate set and then verifies only those icons.

addons.description:
FishingForever is a lightweight, quality-of-life fishing addon for WoW Forever. It streamlines casting, managing lures, and alt-tabbing so you never miss a catch!
Features
• Double-Right-Click to Fish: Forget about dragging the Fishing skill to your action bars! Simply double-right-click anywhere while you have a fishing pole equipped to cast your line.
• Smart Lure Menu: When you don't have a lure applied, the addon automatically detects all fishing lures in your bags and presents a beautifully styled, modern interactive menu right at your cursor.
• Click any lure in the menu to instantly apply it to your pole.
• Don't want to use a lure right now? Click the "Ignore" (cross) button to hide the menu and fish without lures for the next 5 minutes.
• Background Sound Automation: Automatically enables background sound while fishing (perfect for alt-tabbing), and restores your previous setting when you stop.
Usage
• Equip a fishing pole.
• Double Right-Click to start fishing.
• If a lure is required, select one from the popup menu.
• Options Panel: Configure the addon settings from the WoW AddOns Options panel.

addons.description:
Addon, grafica e backup per World of Warcraft: Forever, in un unico programma Windows.

Scarica l'ultima versione
• Catalogo addon con ricerca, download e fonti dichiarate; installazioni e aggiornamenti solo su richiesta.
• Preset per funzione: Avventura in italiano, Interfaccia e comodità, Dungeon e progressione, Guide e social.
• Profili e controlli grafici con anteprima, backup e verifiche per la specifica build.
• Rilevamento del client cambiato e controlli automatici delle versioni Blizzard/ForeverTools, configurabili separatamente.

Estrai lo ZIP e avvia ForeverTools.exe. Per aggiornare una copia esistente, chiudi l'app e sostituisci l'EXE nella stessa cartella. Conserva l'eventuale file di accesso separato.

Dalla 0.2.3, i preset mantengono gli addon da gestire manualmente con motivo e pagina ufficiale.

I download pubblici non contengono chiavi API. Le copie già configurate vengono consegnate separatamente come un solo EXE; un successivo EXE pubblico conserva l’accesso locale già predisposto. L'accesso CurseForge deve essere autorizzato e viene configurato separatamente; le funzioni grafiche non richiedono una chiave. Il programma non aggiorna automaticamente il gioco o gli addon. Supporta i canali Forever ufficiale e beta; la disponibilità di una patch Blizzard non equivale alla verifica grafica in gioco di quella build.

Le raccolte non sono classifiche o configurazioni dell'interfaccia da importare e non attestano che tutti gli addon funzionino insieme. I dati di popolarità identificano la fonte; i download complessivi WoW non sono presentati come download esclusivi Forever.

Le licenze applicabili sono incluse nel pacchetto. ForeverTools è indipendente e non è affiliato o approvato da Blizzard Entertainment, Overwolf o CurseForge.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for WoW: Forever, Classic Era and Retail. It puts the damage (or healing) of each spell on your action buttons and adds a line or two to the spell tooltip. The numbers come from the spell's own description, in English or German, whichever each text is in; an optional estimate adds your spell power, at the share the game's own spell data gives each spell on WoW: Forever and Classic Era (Classic's coefficient rules for a spell the data does not cover), and says so. Debuffs that lower the enemy's damage or attack power, such as Curse of Weakness or Demoralizing Shout, show the reduction in red ("-3", "-10%"). A lower attack power shows what it takes off each hit of your target, "-7" for -50 attack power on a target that attacks every 2 seconds (14 attack power are 1 damage per second of its attack speed), or "-50 AP" while that speed is not known, as in combat on a target you had not selected before.

Abilities that hit with your weapon (Heroic Strike, Maul, Claw, Shred, Sinister Strike, Aimed Shot and the like) show their potential damage in blue: your weapon's average hit, times the ability's percentage, plus its bonus. Spells that raise attack power (Battle Shout, Rockbiter Weapon, Blessing of Might, Seal of the Crusader, Bear and Cat Form, Aspect of the Hawk) show what they add to each hit, as "+103". Both are estimates from your weapon's numbers, read out of combat, and the tooltip says so; /sdi weapon off turns them off. /sdi misses lists the spells on your bars that give no number, which is the list to send when something is missing.

Seals show what they add to every hit (Seal of Righteousness and Flametongue Weapon, whose texts give a range for all weapon speeds, at your weapon's speed), and Judgement shows the damage of the seal that is active. Effects that trigger by chance (Windfury, Seal of Command, Seal of Light, poisons, Frostbrand) show what one trigger does, and the tooltip gives the chance. Shields show what they absorb (in purple), finishers their damage at five combo points with the other points in the tooltip, and totems, Lay on Hands, Execute and Mana Burn what their descriptions work out to (a totem's or trap's number gets no spell power estimate: it is the totem's own spell, which the data does not name). /sdi dump writes your spellbook's descriptions, as your client shows them, to the saved variables, for testing; /sdi dump all does the same for every class's abilities.

The pet bar shows the pet's spells too (the Imp's Firebolt, for example), with the numbers from the description only, since the pet has its own spell power.

The numbers are drawn on Blizzard's own action bars, the pet bar and Forever's Totem Bar. Bars from Bartender4, ElvUI and other addons built on LibActionButton get none (/sdi status says so when one is loaded); the tooltip lines work with them all the same.

On Retail, whose descriptions already include your stats, the numbers are the descriptions' own: the spell power estimate and the weapon arithmetic are off there.

The addon's interface language (labels, chat messages, number formatting) can be switched independently of the game language via the settings window or /sdi lang auto|en|de. Auto follows the game's language.

Install: unzip SpellDamageInfo-0.7.3.zip into Interface\AddOns of your game folder (_classic_beta_ for Forever, _classic_era_ for Classic Era, retail for Retail), then restart the game: a new addon folder is only picked up at start. Type /sdi (or open Options > AddOns > SpellDamageInfo) for the settings window, with a live preview of the numbers on a sample button; /sdi help lists the commands, such as the size (/sdi size 50-200) and place (/sdi position bottom|center|top) of the numbers.

Inspired by DrDamage by Gagorian. The options window is adapted from DoesItDie by Joe Greive (MIT). Licence: MIT (see LICENSE).

addons.changelog:
Forever 0.9.89 / Retail 0.9.102-retail

Syncs the cast prediction tables with WoW: Forever build 1.60.1.70753 (the live build before launch; read from the client's DB2 tables) and Blizzard's launch notes of 3 Nov. Spell numbers that come from tooltips update by themselves.
• Arcane Blast: its buff is now 12% of Intellect as spell power per stack, which the spell power API already holds, so the +10% a stack multiplier is removed. Arcane Blast's own spell coefficient follows the new client data (0.714 to 0.429).
• Lava Burst (the +20% against Flame Shock, Call of Flame) and Piercing Ice are removed together with the spell and the talent.
• Fire Power is held back: it is now 3% per Fire effect on the target, up to 12%, and counting those effects is not read yet.
• Ice Barrier: Frigid Power (+15% Frost for a minute) and the shield's own +5% are read, on Forever only. Power in Light also counts Shadow Word: Pain. Fingers of Frost is x4 (still not applied until verified).
• Shadow and Flame stays at the client's 2% a point. Blizzard announced 4% for launch; it is added once a build or a live description shows it.
• Retail behaviour is unchanged; its package only carries the version bump and the shared files.

Verification: compiled both packages under Lua 5.1, ran a mock of the aura and talent tables, checked the regenerated coefficient table against the repo file entry by entry, and had the change reviewed twice by an independent hostile review. Both ZIPs were verified against source. Not tested in game.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload (a full restart for new files). SHA-256 checksums are attached.
addons.description:
Settings support native gamepads and ConsolePort. Assign Open settings under Options → Key Bindings → AddOns → Useful Plates and Tooltips. LB/RB switches module tabs, the D-pad selects controls, A / Cross activates the selected control, left/right adjusts sliders and B / Circle closes the window. The gold outline shows focus and scrolls into view. With ConsolePort active, its interface cursor and configured hints handle navigation.

It shows DoT marks, shields and range on nameplates, damage and healing numbers on action buttons, and item comparisons in tooltips. Every part can be switched off.

Build the Forever ZIP with python tools/build_zip.py, or the Retail ZIP with python tools/build_zip.py --retail. Packages are written to dist/ and checked against the source files.

Modules are maintained directly in Modules/. The remaining tools regenerate stat weights (make_weights.py, using tools/data/) and textures (make_resource_textures.py, make_ui_textures.py).
DoTInfo
Shows the damage your DoTs or Bleeds still have to deal as a marker on the target's health bar. If the target's health ends inside the marker, a skull on the portrait says the DoTs will kill it. When you cast spell then it shows during cast time estimation how much it might do on target.

Nameplate marks use the visible health bar, with dedicated support for EllesmereUI and Platynator and a cached automatic search for other nameplate addons. If no visible bar is found, DoTInfo can still show the kill icon beside the nameplate when "Marker and kill icon" is enabled.

The same marker (and kill icon) can sit on your focus frame, Blizzard's or EllesmereUI's, for your DoTs on the focused enemy ("Show on focus frame" in the Nameplates tab); [@focus] casts go on the focus. In Forever's instances mob GUIDs are secret: DoTInfo then keeps each mob apart by its nameplate, so tab-dotting a pack works (needs enemy nameplates on). The kill icon can be up to 128 px.

Description parsing covers English, German, Spanish, French, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Chinese (simplified and traditional), after Does It Die; the non-German languages are from Forever's own tooltips and not yet verified on a client in those languages. Other unit frame addons: name their target, focus or player health bar (and a spot for the kill icon, and a nameplate bar the automatic search misses) under DoTInfo > Behavior, with a Pick button that takes the frame you click, or by /upt frame target ElvUF_Target.Health and /upt pick target. ShieldsInfo and HealPrediction use the same frames. A hidden replacement frame hides the marks with it; with nothing set, nothing changes. After Does It Die's custom frames. Threat Plates' health bar is found automatically (it hangs off WorldFrame, not the nameplate). Other addons can read the DoT numbers through the UsefulPlatesAndTooltips_DoTAPI global, see API.md.

/dotinfo check reads every spell in your spellbook and lists the ones whose text mentions seconds but gives no DoT (full texts go to the saved log), so a client in another language can show what is still unread. Parser failures are counted explicitly, with the spell id and original error in the saved log. In Forever, /dotinfo ticks (Behavior tab > View) lists the tick sizes learned from your casts next to what the tooltips predict. The check also keeps its findings in the saved settings (census, one entry per class, 80 of each at most): the unread texts, cut to 320 bytes, and the DoTs it read with the total and duration their text gave, to set against the learned tick sizes.

There are also shields and healing predictions...…

Forever 0.9.89 / Retail 0.9.102-retail

Syncs the cast prediction tables with WoW: Forever build 1.60.1.70753 (the live build before launch; read from the client's DB2 tables) and Blizzard's launch notes of 3 Nov. Spell numbers that come from tooltips update by themselves.

Forever 0.9.88 / Retail 0.9.101-retail
• Parse German and English food descriptions that restore a percentage of health and mana over time as percentage healing, not a flat healing amount. Flat-value item healing is unchanged.

Verification: exercised the real item parser and ComputeItem path with readable and hidden maximum-health values; compiled the changed Lua files and verified both ZIPs against source. Not yet confirmed in-game.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload. SHA-256 checksums are attached.

Forever 0.9.87 / Retail 0.9.100-retail
• Fix cast impact/calibration identity, stale overlays and nameplate recycling; keep hidden native healing values intact.
• Track targeted Renew, Rejuvenation, Regrowth, Riptide and Wild Growth estimates independently of SpellDamageInfo display settings. Different ranks refresh one effect instead of adding duplicates.
• Preserve readable healing power at login, equipment/player-aura changes and leaving combat, including when SpellDamageInfo is disabled. Fixes the first combat HoT losing its precombat bonus.
• Do not invent selected-target HoTs for Lightwell clicks, Tranquility/Mend Pet channels or conditional heals.
• Binding Heal uses the correct spell-power coefficient per recipient. Holy Shock, Penance and Holy Nova show both damage and healing labels. Dark Sacrifice shows health cost, mana gain and cost duration.
• Penance damage uses its described three-bolt schedule; the immediate bolt is already spent. Channel timing changes update remaining bolts; unknown linked coefficients are not invented.
• Correct DoT API snapshots, parser diagnostics, custom-frame resolution and passive quest reward eligibility.

Verification: compared 3052 EN/DE client descriptions and 6104 cast-view variants; exercised real Lua event handlers and before/after failure cases. All 52 Lua files compile under Lua 5.1; both ZIPs checked member-by-member against committed source. No unit-test files added.

Limitations: no in-game confirmation. HoT dispels, talent-modified healing and exact/group Wild Growth effects remain unverified or unsupported. Wild Growth is a linear estimate on the known primary target only. If healing power has never been readable this session, only description amounts are available. Native direct-heal projections are unchanged.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload. Settings are preserved. SHA-256 checksums are in SHA256SUMS.txt.

Forever 0.9.85 / Retail 0.9.98-retail

A Retail fix: the cast marker and the kill icon no longer promise the damage a physical shot loses to the target's armor.

CastPrediction (Retail)
• A Retail description holds your own numbers (spell power, talents) but not the target's armor, which takes a share off a direct physical hit and cannot be read for an enemy. The saved Retail log of a hunter shows it: Steady Shot read 86 and hit for 60, 61 and 60; read 101 and hit for 69; read 115 and hit for 80 and 81. That is 0.70 of the description every time (mean 0.698, spread 0.008), so the marker and the kill icon promised 30% more than the shot dealt.
• Retail now learns from non-crit direct physical hits, with the same running mean Forever uses (about nine hits' memory, shown pulled toward the description by two hits' worth). On Lua mocks that run the real Core.lua in Retail mode, a shot that reads 86 and hits for 60-61 shows 86 on the first cast, then 77, 73 and 69 on the second, third and fifth, 65 on the tenth and 63 from the twentieth. Casts of a spell whose hits never come within reach of the estimate (heavier armor than the learning window takes: under about 0.65) are tallied; /upt castpred learned lists them.
• Magic is not reduced by armor and stays as the description says: nothing is learned from it on Retail. Forever is unchanged (every school learns, as before).
• Learn from hits (/upt cast) switches it off; Reset forgets what was learned. The learned factors are shared by every character of the account.

DoTInfo
• The log of unread descriptions (kept to help clients in other languages) skips texts without a number: a DoT's text always has one, and lines like "Summon a chauffeur" pushed useful lines out of the 500-line log.

What was looked at on Retail and needed nothing
• The saved BugGrabber errors: four, none from this addon.
• A rogue run in the DoTInfo log (Garrote, then Rupture at 5 combo points; both estimates ran down together and were removed once the target was out of combat and no longer carried them): nothing in it looks wrong.
• The 47 German texts the action bar numbers once could not read: the current parser reads the three that carry an amount of your own damage or healing (Rupture, Crimson Vial, Recuperate); the other 44 are utility, crowd control, defensive cooldowns given in percent, pet heals as a share of the pet's health and a healthstone item.

What is not verified
• The armor learning has not been seen in the game; it was checked with Lua mocks that drive the real Core.lua in Retail and Forever mode, and the 0.70 comes from one hunter's saved log (six hits). Spells that hit several times, and pets or auto attacks of the same school landing within the 1.5 s window of a cast, can pull a factor the way they can on Forever.
• No unit tests were created or modified; every TOC-listed file compiles under Lua 5.1 (91 across the two packages).

Replace the whole UsefulPlatesAndTooltips folder (Forever ZIP for _classic_beta_, Retail ZIP for retail) and restart the game or /reload. Settings are preserved. SHA-256 checksums are in SHA256SUMS.txt.

Forever 0.9.84 / Retail 0.9.97-retail

A fix for how CastPrediction learns, health regeneration from Spirit in item tooltips, and two commands that read what this client reports into the saved file.

CastPrediction (Forever)
• The learned factor now settles on the right value. Each hit was compared with the prediction after it had been scaled by the factor learned so far, and that ratio was blended into the factor, so the factor converged on the square root of the truth: a spell that really hits for 80% of its tooltip ended at 0.89. The saved data of one Forever character shows it exactly: Immolate always hit for 22 against a tooltip of 24, and its stored factor was 0.95745, the square root of 22/24 (0.95743), not 0.917. A factor is now the running mean of what each hit says it should have been, shown pulled toward 1 by two hits' worth so one roll of a wide damage range does not swing the marker. With the "min" or "max" estimate the hit used to be compared with the shown value (one end of the range) and taught a false shift; it is compared with the middle of the range now.
• On Lua mocks that drive the real Core.lua (old against new), the marker's error fell from 8.4% to 2.4% (steady, spread of 15%), from 7.4% to 2.1% (a factor drifting by 30%) and from 7.4% to 5.1% (a mob type change every 25 casts), and is level with the old code at a change every 12 casts (8.3% against 8.0%). It follows short bursts a little worse: an effect that adds 30% to 5 casts in 20 gave 8.7% against 6.2%. The factor's memory is about nine hits.
• Factors saved by earlier versions hold the square root: they are squared once on first load and count as five hits, so the marker is right within a few casts.
• A cast whose damage came within reach of the estimate but never matched it (a factor too far from 1 for the learning window), and a hit that matched but fell outside the window, are tallied per spell. /upt castpred learned lists the learned factors with their hits and that tally, so a spell that never learns shows. A resisted cast that lands while a DoT of the same school ticks is also tallied once: the one false count known.

StatsInfo (Forever)
• A Spirit line in the tooltip now also gives health per 5 seconds out of combat, worked out the way the character sheet's Spirit tooltip does it (GetHealthRegenFromSpirit, standing). A warrior or rogue, who has no mana and saw nothing for Spirit before, sees it; casters see it beside the mana line. It takes the regeneration to be proportional to Spirit, as the mana figure is; that was not measured for health. /upt probe now records the regeneration answers of the client, so they can be checked from the saved file.
• Mana regeneration from Spirit was already read from the client, so it is right for every class. The probes saved on Forever (levels 1 to 12, seven mana classes) show a quarter of a mana per second per point of Spirit in nine of the ten readable ones (one druid read double, probably a buff), the same for every class, not the per-class table of the old game. That table may still appear past level 20, where the old game's flat bonus to early-level regeneration ends; the figure is read live, so it follows.

Commands that keep what the client says, only when asked
• /upt castpred census reads the whole talent tree with each talent's live text into the saved settings and marks the talents with a percent next to damage or healing that the curated lists do not use; /upt castpred census clear removes it.
• /dotinfo check also keeps its findings (the DoTs it read with the total and duration each text gave, and the texts nothing reads) in the saved settings, one entry per class.
• Neither runs by itself and nothing is kept until one is used.

Other
• ## Notes-deDE: the AddOns list shows the description in German on a German client (after Does It Die's pull request #21).

What is not verified…
