addons.description:
Your action bars follow you to the highest spell rank you know.

Forever has Vanilla-style spell ranks on the Retail client. Train Frostbolt rank 4 and the button on your bar still casts rank 3 until you drag the new one over. This addon does the drag for you, out of combat, every time you learn something.

Contents
Highlights · How it works · Quick start · Commands · Development · Beta note · Repository map · Credits · Support · License

For contributors: CONTRIBUTING.md · CHANGELOG.md

Highlights
• 🔼 Always the top rank - Every spell button on every bar is checked a few seconds after login and again whenever you learn a spell. A button holding an old rank is replaced in place.
• 🎮 Gamepad UI too - The game's Gamepad UI (Alpha) keeps its own bars in action slots above the normal 180; those are upgraded the same way.
• 🛡️ Only ever upgrades - The client is asked for the highest rank by name, then the spellbook is cross-checked. A swap happens only when the new rank is strictly higher and known to you.
• ⚔️ Combat-safe - Nothing moves while you are fighting; the scan waits for combat to end. Macros, items and empty slots are never touched, and a scan waits if you are dragging something.
• 💬 Says what it did - One chat line per spell, such as Demon Armor -> Rank 3 (2 buttons). Turn it off with /asr report off.
• 🪶 One file, no settings window - Two toggles, both on by default, controlled from chat.

Name-based macros such as /cast Demon Armor already cast the highest rank on their own. This addon covers plain spell buttons dragged from the spellbook.
How it works
• Triggers - Three seconds after login, and one second after any spell-learned event (LEARNED_SPELL_IN_SKILL_LINE, or its older name, plus SPELLS_CHANGED). /asr scan runs it on demand.
• Rank lookup - C_Spell.GetSpellInfo(name) returns what /cast name would cast. If that answer is missing, the same rank, or lower, the spellbook is scanned for every entry with that name and the highest non-low-rank entry wins. Rank numbers come from C_Spell.GetSpellSkillLineAbilityRank, with the "Rank N" subtext as fallback.
• Swap - Pick up the new rank, confirm the cursor holds a spell, place it on the slot, clear the cursor. If PlaceAction throws, the addon prints one line and disables itself for the session rather than retrying.
• Guards - Every value that could be a secret passes through issecretvalue before it is compared. Every C_* call is checked for existence first.
Quick start
1. Install:
• CurseForge app - pick the Forever flavour and search for Auto Spell Ranks, or
• Manual - copy the AutoSpellRanks folder into World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\, or
• Development - run .\install.ps1 to link this repo's AutoSpellRanks folder into the game (-Copy to copy instead, -Path for another install).
2. Start the game and tick Auto Spell Ranks on the AddOns screen.
3. Play. Type /asr to see the status line.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| /asr | Show whether upgrades and chat reports are on |
| /asr on, /asr off | Enable or disable automatic upgrades |
| /asr report on\|off | Print a chat line for each swap, or stay quiet |
| /asr scan | Scan the bars now and print a summary |
| /asr debug | List what each button on screen holds, saved to AutoSpellRanksDB.debug on /reload |
| /asr help | List the commands |

/autospellranks works the same as /asr.

addons.description:
Quality of life for World of Warcraft: Forever, from one settings window.

Sells greys, loots instantly, accepts and hands in quests, repairs, combines bags, and marks the best quest reward. Twelve small modules behind a purple star on the minimap, each one a tick you can turn off.

Contents
Highlights · Modules · Architecture · Quick start · Commands · Development · Beta note · Repository map · Credits · Support · License

For contributors: CONTRIBUTING.md · CHANGELOG.md

Highlights
• 💰 Vendors - Greys are sold the moment a vendor opens, gear is repaired, and chat tells you what it cost or earned.
• 📜 Quests - Accept, hand in, and take the follow-up without clicking. Low-level quests are skipped, the best reward is framed in gold, and a note at the bottom of the window explains anything left for you.
• 🎁 Loot - Everything is taken the instant loot is ready. Optionally leave the greys.
• ⚔️ Combat - A main-hand swing timer under your portrait for melee classes, pet-attack macros so a pet charges when a cast starts, and bar buttons that follow you to the highest spell rank.
• 🎒 Interface - One combined bag with a one-click sort, clean icons without macro names, wider camera zoom, and the beta Issue Reporter tucked away.
• ⚙️ One dialog - A sidebar for Vendors, Quests, Loot, Combat and Interface, with search across every setting. Each feature is a collapsible card with its on/off switch in the header, and the finer settings open under a chevron. Help shows in tooltips. Options for other classes (pet macros, swing timer) stay out of the way unless you turn on Other classes. /mm, the minimap star, or Options > AddOns > MooseMode opens it. Hold Shift at an NPC or vendor to skip automation once.
• 💾 Beta-proof settings - The beta client does not load saved variables yet, so settings are also backed up in an account macro and restored at login.
Modules
| Module | Group | What it does | Default |
| ------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Auto Sell | Vendors | Sells every grey item when a vendor opens, using the game's sell-all. Optional chat summary. | on |
| Auto Repair | Vendors | Repairs all gear at repair vendors. Sub-options: guild funds when allowed, cost in chat. | on |
| Auto Quest | Quests | Accepts quests, hands in completed ones, picks up follow-ups, picks the only gossip option, and can share accepted quests with your party. Skips low-level quests (grey only, or green and grey). Debug log to chat. | on |
| Quest Rewards | Quests | Vendor value on each reward choice. | on |
| Quest Lists | Quests | A line at the bottom of NPC quest windows names what Auto Quest left for you and why. | on |
| Quest Announce | Quests | Questie-style group chat lines: finished objectives and quest-starting items (on); accepted, abandoned, turned in (off). Party, raid, both or off; optional copy in your own chat. | on |
| Fast Loot | Loot | Takes every slot the instant loot is ready. Sub-option: leave grey items. Takes over the game's auto-loot setting while on. | on |
| Fishing | Professions | One toggle (/mm fish, the MooseFish macro, or a dialog button): pole in, Fishing on button 1. Press 1 to cast and press it again when the bobber splashes. Toggle again to get your weapons and button back. | on |
| Pet Attack | Combat | Creates one macro per damage spell with /petattack in front. Shown for Hunters and Warlocks; other classes see it (with an "only on pet classes" switch) under Other classes. | off |
| Spell Ranks | Combat | Swaps bar buttons holding an old rank for the highest one you know. Sub-option: report swaps in chat. | on |…

LibAboutPanel-2.0
LibAboutPanel-2.0 is a World of Warcraft Lua library for displaying addon metadata in Blizzard's Settings UI or as an AceConfig-3.0-compatible options table. It works with all valid WoW clients.
Requirements
• Required: LibStub
• Optional: AceConfig-3.0, if using :AboutOptionsTable()
Quick Usage
For Ace3 addons, embed LibAboutPanel-2.0 when creating your addon object:

For non-Ace3 addons, embed the library into your addon object:

Or use it directly:

Create a Blizzard Settings About panel:

Create an AceConfig-3.0-compatible About options table:

AboutOptionsTable() only returns the table. Your addon is responsible for registering it with AceConfig-3.0 or embedding it in an existing options table.
Documentation
See WIKI.md for:
• .pkgmeta integration
• Ace3 example usage
• API reference
• Supported .toc fields
• Category and localization notes
• Troubleshooting

Copyright and Date, itIT Copyright and Repository). The shim stored the
boolean, so GetVersion's gsub and GetLicense's concatenation raised errors on
those clients for any addon with a Version or X-License. A \_\_newindex now
stores the key for true, as AceLocale does.
Fixes #2

addons.description:
LibResInfo-2.0
LibResInfo-2.0 is a CLEU-free resurrection tracking library for World of Warcraft addons.

The library tracks:
• single-target resurrection casts
• mass resurrection casts
• resurrection targets becoming alive
• self-resurrection availability
• fastest resurrection resolution per target

Supported clients:
• Classic Era
• TBC Classic
• Wrath Classic
• Mists Classic
• Retail
• WoW Forever

Features
• No COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED dependency
• GUID-first tracking
• Fastest resurrection detection
• Multiple simultaneous resurrection casters per target
• Self-resurrection tracking
• CallbackHandler-1.0 support
• Ace3-style embedding

addons.changelog:
ForeverCompanionv2.8.0
• The step window reads like RestedXP: what you do at one place is grouped in a numbered box (every quest to hand in and to take at the same NPC together), one line per action with its icon (! to accept, ? to turn in, sword for objectives), the progress of each objective under its quest, then the NPC and the place.
• The current box is highlighted; the next ones are dimmed. Actions already done inside a box are ticked.
• Click a box: the arrow points to it. Right-click: mark its next action as done.
• New option: width of the step window (300 by default).
v2.7.0
• New Professions tab in the leveling guide (/fc lvl prof, or Professions in the minimap menu):
• The best profession pairs for your class (Skinning + Leatherworking, Mining + Blacksmithing or Engineering, Herbalism + Alchemy, Tailoring + Enchanting...) and why they go together.
• Leveling plan from 1 to 300 for Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Leatherworking, Tailoring, Cooking and First Aid: the cheapest recipe for each skill range, how many to craft, the materials and an estimated cost. Your current step is highlighted and the materials still needed from your skill are added up.
• Recipes come from the trainers; when a vendor recipe is cheaper, the vendor and its place are shown for your faction. Recipes with a cooldown or a reputation requirement are left out.
• Mining, Herbalism and Skinning: what to gather at each skill level and the zones to do it.
• Trainer ranks (Journeyman, Expert, Artisan) with the level they need.
v2.6.0
• Levels 1 to about 22: the leveling routes now follow the RestedXP Forever guides step by step, in their order, with quests grouped the way they do (accept everything around, do the objectives together, hand everything in at once). Credit: RXPGuides by RestedXP (https://github.com/RestedXP/RXPGuides), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; that part of the routes keeps this licence.
• Every race and class has its own version of these guides (Orcs and Trolls through Tirisfal Glades and Silverpine Forest like RestedXP, Hunters with their own start, Night Elves to Darkshore...). About 95 % of the RestedXP quests are kept; the others are missing from the Forever quest database or placed on the wrong continent in it.
• From about level 22 to 60 the route is still computed by the simulator, starting from where the RestedXP part ends.
v2.5.3
• Routes checked against tested leveling guides, quest by quest, for levels 1 to 22, and corrected:
• Orcs, Trolls and Tauren no longer take the boat to Tirisfal Glades at level 3-4: they level in Durotar or Mulgore up to 12, like every guide. No route crosses the sea before level 10.
• Every route now does its starting zone fully (all its quests) before moving on: Durotar, Mulgore, Tirisfal Glades up to 12, Elwynn Forest, Dun Morogh, Teldrassil up to 11, Zephras Isle up to 12.
• 20 quests the database refused to some races although they get them in game are now offered (Elwynn Forest chain from Rascally Rodents for Humans, Skyborne class quests...).
• A route chapter that ends with dungeons now shows the right levels.
v2.5.2
• /fc lvl > Leveling route: right-click a zone to see every step of it (quest, level, quest ID, NPC to talk to and place), to check a route before playing it. Click the first line to go back.
v2.5.1
• Quest requirements checked: a quest that needs a previous quest (all of a list, or one of several) is no longer shown to accept until that quest is turned in. When the route reaches a quest whose previous quest was passed, it passes it too and says in the chat which quest was missing (example: Aggressive Encroachment needs Aetheen of the Gales).
• The "quests around you" list uses the same requirements.
v2.5.0
• First time a leveling route is picked for a character, a window asks: follow it, choose another start in /fc lvl, or no thanks (the step window then shows the quests around you; /fc lvl to follow a route again).…
addons.description:
Le compagnon complet hors combat pour WoW Forever (le Classic+ officiel de Blizzard).
The complete out-of-combat companion for WoW Forever. English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and Russian.

WoW Forever applique les restrictions d'addons de Midnight : aucun addon ne peut lire le combat.
ForeverCompanion se concentre donc sur tout le reste : montée, routes d'XP, donjons et raids avec
taux de drop, rerolls, sacs, carte, campements, interface et sécurité.

Records every detail of your WoW Forever (client 1.60.x) journey for storytelling.

This is the Forever version. For Retail, see wow-storytracker-addon-retail.

Every session is recorded to SavedVariables with timestamps, zones, and details:

|----------|-------------------|
| Quests | Accepted, completed, abandoned — with names and levels |

| Levels | Your dings and your party members' dings |

| PvP | Honorable kills, battlegrounds, duels |

WoW Forever only (client 1.60.x, interface 16001). Does not work on Retail.

Forever installs as the _classic_beta_ client folder (Battle.net may list it

Added

Changed
• Positioning is now driven by SetAnchorType (called after Blizzard's own SetOwner) instead of passing the offset directly to SetOwner. This is what makes the new anchor-side options possible: offsets only actually take effect for ANCHOR_CURSOR_LEFT/ANCHOR_CURSOR_RIGHT on this client, not plain ANCHOR_CURSOR (the only anchor 0.1.x used) — so the offset setting never actually did anything before now. Default offset is 0, 0.

addons.description:
A tiny WoW addon that anchors the default game tooltip to the mouse cursor
instead of Blizzard's default lower-right corner. Built for WoW Forever
(the Classic beta, client flavor wow_classic_beta, version 1.60.x),
which doesn't offer this as a built-in option.
How it works
Blizzard's FrameXML routes almost all "default position" tooltips (action
bars, bags, character panel, quest log, merchant frame, etc.) through a
shared helper function, GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(tooltip, parent).
This addon uses hooksecurefunc to run after that helper and re-anchor
the tooltip to the cursor, using Blizzard's own native ANCHOR_CURSOR /
ANCHOR_CURSOR_LEFT / ANCHOR_CURSOR_RIGHT anchor types (applied via
SetAnchorType, never SetOwner). This gives continuous, zero-lag cursor
tracking straight from the engine with no per-frame Lua involvement — an
earlier manual SetPoint-based implementation was found (through testing)
to interfere with GameTooltip's own internal fade timer, causing unit
tooltips to visibly "stick" for about a second after the mouse moved away
before fading out.

It intentionally does not reassign the global function directly.
Forever taints the global itself when an addon replaces it, and every
later caller — including unrelated Blizzard code such as party/raid frame
updates — inherits that taint for its whole call chain, which then trips
Forever's new "secret value" protections (e.g. health-bar color
comparisons throwing errors). hooksecurefunc runs strictly after
Blizzard's own untainted call, so the original global is never
contaminated.

Tooltips deliberately anchored elsewhere on purpose (comparison tooltips,
contextual anchors next to a specific button, static minimap tooltips,
etc.) are left untouched — they don't go through the shared helper, and
there's no reliable way to tell "the default corner tooltip" apart from an
intentionally custom-positioned one just from the anchor type, so this
addon doesn't try to guess.

Auctioneer (profdumbbelldore's 12.x fork) made to run on the World of Warcraft: Forever beta client. Same nine addon folders, same features; only the calls the Forever client no longer has were changed (see the README on the forever branch for the full list).

Install: unzip, copy the nine folders into World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\, start the game fully (a /reload does not pick up new addon folders).

Beta client bug: builds 1.60.1.69913+ write addon SavedVariables but do not load them back at the next start (forever-bugs #34). Auctioneer's price history is SavedVariables, so it is forgotten at logout unless you use a workaround such as ForeverSVFix. Not something this release can fix.

Checked against Blizzard's Forever UI source for build 1.60.1.69977 (every file compiles, no removed API is called). In-game reports welcome in the issues.
addons.description:
The Auctioneer addon suite made to run on the WoW: Forever beta client. It is
profdumbbelldore's Auctioneer 12.x fork (itself a
continuation of Norganna's Auctioneer, official source
gitlab.com/norganna-wow/auctioneer, GPL v2 - see LICENSE) with the changes the
Forever client needs; the git history keeps the upstream commits. Nothing else is touched: the same nine addon folders, the
same features, the same settings.

Why a separate branch: Forever runs Blizzard's Mainline UI (the retail-style auction house) on the 12.1.5 API set.
Patch 12.1.5 removed the deprecated item functions that the 12.1.0 build still relies on (GetItemInfo,
GetItemQualityColor, GetDetailedItemLevelInfo, GetItemIcon), and the Forever client also has no
GetMouseFocus, MouseIsOver, UIParent_OnEvent, InterfaceOptionsFrame_OpenToCategory or NUM_ITEM_QUALITIES.
Each of those was a Lua error waiting to happen on Forever; on retail 12.1.0 they still work, which is why upstream
never saw them.

addons.description:
A minimap button that reloads your UI. One click, no typing.

Handy when a controller or bar addon breaks and you can't reach /reload:
the button sits on the minimap, independent of your action bars.
Usage
| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Left-click the minimap button | Reload the UI |

| /minireload hide / /minireload show | Hide or show the minimap button |

If another addon also registers /rl, whichever loads last owns it. Both
reload, so it doesn't matter.

addons.changelog:
Changelogv1.0.0 - 2026-10-12Changed
• Automatic /who scans now run at most every 10 seconds instead of every 5,
and the new option "Seconds between /who scans" lets you pick anything from
5 to 60 seconds.
• Chat announcements now default to the first player of each leaderboard only:
the global and class top N sliders start at 1, like the race one. Existing
installs keep the top N values they already have.
• The guild hears far less from the addon. The game client scrolls the chat
window for every addon message sent to the guild although the message itself
is never shown, so the addon now only announces itself to the guild at login
and about once an hour, to meet the guild members who run it. Dings and
leaderboards reach those members by whisper from then on, like they reach
every other player the addon traded with before. Before, every ding and a
sync round every 5 minutes went through the guild.
• The debug window lists at most 20 players of a received or sent batch, then
how many more it held.
• The realm channel is now the one place the addon syncs through, from login
on. The guild announce, the buddy whispers and the group sync only run when
the channel does not work: when the addon could not join it, or when its own
channel messages stop coming back for five minutes. They start the moment
that happens and stop again when the channel is back. Before, they ran next
to the channel until another addon user was heard on it, which on a quiet
realm or with the beta's chat lag meant most of the time.
• Level-ups spotted in the seconds between login and the channel join now wait
for the channel instead of going out by whisper.
Fixed
• Level-ups spotted in the first minute after joining the realm channel now
reach it. They wait that minute for the join sync and then went out as one
message; on a busy day that was hundreds of players, the game client's
channel throttle cut the message off and it was lost. They now go out 50
players at a time, a few seconds apart, and a message the channel throttle
refused is sent again after a longer pause.
v0.1.0-beta16 - 2026-10-10Changed
• The bundled compression library (LibCompress) is updated to r87 from its
new home on GitHub. Nothing changes in what the addon sends; a damaged
compressed message is now dropped instead of raising an error.
v0.1.0-beta15 - 2026-10-10Changed
• The zone sync at login, the beacon that announced your leaderboards to the
zone every minute and the shout of every new level to the zone are gone: the
game client refuses addon messages to the zone (a yell), so none of them ever
reached anybody. Logging in no longer waits 5 seconds for zone answers that
could never come; the guild sync, the realm channel and the players your addon
traded with before carry the data as before.
Fixed
• Turning sharing on after logging in with it off now starts the sync right
away. Before, the addon stayed quiet until the next login.
v0.1.0-beta14 - 2026-10-02Added
• The addon tells you when a newer version is out on CurseForge. Players who
already updated let the others know, so from this version on you get one
line in chat per session, and the options window and the minimap tooltip
name the new version until you update.
Fixed
• Leaderboards and player history sent from one player to another could arrive
with pieces missing, or not at all, when the sender's addon sent several chat
packets at once. The addon now sends its packets one at a time, a moment
apart, so longer messages arrive whole.
• Damaged data that still looked valid could end up in your player history,
as wrong level times or names that don't exist. Every message now carries a
checksum, and one that doesn't match its checksum is thrown away. Messages
from players on older versions carry none, so those can still arrive
damaged.
• When something a player sent you arrives damaged, your addon notices and asks
that player again about a minute later, instead of staying without that data…
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for WoW Forever that keeps track of the top 50 players on your
faction-realm in the race to max level, overall and per class, and records who
was first to reach every level. Data is gathered with /who scans, from the
guild roster and from your party or raid, and shared between addon users over
the addon channel: realm-wide through a hidden chat channel per faction, with
the guild, your group and whispers as the backup.

Built for WoW Forever: the race goes to level 60 and Paladins and Shamans are
tracked on both factions. Other WoW clients are not supported.
Releases
For latest releases that you can just unzip into your Interface\AddOns folder,
see the Releases page on GitHub.

Slash commands: /wfr toggles the leaderboard window, /wfr debug opens the
debug window, /wfropts opens the options.
Dev setup
Everything needed to lint, test and package the addon lives in a Docker image
(Dockerfile), so the only host requirements are Docker and git. This is the
recommended setup on Windows, where Lua, LuaRocks, make and svn are painful to
install.

`bash

addons.description:
WoW: Forever addon that explains how your talents change your character stats.

Supported: all nine classes (Shaman, Druid, Warrior, Priest, Paladin, Mage, Hunter, Rogue and Warlock), all three talent trees each. enUS client, Interface 16001 (beta build 1.60.1.70338).

Talents that change character sheet stats:

| Class | Tree | Talents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shaman | Elemental Combat | none (all spell-specific) |
| Shaman | Enhancement | Thundering Strikes, Ancestral Knowledge, Mental Dexterity, Anticipation, Toughness, Spirit Weapons, Mental Quickness |
| Shaman | Restoration | Tidal Focus (hit), Improved Reincarnation (health) |
| Druid | Balance | Nature's Majesty, Nature's Reach (hit), Moonkin Form (crit aura) |
| Druid | Feral Combat | Heart of the Wild, Feral Swiftness, Thick Hide, Sharpened Claws, Predatory Strikes, Leader of the Pack, Natural Instinct, Natural Reaction |
| Druid | Restoration | Living Spirit (Spirit) |
| Warrior | Arms | Deflection (parry), Weaponmaster (crit with an Axe or Polearm) |
| Warrior | Fury | Cruelty (crit) |
| Warrior | Protection | Shield Specialization (block with a shield), Anticipation (defense, plus 0.04% dodge, parry and block per point) |
| Priest | Discipline | Mental Strength (Intellect) |
| Priest | Holy | Spiritual Guidance (healing and spell damage from Spirit) |
| Priest | Shadow Magic | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Paladin | Holy | Divine Strength (Strength), Divine Intellect (Intellect), Holy Power (spell crit) |
| Paladin | Protection | Precision (hit), Anticipation (defense, as Warrior), Sacred Duty (Stamina), Toughness (item armor, approximated on total armor) |
| Paladin | Retribution | Deflection (parry), Conviction (crit), Champion of the Light (spell damage from Intellect) |
| Mage | Arcane | Arcane Mind (Intellect), Arcane Resilience (armor from Intellect), Arcane Instability (crit) |
| Mage | Fire | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Mage | Frost | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Hunter | Beast Mastery | none (pet and aspect talents) |
| Hunter | Marksmanship | Lethal Attacks (melee and ranged crit), Careful Aim (melee and ranged Attack Power from Intellect) |
| Hunter | Survival | Lightning Reflexes (Agility), Survivalist (health), Deflection (parry), Surefooted (melee hit) |
| Rogue | Assassination | Malice (melee and ranged crit) |
| Rogue | Combat | Lightning Reflexes (dodge), Deflection (parry), Precision (hit), Hack and Slash (crit with a Dagger or Fist Weapon) |
| Rogue | Subtlety | none (all ability- or situation-specific) |
| Warlock | Affliction | Suppression (hit) |
| Warlock | Demonology | Demonic Embrace (Stamina), Demonic Knowledge (spell damage from level, with a demon pet active) |
| Warlock | Destruction | none (all school- or spell-specific) |

Every other talent is listed too, so its tooltip explains it even though it does not change the sheet.

Party auras (Leader of the Pack, Moonkin Form) are attributed to your talent; if a groupmate provides the same aura, the client total already includes it.

Conditional talents depend on your form (Druid) or equipment (main-hand weapon type for Warrior and Rogue, shield) or an active pet (Warlock). When the condition is not met, the effect is shown in grey with its value under that condition, and it is not counted in the talent total.

Anticipation's 0.04% per Defense point is the Classic rule and is not yet confirmed on Forever.
What it shows
• Character panel next to the character window: each stat with the talents that contribute to it, including chained effects (for example, Ancestral Knowledge raises Intellect, which Mental Dexterity turns into Attack Power).
• Talent tooltips: what the talent gives you now and what the next point would add, using your current stats.
• Character stat tooltips: hovering a stat row (Intellect, Attack Power, ...) appends the talents behind it, in the native tooltip style.…

releases.changelog:
Changed
• Updated for the latest Forever client (build 1.60.1.70658).
• Loot lists refreshed for the dungeon bosses. The Stormwind Stockade now shows all its loot.

New
• Works with OpenMap. If you use the OpenMap addon, a click on one of its dungeon icons now opens the Dungeon Crawler dungeon map, with bosses, loot, quests and routes. Several dungeons at one icon, such as the Scarlet Monastery wings, show a small list to pick from. OpenMap's own buttons step aside while our map is open, and our map sits above its frames. You can turn this off in the options ("Open this addon's map from OpenMap's dungeon icons").
• Level range under the entrance icons. Each dungeon entrance on the zone maps shows its recommended levels, coloured for your level like quests: orange when you are in the range. Where several dungeons share an entrance, one combined range.
• One icon per entrance. Dungeons and wings that share a door (Scarlet Monastery, Dire Maul, Blackrock) are now one icon with a list, instead of a cluster of icons.
• A new route editor bar. Edit route now opens a toolbar over the map in the same style as the sidebar. It has tiles for Previous, Next, To the end, Cut here, Join here, Delete, Undo and Start over, plus Save route and Reset to Default. It also shows the stops of the route as numbered badges (click one to select it; hover for your best time), the split timer switches, and a close button in the corner.
• Route buttons in the corner. A red Hide route or Show route button sits above the red Edit route button, bottom left on the map.
Improved
• The map covers Blizzard's quest panel when it is open, instead of showing the quest list next to ours.
• Tooltips on the route buttons open under the editor bar or beside the corner buttons, so they no longer cover the button.
• Gnomeregan: Grubbis has a second Forever item, the Skullduggery Belt, from the latest AtlasLoot.
Fixed
• Boss pictures are no longer squeezed. The pictures that come from the Encounter Journal are twice as wide as high and were being pressed into a square; the middle of the picture is used now.

New
• Sunken Temple route. A built-in route through the whole temple, with its stops, stairs and triggers. Tick Show route to see it.
• Cutting a route is much clearer. The Cut here button is always in the bar while you draw (greyed until you select a dot), with a tooltip that walks you through it. After a cut the old part turns dark grey, a red ring marks the cut, and a new Join here button joins your new section to any point of the grey part, including stops and steps that the mouse cannot click.
Improved
• Route stops now always sit on their boss's pin, so a route never drifts away from a boss whose position was refined. Removing a stairs or door marker also removes its route steps.
• Better positions for Hazzas, Morphaz, Jammal'an and Ogom in Sunken Temple.
Fixed
• Rare bosses now get the silver ring in the boss list and the boss header, not only on the map pins.

New
• Draw your own route. Under the Show route box there is now an Edit route button. Click the map to add points, a boss to add a stop, and stairs or doors to add a step. Click a dot to select it and drag it to move it, or Ctrl-click a line to add a point on it. Cut the route at a point to draw a new section; the rest turns grey until you join it up again. Undo takes back the last thing you did, whatever it was. Save route keeps it, and Reset to Default brings back the built-in route.
• Routes for more dungeons. Built-in routes now cover Ragefire Chasm, Deadmines, Shadowfang Keep, Stockade, Wailing Caverns, Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs, Blackfathom Deeps, Uldaman, Gnomeregan, all four Scarlet Monastery wings, Zul'Farrak, Maraudon, City of Dalaran and Ruins of Lordaeron. Routes stay hidden until you tick Show route.
• Options at a glance. The options page is split into sections (Map, World map entrances, Dungeons and raids, Bosses and loot, Routes, Timers), and there is an Options button with a gear at the top of the map's side panel.
• Missing bosses and rares added:
• Scarlet Monastery: Azshir the Sleepless, Fallen Champion and Ironspine in the Graveyard, and Scarlet Commander Mograine with Whitemane in the Cathedral.
• Zul'Farrak: Sandarr Dunereaver, Dustwraith, Zerillis and Ruuzlu.
• Maraudon: Maraudos and Veng, two of the five Khans.
• City of Dalaran: Lyn the Ignored is marked as a summoned boss and names the item you need, the Tome of Dalaran. A marker shows where to talk to Grindle Firespark to free the Fel Ancient.
Improved
• More boss positions and activation markers recorded, for example in Razorfen Downs and Zul'Farrak.
• The route colours are easier to tell apart: the purple leg is now darker.
Fixed
• No more "blocked from an action" popup if the map redraws during combat while a rare is selected.
• Start over on a dungeon that only has the built-in route now gives you an empty route to draw.

New
• The split timer can start by itself. It now starts when you enter a dungeon, and there is a Start button on the timer window. If you prefer the old behaviour, turn off "Start the split timer when I enter a dungeon" in the options and it starts with the first fight.
Fixed
• "Blocked from an action only available to the Blizzard UI" popup when pressing Escape. The addon no longer touches the game's own popup list, so Escape works normally again.
• Lua error when opening the world map (M) a second time, and a game crash when opening a dropdown on the map's top bar. The addon no longer hooks into the world map; it follows the map with its own light-weight watcher instead.
• The dungeon map's top bar now looks and behaves like the game's own: same spacing, colours and arrows. Clicking a place name leaves the dungeon and opens that map.

Players post a "looking for guild" ad, guilds post a recruiting ad, and both

v1.0.0 (2026-11-03)
• First stable release, for the launch of WoW: Forever.
• Trial accounts on Forever can't send addon messages, so posting an ad is disabled there and the window says why. Browsing ads still works.

v0.1.1 (2026-10-25)
• Maintenance release: internal cleanup (code structure, unused code removed). No functional changes.

Changelogv0.1.0
First release. Guild Finder Forever is community driven: it only knows the
ads of other players running it, so the lists start short and grow with
every player and guild that posts one.
Find guilds
• Guild ads as cards sorted by how well they fit your own ad, with faction
crest, goals as coloured chips and a raid box (style, raid days and time,
wanted classes per role, whether your class fits).
• Search box and filters: faction, language, goals, raid style, "wants my
class" and, on Forever, "same ruleset".
• Details dialog with the full text, raid schedule and wanted classes by
role. Opening it checks in the background whether the poster is online
and in that guild.
Find players
• Compact list of player ads with class, level, roles, languages and goals,
sortable by any column.
• Filters for role, level range and class; a click on a row shows the text.
My ad
• Player ad per character and guild ad per guild (members who may invite),
with a live preview and the number of matching ads.
• Raiding guilds add style, raid days, start and end time, raids per week and
a class × role table of wanted classes.
• Ads can name several languages: the seven UI languages plus Czech, Danish,
Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Norwegian, Polish, Romanian, Swedish,
Turkish and Ukrainian.
• Ads are renewed on login and expire after 14 days without one.
• Play times are switched off for now.
Contact and moderation
• Whisper opens a whisper and checks the poster via /who.
• Hide an ad, Block a character or guild (/gff blocked, /gff unblock).
General
• Ads travel player to player over a hidden addon channel; nothing is sent
during encounter lockdown, queued messages go out afterwards.
• Welcome dialog on first start, minimap button, addon compartment entry,
settings (minimap button, chat notice for new matching ads).
• Chat commands: /gff, /gff ad, /gff settings, /gff sync,
/gff status, /gff debug (sync traffic in chat, for bug reports).
• UI in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian and Portuguese.
• Runs on WoW Forever and, until Forever launches, on retail (Midnight).
Known limitations
• No cross-faction sync: the addon channel is separate per faction.
• The ruleset list for the "same ruleset" filter is not final until Forever
launches.

addons.description:
Formerly TOG Profession Master.

Stop whispering every alchemist in your guild to ask "is your transmute up?" and stop logging into five different alts to remember who knows the recipe you need. Ultimate Profession Master keeps a live, shared view of every guildmate's professions, recipes, and cooldowns — and lets you mail reagents straight to the crafter without typing a single character name.

Works on Classic Era / Anniversary, TBC Classic, Wrath Classic, Cataclysm Classic, and Mists of Pandaria Classic, with early support for WoW Forever and Retail.
Quickstart
1. Install via CurseForge (recommended — handles dependencies automatically) or drop the folder into Interface\AddOns
2. /reload or restart WoW
3. Click the UPM minimap button to open the main window
4. Open your own profession windows (Alchemy, Tailoring, etc.) at least once on each character — UPM scans them automatically and starts syncing with the guild

That's it. Within a minute or two you'll see your guildmates' recipes and cooldowns alongside your own.
What it does
Profession Browser — Every recipe known by anyone in your guild, with a list of crafters per recipe. Filter by profession, search by name, see who's online, right-click to whisper the crafter.

Cooldowns Tab — Every guildmate's active and ready profession cooldowns in one view: transmutes, Mooncloth, Salt Shaker, Northrend Research, Icy Prism, Truegold, Living Steel, JC daily cuts, and more. Hit the one-click [Mail] button to send the crafter a pre-composed supply mail with every reagent of that cooldown on it — one mail per cooldown, even for a two-reagent transmute like Arcanite; the click splits whatever stacks need splitting, attaches them all and fills in the recipient, and it sends nothing at all if you are short of any reagent. A crafter on another realm gets the mail on their own realm, and if the game refuses the mail, chat says why. Click [Mail] again once the mail is ready and it sends. A Sent column then shows how long ago you supplied that crafter ("5m ago", "3h ago", date and time on hover), and clears itself once they use the cooldown. The reagent column is white when your bags hold enough of it to fill that mail and grey when they don't, so a glance down the list tells you which cooldowns you can actually feed — and it recolours as you loot or send things, without a tab switch.…
addons.name: Ultimate Profession Master Forever

(Discord 2026-10-24, deDE Era). Era has no GetProfessions, so the

addons.changelog:
What's new in v1.00
• First release, made for World of Warcraft: Forever (beta 1.60.1).
• Move and resize any window or interface element, in three categories: Windows (58, on by default), Interface (23) and Edit Mode (51).
• Drag windows directly: character, spellbook & talents, professions, map, bags, bank, merchant, mail, auction house and many more. They stay where you leave them, even when the game reopens them.
• Move mode (/amf move): a box over every enabled element. Drag to move, mouse wheel to resize, right-click to reset.
• A checkbox per element in Options → AddOns → AnyMove Forever, plus Reset everything (/amf reset). Everything is saved between sessions.
Installation
1. Download the release zip.
2. Extract the folder into your WoW {game_version}/Interface/AddOns/ directory (for WoW Forever: _classic_beta_).
3. Restart WoW and enable the addon.
Notes
• This addon only loads on WoW Forever.
• The Edit Mode category is off by default: moving those elements from outside Edit Mode can clash with it.
• Protected frames are never moved in combat; the change is applied as soon as combat ends.
• Inspired by MoveAny by D4KiR, written from scratch (no MoveAny code is used).

Novedades v1.00 (Español)
• Primera versión, hecha para World of Warcraft: Forever (beta 1.60.1).
• Mueve y cambia de tamaño cualquier ventana o elemento de la interfaz, en tres categorías: Ventanas (58, activadas por defecto), Interfaz (23) y Modo Edición (51).
• Arrastra las ventanas directamente: personaje, hechizos y talentos, profesiones, mapa, bolsas, banco, mercader, correo, subasta y muchas más. Se quedan donde las dejes, aunque el juego las vuelva a abrir.
• Modo mover (/amf move): un recuadro sobre cada elemento activado. Arrastra para mover, rueda del ratón para el tamaño, clic derecho para restablecer.
• Una casilla por elemento en Opciones → AddOns → AnyMove Forever, y Restablecer todo (/amf reset). Todo se guarda entre sesiones.
Instalación
1. Descarga el archivo zip de la release.
2. Extrae la carpeta dentro del directorio {version_juego}/Interface/AddOns/ de WoW (para WoW Forever: _classic_beta_).
3. Reinicia el juego y activa el addon.
Notas
• Este addon solo se carga en WoW Forever.
• La categoría Modo Edición va desactivada por defecto: mover esos elementos por fuera del Modo Edición puede chocar con él.
• Los marcos protegidos no se mueven en combate; el cambio se aplica en cuanto termina.
• Inspirado en MoveAny, de D4KiR, escrito desde cero (no usa nada de su código).

addons.description:
Move and resize any window or interface element in World of Warcraft: Forever

🇪🇸 Español

What it does
AnyMove Forever lets you move and resize the windows and interface elements of WoW Forever, grouped in three categories:

| Category | What | Default | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | Character, spellbook & talents, professions, map, bags, bank, merchant, mail, auction house, trade, quests, friends, achievements, collections, calendar, settings... | On | Drag them directly |
| Interface | Top widgets, error messages, zone texts, alerts, group loot, totems, combo points... | Off | Move mode |
| Edit Mode | Action bars, unit frames, minimap, chat, bags bar, buffs, quest tracker... | Off | Move mode |

Edit Mode already moves most of the HUD, but not the windows: that is the part this addon adds. The Edit Mode category is off by default because moving those elements from outside Edit Mode can clash with it.
Features
• Drag any window and it stays there, even when the game reopens it.
• Move mode: a box over every enabled element. Drag to move, mouse wheel to resize (30–250%), right-click to reset.
• Everything is saved between sessions.
• Protected frames are never touched in combat: changes wait until combat ends.
• A checkbox per element in Options → AddOns → AnyMove Forever, plus Reset everything.
• Translated to every client language.

addons.description:
Always-visible health and power text on the player, pet, target and focus frames for World of Warcraft: Forever

🇪🇸 Español

📸 Screenshots
Health and power text on the frames

Options

What it does
By default, WoW Forever only shows your health and power numbers when you hover the bar. Health Bar Text Forever keeps them always visible on the player, pet / minion, target, target of target, focus and target of focus frames, in the format you choose for each one.

| Format | Example |
|---|---|
| Value | 1.203 / 1.500 |
| Percent | 86% |
| Short | 13K / 14K (999 / 1K below 1,000) |
| Both | 86% 1.203 / 1.500 |
Features
• Always-visible health and power (mana, rage, energy...) on the player, pet / minion, target, target of target, focus and target of focus frames.
• Turn each frame on or off: an off frame goes back to Blizzard's default behavior.
• Four formats, chosen per frame: value, percent, short or both.
• Optional text on the power bars (on by default). Turn it off and those bars go back to Blizzard's default behavior.
• The text hides with no unit or a dead one, so it never covers the game's own "Dead" label.
• Lightweight, no libraries. Settings live in the game's own Options → AddOns panel.

addons.description:
No more green world map in non-English World of Warcraft: Forever clients

🇪🇸 Español

📸 Screenshots
Before: green map

After: original map art

The problem
In the WoW Forever beta (1.60.1), the new world maps (the world map, Kalimdor, Durotar, Zephras Isle, Hyjal and the other redrawn zones) only shipped for English clients. In any other language the client can't find them (Logs/AsyncFile.log: "Can't find file in build manifest") and draws them solid green, both the zone map and the explored areas.
What it does
Map Fix Forever ships the original map textures of the English client (build 1.60.1.69913, 1554 textures in 55 map folders) and swaps them in whenever the game draws one of those maps. Your map looks exactly like it does in English, explored areas included.
• Nothing to set up: install it and open the map.
• On English clients the world map is left alone (only the minimap fix below runs).
• Only post-hooks: Blizzard's map code is never replaced.

Grey minimap in Orgrimmar and Stormwind (build 1.60.1.70291, every language): inside those two cities the minimap turns light grey and black. The addon hides the broken city minimap and draws the ground minimap tiles the game already has underneath, following your position, zoom and minimap rotation. Icons stay on top. Outside those cities nothing changes.

1.0.0
Terminal 1.0, for WoW Forever's launch.

Share by invite
• .share invite invites a friend, guild member or Battle.net friend who's online (Tab lists them); they type .share accept. Terminal makes the group a code nobody can guess and hands it over only after their yes, only to that character, within 10 minutes. The empty prompt suggests the yes, and the badge shows invites.
• .share code gives a group's code to someone out of reach of an invite; they type .share join (typos are caught). .share new makes a group, .share rename calls it something else: names are yours alone.
• Typed passwords are gone: anyone in your guild could guess one at home. Groups made with a password are forgotten at login, with a line saying how to make them again. Your friends need this version too: invite them again.
• No kick: a group has no owner. To leave someone out, start a new group with the friends you trust. .share and the badge show who's connected.

In your language
• Simple mode's questions in German, Spanish, French, Russian and Chinese: "Quests zum Abbrechen", "où est mon corps", "мои аукционы", "我的邮件" and 45 more. English works on every client as before.
• Stats, food, drink and weapon damage by your language's words ("Ausdauer Essen" finds stamina food); your language's little words are left out of a search ("Essen, das Ausdauer gibt"); shorthand finds places as your client names them ("brd": Schwarzfelstiefen); Chinese typed without spaces is read as the words it's made of.
• Trainers are found by their translated titles ("Bergbaulehrer"), Chinese searches find only names with the characters you typed, and every font choice shows Russian, Chinese and Korean letters.

Also
• After an update, one line in chat says how many new things there are; .changelog shows them.
• English searches answer as they did, as fast.

1.0.0
Terminal 1.0, for WoW Forever's launch.

Share by invite
• .share invite invites a friend, guild member or Battle.net friend who's online (Tab lists them); they type .share accept. Terminal makes the group a code nobody can guess and hands it over only after their yes, only to that character, within 10 minutes. The empty prompt suggests the yes, and the badge shows invites.
• .share code gives a group's code to someone out of reach of an invite; they type .share join (typos are caught). .share new makes a group, .share rename calls it something else: names are yours alone.
• Typed passwords are gone: anyone in your guild could guess one at home. Groups made with a password are forgotten at login, with a line saying how to make them again. Your friends need this version too: invite them again.
• No kick: a group has no owner. To leave someone out, start a new group with the friends you trust. .share and the badge show who's connected.

In your language
• Simple mode's questions in German, Spanish, French, Russian and Chinese: "Quests zum Abbrechen", "où est mon corps", "мои аукционы", "我的邮件" and 45 more. English works on every client as before.
• Stats, food, drink and weapon damage by your language's words ("Ausdauer Essen" finds stamina food); your language's little words are left out of a search ("Essen, das Ausdauer gibt"); shorthand finds places as your client names them ("brd": Schwarzfelstiefen); Chinese typed without spaces is read as the words it's made of.
• Trainers are found by their translated titles ("Bergbaulehrer"), Chinese searches find only names with the characters you typed, and every font choice shows Russian, Chinese and Korean letters.

Also
• After an update, one line in chat says how many new things there are; .changelog shows them.
• English searches answer as they did, as fast.

0.69.0
!t: your guild asks Terminal
• Someone in your guild or group types !t nearest innkeeper (or !t where is hogger, !t what drops thunderfury) and one Terminal in the guild answers in the same channel, from their side: nearest to where they stand, their class trainer, their level. World facts only, never your bags, mail, alts or position.
• Off until you switch it on: .ask guild on, .ask group on, .ask whisper on (whispers only from friends, guildies and your group). .ask test shows what it would send. Your own !t is answered in your chat only.
• Several Terminals in a guild agree on one answer, and share the limits: 10 s per asker, once a minute per question, 6 a minute per channel. Never in a battleground's chat; a question in another language is left unanswered.
• Answers are headed as >>> heads a list in your own chat: "Nearby innkeeper (15): ...", "Vendor in Ratchet (12): ...".

Spells by what they do
• Your spellbook's and every class's spells (@spell) are found by their descriptions: "spells that stun", "druid spells that root", @spell movement speed.
• Four new filters, as the game gives them: cast:instant, cast:<2; cost:0, cost:mana, cost:<100; range:melee, range:30; cd:0, cd:<10. In Simple mode: "instant spells", "spells with no cooldown", "spells that cost no mana", "30 yard spells", "spells under 100 mana", read only in a line about spells or abilities.

Cooking fires and moonwells
• "nearest cooking fire" lists every fire you can cook at: campfires, bonfires, braziers, stoves, cauldrons, meat racks, about 2,000 places (the objects the server marks as a cooking fire, from Mangos Zero's object table; scenery fires stay out). Each row says what it is ("Campfire", "Cozy Fire").
• "nearest moonwell" lists QuestieDB's moonwells. Advanced: @cookingfire, @moonwell with sort:distance, near: and in:. Both need Questie or QuestieDB.
• The object lists (mailboxes, forges, anvils, cooking fires, moonwells) are made the first time you ask, not at login, and let go after 10 minutes unused.

Simple mode understands more of how people ask
• "nearest" after a request's opening words: "where is the nearest mailbox", "find the closest innkeeper", "show me the nearest anvil". "near me" anywhere: "repair near me", "innkeeper near me in stormwind".
• An object or a role said alone is the nearest of them: "mailbox", "anvil", "inn", "repair"; "mailboxes in westfall" those there.
• Roles in the plural ("nearest innkeepers", "banks", "flight masters"), "nearest auction house", "deadmines entrance", Stormwind by its name alone.
• A word naming the kind you want looks only there: "hogger quest", "quests in westfall", "npcs in westfall", "linen recipes".
• "where to learn tailoring", "who teaches mining", "where to learn warrior", "where can i learn riding": the nearest trainers.
• "who drops spiritshroud leggings", "vendors that sell woven vest", "which vendors sell ice threaded bullet": where to get it. An item only the other faction sells says who: "Sells it to the other faction only". A name beginning with "the" or "a" is found whole ("where to get the collector's ring").
• A place said with nothing there says so: "None of those in Moonglade that Questie knows of." A place on another continent lists what's there, with no distance.
• Names come first: "thrall" names Thrall, not his advisor; "dalaran mage" and "stockade guard" are those NPCs, not a mage in Dalaran; a quest named like a question ("What Is Going On?") is the quest.

Typos as hands make them
• A neighbouring key ("linrn"), a key pressed twice ("linnen"), a key missed ("lien", "hoger"), two keys swapped ("marhsal") or a neighbouring key pressed as well counts as one slip, on your client's keyboard (QWERTZ in German, AZERTY in French). A key far from its place counts for more.
• A word that is exactly a name is never a typo: "linken" is the NPC Linken, not your Linen Cloth. Simple mode corrects names only Questie knows: "marshal dughn" finds Marshal Dughan.

Alt+…

0.68.0
A console
• .console (also .tty): a Linux-like console over everything Terminal knows. Every list is a folder and every row a file: ls, cd, cat shows a row's tooltip, grep searches stats and tooltips, with pipes, aliases, history and z.
• Up to four tiled panes, themes and prompts; the panes come back after a /reload. Lines wider than a pane slide sideways (Shift+wheel, or Left/Right with nothing typed). Passwords typed into it are masked.
• .console and .atop now live in Terminal Extras and load the first time you use them.

Smaller saved data
• Terminal.lua now keeps only your settings, tabs, picks and search history. What Terminal records and learns (logs, item and loot indexes, talents, mail, recipes, the console's history) moves to a new TerminalCache.lua, written about half the size and safe to delete. Your old file is moved over by itself.
• .saved shows how big each part is. .saved keep
off|small|normal|large (or .saved keep all minimal|normal|everything) sets how much is kept between sessions; .saved clear
forgets one. By default the loot log keeps 250 drops, the combat log 150 (deaths first) and item details 4000 items.

Report a problem
• .report [what happened] (also .bug) puts a report in a window to copy and paste as a comment on Terminal's CurseForge page (a GitHub issue works too): versions, the addons found, the searches that found nothing, errors and Terminal's last steps. Your characters', alts' and guild's names are left out.
• It's offered when a search finds nothing, on a result's right-click menu (Report a problem with this result) and after an error.

Nearest forge and anvil
• nearest forge and nearest anvil (also closest, farthest, 2 anvils), for blacksmiths and engineers: the closest first, an arrow pointing the way, Enter shows it on the map. Needs Questie or QuestieDB. Advanced: @forge, @anvil, with sort:distance, near: and in:.

Simple mode reads your line once
• The search, the bar, Alt+ and .explain share one reading of the line. Alt+ keeps your capitals and writes linen to csv as linen >>> csv.
• not in my bank or not on my alts on its own lists your items that aren't there.
• Unticking a typed filter on the bar takes out exactly the words that said it, never another filter's or anything inside a "quoted phrase".

World data from the game's own sources
• Flight paths, dungeon and raid entrances, zone levels and fishing skills come from the game's own data and public sources, each cited in docs/DATA_SOURCES.md. Dungeon levels are the Group Finder's; with Questie or QuestieDB, entrances show at their doors.
• @cvar lists the console settings WoW Forever's own interface uses, each explained in the options panel's words, in your language.
• Your race's capital counts as a learned flight path from the start (a Windshaper's: Orgrimmar).

Fixes
• The combat log kept between sessions keeps deaths over crits, so what killed me still answers after a /reload.

New files: restart the game once after updating, not just /reload.

0.67.0
Plain words for numbers, levels and dates
• Numbers: swords between level 20 and 30, quests under level 25, items worth more than 1g, bags with at least 10 slots, gear under 50% durability.
• Levels from yours: quests 3 levels above me, dungeons around my level, gear for next level. They move with you as you level, in a saved search or alias too.
• Dates: loot from yesterday, mail older than 20 days, auctions sold this week, what killed me today, in the last 3 days.
• Advanced: lvl:me+3, lvl:me-2..me+3, value:>1g, slots:>=10, since:yesterday, older:20d.

Top N
• the 3 nearest mailboxes, top 5 upgrades, my 10 most valuable items, the closest innkeeper. Orders in words too: cheapest, most valuable, highest level. The footer says "3 of 41".
• Advanced: | first 3.

Compare two searches
• cloth but not in my bank, linen plus my alts. Advanced: | except @bank, | also @stored.

Sort by more than one field
• sort:quality,-level sorts by quality, then by level on a tie; sort:level,distance puts the nearest first among equals. In Simple mode, Shift on a Sort pick makes it the "then by".

Undo in the prompt
• Ctrl+Z undoes your last edit (a word, a Ctrl+W, a paste); Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it.

Understand a search
• Point at an Advanced line in the prompt to read it in plain words, or .explain it ("Vendors, that sell arrow, nearest first"). .explain alone explains the last line you ran.
• Why is this here? in a row's menu: the words it matched and where, the filters it passed, its sort value, and for an upgrade what it gains.

Upgrades
• With no tree picked, upgrades are judged for the talent tree holding most of your points, and follow a respec. .weights all goes back to that.
• Hit past your cap counts for nothing: 5% melee and 3% spells below 60; 9% and 16% at 60. .weights says where you stand.
• upgrades i can buy (vendor upgrades): the friendly vendors selling a clear upgrade for you, nearest first, with what it gains and any standing it needs. Advanced: @npc sells:upgrade. Needs Questie.
• ah upgrades: bind-on-equip upgrades at Auctionator's last-scanned price, the most gain per gold first. Needs Auctionator and AtlasLoot.

Fixes
• Upgrades are always judged against what you wear, including a worn piece whose stats the game didn't give (it counted as nothing) and random-suffix gear.
• Names with a date or level in them ("Tonight We Dine", "Last Day of Summer") are still found.

0.66.0
Your own key, on any keyboard (a player on CurseForge: "how can I keybind the terminal on a German layout?")
• Bind any key to Terminal (Key Bindings > AddOns > Terminal, or .bind) and in the open terminal it does what does: it closes it, Alt+ it writes the search in Advanced mode, Tab+ it is pure fuzzy finding. Keys like ^, ², Ctrl+Space, Shift+Space or Alt+Q work; letters, digits and the characters a search needs still type.
• The hints, F1's keys and the windows' footers name your key. With bound, nothing changes.

Quests that reward bags
• quests that reward bags (bag quests, quivers from quests, quests that reward ammo pouches) lists the bags your race, class and faction can still get, the most slots first, each saying which bag and its slots; the footer says how many you've done already. Needs Questie.
• Advanced: @questie reward:bag -is:done sort:slots (reward:quiver, reward:ammo_pouch) lists the same in the same order, with the bag and slots in each row.

Sort either way
• Simple mode's Sort shows an arrow by the sort in use: down for the highest (or Z) first, up for the lowest (or A) first. Pick it again to turn it round. Numbers start with the highest, names with A.
• Advanced: a - turns a sort round (sort:-level, sort:-name, sort:-quality).

Nearest or farthest
• sort:distance lists the nearest first, sort:-distance the farthest (sort:nearest and sort:farthest still work). In plain words: farthest innkeeper, farthest mailbox. Sort's Distance starts with the nearest; pick it again for the farthest.
• A row whose distance isn't known (on another continent, in an instance) counts as infinitely far: last when nearest, first when farthest.

Upgrades by talent tree
• .weights picks a tree: .weights arms, fury, prot, holy, resto, shadow, bear... ("tank" and "healer" pick your class's). One at a time; none picked, your class's levelling tree.
• New weights made for WoW Forever, one scale per tree for levels 1-60: healing is its own stat, a school's spell damage counts for its tree, a ranged weapon's DPS is apart from a melee one's, block value apart from block chance, a feral's weapon DPS counts.
• Your own weights: .weights set str=2 agi=1.5, or paste a Pawn scale string (.weights pawn opens a window for it). .weights custom picks them again, .weights clear forgets them.
• An upgrade search's footer says .weights is how to judge them otherwise.

Fewer commands
• .xp, .history, .durability, .mail, .combatlog and .lockouts are gone: their lists are searched like anything else. .forget drops an alt's mail, experience and lockouts; .forget history and .forget combatlog clear those; .set mailWarn off stops the login warning about expiring mail.
• .talentdebug and .profdebug are .debug talents and .debug professions.

Fixes
• An answer sorted by distance is in that order; sort:-distance is faster.
• reward:pouch (satchel, sack) finds items with that name; reward:bag is every bag.
• Turning "nearest mailbox" round on Sort gives "farthest mailbox"; a typed nearest or farthest wins over the bar.
• Advanced bag searches ask the game for bags it hasn't loaded yet, and read their slots in other languages too.

addons.description:
> 🎨 Artists wanted! The journal already records map coordinates, creature IDs and item IDs for everything it sees — it just doesn't draw any of it yet. If you can make icons, portraits, or a journal-style map, see issue #6. No Lua required to contribute a mockup or asset set.

Open the journal with /fj or /fieldjournal. This version has four tabs:
• Quests keeps the quest log text, observed NPC dialogue, readable notes, kills and picked up quest items in chronological margins. It links speech from a recent quest giver when the speaker and location match one unambiguous quest. Previous quest stages and completed objectives are crossed out.
• Daily diary records newly learned spells, group joins, and merchant purchases and sales when the client exposes enough information.
• Bestiary counts creatures seen falling, their locations, and items actually looted from those creatures. Counts are personal observations, not drop rates.
• Crafting & gathering records loot from world objects, completed crafts reported by the client, and skill milestones at 20, 25, 35, 40, 50, 75, 100 and every 25 thereafter.

The addon never registers the protected combat log event. Kill detection uses party kill and observed unit death events; missing client events can leave gaps. Loot is attached to a creature or object only when the loot window supplies its source GUID and the item is actually taken. Merchant entries compare bags and money while a merchant is open; unrelated simultaneous changes can affect the account. Speech and note links can be changed manually from the quest tab.

See CHANGELOG.md for the version history.
Current status
This is beta software, developed and tested against one live account. The codebase is split into a namespaced module layout (Core/, Data/, UI/) with a hand-rolled Lua test suite (tests/run_tests.lua).

Journal data is stored per character via AceDB-3.0 (FieldJournalDB.char). Existing data from before this migration is imported automatically, once, the first time each character logs in — see CHANGELOG.md for details. The old data is never deleted, only read, so it remains a fallback if anything about the migration ever needs to be redone.

Each character also keeps a rotating ring of five automatic backup snapshots, taken at login, plus a second complete copy in its own per-character saved-variables file. /fj repair restores from those snapshots. There is still no manual export/import, and no guarantee that a manual edit to an entry survives auto-regeneration or a future merge — see Roadmap below.
Roadmap
This follows a phased resilience plan (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-phase1-resilience-design.md in this repo's history, not distributed with the addon). See the milestones and open issues for what's up for grabs — issues labeled good first issue are small, self-contained, and don't need deep addon-development experience.
• Export / Import — a manual /fj export / /fj import safety valve so players can back up or transfer their own data without touching SavedVariables files directly.
• Edit-safety guarantees — a per-record edited flag so a manual correction (via the note editor) is never silently overwritten by auto-regeneration, a merge, or a backup restore.
• Repository polish — a CLAUDE.md for future coding-agent sessions, once the data layer above has proven stable. (Contribution guidelines now live in CONTRIBUTING.md.)
• Phase 2 (UI/UX) and Phase 3 (visual polish, art) — exploratory, no design work started; see the open issues.

None of this is scheduled; it lands as time allows.

addons.changelog:
What's new in 1.5
Nothing new to set: 1.5 only changes how the voices move between the settings you already have.
• Voices that fade instead of stepping. A position is shared every two seconds, and the volume moved at every one of them: someone walking towards you got louder in steps. Their position is now walked from the old one to the new one, so the distance changes all the time and the voice follows it.
• The volume is followed twelve times a second instead of four, and its fade is taken from the time really elapsed rather than counted in ticks.
• The range, the curve and the volume up close are unchanged. They are simply reached without the staircase.
• Each member's name and group slot are looked up four times a second instead of at every volume step, so the faster fade costs nothing in a raid.
Install
Extract the ForeverVoice folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named ForeverVoice.

In the game settings, turn on Voice Chat and set your microphone and talk mode. Everyone needs the addon for proximity to work: a player without it doesn't share their position and hears the whole channel at normal volume.
addons.description:
Proximity voice chat for your guild or your party in World of Warcraft: Forever.

-c8a14a)

Walk into a zone, cross a guildmate on the road, and just talk to them. ForeverVoice turns
Blizzard's built-in voice chat into proximity voice: you hear the players close to you, their
voice fades as they walk away, and they go silent once they are out of range.

No external program, no Discord, no server to host. ForeverVoice uses the game's own voice
chat and only changes how loud each player is. No libraries, no dependencies.

How it works
1. ForeverVoice joins the voice channel you picked when you log in: your guild, your
group, or Auto (the guild, else the group).
2. Every player who has the addon shares their position with the guild, using a small hidden
addon message.
3. Your addon sets the volume of each player based on how far they are: full voice up
close, a smooth fade, then silence.

> Everyone needs the addon. Proximity is applied on the listener's side. A guildmate
> without ForeverVoice doesn't share their position, and hears the whole channel at normal volume.
Features
• Proximity volume: full voice up to a distance you choose, then a fade (linear, natural
or smooth), with silence past the maximum range. A live graph in the options shows the curve.
• "X is in voice range" alert: a sound and a message when a guildmate comes within earshot.
• Group audible in dungeons: the game hides positions in dungeons and battlegrounds, so
your group stays audible there.
• Always hear someone: right-click a player in the window to hear them at any distance,
for example a friend or a raid leader.
• Voice window:
• who is in the channel and who is talking;
• how far each player is and how loud you hear them;
• your own line with your push-to-talk key.
• Speaker above heads: a green speaker icon above the players who are talking (needs
friendly nameplates, Shift + V by default), and above your own character while you talk.
• Minimap button with a tooltip listing who is in range, and a halo while someone talks.
• Guild or group: pick the voice channel in the options (Auto, Guild or Group). In Group mode,
you join group voice as soon as a group forms.
• Join and leave voice in one click: the join button asks "Guild or Group?".
• English and French, switched in one click.
• Settings that stick, even with the Forever beta bug that resets addon settings (see
below).
• Safe: ForeverVoice only changes volumes, never the Blizzard mute. Everyone is put back to
full volume when you turn proximity off, leave voice or log out.
Controls
Minimap button

| Action | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Options menu |
| Right-click | Proximity on / off |
| Middle-click | Join / leave voice |
| Shift + click | Show / hide the window |
| Drag | Move the button around the minimap |

Slash commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| /fv | Show / hide the window |
| /fv options | Open the options menu |
| /fv on / /fv off | Turn proximity on / off |
| /fv join / /fv leave | Join / leave voice |
| /fv join guild / /fv join group | Switch to guild or group voice |
| /fv range 40 8 | Silent from 40 yards, full voice up to 8 yards |
| /fv who | Who in the guild has the addon, and their version |
| /fv debug | Voice, positions and settings backup status |
Options
| Section | What you can change |
| --- | --- |
| Range | Full voice distance (0-30 yd), silent distance (10-100 yd), fade curve with a live graph, volume up close |
| Behavior | Voice channel (Auto, Guild, Group), proximity on / off, auto-join voice, group audible in dungeons, hear players without the addon, in-range alert, icon above heads, minimap button |
| Window | Show, lock, only players in range, your own line, size, background opacity |

addons.changelog:
What's new in 3.9
• MyXPBar now runs on Classic Era 1.15.9 — Hardcore realms, Season of Discovery — as well as on WoW Forever. Same addon, same options, same profiles, same files: one package, whose TOC lists both interfaces (16001, 11509).
• No backup copy on Classic Era. The workaround for the Forever beta saving bug is switched off there: the game keeps its saved variables, so the addon creates no macro and no CVar, and takes none of your macro slots. It only does so on a build it knows to be Classic Era; on any other it stays on, which is the safe side of a wrong guess.
• The close button of the options menu works on every client. The strip that lets you drag the menu spans its whole top at the very same frame level as the cross, so on Classic Era it took the click. The cross has its own level above the strip now, and closes the menu itself instead of relying on the button template. Same for the What's new panel.
Two zips, one addon
MyXPBar-Forever3.9.zip and MyXPBar-Classic3.9.zip hold exactly the same files. Take whichever carries the name of your game.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into the Interface\AddOns folder of your game, then relaunch it:
• WoW Forever: World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns
• Classic Era / Hardcore: World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns

The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.
addons.description:
A clean, lightweight and fully customizable XP bar for World of Warcraft: Forever.

-c8a14a)
-c8a14a)

MyXPBar replaces the default Blizzard experience bar with a sleek, readable bar you can place
anywhere on your screen. Inspired by the popular Luxthos WeakAuras look, it shows your rested XP,
estimates how many mobs you still need, and comes with a full in-game options menu built in the
World of Warcraft style. No libraries, no dependencies.
Features
• Replaces the Blizzard XP bar — the default bar is hidden automatically, and comes back at max
level for reputation and honor.
• Profiles with names — make one from the bar you have, name it, and pick it again on any
character from the list at the bottom of the menu. Position, size, colors, style, texture,
options: everything lives in the profile, and everything you change goes into it right away,
with nothing to save by hand.
• A switch for the bar — one checkbox, a middle click on the minimap button, a key binding or
/mxp off hides the bar at any level, without disabling the addon. The bar of the game stays
hidden too, as long as you asked for it to be.
• Reputation at max level — instead of disappearing at max level, the bar can show your tracked
faction, standing and progress (optional).
• Told when it is updated — one line in the chat after an update and a short "What's new" panel,
once per version. /mxp news shows it again, and the option can be turned off.
• 11 bar textures — default, smooth, flat, glass, shine, steel, stripes, ticks, grain, edge and
fade, each one a swatch in the options.
• 6 bar styles — classic, gold framed, segmented, thin line, spark and split rested, switched in
one click with a live preview.
• Smooth and alive — the bar slides to its new value, a floating +245 XP rises on every gain,
and the bar flashes on level up. Both can be turned off.
• Rested XP overlay — a translucent layer shows exactly how far your rested XP will take you.
• Mobs-to-level estimate — how many kills you still need, based on your last XP gain.
• Detailed stats — level, current / max XP, percentage, and projected percentage with rested XP.
• 7 languages — English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Italian, picked from a
drop-down in the options menu.
• Settings that stick — position, size, colors, style and options survive a reload, a relog
and a full restart of the game, even with the Forever beta bug that resets other addons
(see below).
• Full screen width — one click and the bar runs from one edge of the screen to the other,
at any resolution.
• Reputation bar — a thin bar with your tracked faction, standing and progress, under the XP
bar or beside it when vertical space is tight. It wears the style you picked, like the XP bar.
• Reputation only — the bar can show your tracked faction instead of the XP at any level, not
only at max level.
• XP per hour and time left — your rate since login, and the estimated time to the level
you aim for.
• XP of finished quests — the XP of the quests you finished but did not turn in yet, in gold
on the bar, with the list on hover. Tells you when turning them in will level you up (optional).
• Reputation on hover — mouse over the bar to see your tracked reputation: faction, standing
and progress.
• Lightweight — texts are only redrawn when they change, and nothing runs while the bar is
hidden.
Options menu
Open it from the minimap button or with /mxp. The menu is built in the World of Warcraft
style — stone frame, gold ornaments, gothic titles, Blizzard checkboxes — and every change is
applied live.

| Section | What you can change |
| --- | --- |
| Style | Classic, gold framed, segmented, thin line, spark, split rested |
| Texture | Default, glaze, satin, minimal, glass, bevel, tube, brushed, linen, diagonal, ember |
| Size | Width (200 px up to the width of your screen), height (8 to 60 px) and target level |…

What's new in 3.9
• MyXPBar now runs on Classic Era 1.15.9 — Hardcore realms, Season of Discovery — as well as on WoW Forever. Same addon, same options, same profiles, same files: one package, whose TOC lists both interfaces (16001, 11509).
