The cross has its own level above the strip now, and closes the menu itself instead of relying on the button template. Same for the What's new panel.
Two zips, one addon
MyXPBar-Forever3.9.zip and MyXPBar-Classic3.9.zip hold exactly the same files. Take whichever carries the name of your game.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into the Interface\AddOns folder of your game, then relaunch it:
• WoW Forever: World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns
• Classic Era / Hardcore: World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns

The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.8
• The reputation bar can sit beside the XP bar. Tick Reputation beside the bar and it moves to the right of it instead of under it, at the same height, so it costs no vertical space at all. Asked for by a player who keeps the bar under his hotbars, where space is a premium. Ignored while the bar runs the full width of the screen, since there is no room left on the side.
• It wears the style you picked, like the XP bar: the gold frame and its shine, the separators of the segmented style, and the thin line, which it follows down to the bottom of the bar.
• New "Reputation only" option. The bar shows your tracked faction instead of the XP at any level, not only at max level. With no faction tracked there is nothing to show, so the bar goes and the Blizzard one stays hidden with it.
• A switch flicked in the options now applies while the menu is open. The menu keeps the bar on screen so it can be styled where there is no XP left to show, and that was hiding what "Reputation only" did until you closed the menu.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.7
• Profiles have names. Create one from the bar you have in front of you, give it a name, and pick it again on any character. The list sits at the bottom of the options menu, next to the language: New makes a profile out of what is on screen, Delete removes the one in use and sends the characters that had it back to the first one.
• Nothing to save. Move the bar, change a colour, a texture, an option: it goes into the profile that character uses, right away. Another character picking the same profile gets the same bar, and a character that picks another one keeps its own.
• Your settings were kept. What every character shared becomes the first profile, and a character that had its own settings in 3.6 keeps them as a profile of its own, named after the character.
• The Character profile checkbox of 3.6 is gone: picking a profile in the list is what gives it to a character now.
• The minimap tooltip says which profile is in use, and the list names the character it is about.
• On the Forever beta, the macro copy carries the name of the profile: a character finds the one it picked again after a full restart of the game.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.6
• One profile per character. Move the bar on one character and your others keep theirs. Position, size, colours, style, texture, every option: a character can have its own set, or use the ones shared by the whole account. Tick Character profile in the options — its tooltip names the character and says which settings are in use.
• Two buttons at the bottom of the menu to go with it: Copy the shared ones puts the shared settings back on this character, Share these settings turns what you see into the ones every other character starts from.
• Everything you had set up becomes the shared profile, so no bar moves on any character when you update.
• A switch for the bar. Bar enabled hides the bar at any level, not only at max level, without disabling the addon — and the bar of the game stays hidden with it, as long as Hide Blizzard XP bar is checked. Four ways to reach it: the option, a middle click on the minimap button, a key of your own (Game Menu > Key Bindings > MyXPBar), and /mxp off / /mxp on.
• Reputation at max level. Instead of simply disappearing at max level, the bar can show your tracked faction, its standing and its progress, in the place of the XP. Optional, off by default, and the bar still disappears when you track no faction.
• The addon tells you when it was updated. One line in the chat and a short What's new panel, once per version and never again. /mxp news opens it whenever you want, and Announce updates turns the whole thing off.
• The narrow options menu is gone, and with it the Wide options menu option from 3.2. Stacked in one column the menu was around 1240 units tall where a screen offers 768: its lower half, the buttons included, was out of reach. The menu is always two columns side by side now.
• The language is now saved for the whole account, next to the profiles, so it no longer changes from one character to the next.
• On the Forever beta, a character with its own profile keeps a character macro of its own (MyXPBarChar), so its bar is still there after a full restart of the game. It is deleted again if you send that character back to the shared settings.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.5
• Bar textures, asked for by a player on CurseForge. Eleven of them: the game's own one, which stays the default, plus ten drawn for the addon — glaze, satin, minimal, glass, bevel, tube, brushed, linen, diagonal and ember.
• They are grey on purpose: a bar multiplies its texture by the colour you picked, so every texture wears your own colour instead of imposing one. Nothing else in your settings changes.
• They are chosen from a drop-down that shows each texture under its name, already painted in your bar colour, so you see what you are picking before you pick it.
• The texture applies to the whole bar family: XP, rested, the finished quests and both reputation bars.
• Each one carries the crisp top light and bottom shadow that make a bar read as solid, and the patterns are anti-aliased, so nothing turns into a staircase when the bar is stretched across the screen.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

addons.changelog:
v0.7.0
Turning up counts. A fairness review: regulars roll first, real attendance, tighter rules for officers, and a one-click installer.

New:
• Regulars roll first. Players who came to at least 3 of every 4 recent raids (75% of the last 8 in that instance) roll first on items they want. This replaces "no loot last raid rolls first".
• Attendance is real time in the raid: you count as there if you were in the group and online for 75% of it. Nights under 10 players in the group don't count (bench does not make up the 10), and raids within 12 hours of the night's first raid count as one night.
• Officers can mark a player Bench for the night. Bench counts as present. Players on v0.6.1 no longer reload the whole raid each time someone is benched.
• A one-click installer for Windows (Install-RaidLootController.bat) and Mac or Linux (install-raidlootcontroller.command). It finds WoW: Forever, installs or updates, and keeps your settings. Run it again to update. If the game folder needs permission, it offers to try again as administrator. A linked addon folder (a dev checkout) loses only the link, never the files.
• A glowing next-step button for every role, and a "Next:" line at the top of the window.
• History shows removed items and wins taken back. Stats shows attendance. The Raid tab lists tonight's regulars.
• Adding an item when loot is not on Master Looter, and it is not in your bags, warns that whoever looted it must trade it.

Fairer:
• A reserve pays out as a second item only for regulars. For anyone else, a normal win uses it up.
• Several players on one reserve: those without an item roll first.
• Reserves close when the first boss is pulled, even if nobody clicked Start raid.
• In a tie or a roll-first pass, a player who already has an item can no longer win a second.
• A spec first picked after the raid started is judged by class only on items open to everyone. It can be picked between items (not mid-roll, not for an item you already asked for), so a player without a spec is never stuck.
• A reserve used up by another win no longer pays out when its item comes up.
• Without the addon (no loot spec), you can roll only on items that suit every spec of your class. Skipping the addon no longer lets a fury warrior roll on tank plate. An officer can set your spec with Set spec.
• Undo win keeps the player locked if they hold a free win they could have asked for normally.
• A reserved item that falls back to normal rolls keeps its class limit.
• Best for: healing gear goes to healers and spell damage gear to casters. Ranged attack power is for hunters only, feral attack power for cat and bear. Use: lines, hit and crit now count. Dodge and parry no longer make an item tank-only. Protection paladins no longer roll on spell damage gear, and cat and bear are told apart.

Officers held to the rules:
• No unlock, spec change or Who can roll change while a roll is open, and no Give to player or Undo win on another item.
• No Close roll in the first 15 seconds, unless only some players may roll (reservers, regulars, a tie) and all of them rolled. The Close roll glow follows the same rule.
• No Call roll during a boss fight. A boss pull during a roll wipes it after the fight, and everyone rolls again.
• No spec change for a player holding a reserve once reserves close.
• The officer log never drops gives, take-backs, closes, removals or unlocks to make room: a flood of one kind only pushes out its own kind. Starting a raid twice is refused.
• Undo win keeps the old winner and rolls on the item, for History.
• A master looter giving a raid item to someone other than its winner is logged for everyone, once per item, and only for a player in the group.
• A resync from the raid host never shortens your officer log.

Fairer and steadier. A second security review, fixes for a crash and for raids that could lock players out.

v0.6.1
• The minimap button no longer has a black disc spilling past its gold ring.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.6.0...v0.6.1

v0.6.0
Harder to cheat, lighter to run, and a family look. A security and performance review, and the shared look with WoWClearance.

Safer:
• A raid can no longer be started with a faked start time, and a flood of new raids is cut off, so saved history and the "rolls first" list cannot be pushed out or rigged.
• Once a raid ends, its old host can no longer change it.
• If two players in the group share a name spelling, their rolls and messages are refused rather than credited to the wrong one.
• One raider can no longer hold up live rolls by asking for resyncs or toggling "I want this" over and over.
• The loot catalogue only takes drops from your own group, ignores items the game does not know, and limits how much one guildmate can add.

Faster:
• The Raid tab no longer scans your bags on every redraw to show trade time left.
• A catalogue search shows the first 200 matches and stops re-reading every item; the Stats tab no longer recounts all history on every roll.
• A large catalogue share is no longer cut short at 5000 entries.

Looks:
• Help looks like WoWClearance's: gold section headers, blue questions, more space between answers, a "no matches" line, and open or closed sections are remembered.
• The minimap button uses a background that exists on this client, and starts at a different spot from WoWClearance's so the two never overlap. Its tooltip has the same layout as WoWClearance's.
• Chat lines start with "RaidLoot:".

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0

v0.5.0
Tighter and lighter. An audit against the Forever API, a performance pass, and ideas from RCLootCouncil, Gargul and RollFor.
• No addon? Reserve by whisper. Players without the addon whisper the raid host !rlc reserve , and the host's addon whispers back. Same rules as the Reserve button.
• Master loot is confirmed. An item only counts as delivered once it leaves the loot window. If the give fails (full bags, a unique item, out of range), it goes on the "still to trade" list instead of being lost.
• Trade time left. The "still to trade" list on the Raid tab shows how long each bound item can still be traded.
• Safer trade window. Won items go into the trade window one at a time, and stop if the trade closes. If the game hides who you are trading with, you are told.
• Out of date? If the raid host's addon sends something yours does not know, you get one line with the download link.

Faster:
• A resync after a reload sends a third less, so live rolls wait less behind it.
• Less work on every message, bag update and tooltip: history is no longer copied on each change, bags are only repainted when the "still to trade" list changes, and your spec is read from talents once.
• The catalogue search waits until you stop typing, and only one raider shares each drop with the group. Catalogue sharing waits until a fight ends.
• Saved data is smaller: gear notes are dropped once an item is won, and old catalogue kill records are cleared.

Fixes:
• Boss names, item links and chat senders that the game hides during a fight are now checked properly before use.
• A resync no longer prints "X won Y" a second time.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.4.1...v0.5.0

v0.4.1
Master Looter is the way to run it.
• The master looter hands items over, not only the raid host. Make the host or an officer master looter: their addon gives the winner the item straight from the loot window, and anything left goes on their "still to trade" list.
• A master looter who wins an item now gets it from the loot window too.
• The README and Help explain why Master Looter matters: without it the game's own Need/Greed rolls come first, and the addon only gets items everyone passed on.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1

addons.description:
A customizable way to view your equipped gear within the default character UI

Feedback on this AddOn or any others that I develop/maintain is always welcome. If you enjoy using any of my AddOns and would like to support future development, it is greatly appreciated.

Highlights
• Allows for a wide range of text customization (size, color, outline, and more to come!)
• Lets you know when items are missing sockets, gems, and enchants
• Can show gear information when inspecting players
• Provides an interface for customizing the order of secondary and tertiary stats under the Enhancements category based on class and specialization
• Shows abbreviated names for item enchants to reduce visual clutter
• Allows quick showing/hiding of enchant text if you are only concerned with the quality of the enchant (Dragonflight enchants and onward)
• Indicates when equipped items have embellishments
• Option to expand Character Info window so that gear information is more easily readable
• DataBroker integration for quick access to options via minimap icon or other DataBroker AddOns
Summary
PranGearView allows you to display customized information about your character in the Character Info window. If you want to know what item level each equipped item is, whether any sockets, gems, or enchants are missing, or what each equipped item's durability is, then this AddOn will serve you well. It is designed to be used on top of Blizzard's default Character Info window with the goal of not needing to install entire UI packs to have this information available.

As mentioned earlier, this AddOn was developed to work on Blizzard's default Character Info UI, so this may cause unexpected interactions when run with other AddOns or UI packs. If you would like to report any issues, please reach out with a description of the problem along with a list of all AddOns that were enabled when this was observed. Screenshots can also be helpful in troubleshooting and fixing these types of issues.
Current Locales/Languages Supported:
• English (enUS)
• French (frFR)
• Portuguese (ptBR)
• German (deDE)
• Russian (ruRU) [partial]
• Traditional Chinese (zhTW) [partial]
Usage
You can use the options window to modify all available options. To open the options window from the Chat window, type the slash command /pgv.
Options Window
• Item Level: Display item levels for equipped items
• Upgrade Track: Display upgrade tracks for equipped items
• Gems: Display gem and socket information for equipped items
• Enchants: Display enchant information for equipped items
• Durability: Display durability percentages for equipped items
Customization Options
• Item Level: Change text size, outline, and color
• Option to place item levels on top of equipment icons
• Upgrade Track: Change text size, outline, and color
• Gems: Change icon size, show missing gems and sockets, only show missing gems and sockets for max level characters
• Enchants: Change text size, text outline, show missing enchants, only show missing enchants for max level characters, show or hide button to display enchant text, change text color
• Durability: Change text size, show as bar, change colors used for durability thresholds
• Inspect Window: Choose which information to display when inspecting other players
• Character Stats: Set stat order based on class and specialization, show stats with decimal places
• Main options page: Show minimap icon, increase the size of the Character Info window, show embellishments, show decimals for equipped item level, hide shirt & tabard info, show debugging messages (you should never need to enable this)
Slash Commands
All slash commands can be invoked using the prefix /prangearview or /pgv. Examples listed here use /pgv for brevity.
• /pgv: Opens the Options window
• /pgv help: List all available slash commands for the AddOn
• /pgv ilvl: Toggle showing item level
• This is the same as clicking the Item Level checkbox in the Options window…

Metails 2.14.0
Everything since 2.9.4, which was mislabelled as further 2.9.4 uploads:
• Boss records with real damage curves imported from your combat log: records.py reads the log the game writes, builds a per-second curve for each boss kill, and the race box plays it against your live total

addons.description:
A personal combat meter for WoW Forever. It shows you and your pets, and nobody else.

No raid syncing, no comparing yourself to the group, no plugin system. One small window that answers "how did I do?" and gets out of the way.
How it works
WoW Forever runs on the Midnight client, where addons can no longer read the combat log. Blizzard's own damage meter does the collecting and exposes it through the C_DamageMeter API. Metails! is a personal view over that data: it finds your row in each of Blizzard's meters and shows your spells, your targets and your deaths. That means it only ever shows what Blizzard tracks, and it costs almost nothing while you play.

During a fight the client hands addons locked numbers. Metails! still draws them live, straight onto the bars and text, and fills in sorting, percentages and tooltips the moment the numbers unlock.
Features
• Nine views: damage done, damage taken by spell or by attacker, avoidable damage, healing, absorbs, interrupts, dispels and a death log.
• Per-second rates for damage and healing, overall and per spell.
• Hover a row for per-second, overkill and the top five targets or attackers.
• Pet spells show with the pet's name on the row.
• Fights: the current fight, the previous one, an overall total, and every fight Blizzard still holds, named after the encounter.
• Report any view to say, party, raid, guild or a whisper.
• Open a second window to watch damage and healing at once.
• Hide automatically in or out of combat, change rows, opacity, bar texture and font size.
• Minimap button, a keybind, and an entry under Options, AddOns with the command list and the main buttons.
• Boss records: kill a dungeon or raid boss without dying and your damage, rate, time and spells are saved. Next time that boss starts, a separate movable box shows up to three damage bars on one scale: Best, Previous kill, and Current, live. Previous is left out when it is the same kill as Best. Best and Previous fill by elapsed time at an even pace, so a longer Current bar means you are ahead. Turn it off with /metails racing off.
• Real curves from your combat log: Metails turns combat logging on whenever you enter a raid or dungeon and off when you leave. With Sam's WoW Helper running (a small program that ships separately and installs with one double-click, no Python needed), a boss kill makes Metails flash a few coded pixels in the corner of the game window, the watcher sees them and rebuilds your records within seconds. Reload and the curve is there. Without it you still get the meter and the pace race. It reads the log, builds a per-second damage curve for every boss kill, and writes them into a small Metails_Records addon next to Metails. After a reload, the race box plays your record's actual damage second by second instead of an even pace. The kill prints how you did and updates the record if you beat it.
Views
| View | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Damage Done | Your damage by spell, with DPS |
| Damage Taken | Damage you took, by spell |
| Damage Taken by Source | Damage you took, by attacker |
| Avoidable Damage Taken | Damage Blizzard flags as avoidable, by spell |
| Healing Done | Your healing by spell, with HPS |
| Absorbs | Shields you cast, by spell |
| Interrupts | Your interrupts by spell |
| Dispels | Your dispels by spell |
| Deaths | Your most recent death, hit by hit, with your health after each |
Controls
| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Next view (shift for previous) |
| Right-click | Menu: pick a view or fight, report to chat, lock, reset |

The minimap button shows or hides the window on left-click, opens the menu on right-click, and can be dragged around the minimap. A keybind to show or hide the window is under Key Bindings, AddOns, Metails!. The same command list and the main buttons live under Options, AddOns, Metails!.

addons.description:
LuaWorkbench is a Lua editor for World of Warcraft. Write and run code in-game, save snippets for later, and keep them organized in folders. It works on its own and does not require another addon.

The editor includes syntax highlighting, code search, and a separate output panel for printed messages, return values and errors. You can also search through all your saved snippets, including their code.
• Run code with the Play button, Ctrl+Enter, or F5.
• Save with Ctrl+S, recover drafts after a reload, or return to the last saved version.
• Run saved scripts at startup, login or on a WoW event you choose.
• Adjust fonts, indentation, bracket completion and the output limit in Options.
• Resize the window, give the code editor more space, or minimize it while you play.

Open it with /lua, /le, /luaeditor or /luaworkbench. The ? button lists the shortcuts and explains the available options.

Supports Retail, Forever and TBC, with translations for all 11 WoW languages.

Please keep in mind: This runs real Lua code in your game. Only run scripts you trust. A running script cannot be interrupted; an infinite loop can freeze the game. Automatic runs are off by default. Enable startup, login or a custom WoW event for each script; only its saved code will run.

LuaWorkbench's own code is MIT-licensed. Bundled libraries keep their original licenses and notices. The repository is private during initial development; contributions and translations will be welcome when it opens.

SpellPad Studio 1.4.0
Most things now take two clicks. Ready-made macros, your game macros and the new import tools live in one place, and the footer has a Tools menu.
New
• The Arsenal has four tabs: Spells, Items, Easy Macros and My Macros. Easy Macros replaces the old Easy Macros menus (Class, Group & Raid, Emotes, Advanced) with one searchable list, in categories: Class, Group & Raid, Emotes, Advanced, Travel, Interface. Search looks through every category. My Macros lists the macros saved in the game's own Macros window. On both tabs a click puts the macro on the selected card, and you can drag one onto any card or SpellPad button. The card is left waiting for Save & Apply, and a snapshot is taken first.

Flyouts, the Single-Button Assistant and the stance and vehicle bars are skipped, and the preview says how many. /sps bars shows what the import would write.
• Offers when you start. On a page with no macros the footer offers the Setup Guide and, when the game has something to bring over, the two imports. The Setup Guide's finish screen offers them too. Nothing is shown when there is nothing to import.
• The unapplied-edits marker is a flashing circle (Pages list and footer), like the Save & Apply glow.
• Click "N changes not applied" in the footer to see which cards, then click one to go to it.
• Context icons in the Pages list. A page that switches by itself shows a small icon for its context (a sword for In Combat, a horse for Mounted, and so on). The icon is dimmed while contextual page switching is off.

Known issues…
addons.description:
A macro and keybind manager with action bars of its own. Built for Stream Deck and other macro pads.

Put a spell, item or macro on every key. See them all in one window, and on screen as a button pad. Made for WoW Retail (Midnight), and it works the same on WoW Forever.

Works with: Elgato Stream Deck, Corsair iCUE, other macro pads and keypads, a numpad, or just your keyboard.

Download: SpellPad Studio on CurseForge
Your own action bars
SpellPad Studio is a second set of action bars that lives inside the addon.
• Up to 36 buttons per page, and dozens of pages.
• It doesn't use Blizzard action bar slots. Your own bars stay as they are, and you can still work with them: drag a spell off a Blizzard bar onto a card and it stays on the bar, or hold the middle mouse button on a SpellPad button to copy its spell or item onto a bar.
• Your saved Key Bindings are not changed. A card's key works as a temporary override while the addon is running. The original binding stays in the game's Key Bindings screen and works again as soon as the card no longer uses that key. If a card takes a key the game already uses, the card tooltip, the Audit and the import preview tell you which action it overrides.
• Pages switch by themselves: mounted, stealthed, in a group or raid, in combat and more.
• Every button is a key you choose. Page 1 starts at ALT-1, ALT-2 and so on. Any key works.
What you can do with it
• See every key in one place. A card for each key, with a name, icon and macro. Search them, drag them to reorder.
• Build macros by clicking. No syntax to remember. The SpellPad Builder shows in plain English what a macro does.
• Know it works before you start. The setup guide checks that your keypad really reaches the game.
• Never lose your work. A backup (snapshot) is saved before every risky change.
Features
Organize
• One card per key, with a name, icon and macro.
• 4 to 36 cards per page, in any grid shape that fits your device.
• Search your pages and cards. Drag pages to reorder them.

Build macros
• Ready-made macros for your class, travel and teleports, target markers, world markers, group tools and emotes. (Forever also has consumable and raid-prep sets.)
• Macro text is colored and flags mistakes as you type. It suggests spell names too.
• Arsenal: click or drag a spell or item you know onto a card, or pick a ready-made macro or one of your game macros on its Easy Macros and My Macros tabs.
• SpellPad Builder: build a macro by clicking and dragging, with conditions like mouseover, focus and modifier keys.

The SpellPad (on-screen buttons)
• A copy of your macro pad on screen. Set its size and shape to match your device.
• Icons work like a normal action bar: cooldowns, charges, counts, range and procs.
• Click a button to run its macro.

Bring in what you already have
• Import Game Macros and Import Action Bars (footer > Tools) copy them onto new pages. Nothing is replaced, and you see a preview first.

Stay safe
• Snapshots: go back to how a page looked before a change.
• Audit: one list of every problem on every page. Click an entry to jump to it.
• Import preview: see what a shared page or profile will do before it is applied.

Share and customize
• Export and import pages and profiles as text. Keep several profiles per account.
• Save a card as a normal game macro.
• 7 window styles, a macro font size slider and many SpellPad options.
Getting started
1. Install the addon (below) and log in. A setup guide opens by itself the first time. To open it again, type /sps setup.
2. Tell it how many buttons you have, and whether the pad is wider than tall or taller than wide.
3. In your keypad app (Stream Deck, iCUE or another), make the top-left button send Alt + 1, the next one Alt + 2, and so on. The guide shows the key for every spot, and lights a spot up when the game receives it.
4. Click a spell in the Arsenal (or drag one onto card 1), then press the button.…

Pages can now live in folders, and a folder can switch by itself when its context starts.
New
• Page folders. A folder is a named set of pages. In Page Options, "Page folder" puts the page in a folder (Default, a folder you have made, or None to skip it) or makes a new one. The Pages list always shows its folders as headers, with the page count and, if the folder has a context, its icon. Pages in a folder get a thin gold bar on their left edge.
• !PAGE Forward and !PAGE Backward stay inside the folder of the page you are on, and wrap around at the ends. Pages set to None are skipped. Pages that have a context of their own step through the pages that share that context.
• A folder can have a context. When it starts (you mount, enter a dungeon, the fight begins) the folder's first page is shown, and while it holds, Forward and Backward move inside it without snapping back. Choose the context in Page Options (it then applies to the whole folder) or right-click the folder's header in the Pages list: the menu has Rename Folder and the same context list, one click each. A folder with the context In Combat only ever shows its first page, because pages can't change during a fight.
• Drag pages between folders. Drag a page in the Pages list: drop it between two pages of a folder to join it at that spot, on a folder's header (or just under its last page) to be its first (or last) page, on the Default header to leave the folder, on the Skipped header to skip it. The ghost reads, for example, "Heal to Mounted, position 3". Moves the page can't make (a page with a context of its own onto Default) turn the ghost grey and do nothing.
• Pages with a context of their own group together. Pages that share the same context sit side by side under "Context pages". Rules are now stored per character, specialization and profile; a new profile starts with none. If you used more than one profile, only the profile in use when you first load this version keeps your existing rules.
• Flying and Swimming win over Mounted. On a flying mount both Mounted and Flying are true, and the page with the lowest number used to win, so a Mounted page ahead of your Flying page stayed on screen after lift-off. The more specific context now wins; other pairs of contexts still go to the lower page. "Enable context override" still beats everything.

• More travel macros for mages (Retail): 19 more teleports and portals, plus Silvermoon City.
• Spellbook, Talents and Achievements entries in the Interface menu on Retail. They work from a key and from a SpellPad click.…

SpellPad Studio 1.2.1
This is the first release that runs on Retail (Midnight) as well as WoW Forever. One download works on both.
New
• Retail (Midnight) support. Tested on Midnight 12.1.5. On Retail the main window reads "SpellPad Studio Midnight". Your buttons and keys work in combat, and the SpellPad's cooldowns, charges and range keep working under Midnight's new combat rules.
• Drop a mount on a card or a SpellPad button (Retail). Drag a mount from the Collections journal, or the Summon Random Favorite Mount button, onto a card or SpellPad button and it becomes /cast with the mount's icon.
• Swap two cards by dragging. Drop a card on the middle of another card and the two swap their macro, icon and name. The target glows gold while you hover. Dropping near the top or bottom edge of a card still moves it to that spot, as before. A snapshot is taken first, and the keys stay with their positions.
• Class macros for all 13 Retail classes, including new sets for Death Knight, Demon Hunter, Monk and Evoker, with Retail spell IDs.
• More travel macros for mages (Retail): 19 more teleports and portals, plus Silvermoon City.
• Spellbook, Talents and Achievements entries in the Interface menu on Retail. They work from a key and from a SpellPad click.
• Reports for bug hunting: /sps retail (a Retail compatibility report), /sps combat and /sps cursor (what the cursor is holding). Copy the text into a comment or issue if something looks wrong.
Changes
• The setup guide remembers Horizontal / Vertical. Pages you add later follow the choice you made in the guide. Existing pages keep their look.
• Dismount / Leave Vehicle has its own icon. A card whose only lines are /dismount or /leavevehicle shows the vehicle exit icon.
• Fewer false "unknown command" warnings. The macro checker now reads the commands and emotes the game itself lists, so emotes and commands like /usetalents are no longer flagged.
• Spell proc glow and /equipset icons (Retail): a proc lights the SpellPad button, and an /equipset card shows the set's own icon.
• Menus fit each client. On Retail the Consumables and Raid Prep menus, /joke, /rolecheck and the Primary / Secondary Specialization entries are hidden, because they don't exist or don't apply there. Forever keeps them.
• The window frame is trimmed to sit correctly on Retail, and /sps help lists the report words on short lines.
Known issues
• On Retail, in combat, a charge spell that still has a charge left doesn't show its recharge ring.
• Forever: this release hasn't been re-tested there since Forever's beta went offline. It will be checked again at Forever's launch.
• The Class Specializations entries (/usetalents) do nothing until dual specialization exists on Forever.
• The "Toggle Legacy Menu" preset may not open the Legacy panel on Forever.
• Two characters with the same first name on the same realm share one set of per-character settings.
SpellPad Studio 1.2.0 (WoW Forever)New
• Setup guide. A short, hands-on guide that opens by itself the first time you install the addon (never for existing users). It walks you through five steps: pick how many buttons your device has, tell your device software which key each button sends (click paths for Elgato Stream Deck and Corsair iCUE, plus generic wording for other apps), press a button to prove it works, put a spell on card 1, and press the button to cast it. Reopen it any time with /sps setup, from Options > General > Getting Started, from the game's Settings > AddOns page, or from the hint on an empty page.
• "Nothing happening?" button check. In the guide, it listens to what a physical button really sends (including Shift, Ctrl and Alt) and offers a one-click fix, such as switching a page to the right prefix.
• Drag pages to reorder them in the Pages list. !PAGE cards follow the move (can be turned off in Options > General), page keys, shapes and context rules travel with the page, and a snapshot is taken first. Double-click a page to rename it.…

addons.description:
Better Level-Up! (Forever) is the WoW Forever (Classic beta, Interface 16001) build of BLU: replacement sounds for the level-up moments that matter, powered by RGX-Framework. Everything that cannot exist on the Forever client has been removed — this build ships only what the game can fire.
Features
• Level-Up sounds — a sound of your choice when you ding, with queueing, volume, and channel control.
• Quest sounds — accept, complete, progress, and turn-in triggers.
• Reputation sounds — rank-up triggers for faction grinds.
• Honor rank sounds — PvP rank progression triggers on the classic honor system.
• Combat triggers — Bloodlust/Heroism and proc-style combat cues through the RGXCombat integration.
• Collections tab — collectible milestone triggers (mounts, pets, toys, transmog) are reserved for the Forever client's Collections system.
• Minimap button — left-click opens the options panel; drag to reposition; Ctrl+Right-click hides it (/blu icon on restores).
• Full options panel — General, Combat, Honor, Level Up, Loot, Quest, Reputation, Profiles, and Sounds tabs with profile support.
• Custom sounds — add your own .ogg files, or choose from the bundled BLU defaults and shared-media packs.
Removed vs Retail BLU
WoW Forever is an Era-lineage client; these retail systems do not exist there and their modules, tabs, sounds, and defaults are gone: Achievements, Battle Pets, Collectibles, Delves, Housing, Prey, Renown, and the Trading Post.

addons.description:
RGX | Path of Exile Level-Up!RGX Mods - RealmGX Community Project

Overview
Path of Exile Level-Up! (POELU) replaces World of Warcraft's configured default level-up sound with a Path of Exile-inspired chime whenever the player gains a level. It is a small, automatic sound addon built on RGX-Framework.

The Kiwi Says: "Exile ding! Bwwiiiee."

Deprecation Notice
This addon is no longer receiving updates. Its functionality and Path of Exile sound are available in BLU | Better Level Up! and BLU Classic | Better Level Up!, which combine this sound with a larger sound collection.

Existing standalone users may continue to use this repository as-is, but new installations should prefer the appropriate BLU addon.

Behavior and Features
• Plays the selected Path of Exile-inspired sound on PLAYER_LEVEL_UP.
• Provides high, medium, and low OGG variants; medium is selected by default.
• Plays through the Master sound channel by default.
• Requests that RGX-Framework mute the configured default level-up sound while POELU is enabled.
• Persists enablement and sound-variant choices in POELUSettings.
• Shows a welcome message on login while that saved preference remains enabled.
• Includes a test command for checking playback immediately.

POELU does not alter leveling, experience gains, UI frames, or game data. It only handles the sound associated with the player's level-up event.

Requirements and Compatibility
RGX-Framework is a required dependency and must be installed and enabled. The current TOCs declare these game interfaces:

| WoW flavor | TOC | Interface |
|---|---|---:|
| Retail | PathOfExileLevelUp.toc | 120100 |
| WoW Forever (Beta) | PathOfExileLevelUp_Forever.toc | 16001 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Mists.toc | 50504 |
| Cataclysm Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Cata.toc | 40402 |
| Wrath Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Wrath.toc | 38002 |
| Burning Crusade Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_TBC.toc | 20506 |
| Classic Era | PathOfExileLevelUp_Vanilla.toc | 11509 |

These values describe the current release metadata. The addon is deprecated, so they are not a promise of compatibility with later game clients.

Language Support
POELU is fully localized across all 12 World of Warcraft client locales. The addon ships a single data/locales.lua that selects a locale block via GetLocale(), with an unconditional enUS base table providing the structural fallback — every key is present in every block. Supported locales (enUS plus eleven translations):

| Locale | Native name | Block |
|---|---|---|
| enUS | English (base/fallback) | unconditional base table |
| deDE | Deutsch | deDE |
| esES | Español (Europa) | esES |
| esMX | Español (Latinoamérica) | esMX |
| frFR | Français | frFR |
| itIT | Italiano | itIT |
| koKR | 한국어 | koKR |
| ptBR | Português (Brasil) | ptBR |
| ptPT | Português (Portugal) | ptPT |
| ruRU | Русский | ruRU |
| zhCN | 简体中文 | zhCN |
| zhTW | 繁體中文 | zhTW |

Each TOC declares ## X-Localizations listing all twelve locales. ptBR and ptPT use separate blocks; esMX has its own dedicated block (no longer sharing esES's block). Every block translates the complete key set — including the shared RGX_MODS_PREFIX brand key — so no untranslated key can leak into the game UI.

addons.changelog:
RGX-Hello v1.5.0
• Track RGX-Framework v2.11.0: X-RGX-Framework-MinVersion and the RGX:RequireContract("RGX-Hello", 1, "2.11.0") handshake floor both move to 2.11.0, so the reference addon exercises the framework's new module floor.
• No new RGX-Hello features this cycle; the addon remains the contract-congruent reference consumer.
addons.description:
The RGX-Framework reference addon and its in-game testing suite, in one install. It exists for two audiences at once:

> The TOCs own RGX-Hello's version and minimum Framework version. The source reference tracks the Framework stable release for strict release conformance; source metadata is not a new release announcement.
• Addon developers — data/core.lua is the canonical "hello world": the smallest complete RGX addon, written in the declarative RGXAddon style you should copy when starting your own.
• Framework development — data/visualtest.lua is the visual QA harness used to test RGX-Framework's features in-game before releases. As the framework grows, this suite grows with it; the goal is coverage of every framework feature.
Source Contract Conformance
RGX-Framework owns the runtime Lua API and the reusable declarative contract, generation, validation, audit, MCP, and editor/authoring infrastructure. Its tools/rgx-mcp/ transport is a private source-tree contract-conformance fixture, not a separately published product or part of the player addon. Developer tooling is optional: RGX-Hello and the framework runtime do not depend on MCP, Node.js, or an editor. A future RGX Studio application is a downstream consumer of that foundation, not the owner of runtime semantics or a shipped prerequisite. RGX-Hello remains wired into the fixture in both directions:
• rgx_generate_addon can reproduce data/core.lua's structure from a short spec — the hand-written file and the generator's output are kept convergent.
• The framework's end-to-end test (tools/rgx-mcp/test/test-rgx-hello.mjs) runs the real MCP server against this repo: it validates core.lua's opts table against the schema and audits every Lua file here for unsafe patterns. If this repo drifts from the contract, the framework's own test fails.

That loop has already paid off: its first run caught a framework bug (the declarative slider's suffix was silently dropped — this addon's own Volume slider shipped without its "%" until RGX-Framework v2.4.1 fixed it).
The Hello World (data/core.lua)
That single call gives you saved settings with automatic persistence, a tabbed options panel with declarative pages/card grids and db-bound controls, a named repeating timer, a slash command, a minimap button, branded chat output, and framework-scoped startup logic. No event frames, no C_Timer, no SLASH_X globals, no SavedVariables boilerplate.
The Testing Suite (data/visualtest.lua)
A hand-built options panel exercising the framework's manual API (RGX:GetUI(), RGX:GetColorPicker(), RGX:GetDropdowns(), RGX:GetFonts(), RGX:GetTextures()) — this is also the reference for going beyond the declarative surface.

| Command | Opens |
|---------|-------|
| /rgxhello | RGX-Hello's own options panel (the hello-world addon) |
| /rgxvisual or /rgxviz | The full test suite (tabs below) |
| /rgxcolor or /rgxcp | The color picker directly |

Current coverage:

| Tab | Framework features exercised |
|-----|------------------------------|
| Colors | RGXColorPicker (SV box, hue bar, HEX/RGB inputs, presets, OK/Cancel), UI:CreateColorPicker swatches + Reset |
| Controls | UI:CreateToggle, UI:CreateSlider, UI:CreateVolumeSlider, reset buttons, label word-wrap |
| Dropdowns | RGXDropdowns:CreateNestedDropdown (groups, separators, checked state) |
| Media | RGXFonts font dropdown, RGXTextures statusbar textures |
| Tooltip | RGXTooltip — Tip:Attach builder, manual Show/Hide, HookNative("item") injection |
| Auras | RGXAuras — accessible-only player/target scans, WatchUnit + OnApplied/OnUpdated/OnRemoved live log, phase counter snapshots, restricted-target suppression, unsubscribe |
| Minimap | RGXMinimap — MM:Create (icon, tooltip, drag, persistent angle), Toggle/IsShown |
| Design | RGX:Font one-call styling, RGXDesign CreateButton/CreateSectionHeader/CreateDivider, theme tokens |
| System | declarative every.heartbeat self-cancellation, RGX:After, RGX:Every, RGX:CancelTimer |…

Stand Upv1.0.0 (2026-10-19)
First public release, for WoW Forever.
• "Sedentary" debuff after 45 minutes of play, +1 stack every 15 minutes.
• Clears when you go AFK, log out, left-click it or type /stretched, and gives a 10-minute "Well Rested Legs" buff.
• Right-click to snooze for 15 minutes. The ding waits until combat ends.
• Sits beside the minimap by default; /standup unlock to move it.
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft add-on that reminds you to get up and stretch, using a debuff that looks like it belongs in the game.

After 45 minutes of play you get Sedentary. It gains a stack every 15 minutes until you take a break. Walk away from the keyboard and it clears, and you get a 10-minute Well Rested Legs buff for coming back.

Built for WoW Forever (interface 16001).
What it does
| | |
|---|---|
| First stack | After 45 minutes of play without a break |
| More stacks | +1 every 15 minutes |
| Where it shows | A red-bordered icon beside the minimap, with the stack count and the time to the next stack. Movable. |
| Reminders | A soft alarm-clock ding when a stack is added (held until combat ends) and a slow pulse at 3+ stacks. No popups or screen effects. |
| Tooltip | Gets snarkier with each stack, and shows how long you've played since your last break |
| Clearing it | Go AFK (the game flags you after about 5 minutes away), log out, left-click the icon, or type /stretched |
| Snooze | Right-click the icon to stop new stacks for 15 minutes, for a raid or a dungeon you can't leave |

Time spent AFK or snoozed doesn't count. A /reload doesn't count as a break; logging out for a minute or more does.
Commands
• /stretched: clear it (I stretched!)
• /standup: minutes played since your last break
• /standup test: jump to 3 stacks to preview it
• /standup unlock / /standup lock: drag the icon somewhere else
• /standup reset: put the icon back beside the minimap
addons.name: wow-standup

TurboFace 0.20.0
TurboFace 0.20.0 adds a saved sticky note and weapon-stone reminders, fixes
class spell-rank detection after trainer visits, and prevents a dungeon
swing-timer error involving protected target identities.
New features
• Sticky Note: Enable it in Options > Speedrun, then open it with
/tf note or /tfnote. Drag the header to move it, collapse it to the
header, or close it. Text, position, and collapsed/open state persist per
character. The dark background is easier on the eyes, and the feature
remains dormant when disabled.
• Weapon stones: The Class reminder queue now checks both hands for an
uncoated melee weapon and a compatible, level-eligible sharpening stone or
weightstone in your bags. Supports ordinary Rough through Dense stones.
Existing temporary enchants, poisons, and imbues satisfy the reminder.
Enabled by default, with a toggle in Class Features; hidden during combat
and while dead. Keep the queue's “Only show while in combat” option off to
see this out-of-combat reminder.
Fixes
• Class Training uses explicit learned spell IDs and client-specific rank
replacement chains across all nine classes, preventing starter-rank aliases
from incorrectly hiding later ranks.
• Trainer visits preserve rank metadata when the client omits rank labels,
and resolve ambiguous spell families using catalog rank and level data.
• The training queue respects the same learned-rank result as the list.
• Target and nameplate swing timers reject unreadable GUIDs before cache
lookup, avoiding the secret-table-key error reported in dungeons.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79. Existing settings and
character data are preserved.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.20.0.zip — Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.20.0.zip — Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to one
TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.4
TurboFace 0.19.4 fixes starter-rank detection in Class Training, including
Forever spellbook aliases that could hide untrained Warrior abilities.
Highlights
• Learned-rank detection prefers the base spellbook slot identity over an
active spell override. Heroic Strike and Rend Rank 2 remain available for
training when the character still knows only their starter ranks.
• Catalog level requirements cap impossible future-rank aliases, keeping
Battle Shout Rank 2 in a level-10 Warrior's future training list. The cached
snapshot refreshes when the character's level changes.
• Heroic Strike Rank 2 now correctly requires Rank 1 instead of itself.
• Both Classic and Forever include the shared training fixes and modern
spellbook compatibility fallback.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.19.4.zip — World of Warcraft Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.4.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to a
single TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.3
TurboFace 0.19.3 adds a safe mover for Forever's native target-unit castbar
and refreshes the built-in Rumblecrush preset from the latest live profile.
Highlights
• Forever players can position Blizzard's native Target Unit Cast Bar from
TurboFace's Blizzard Movers section. TurboFace moves only the native bar's
anchor and leaves cast state, rendering, animations, and interaction under
Blizzard ownership.
• The mover reapplies its position after Blizzard target and aura layout passes,
defers protected writes during combat, and restores Blizzard's layout when the
mover or the global Movers module is disabled.
• Position-only movers do not expose Hide or Click Through controls, preventing
those generic controls from changing native-frame behavior.
• /tfmove targetcastprobe reports the resolved native frame, protection state,
anchor ownership, deferred state, geometry, and last write error.
• Rumblecrush's Preset is refreshed from the 2026-10-06 profile export. It
positions the native target castbar at CENTER (145, -375), moves Target of
Target to CENTER (350, -260), and enables nameplate swing timers and
Speedrun Splits.
• The Forever-only native castbar mover data is safely inert in the Classic
package; the shared preset updates continue to apply normally.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.19.3.zip — World of Warcraft Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.3.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to a
single TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.2
TurboFace 0.19.2 makes nameplate combo points persist on their actual target
while preserving Classic's single-target ownership rules.
Highlights
• Combo points remain visible on their target's nameplate after deselecting it
or selecting another unit, much like retained nameplate debuffs.
• Only the current target is queried. TurboFace stores the last readable count
in addon-owned per-nameplate state and never probes protected non-target data.
• Earning the first combo point on a different target transfers ownership and
immediately clears every older visible combo snapshot.
• Nameplates with zero combo points show no combo row, whether selected or not.
Positive snapshots continue to display the full five-slot progression row.
• Nameplate removal and pooled-frame reuse clear retained snapshots so combo
points cannot leak onto another unit.
• Forever's detached aura guides release or restore combo-row spacing whenever
a retained row changes visibility, without reanchoring secret-bound aura
containers.
• Druid form transitions hide retained rows outside Cat Form and restore valid
positive snapshots on returning to Cat Form.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.19.2.zip — World of Warcraft Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.2.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to a
single TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.1
TurboFace 0.19.1 is a focused hotfix for movable nameplate combo points and
starter-spell ranks in Class Training.
Highlights
• Forever nameplate debuffs now follow an addon-owned movable anchor guide.
Moving combo points downward dynamically releases their reserved space, while
the default upper position continues to keep debuffs clear of the combo row.
• The aura fix does not reanchor Blizzard's secret-bound AuraContainer after it
has been attached, preserving the Midnight-safe ownership boundary.
• Class Training now matches the exact spell ID in each live spellbook slot to
the class rank catalog.
• Starter abilities whose first trainer purchase is Rank 2—including Sinister
Strike and Heroic Strike—no longer lose Rank 2 while still showing Rank 3.
• Learned higher ranks continue to collapse their older rows correctly, and the
fallback applies across all class starter-spell families rather than using
Rogue- or Warrior-specific exceptions.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.

• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.1.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

version numbers Semantic Versioning.

• With Auctionator and no AuctionDB, AH sales and Profit's auction house rows were empty: Craft Ladder now reads how
many are listed from Auctionator's own database, which its API doesn't give. With AuctionDB installed nothing
changes.

Craft Ladder): a click shows that character's professions and ladders as its last session left them, with its
skills, recipes, bags, bank and level, and says how old that is. To read, not to craft from: no Craft bar, Camp or
Disenchant for them. Click yourself to come back.

• Your skill on the bar is a gold "Skill 142" badge.
• Easier to read: lighter grey notes, bigger text in a step's details, coin icons for money, items in their
quality's colour.
• Profit: no "Sell at the auction house" heading when nothing sells to a vendor.
• A neutral line under the window's title instead of the faction's colour.
1.3.0 - 2026-10-20Added
• Specialization (Blacksmithing, Engineering, Leatherworking): a button beside the ladder's modes shows the steps
to each specialization of the profession, the one you pick remembered: Weaponsmith (and a weapon mastery after it)
or Armorsmith, Gnomish or Goblin Engineer, Dragonscale, Elemental or Tribal Leatherworking. Each step has its quest
givers on the map, says when a quest is in your log or done, and counts what it asks for against your bags and bank
("2 / 4 Moonsteel Broadsword"). The recipes it takes say whether you know them and where to learn the rest; what's
still missing is made or bought, whichever costs less, with its ingredients and the total still to spend.
• Disenchant (beta) (Enchanting): a mode for what's worth disenchanting. First what's in your bags that can be
disenchanted, whatever made it, each with what brings more: disenchant it, sell it at the auction house (not when
it's soulbound) or to a vendor. Then what your crafting professions make with the recipes you know that's worth
more disenchanted than sold, the best first, in red when making it costs more than disenchanting brings; grey when
your Enchanting can't disenchant it yet. A card shows what one disenchant gives (chance, count and price of each
material), what 10 (or yours) bring on average and at least 9 times out of 10, and the Craft bar to make it. What a
disenchant gives is Classic's table, except WoW Forever's low-level blue items, which give dust and essences like a
green of their level, one more of each. Craft Ladder records your disenchants: from 5 of one kind of item, what you
got replaces the table.

• Each step in the ladder says how many of its crafts what you already have covers, under its cost: "12 ready" or…
addons.description:
Craft Ladder is a smart profession leveling and crafting optimization addon for World of Warcraft: Forever. It helps you find cost-efficient routes from skill 1 to 300 using auction house prices, vendor costs, and materials already in your bags.

Whether you're leveling Engineering, Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Tailoring, Cooking, or gathering professions, Craft Ladder creates a step-by-step plan showing what to craft, how many items you need, where to learn each recipe, and how much it will cost. It also helps you discover profitable crafting opportunities and gathering zones.

Download Craft Ladder on CurseForge
Professions
• Crafting: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Leatherworking, Tailoring, Cooking, First Aid, Poisons
• Gathering: Mining, Herbalism, Skinning, Fishing, Lockpicking
Modes
• Vendor sales (gathering: Skill): level up for the least gold you're sure to spend. What you make is counted
as sold to vendors only: no auctions to post or wait for (gathering: the fastest points).
• AH sales: level up counting what the auction house pays for what you make too: cheaper than Vendor sales if it
sells (gathering: where an hour earns the most on the way).
• Profit: no ladder, just what you can make now that earns the most per craft (for gathering: the zones where an
hour earns the most at your skill).
• Food (Cooking): the dishes worth eating for your class, grouped by role, by what their Well Fed raises, each in
its skill-up colour.
What each step tells you
• The recipe, the skill range and about how many crafts it takes, coloured as the game colours it.
• Where to learn it: trainer, vendor, quest, auction house or a recipe already in your bags, with the NPC and its
place.
• Every reagent: bought at a vendor, at the auction house, or made by you, and what the whole step costs (red, with a
minus) or earns back (green, with a plus).
• What you already have counts: bags and, with Bagnon, the bank. A step you can make from your bags goes first, and
each step says how many of its crafts what you have covers ("12 ready"; vendor reagents aside).
• The recipes you know are read from your profession window; a recipe you just learned counts at once.

For gathering: the zones to level in, the nodes, herbs, creatures or fishing pools that still give a point, and the
gold an hour each zone earns.
Also
• Auction house tab: the ladder as a shopping list, a row per step with its reagents. With Auctionator, its
Search button opens Auctionator's Shopping tab with exactly what to buy.
• Merchant's Favor recipes: the supply camps' quartermaster recipes, with their favor prices and what one craft
takes (your bars and ore counted first), and a Favor mode in the auction house tab to buy it. They can join the
ladder too.
• Camp: what each camp feature gives around a campfire at your level, in the order your role wants them, and how
to get it.
• Specialization (Blacksmithing, Engineering, Leatherworking): the steps to each specialization, with the quest
givers on the map, the quests done or in your log, what they ask for against your bags and bank, the recipes you
know or still need, and what's left to make or buy.
• The range to level: From and To over the ladder (or a rank's name under the skill bar), Reset for your skill
to 300.
• A minimap button and the addon compartment; the window remembers its size, scale and place.
Screenshots
Profit: what earns the most per craft now.

Mining in AH sales: the zones to level in, the nodes there and what they're worth.

The auction house tab, and what its Search button opens in Auctionator.

Camp: the camp features in the order your role wants them.

Cooking's Food mode: the dishes worth eating for your class.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for Classic Era and World of Warcraft: Forever:
every faction's road to Exalted from where you stand, and a chapter of its
story at each standing you reach.
• The road. For each faction: how far to the next standing, the turn-ins
your bags and bank already hold (and how many times they'd go in), the
quests still open to you, the kills that still count and the standing they
stop at.
• The unlocks. What each standing opens, as the game's items: the
quartermasters' goods, the recipes (with their trade), the quests.
• The stories. Thirty-five factions have a voice of their own: Gorn One
Eye of the Timbermaw, Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff of the Argent Dawn, Lokhtos
Darkbargainer of the Thorium Brotherhood and thirty-two more tell you a
little more at every standing you reach with them, from the stranger's
warning to what they keep for those they trust.
• The achievements. The book keeps its own: your first gain with a
faction, the standings you reach, whole groups at Exalted and the stories
you open, each with the game's fanfare and alert.

English and French. /goodwill opens the book.

The game's data comes from wow-data:
the game clients' tables, Questie's
database and the cmangos Classic
database.

MIT licence.

addons.description:
Hearthtale keeps a journal for your World of Warcraft character as you play.
Quests, close calls, new places and the people you travel with become entries
written in your character's voice. Each race has its own way of telling the
story. On Hardcore, a death closes the journal with an epitaph and saves it
in the Hall of the Fallen.

You can read the books in game or on hearthtale.app.
The optional Ravenpost companion
uploads them after you log out or reload.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of Warcraft:
Forever. One download covers both games.
In game
Type /hearthtale or /ht, or click the minimap button to open the journal.
Each login says in chat whether you're resuming an entry or starting a new
one.
Choose an entry from the list to read it. The second tab holds the Hall of
the Fallen, which you can also open with /ht hall. The third holds your
fellow travellers: the players you have grouped with, when and where you met,
the days you spent together, and a note of your own on each. They stay on your
computer, never in the book or on the site.

An entry follows the time between rests. Logging out at an inn, in a city
or by a campfire closes it. Logging out in the wild records a night outdoors
and keeps it going. After four hours of play, the next logout closes the entry
wherever you are. A character you already play starts with a prologue, then
builds a journal from that point on.

Use an entry's Edit button to give it your own title or add a note. You
can also use /ht title [N] TEXT and /ht note [N] TEXT. Leave out N to
change the latest entry. Your words are kept separately from the journal's
text.

A finished entry keeps its words, even after an update improves the
writing. /ht rewrite writes the whole journal again with the current
version, after asking. Your titles and notes stay.
Read on hearthtale.app
Install Ravenpost and click Sign in with Battle.net in its window. For
Forever characters, or any character Battle.net cannot find, get
a code from Link a character on the site and enter /ht link CODE in
game. Your book arrives after your next logout or /reload.

The website is optional, and books are private unless you choose to share
them. Your notes stay out of a shared book and the Hall. Setup instructions
are at hearthtale.app/start.

The interface is available in English and French.

The journal is written in English, on any game client. On other clients the
game's names in it (places, creatures, people, quests, items, trades, spells)
are kept in English too. In Forever dungeons, the journal can
only tell kills that a quest also counts.
Settings
The welcome page appears once per character. Open it again with
/ht welcome. Settings are under Options > AddOns > Hearthtale, through
/ht settings or by right-clicking the minimap button.

Choose the alert when a book closes and the minimap button's visibility and
position (chat lines always show). You can mark a character as Hardcore when
the game cannot identify it. Settings are saved per character and can be
transferred with /ht export and /ht import CODE. Use /ht minimap to
show or hide the button.

Hearthtale shares its book style with its author's other addons, listed on
its store page. Each addon works independently.

The full store description is in addon/CURSEFORGE.md.
PLAN.md records the design decisions, and CLAUDE.md
describes how the journal is written and the rules its sentences follow.

addons.description:
Keyring gathers your addons' minimap buttons into a drawer, leaving one key on
the minimap. Click the key to open the drawer, and close it with Escape,
another click on the key or a click elsewhere.

One download covers Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. Keyring speaks English and French. Other
clients get English.
Using Keyring
• Left-click the key to open or close the drawer.
• Right-click the key for the settings.
• Drag the key to move it around the minimap.
• Untick a button in the settings to leave it on the minimap instead.

The drawer arranges buttons in a grid and follows your minimap's scale. The
drawer stays open while you use a menu opened from one of its buttons.

Keyring finds buttons made with LibDBIcon, which most addons use, and other
addons' buttons on the minimap that it recognises by name. The game's own
buttons stay where they are: tracking, mail, the clock, the zoom buttons and
Forever's addon compartment. So do map pins and anything over twice the size
of a minimap button. Buttons hidden by their own addon stay hidden. Protected
buttons are left in place because the game restricts moving or hiding them
during combat.

The key uses the game's minimap ring and highlight, with a painted keyring
icon. Keyring works as soon as you install it.
Commands
• /keyring opens or closes the drawer.
• /keyring settings opens the settings.
• /keyring list shows in chat the buttons in the drawer and those left on the
minimap.
• /keyring reset puts the key back in its place.

addons.description:
Lorekeeper's Codex adds a book of Azeroth's lore that fills in as you explore.
Visit Kharanos, speak with King Magni, defeat a Frostmane troll or finish a
quest, and you might discover a page about the history behind it. Each page
is an original text written as a note from Archesonus, Royal Historian of
Ironforge. A Horde character's copy comes from Parqual Fintallas, a historian
of the Undercity, who adds notes of his own in the margins.

The Codex has 441 pages in 44 chapters, or **456 pages in 46 chapters on
Forever**. It covers the original world's zones, landmarks, figures, peoples,
classes and history. Each race gets its own foreword.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. One download covers all of them. See
FOREVER.md for Forever support.
In game
Type /codex or click the minimap button to read. Browse by chapter, search
your discovered pages or filter by type. Related pages link to each other.
Each character keeps a separate codex, with the date, level and location of
every discovery. Undiscovered pages stay hidden.

Pages unlock by exploring, meeting people, defeating creatures, finishing
quests, gaining reputation and reading books or inscriptions. A chat link,
an alert and a sound announce each discovery. Tooltips point out creatures
and players who can unlock a page.

The lore covers the world's past up to the original game, using Warcraft I
to III, WoW's quests and books, and the novels and histories about that
period. Later expansion events and answers to mysteries left open in the
original game are kept out. The Codex reads in English and
French. Other clients get English,
with the places and the Library's titles in their own language. Most unlocks
use game ids, and reading-based unlocks
recognise titles in every client language. Where you found a page is kept by
the game's ids, so it follows your client's language, even after you switch.

On Forever, kill-based unlocks work in the open world. Creatures inside
dungeons and raids are hidden from addons, so kills there cannot unlock pages.
Some pages, paragraphs and unlocks differ between Classic and Forever.
Library and achievements
The Library saves the books, notes, quest letters and plaques you read
in the world. Texts are copied in full, with where and when you found them,
so you can return to a quest letter after handing it in. Letters written by
players are never copied. The top of the shelves brings back the Library at a
glance: what each shelf holds and the texts copied lately.

The Achievements tab tracks page milestones, completed chapters, Library
progress, notable encounters and feats. Each achievement records the day
and level you earned it. Open the tab with /codex achievements.
Settings and commands
The welcome page appears once per character. Use /codex welcome to see it
again. Settings are under Options > AddOns > Lorekeeper's Codex, through
/codex settings or by right-clicking the minimap button.

Choose the alerts for new pages and for achievements, their duration,
sounds, tooltip hints and the minimap button (chat lines always show). Each character has its own settings. Copy another
character's settings in the same game, or transfer them with /codex export
and /codex import CODE.
• /codex minimap shows or hides the minimap button. Drag it to move it.
• /codex banner toggles page alerts.
• /codex reset clears this character's codex after confirmation.
• /codex where prints your position and target for writing new pages.
• /codex scan on records areas, creatures, quest texts and books to help
write Forever content. scripts/scan-export.lua converts the saved data
to JSON.

Known Library texts also follow your client's language (English and French
for now). Original game wording is used where available, with documented
translations for missing bodies. Unrecognised copies stay as recorded.

addons.description:
Quests and conversations with NPCs in a panel beside them, read and answered
from the keyboard, in the look of its sibling addons.

One download for Classic Era and World of Warcraft: Forever.
Using it
Talk to an NPC: their words, their quests and their options open in a
panel in the look of its siblings, the NPC's face in its corner and the NPC
still in view.
• Space (or Enter) answers yes: Accept, Continue, Complete Quest.
• Escape says goodbye, with the keys on or off.
• 1 to 9 pick a line, or the reward to take when a quest offers a choice.

A key acts when you let it go, and only on the page you pressed it on: a
held Space never accepts the next quest. On a page longer than the panel,
Space or Enter first scrolls down, so you never accept a quest with its
rewards unseen. In combat, while typing or with a modifier held, the keys stay
the game's. Drag the panel to move it.

A quest's offer shows what the game's own window keeps quiet: its level in
the colour of how hard it is for you, whether it's elite, a dungeon, a raid
or PvP, where it sits in its chain, like part 2 of 7, and the group size the
game suggests.

Books, letters and plaques open in the same panel. Space turns the page,
Backspace turns back.

While you talk or read, the game's interface fades away, so only the panel and
the one you speak to stay on screen. It comes back for a fight, a vendor, a
trainer or a question from the game. Keep it on screen with /palaver hud or
the game's Options.

When a quest offers a choice of rewards, two marks help you pick. A green
arrow sits on the best upgrade for your character, and a gold coin on the
best value, the one that sells for the most. Hover a marked reward to see
why. The arrow weighs the stats your class wants against what you wear, and
Palaver needs no other addon for it. The marks never choose for you.

Every setting is also on Palaver's page in the game's Options, under AddOns.

If DialogueUI, Immersion or Storyline is installed, Palaver stays out of its
way and says so.
Languages
The NPCs' words, the quests and the game's buttons are the game's own, in
your client's language. Palaver's few words of its own are in English and French.
Thanks
Palaver's way of talking to NPCs follows DialogueUI, by Peterodox and
Raenore. Quest levels and chains come from QuestieDB (Wowhead for Forever's
newest quests), the quest kinds' names from the game's own tables.

addons.description:
Second Wind gives you a debrief after a close call or death in World of
Warcraft. Once the fight is over, it shows the hits that hurt most, how
your health fell, and which potions or abilities were ready but went unused.
After a few debriefs, you can compare what your dangerous fights have in
common.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever, in English and French. Nothing pops up
during combat. Duels and battlegrounds are excluded.

Get it from CurseForge,
Wago or
GitHub releases.
One download covers all of them.
In game
Type /secondwind or /wind, or click the minimap button to open the book.
By default, surviving below 15% health counts as a close call. The threshold
can also be set to 10%, 20% or 25%.

The Debriefs tab shows individual fights, with a health graph, foes,
large hits, healing, stuns and fears, and the tools you used or left ready.
Patterns compares close calls after your third debrief. Lifelines
shows the emergency supplies you carry now and their cooldowns.

Debriefs are saved across your account, separately for each game. A fallen
Hardcore character's last fight remains available from your next character.
An optional word before a pull gives, in chat, the counts of your close calls
against foes like the one you target.

Forever limits the health and combat information addons can read. Second
Wind reconstructs health estimates from damage, healing and the game's
low-health warning or death recap. That warning must stay on
(Options > Combat). The debrief shows when a health value is an estimate.

Second Wind reads in English and French. Other clients get English, with the game's own names for your foes, spells,
items and places in their language. Debriefs keep them by the game's ids, so
they follow your client's language, even after you switch.
• /wind copy opens a text version of the debrief for you to copy.
• /wind lifelines opens the Lifelines tab.
• /wind probe reports what the game let the addon read after your next fight.
• /wind settings opens settings for thresholds, alerts and the word before a pull.
• /wind welcome reopens the welcome page.
• /wind minimap shows or hides the minimap button.
• /wind export and /wind import CODE transfer settings.
• /wind reset clears this character's debriefs after confirmation.

Second Wind shares its book style with the other addons of the family. Each
works independently, and Keyring can gather their minimap buttons behind one button.

addons.description:
Yonder gives you riddles to solve, rare creatures to hunt
and a record of what you find along the way. Follow a clue to a forgotten
grave, track down a rare you've never fought, or fill in your bestiary while
levelling. Notes from an Explorers' League naturalist accompany your finds.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. One download covers all of them.

Yonder was called Explorer's Field Journal until version 0.8.0: another
addon used the same folder. A character's old journal moves over on its own
at its first login with Yonder, through the small FieldJournal folder in the
download (on Classic Era, removed in a later update).
What's in the journal
• Expeditions. 162 riddles and 38 rare hunts across the original world.
Forever adds four riddles and a hunt on Zephras Isle. Riddles lead to
overlooked places and are solved by reaching a spot, speaking to someone,
reading something or working out a gesture from the verse. They never
require a kill.
• Bestiary. Around 3,500 creatures in 96 families, each with a
naturalist's note. Creature pages keep your first sighting, observed levels,
kill counts, loot and drop rates. Rares and bosses become trophies.
• Finds. Fish, plants, ores and gems, cloth and leather in one tab,
with a naturalist's note for every item. Gathering professions open their
collections, while cloth is available to everyone. Once opened, a collection
stays with you even if you change professions.
• Atlas. The zones you've visited, with maps, explored places, surveyor's
notes, flights, deaths and close calls.
• Achievements. For exploring, completing expeditions, collecting
trophies, fishing and gathering.

Each riddle has two optional hints: a clearer clue, then a location marked
on the world map. Solve it without hints for a gold seal and an extra piece
of the story. Rare hunts have posters describing the creature and its
haunts. Track a hunt to mark those haunts on your map, or complete it without
tracking for a gold seal. You can pin a riddle or a poster to your screen.

Creatures join the Bestiary when you first kill them. Kills by you, your pet
or your group count, including damage over time and area spells. A tagged
creature finished by another player also counts when your quest credits
the kill. A chat link announces each new creature, without a banner or sound.
Rares and bosses have a trophy sound.

Search by family or creature name, sort your records and browse trophies.
Tooltips show whether you've recorded a creature and how many you've killed.
Each character has its own journal. Undiscovered creatures stay hidden,
with no count showing how many remain.

Forever hides creatures inside dungeons and raids from addons, so the
journal cannot record them there.

Yonder reads in English and French. Other clients get English, with the game's own names in their
language: creatures, places, flight points, fish, and the riddles' and
quarries' answers. The journal keeps everything
by the game's ids, so what you recorded follows your client's language, even
after you switch.
Opening the journal
Type /yonder or click the minimap button. The journal opens on Expeditions.
Each login says in chat what the journal holds.

Waypoint Tracker is a free, open-source addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW Forever, the new classic-style World of Warcraft, sometimes called Classic+). A 3D arrow over your character points to your waypoint, shows the distance and time to arrive, turns from gold to green as you get close, and clears itself when you arrive. Set waypoints from coordinates (/way 42 65), the world map, or by name: the built-in Find window searches quests, NPCs, enemies, objects and items, including WoW Forever's new content. Share any spot in chat as a clickable map pin. New in 1.1, Treasure hunt (beta) pings you when a chest or rare appears near you.

It's a TomTom-style arrow and a quest and NPC finder in one addon, with nothing to configure.
