2.0.3 (2026-10-27) — Ranked spell and retail combat fixesBug Fixes
• A spell with ranks no longer shows its cooldown twice on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. After you cast rank 2 or higher of a spell that puts a buff on you and has a cooldown, such as Divine Protection, Divine Shield, Blessing of Protection or Sprint, a second copy of its cooldown appeared once the buff wore off: a second bar, a second lane icon and a second ready icon. Cooldown Master lists a spell under its first rank, so it took the higher rank's buff for a separate spell and then read the shared cooldown for it too. The buff still shows while it is up, and the cooldown now shows once.
• A higher rank's buff no longer pops a ready icon while its spell is still on cooldown. Casting Divine Protection rank 2, for example, popped a "Divine Protection" ready icon the moment its buff wore off, with nearly 5 minutes of cooldown left. A buff that outlasts its cooldown, such as Ice Barrier, still pops when it ends, since the spell really is ready by then.
• Ticking the Buff column on a spell with ranks now works at every rank, the same as at rank 1. It only ever matched rank 1's buff, so from rank 2 up the buff ignored the lane, ready box and bar you chose for it, and Filters > Buffs listed the spell twice.
• Aura gained custom cooldowns no longer raise a Lua error in every fight on retail. Since patch 12.1 the game raises an error when an addon reads your buffs during combat, where it used to hand back hidden values. With an Aura gained custom cooldown set up, that error came up again and again through every fight. Cooldown Master now reads your buffs only once combat ends, as it already did on WoW Forever. An Aura gained custom still cannot fire mid-fight on retail, because the game keeps your buffs hidden until combat ends. /cm buffs in combat now says the read was blocked instead of raising an error.
• Pressing Detect on a custom cooldown during a fight on retail no longer raises a Lua error or fills in a buff you already had. Detect now does nothing until combat ends, as on WoW Forever, so press it after the fight.

2.0.2 (2026-10-20) — Masque and WoW Forever fixesBug Fixes
• Turning off a Cooldown Master group in Masque no longer leaves its icons as black squares. Masque moves an icon behind its border while it skins it, and nothing moved it back when you switched the group off, so Cooldown Master's own black icon border covered the art until a /reload. Lane icons, ready boxes and bars now come straight back the moment you turn a group off, including icons that were not on screen at the time, and bar icons no longer keep a leftover Masque ring.
• Buffing a groupmate mid-fight on WoW Forever no longer shows up as your own buff. Forever blocks addons from reading your buffs in combat, so Cooldown Master follows what you cast, and until now it could not tell who a buff landed on. A blessing you put on a groupmate appeared on your own lane and could clear the icon of your own blessing until combat ended. Cooldown Master now reads who each buff was cast on. Seals and anything you cast on yourself restart at once, as before. When the buff you put on someone else shares its name with one you are wearing, or is a party-wide buff such as Arcane Brilliance or Prayer of Fortitude that may have reached you too, your own icon keeps its old timer and leaves quietly instead of popping a ready box, and comes back with its real timer if the buff is still up when combat ends.
• /cm help no longer lists the offensives commands on WoW Forever, where offensive tracking does not run.
Thanks
• yisisixu on GitHub — for the Filters page suggestions that shaped 2.0.0's search box, per-category defaults and Defaults overview, which went uncredited in 2.0.0's notes.

2.0.1 (2026-10-13) — Holy Strike fix for WoW ForeverBug Fixes
• A spell you use again the moment it comes off cooldown no longer gets stuck at the ready end of its lane on WoW Forever. Holy Strike showed it most, but any spell with ranks could do it, Hammer of Justice included. Forever reports the rank you cast, while Cooldown Master had the spell listed under a different rank, so it never saw the recast. The icon sat at the ready end through the whole next cooldown, its ready box came a full cooldown late, and it stayed stuck for as long as you kept using the spell the moment it came back. It now restarts the instant you cast. This is Forever only. Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and retail are untouched. Thanks to wimpby on Discord for the report.

2.0.0 (2026-10-12) — A new settings windowNew Features
• A brand new settings window. Cooldown Master's options now open in the same window as Everything Quests, EQ Objective Tracker and Everything Delves. A sidebar on the left holds Global, Lanes, Ready, Bars, Filters, Colors, Profiles and About, and each page is laid out in cards. Lanes, Ready and Bars open into their sections, and a switch across the top of each page picks which lane, box or bar frame you are editing. Click an open group again to fold it away. The window opens on the last page you used, per character. Every setting carries over exactly as you left it, and nothing resets.
• Unlock Frames and Test sit at the bottom of every page that changes what you see, so you can drag a lane or run a test without leaving the page you are tuning. Test turns into Stop Test while one is running, and closing the window ends it, as before.
• Click any slider's number to type an exact value.
• Find a cooldown in seconds. Each category's list in Filters has a search box that narrows it as you type, and the column headings carry the explanations instead of every row. The Defaults page now shows at a glance where each category sends its cooldowns, and clicking one opens it.
• What's New now appears only for releases that bring new features. A release with only fixes stays quiet, and the next feature release lists it too, so nothing is missed. If you have been away for several versions, it lists everything since you last looked, and a first install no longer opens it at all. The chat link option and Don't show these again work as before.
Improvements
• Settings that do nothing in your current setup are hidden, and settings a switch turns off are dimmed. Grow Direction and Height disappear for a Spread lane, for example, In Group and In Instance dim while Always is ticked, and Raise On Mouseover dims unless tooltips are on and frames are locked.
• A lane's labels are one table in its Text section, a row per label, with each label's position in percent or seconds to match how it is anchored.
• Bars has its own Text section for the name and time text, which makes its other sections much shorter.
• Highlight Style offers None, Border and Flash. Glow and Border + Flash always drew exactly what Flash draws, so they are gone from the list. If you had one picked, it keeps drawing as it always has and shows as Flash.
• Four tooltips that described their setting wrongly are corrected: a lane's Mode, Hand Off Below, Flags and Route by Cooldown Length. Many settings that had no tooltip now have one, and the bars' time font settings no longer claim to work on retail only. They work on every client.
• Medium Up To can no longer be set below Short Up To. Cooldown Master already treated it that way, so the slider now matches what it does.
• Copying a profile now asks first. It used to overwrite your current profile the moment you clicked. Everything in the window that erases or overwrites settings now asks in red: Copy, Delete, Reset, Import, Set All and deleting a custom cooldown.
• Profiles is one list. Your active profile is highlighted, and every other one has Switch, Copy and Delete beside it. New Profile, Duplicate Current, Export and Import are on the same page.
• The Colors page lists your own class first.
• Test Mode no longer offers Buff Bars on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic or WoW Forever, where that category does not exist.
• Links open in a copy box you cannot accidentally edit, for Discord, CurseForge, GitHub and exported profiles.
• The Options Window scale now stops at the largest size that fits your screen.
• The About page lists EQ Objective Tracker with the other addons.
• Escape closes the window out of combat. In combat, use its close button.
• All seven languages are complete for this release.
Bug Fixes…

addons.changelog: v1.0.0 of F-Perl (Forever Perl)
addons.description:
Unit frames for World of Warcraft: Forever: player, pet, target, focus, target of target, party, party pets and raid. F-Perl keeps the look of the classic X-Perl unit frames, rebuilt for the Forever client. Three optional raid tools come with it: Raid Admin, Raid Helper and Raid Monitor.
What F-Perl does differently
• Auras are drawn by the game's own aura display, so buffs and debuffs keep showing in content where the game hides aura details from addons.
• Light on the game: frames update when the game reports a change, not by checking on a timer, and no setting or event redraws every frame when only one part changed.
• A new settings system, built into the game's settings panel: every option in one place, one page per frame group, and changes take effect at once (only switching the Player, Pet or Target frame on or off needs /reload).
• Layouts: named sets of positions and settings, shared by all your characters, switched in the options or with /fperl layout .
• A new unlock mode: unlocking hides the options and shows a small toolbar with an alignment grid and snapping, and a right-click on any frame opens a menu of its common settings. Changing a frame's scale keeps it where it is.
• Automatic range fading: F-Perl picks your longest-range spells from your spellbook, so out-of-range units fade without any setup for your class.

Changelogv1.11.3 (2026-10-23)Fixed
• A macro like /cast !Stealth was saved as a spell called "!Stealth", so its button stayed empty on a new
character. A "!" in front (it keeps Stealth, an aura or a stance from toggling off) now keeps it a macro. A plan
saved before puts the macro back on that button when applied.
v1.11.2 (2026-10-23)Fixed
• Apply from the window could freeze the game for a moment when it changed many keybindings: the window redrew
itself once for every key. It now redraws once.
• Export and Export all took noticeably long with several plans. They use a faster compression setting now (the text
is a little longer; Import reads both).
• After the Import window had been open, Export showed Import's summary and its "macros that run code" checkbox under
the text. It shows the character count again.
v1.11.1 (2026-10-21)Fixed
• A button BarPlan couldn't read when a plan was saved was left out of the plan, so Apply cleared it and put
nothing back. Such a button is now kept in the plan as "keep as it is", and Apply leaves it alone.
New
• /barplan debug [from-to] (default 1-12) lists what BarPlan sees on those buttons and what the plan has there,
for bug reports.
v1.11.0 (2026-10-21)New
• The plan list in the window shows the plans of every class (yours first, each with its class), so you can
export, delete or choose the plan offered to new characters of any class from any character. Apply stays for
plans of your own class. /barplan export finds a plan of another class by its name too.
• Export all (in the window, or /barplan exportall): every plan of every class in one text. Import adds them
all back.
• Import no longer replaces a plan by default: a name you already have gets a number ("Paladin (2)"). The window
says for each plan what will happen; for a single plan you can still type an existing name to replace it.
• Macros that run code are still left out of an imported plan by default; a checkbox in the import window (shown
when the text has such macros, off each time) imports them too, at your own discretion.
v1.10.1 (2026-10-21)Fixed
• The reload question after Apply could sit behind or overlap other windows. It now stays in front of everything,
in the middle of the screen.
v1.10.0 (2026-10-20)New
• Share a plan as a text string: Export in the window (or /barplan export [name]) shows it to copy; Import
(/barplan import) adds a plan from one to its class, on any character or account. Macros that run code
(/run, /script, /console, /click ...) are left out of an imported plan.
v1.9.1 (2026-10-20)Fixed
• A spell you learn was left where the game put it, on the first empty button: on a button the plan keeps for a
spell you haven't learned yet (which then never went there), or on one the plan keeps empty. A spell the game
places as you learn it now goes off any button the plan doesn't have it on, so the plan's buttons stay free.
v1.9.0 (2026-10-19)New
• Edit Mode layout: a plan keeps the Blizzard Edit Mode layout its character uses. Applying it adds the layout
(replacing an older one of the same name), makes it the new character's and offers a reload to set it up.
Its own On/Off switch in the window, /barplan editmode on|off. Save a plan again to add its layout.
• The reload question after Apply covers addons and the layout together.
v1.8.0 (2026-10-19)New
• A plan saved on a character using the account-wide keybindings now keeps those keys too. Applying it sets the
account-wide keys to the plan's, so a new account or a fresh WoW folder gets your keys as well (before, it only
switched the character to the account-wide keys, whatever they were). Save such a plan again to add its keys.
v1.7.0 (2026-10-19)
First release on CurseForge.
New
• A macro that only casts one spell (#showtooltip X / /cast X) is saved in a plan as that spell. Keep such
placeholders on the character you save from (for spells it can't learn yet): new characters get the plain
spell on that button when they learn it, and no macro.…

• The reload question after Apply could sit behind or overlap other windows. It now stays in front of everything,

v1.10.0 (2026-10-20)New
• Share a plan as a text string: Export in the window (or /barplan export [name]) shows it to copy; Import
(/barplan import) adds a plan from one to its class, on any character or account. Macros that run code
(/run, /script, /console, /click ...) are left out of an imported plan.
v1.9.1 (2026-10-20)Fixed
• A spell you learn was left where the game put it, on the first empty button: on a button the plan keeps for a
spell you haven't learned yet (which then never went there), or on one the plan keeps empty. A spell the game
places as you learn it now goes off any button the plan doesn't have it on, so the plan's buttons stay free.
v1.9.0 (2026-10-19)New
• Edit Mode layout: a plan keeps the Blizzard Edit Mode layout its character uses. Applying it adds the layout
(replacing an older one of the same name), makes it the new character's and offers a reload to set it up.
Its own On/Off switch in the window, /barplan editmode on|off. Save a plan again to add its layout.
• The reload question after Apply covers addons and the layout together.
v1.8.0 (2026-10-19)New
• A plan saved on a character using the account-wide keybindings now keeps those keys too. Applying it sets the
account-wide keys to the plan's, so a new account or a fresh WoW folder gets your keys as well (before, it only
switched the character to the account-wide keys, whatever they were). Save such a plan again to add its keys.

v1.3.1 and earlier
• Save a character's action bars as a named plan of its class; a new character of that class is offered the
plan at its first login. Spells you haven't learned yet go onto their buttons when you learn them, a new rank
replaces the old one, and macros of the plan are made when missing. Minimap button and /barplan window.

addons.summary: Your action bars as a plan: record a character's bars once, set up a new character of that class from it, and every spell you learn later goes straight into its slot. Keeps which addons are on, your chat tabs, keybindings and Edit Mode layout, too.
